method: The rest of the benchmark (sets/rest145: every runnable v1.0 PR not in smoke10/dev10/holdout10/fresh10), 2026-09-28. Per PR: an expert hunt from the code (diff, base and head files, the whole repo at head) that also checked every AACR v1.0 reference comment as a lead; then an independent verifier re-checked every candidate against the code — the hunt's defects, every reference, and every comment posted by all three benchmarked reviewers (default, low, open-code-review 1.3.1; anonymised and shuffled, the reviewer key never shown) — merged duplicates, graded high/medium/low on consequence and recorded every rejection with its reason; then an adversarial critic per group of ~15 PRs spot-checked high-severity defects, exclusions, merges and grades against the code and fixed the truth in place. Claude agents throughout (a model family independent of the reviewer's).

defects.title: simplifyCompound lists TopAbs_SHELL twice and drops TopAbs_EDGE, so single-edge compounds are no longer reduced to their edge
defects.statement: The new Feature::simplifyCompound (src/Mod/Part/App/PartFeature.cpp:1326-1343) iterates {SOLID, COMPSOLID, FACE, SHELL, SHELL, WIRE, VERTEX}; the replaced inline code checked SOLID, COMPSOLID, FACE, SHELL, EDGE, WIRE, VERTEX. With EDGE missing, getTopoShape(..., NeedSubElement) on a sub-object that resolves to a compound holding one edge now returns the whole compound (an open edge has no wire and two vertices), and for a single closed edge (one vertex) it returns that VERTEX instead of the edge. Edge-expecting callers (extrusion/revolution axis links, blend curves, sweep/ruled-surface edge checks) then reject the shape or use the wrong geometry. It runs on every NeedSubElement call unless DontSimplifyCompound is set.
defects.evidence: head PartFeature.cpp:1328-1335 `std::array<TopAbs_ShapeEnum, 7> simplificationPriority = { TopAbs_SOLID, TopAbs_COMPSOLID, TopAbs_FACE, TopAbs_SHELL, TopAbs_SHELL, TopAbs_WIRE, TopAbs_VERTEX};`; the deleted base code had `else if (shape.countSubShapes(TopAbs_EDGE) == 1) shape = shape.getSubTopoShape(TopAbs_EDGE, 1);` between SHELL and WIRE.
defects.notes: Must identify the duplicated SHELL / missing EDGE in the simplification list, or equivalently that single-edge compounds are no longer simplified to the edge. Comments only about initializer_list/find_if/renaming (R9, R11) or about consolidating with TopoShapeExpansion (C8) do not count.

FreeCAD__FreeCAD@82fef4a.pr_summary: ParameterManager::LoadDocument(InputSource&) in src/Base/Parameter.cpp now owns the XercesDOMParser and DOMTreeErrorReporter through std::unique_ptr instead of raw new/delete, installs a new NoOpEntityResolver (returns nullptr for every entity) alongside the existing setDisableDefaultEntityResolution(true), replaces std::endl with "\n" in the three parse-error messages, and fixes the errorsOccured typo. defects.title: NoOpEntityResolver's 'Block all external entity resolution' comment is false: returning nullptr falls back to default resolution
defects.statement: The new NoOpEntityResolver::resolveEntity (src/Base/Parameter.cpp:1863-1870) returns nullptr with the comment 'Block all external entity resolution', and the PR presents the resolver as what 'completely block[s]' entity resolution. In Xerces-C, an EntityResolver returning a null InputSource means 'no custom source — use the parser's default resolution'; the only thing actually preventing external entity loading is the pre-existing parser->setDisableDefaultEntityResolution(true) at :1886. The resolver adds no protection, and the comment credits it with the safeguard, inviting a future maintainer to drop the real setting and reintroduce XXE.
defects.evidence: Parameter.cpp:1868 `return nullptr;  // Block all external entity resolution`; :1886 `parser->setDisableDefaultEntityResolution(true);` (pre-existing); Xerces EntityResolver contract: a null return lets the parser open the entity itself unless default resolution is disabled.
defects.notes: Must say the null-returning resolver does not itself block entities (null = default resolution) and the comment/stated purpose is misleading, the real safeguard being setDisableDefaultEntityResolution. Tests-only requests (C3) do not count.

excluded.reason: Says the unnamed parameters of NoOpEntityResolver::resolveEntity trigger a linter warning and should be named and marked unused. Style/lint only: unnamed parameters in an override (Parameter.cpp:1866) are standard C++ and the idiomatic way to mark them unused; no warning is produced for unnamed parameters by the compilers FreeCAD builds with, and naming them would not change behaviour.

Says the catch(...) message prints two consecutive newlines. The catch(...) message at Parameter.cpp:1911 prints "...parsing\n " then "\n" — the same bytes the base version printed with std::endl (minus the flush). Cosmetic, pre-existing text layout, not a defect.

Says replacing std::endl with "\n" in the error messages may delay error output because nothing flushes. std::cerr is unit-buffered (unitbuf set by default), so every insertion is flushed immediately; replacing std::endl with "\n" on cerr does not delay any error output.
Asks for a load test with an external-entity document asserting its content is not retrieved. A test request, not a defect.

FreeCAD__FreeCAD@ec3da2e.pr_summary: TechDraw refactor that moves the three predicates isCosmeticVertex / isCosmeticEdge / isCenterLine out of DrawUtil (static helpers taking an owner DocumentObject*) into DrawViewPart. The DrawUtil definitions and declarations are deleted, new definitions are added to DrawViewPart.cpp as one-argument member functions, and declarations are added to DrawViewPart.h.

defects.title: DrawViewPart.h declares static two-argument functions but DrawViewPart.cpp defines one-argument non-static members, so TechDraw does not compile
defects.statement: DrawViewPart.h:242-244 declares `static bool isCosmeticVertex(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);` (and the same for isCosmeticEdge / isCenterLine). DrawViewPart.cpp:1502, 1513 and 1523 define `bool DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(std::string element)` and the other two as one-argument members that call getProjVertexByIndex/getEdge on `this`. No declaration in the class matches these out-of-class definitions, so the compiler reports 'no declaration matches' / 'member function not declared', and the TechDraw App library fails to build. Even if the header were fixed to make them static, the bodies use `this`.
defects.evidence: DrawViewPart.h:242 `static bool isCosmeticVertex(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);` vs DrawViewPart.cpp:1502 `bool DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(std::string element)` and 1505 `auto vertex = getProjVertexByIndex(vertexIndex);`, which is an implicit this-> call.
defects.notes: The comment must point out the mismatch between the header declaration (static, owner parameter) and the cpp definition (non-static, one parameter), or say the definitions don't match any declaration. Just saying 'the refactor might not compile' without naming the signature mismatch does not count.

defects.statement: The PR removes DrawUtil::isCosmeticVertex, isCosmeticEdge and isCenterLine from DrawUtil.h and DrawUtil.cpp (base DrawUtil.h:252-254). defects.evidence: git grep at head: CosmeticExtension.cpp:71 `DU::isCosmeticVertex(getOwner(), name)`, :77 `DU::isCosmeticEdge(getOwner(), name)  ||`, :78 `DU::isCenterLine(getOwner(), name)`. No DrawUtil declaration of these remains at head.
defects.notes: The comment must name the unchanged caller in CosmeticExtension (or say that the remaining DU:: call sites were not migrated). The DrawUtil.h line numbers are base-side for the deleted declarations. Distinct from D1, the header/cpp mismatch. C7 also mentions the declaration/definition mismatch in passing, but it leads with the unmigrated CosmeticExtension callers, so it is credited here.

FreeCAD__FreeCAD@290bdc7.pr_summary: A set of small Coverity-driven fixes: updateLinkSubs no longer std::forwards its arguments repeatedly inside a loop; PropertyEnumeration::getPyPathValue returns false when the enumeration's maxValue() is negative; the Python workbench manipulator refuses to remove the menubar/toolbar root item itself; and TechDraw's WalkerEdge gets a constructor and in-class initializers for its members.

defects.title: Empty PropertyEnumeration's .Enum/.All path now fails instead of returning an empty tuple
defects.statement: Enumeration::maxValue() returns -1 for an enumeration with no entries (src/App/Enumeration.cpp:260-267), so the old `Py::Tuple res(_enum.maxValue() + 1)` built a valid empty tuple. The new guard in PropertyEnumeration::getPyPathValue (src/App/PropertyStandard.cpp:604-607) returns false for exactly that case. Callers then diverge: getPathValue (PropertyStandard.cpp:581-589) ignores the bool and converts the untouched default Py::Object (None) instead of an empty tuple, and ObjectIdentifier::getPyValue (ObjectIdentifier.cpp:1976-1985) falls through to generic attribute access, which fails for `.Enum`/`.All`. So expressions/bindings reading `Prop.Enum` or `Prop.All` of a not-yet-populated enumeration change from `()` to None/an error. The Coverity 'negative size' concern was only real for values below -1, which maxValue cannot return.
defects.evidence: Enumeration.cpp:262-266 `int num = -1; if (!enumArray.empty()) num = size-1; return num;`; head PropertyStandard.cpp `if (maxEnumValue < 0) { return false; }`; getPathValue: `Py::Object res; getPyPathValue(path, res); return pyObjectToAny(res, false);`.
defects.notes: Must point out that maxValue() is -1 for an empty enumeration (a legitimate state that previously produced an empty tuple) and that the new early return changes that result. A const-correctness remark (R1) does not count.

defects.title: Toolbar-root guard sits in an unreachable branch; the path that can actually delete the root toolbar is left unguarded (incomplete Coverity 513838 fix)
defects.statement: The new `if (item == toolBar) return;` (src/Gui/WorkbenchManipulatorPython.cpp:317-320) is inside the else branch that searches `it->findItem(command)` for each child `it`; ToolBarItem::findItem (src/Gui/ToolBarManager.cpp:84-97) returns `it` itself or one of its direct children, never the root `toolBar`, so the guard can never fire. The root can only be matched by the preceding `toolBar->findItem(command)` (WorkbenchManipulatorPython.cpp:310-313), which returns `this` when the root's own name equals the command (the root ToolBarItem is created with an empty command) and then runs `toolBar->removeItem(item); delete item;` — deleting the caller-owned root and leaving a dangling pointer. The fix protects the wrong branch and leaves the case it was meant to close open.
defects.evidence: ToolBarManager.cpp:84-88 `ToolBarItem* ToolBarItem::findItem(const std::string& name) { if ( _name == name ) { return this; } ...`; WorkbenchManipulatorPython.cpp:310-313 `if (ToolBarItem* item = toolBar->findItem(command)) { toolBar->removeItem(item); delete item; }` with no root check; the new guard at 317 compares a result of `it->findItem` (it = child of toolBar) against toolBar.
defects.notes: Must say the item==toolBar guard is in the wrong/unreachable branch and the first `toolBar->findItem(command)` branch can still delete the root. A comment saying only that the guard is dead code and should be removed (without noting the root is still deletable) is a near-miss; the menubar guard (C6/C8) is a different site and is reachable.

excluded.reason: Suggests declaring `maxEnumValue` as `const auto`. Const-correctness style only.

FreeCAD__FreeCAD@870d7f5.pr_summary: Adds ModelManagerExternal, an LRU-cached front for the Python external materials interface built under BUILD_MATERIAL_EXTERNAL, and wires it into ModelManager behind a 'UseExternal' preference watched through a ParameterGrp observer. External libraries and models take precedence over local ones, and migrate/validate/hit-rate helpers are added. ModelLibrary is split into a base ModelLibrary (with an isLocal flag) and ModelLibraryLocal, which owns the path map and addModel/getModelByPath; the loader and local manager switch to ModelLibraryLocal. ModelLibrary::getModelTree is rebuilt from ModelManager::libraryModels() (uuid, directory, name) instead of the library's own path map. Library gains a copy constructor.

defects.title: With UseExternal on and the external interface unavailable, ModelManager::libraryModels lets ConnectionError escape, so building any library's model tree fails
defects.statement: ModelManager::libraryModels (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:205-221) calls _externalManager->libraryModels when _useExternal is set and catches only LibraryNotFound and InvalidModel. ModelManagerExternal::libraryModels (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:115-118) forwards straight to ExternalManager::libraryModels, whose connect() throws ConnectionError whenever the external module is not configured ('Current' defaults to 'None') or fails to instantiate (ExternalManager.cpp:136-145, 453). That ConnectionError is not caught, so instead of falling back to the local models it escapes through ModelLibrary::getModelTree (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelLibrary.cpp:75) into ModelSelect::fillTree. Every library tree in the model selector fails whenever a user turns UseExternal on without a reachable interface. The sibling paths show what was intended: getLibraries and getModel in ModelManagerExternal do catch ConnectionError (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:86, 141).
defects.evidence: src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:210-219: `auto models = _externalManager->libraryModels(libraryName); ... catch (const LibraryNotFound& e) {} catch (const InvalidModel& e) {}`. ExternalManager.cpp:136-143 `if (!_instantiated) { instantiate(); if (!_instantiated) { throw ConnectionError(); } }`, and ExternalManager::libraryModels calls connect() first (line 453). getModelTree (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelLibrary.cpp:75) is reached for every library by Gui/ModelSelect.cpp:342-349 fillTree, which has no try/catch.
defects.notes: A finding must say that ConnectionError (or 'other exceptions from the external manager') is not handled in ModelManager::libraryModels / the external libraryModels path, so the local fallback does not happen. Generic 'empty catch blocks should log' comments (R28) do not count.

defects.title: Models at a library's root now sit under a folder with an empty name in the rebuilt model tree
defects.statement: getModelTree now splits the model's directory (the second tuple element, model->getDirectory()) on '/' (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelLibrary.cpp:83) and then adds the model under that folder chain (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelLibrary.cpp:104). For a model file at the library root, addModel sets the directory to getLibraryPath('Foo.yml', 'Foo.yml') == '' (Library.cpp getLibraryPath; ModelLibrary.cpp addModel). QString('').split('/') returns [''] (KeepEmptyParts), so the loop creates a folder node keyed '' and puts the model inside it. Before this PR the relative file name was split, so a root-level model became a direct leaf. In a User or Custom model library, root-level models therefore show up under an unnamed folder in ModelSelect.
defects.evidence: src/Mod/Material/App/ModelLibrary.cpp:78 `auto path = std::get<1>(it);` :83 `QStringList list = path.split(QStringLiteral("/"));` (no SkipEmptyParts), :86-97 create a folder for each element, :104 `(*node)[filename] = child;`. ModelManagerLocal.cpp:166-168 builds the tuple from `it.second->getDirectory()`. Library.cpp getLibraryPath strips the filename, returning '' for a root file.
defects.notes: Counts if a comment points out that splitting an empty/leading/trailing-slash path produces empty segments and hence empty folder nodes (R7's SkipEmptyParts suggestion lands on this). A pure style comment about the split does not count. C12/C22/C46 state it directly (empty directory -> empty-name folder).

defects.title: ModelManagerLocal::getLibraries reinterpret_casts shared_ptr<list<shared_ptr<ModelLibraryLocal>>> to shared_ptr<list<shared_ptr<ModelLibrary>>>, which is undefined behaviour
defects.statement: Once _libraryList becomes a list of shared_ptr<ModelLibraryLocal>, getLibraries (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerLocal.cpp:99-103) returns it by reinterpret_cast to a reference to a different, unrelated template instantiation. That is a strict-aliasing violation and undefined behaviour. It only 'works' because ModelLibrary is the first, non-virtual base, so the pointers happen to coincide. The returned list also claims to hold ModelLibrary: any caller that inserts a non-local ModelLibrary into it corrupts the local manager's list, which is later static_cast to ModelLibraryLocal.
defects.evidence: src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerLocal.cpp:101 `return reinterpret_cast<std::shared_ptr<std::list<std::shared_ptr<ModelLibrary>>>&>(_libraryList);` with ModelManagerLocal.h:80 `static std::shared_ptr<std::list<std::shared_ptr<ModelLibraryLocal>>> _libraryList;`.
defects.notes: Must name the reinterpret_cast between the two list types as unsafe/UB, or say a proper copy/conversion is needed. R32's generic 'prefer polymorphism' design remark does not identify the cast and does not count.

defects.title: validateMigration dereferences a null external model when a migrated model is missing, crashing instead of reporting a validation failure
defects.statement: ModelManagerExternal::getModel swallows ModelNotFound and ConnectionError and returns nullptr (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:137-144). ModelManager::validateMigration passes that result straight to model->validate(externalModel) (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:353-354), and Model::validate dereferences it immediately (`*(other->_library)`, Model.cpp:208). Exactly the case the validation exists to catch, a model that did not reach the external store, becomes a null-pointer crash rather than an InvalidModel.
defects.evidence: src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:353-354 `auto externalModel = _externalManager->getModel(uuid); model->validate(externalModel);`. src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:137-140 `catch (const ModelNotFound& e) { _cache.emplace(uuid.toStdString(), nullptr); return nullptr; }`. Model.cpp:205-208 `void Model::validate(const std::shared_ptr<Model>& other) const { ... _library->validate(*(other->_library));`.
defects.notes: Needs the null result of the external getModel reaching validate() in validateMigration. R30 (null check on the `model` parameter of addModel/migrateModel) is a different site and does not count. There are no in-tree callers yet (the API is being laid down for the migration tooling), hence low.

defects.title: ModelManager::getLibrary's local fallback is unreachable with UseExternal on: the external getLibrary throws LibraryNotFound instead of returning null
defects.statement: ModelManager::getLibrary (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:168-179) calls _externalManager->getLibrary(name) and falls back to _localManager->getLibrary only if the result is null. ModelManagerExternal::getLibrary (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:92-105) never returns null: it rethrows LibraryNotFound and maps ConnectionError to LibraryNotFound (ExternalManager::getLibrary raises CreationError on a Python error, which also escapes). So with UseExternal on, looking up any local-only library (e.g. User, workbench libraries) or any library while the provider is unreachable throws, whereas before this PR getLibrary was local-only and succeeded.
defects.evidence: ModelManager.cpp:172-175 `auto library = _externalManager->getLibrary(name); if (library) { return library; }` with no try/catch; ModelManagerExternal.cpp:99-104 `catch (const LibraryNotFound& e) { throw LibraryNotFound(e); } catch (const ConnectionError& e) { throw LibraryNotFound(e.what()); }`. Base ModelManager.cpp:161-164 was `return _localManager->getLibrary(name);`. isLocalLibrary (ModelManager.cpp:228-235) shows the intended try/catch shape. No in-tree caller of ModelManager::getLibrary was found, hence low.
defects.notes: Must say the external getLibrary throws (LibraryNotFound) rather than returning null, so the null check/local fallback never runs. Comments about precedence of same-named libraries do not count.

defects.title: A transient ConnectionError is cached as a permanent 'model missing' (nullptr) in the external model cache
defects.statement: ModelManagerExternal::getModel (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:141-144) stores nullptr in the process-wide LRU cache when the provider raises ConnectionError, and line 128-129 returns any cached entry without retrying. After the outage ends, the UUID keeps resolving to null from the external source (ModelManager::getModel then falls back to local, or throws ModelNotFound for external-only models) until LRU eviction; nothing in normal operation clears the cache (resetCache is reached only via ModelManagerExternal::refresh, which ModelManager::refresh does not call).
defects.evidence: ModelManagerExternal.cpp:128-130 `if (_cache.contains(uuid.toStdString())) { return _cache.lookup(uuid.toStdString()); }`; :141-143 `catch (const ConnectionError& e) { _cache.emplace(uuid.toStdString(), nullptr); return nullptr; }`. grep: resetCache is called only from ModelManagerExternal::refresh (line 65).
defects.notes: Must say the connection-failure branch caches null (negative caching of a transient error) so later lookups don't retry. A comment only asking to log the error does not count.

defects.title: ModelManager::refresh refreshes only the local manager; the new external cache is never invalidated
defects.statement: The PR adds ModelManagerExternal::refresh (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:63-66, clears the LRU cache) but ModelManager::refresh (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:119-122) still only calls _localManager->refresh(). With UseExternal on, a public refresh leaves stale external models (and cached nulls) in place; the external refresh is dead code.
defects.evidence: ModelManager.cpp:121 `_localManager->refresh();` only; grep shows no caller of ModelManagerExternal::refresh or resetCache. OnChange (ModelManager.cpp:100) even has `// _dbManager->refresh();` commented out.
defects.notes: Must say ModelManager::refresh should also refresh/clear the external manager/cache.

defects.title: External model-library discovery uses libraries() instead of modelLibraries(), so material-only libraries appear in the model selector
defects.statement: ModelManagerExternal::getLibraries (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:78) calls ExternalManager::libraries(), which the external API documents as returning all libraries; modelLibraries() exists precisely to return only libraries containing models (MaterialAPI/MaterialManagerExternal.py modelLibraries docstring; ExternalManager::modelLibraries). ModelManager::getLibraries feeds ModelSelect, so libraries with no models are offered as model libraries.
defects.evidence: ModelManagerExternal.cpp:78 `auto externalLibraries = ExternalManager::getManager()->libraries();`. MaterialManagerExternal.py: `def modelLibraries(self)` ... 'This differs from the libraries() function in that it only returns libraries containing model objects.'
defects.notes: Must name libraries() vs modelLibraries() (or 'material-only libraries listed as model libraries').

defects.title: ModelManager::cleanup returns before the new external cleanup block, making it unreachable
defects.statement: src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:111 `return ModelManagerLocal::cleanup();` precedes the newly added `#if defined(BUILD_MATERIAL_EXTERNAL) if (_externalManager) _externalManager->cleanup();` block (lines 112-116), so the external cleanup never runs. ModelManagerExternal::cleanup is empty today, so there is no runtime effect yet, but the added code is dead and will silently not run once cleanup gains content.
defects.evidence: ModelManager.cpp:111-116 as quoted; ModelManagerExternal.cpp:59-61 `void ModelManagerExternal::cleanup() {}`.
defects.notes: Must point out the early return making the external cleanup unreachable.

defects.title: getModelTree aborts the whole library tree when one listed external model cannot be fetched
defects.statement: ModelLibrary::getModelTree (src/Mod/Material/App/ModelLibrary.cpp:75-82) calls ModelManager::getModel for each UUID the (external) library lists. If ModelManagerExternal::getModel returns null (ModelNotFound or a cached ConnectionError, ModelManagerExternal.cpp:137-144), ModelManager::getModel falls back to _localManager->getModel, which throws ModelNotFound for an external-only UUID (ModelManagerLocal.cpp:184-185). Nothing in getModelTree or ModelSelect::fillTree catches it, so one unavailable entry prevents the entire library's tree from being built.
defects.evidence: ModelManager.cpp:282-289 `auto model = _externalManager->getModel(uuid); if (model) return model; ... return _localManager->getModel(uuid);`; ModelManagerLocal.cpp:184-185 `catch (std::out_of_range const&) { throw ModelNotFound(); }`; ModelLibrary.cpp:81 no try/catch.
defects.notes: Must say that an unavailable listed model leads to an exception (ModelNotFound) that aborts tree construction. Comments claiming a null dereference at ModelLibrary.cpp:82 (C15, C49) are wrong about the mechanism: ModelManager::getModel never returns null.

FreeCAD__FreeCAD@39c5968.pr_summary: Static-analyzer tidy-up of src/App/Application.cpp with no intended behaviour change. It switches Base::Interpreter().addType to the static InterpreterSingleton::addType, replaces the repetitive custom Python exception setup with a local `setup` lambda, uses auto/if-init/ternaries, adds vector reserve() calls, replaces std::endl with '\n', renames shadowing locals (obj→obj2, args→args2), adds static_casts, and restructures the macOS FindHomePath buffer allocation into an if-with-initializer. Verified: InterpreterSingleton::addType is static (Base/Interpreter.h:288); the if-init buffer in FindHomePath is freed in both branches; std::string(RESOURCEDIR) is equivalent to the old .c_str() round-trip (both stop at the first NUL).

excluded.reason: The claim is that the setup lambda's `str` init-capture/std::string parameter causes needless string conversions. This is a micro-optimization/style remark about the lambda's init-capture (deduced as const char*, concatenated once per exception) in one-time startup code (Application.cpp:402-407). There is no functional or measurable impact.

The claim is that the `str {"Base."}` init-capture should be declared const. Const-correctness of an init-capture is a style preference. The lambda is not mutable, so the captured copy is already const inside operator().

The claim is that the unqualified PyExc_FC_* assignments in setupPythonException may fail to compile or assign different symbols than the old Base::PyExc_FC_* globals. Wrong: Application.cpp:174 has `using namespace Base;`, so the unqualified PyExc_FC_* names resolve to the Base:: globals declared in Base/PyObjectBase.h (e.g. :432) and defined in PyObjectBase.cpp. No other symbols with those names exist, so the assignments target the same variables as before. Verified: head Application.cpp:174-175 has `using namespace App; using namespace Base;`, and PyExc_FC_* are declared only in Base (PyObjectBase.h).
The claim is that `path[0] == '\0'` in getDocumentByPath should use an isNullOrEmpty() helper. `path[0] == '\0'` vs `!path[0]` is equivalent, and whether to use a helper is style.

The claim is that FindHomePath's manual new[]/delete[] of the _NSGetExecutablePath buffer can leak and should use unique_ptr. This is pre-existing manual new/delete, which the PR only restructured. Both branches still delete the buffer (head Application.cpp:3491 and :3502), and realpath/_NSGetExecutablePath are C functions that cannot throw, so no leak path exists. Verified: the if-with-initializer's else branch still runs `delete [] buf` (head Application.cpp ~3502), so both paths free the buffer, as the base did.

FreeCAD__FreeCAD@e596925.pr_summary: Adds a C++ CalculiX .frd reader (namespace FRDReader in src/Mod/Fem/App/FemVTKTools.cpp) that parses the node block, element block and nodal result blocks into a vtkMultiBlockDataSet with one vtkUnstructuredGrid per (step, analysis type), writes it as a .vtm next to the input with vtkXMLMultiBlockDataWriter, and exposes it as FemVTKTools::frdToVTK and the Python function Fem.frdToVTK(filename).

defects.title: Result loop exits on the node count before the last node's ' -2' continuation line is read
defects.statement: readResults loops `while (countNodes < info.numNodes && std::getline(...))` (FemVTKTools.cpp:1453) and increments countNodes when it reads each node's first ' -1' record (1482). The tuple is written only when vecValues+scaValues reach numComps (1498). For datasets with more than 6 components the remaining values are on ' -2' continuation lines; after the LAST node's ' -1' line countNodes == numNodes, the tuple is not yet complete, and the loop terminates before the continuation is consumed. The last node's result silently stays at the 0.0 fill.
defects.evidence: 1453 `while (countNodes < info.numNodes && std::getline(ifstr, line))`; 1482 `++countNodes;` at the end of the code1 (' -1') branch; 1484 `else if (view.rfind(code2, 0) == 0)` handles continuations; 1498 `if ((vecValues.size() + scaValues.size()) == numComps)`. A ' -1' record carries at most 6 E12.5 values (node lines in box_static.frd are 85 chars = 3+10+6*12).
defects.notes: Must say the loop stops on the node counter after the final ' -1' record so the final node's ' -2' continuation is never read and its tuple is missing/zero for >6-component datasets. The countScaPos classification bug (D2) is a different defect.

defects.title: countScaPos not advanced on ' -2' continuation lines, misrouting scalar/vector components
defects.statement: In the code2 branch (FemVTKTools.cpp:1486-1496) the loop over continuation values is `it += 12` without `++countScaPos`, unlike the code1 loop at 1467. Every continuation value is looked up in scalarPos at the same position, so in a >6-component dataset that mixes scalar and vector/tensor entities values go to the wrong collection (vecValues vs scaValues) and the arrays are filled with misplaced components.
defects.evidence: 1467 `for (auto it = sub.begin(); it != sub.end(); it += 12, ++countScaPos)`; 1486 `for (auto it = sub.begin(); it != sub.end(); it += 12)`; 1489 `std::find(scalarPos.begin(), scalarPos.end(), countScaPos)`.
defects.notes: Must identify the missing countScaPos increment in the continuation branch. Comments that ALSO claim skipping `digits` chars on the ' -2' line loses the first value count for this defect only via the countScaPos part (the skip itself is correct: CalculiX writes the node-width field blank on continuation records).

defects.title: valueFromLine<double> parses with strtof, rounding doubles to float
defects.statement: The double specialisation of valueFromLine (FemVTKTools.cpp:1098-1102) uses std::strtof, so every node coordinate, result value and the result header's time/frequency value (read from a 12-char field with up to 10 decimals, 1339) is rounded through 32-bit float before being stored in double/vtkDoubleArray, adding float-rounding noise and losing precision in e.g. time values.
defects.evidence: 1101 `value = std::strtof(sub.data(), nullptr);` inside `void valueFromLine<double>(..., double& value)`.
defects.notes: Must say strtof (float) is used where strtod is needed. Generic 'no error checking on strtol/strtof' remarks do not count.

defects.title: vtkXMLMultiBlockDataWriter missing from PreCompiled.h, breaking precompiled-header builds
defects.statement: The new `#include <vtkXMLMultiBlockDataWriter.h>` is added only inside the `#ifndef _PreComp_` block of FemVTKTools.cpp (61). With FREECAD_USE_PCH (default ON, MSVC PCH set up in src/Mod/Fem/App/CMakeLists.txt:194-197) that block is skipped and PreCompiled.h does not include the header, so vtkXMLMultiBlockDataWriter is undeclared at 1606 and the Fem module fails to compile.
defects.evidence: FemVTKTools.cpp:26 `#ifndef _PreComp_`; PreCompiled.h VTK list (155-194) has vtkXMLDataSetWriter/vtkXMLUnstructuredGridWriter but no vtkXMLMultiBlockDataWriter; InitializeFreeCADBuildOptions.cmake:31 `option(FREECAD_USE_PCH ... ON)`.
defects.notes: Must mention the precompiled-header (PreCompiled.h / _PreComp_) build. Generic include-hygiene remarks do not count. Severity raised to high by critic: FREECAD_USE_PCH defaults ON under MSVC (InitializeFreeCADBuildOptions.cmake:31, inside if(MSVC)) and Fem's CMakeLists adds -D_PreComp_, so the default Windows build of the Fem module fails to compile; a build break on a primary platform is merge-blocking.

excluded.reason: Claims filename leaks if frdToVTK throws because PyMem_Free comes after the call. Wrong: AppFemPy.cpp copies into encodedName and calls PyMem_Free(filename) BEFORE FemVTKTools::frdToVTK.
Claims the std::string copy of filename is unnecessary. Wrong: filename is freed before the call, so the copy is required.
Suggests marking the lookup maps const/constexpr. Style; no behavioural effect.
Suggests std::array instead of std::map for the type tables. Micro-optimisation, not a defect.

Claims identifyScalarEntities classifies D1-D3 as scalars so displacement becomes scalar arrays/no DISP vector. Wrong: the -5 parse skips the MENU field (1393), so for ` -5  D1          1    2    1    0` et = {2,1,0,0} (type 2, row 1) and the predicate `et[0]==1 || et[1]<1` is false -> vector.

Claims displacement (and stress) components are treated as scalar arrays because the first metadata field is 1. Wrong: that first field is MENU, skipped at 1393; et[0] is TYPE (2 for DISP, 4 for STRESS) and et[1] >= 1, so they are classified as vector/tensor components.

Says the converter ignores the 1D-flow `_inout_nodes.txt` remapping done by the Python importer. The converter is a new standalone entry point, not wired to replace the importer; unsupported special topology is a scope gap, not a regression.
Asks to remove the unused mapElem. Dead code/style, no functional effect.
Asks to remove the unused element-ID map mapElem. Dead code/style, no functional effect.
Asks to remove the unused `nodes` vector. Dead code; trivial memory, no functional effect.
Asks to drop the unread `nodes` collection. Dead code; no functional effect.

Claims a missing result node can still reach mapNodes.at(node) at 1500 and throw, especially after a -2 continuation. When at() throws in the -1 branch no values for that node are collected, so vec+sca sizes stay below numComps (continuations can add at most numComps minus the first line's values) and 1498 never fires for that node.

Claims an unknown node's record later reaches mapNodes.at(node) outside the catch and throws. Same as C10: the values are never collected for that node, so the completion check at 1498 is never satisfied and at() is not reached.
Asks for a selectable output destination / returned filename. API design request, not a defect.
Asks the Python API to return the written VTM path. API design request, not a defect.

Asks to remove the empty readParameter handler and its dispatch. Style/dead code.

Claims strtol reads past the fixed-width field and &*it is UB when a record ends early. On CalculiX's fixed-width records fields are delimited by blanks or signs, strtol stops there, and loops only dereference while it != end; no concrete misparse is shown.
Asks to remove the commented-out from_chars implementation. Style.
Asks to delete getFirstNotBlankPos and the commented-out parser. Dead code/style.

Claims et[3] is not an ignore flag and all STRESS components are dropped. Wrong: the parse skips MENU (1393), so et = {TYPE, IND1, IND2, IEXIST}; for ` -5  SXX         1    4    1    1` IEXIST is absent -> et[3]=0 and the component is kept; only the predefined `ALL` entry (IEXIST=1) is dropped.

defects.title: Watch-mode status lines print a doubled space after switching Fprint to Fprintln with trailing-space literals
defects.statement: internal/execute/watch.go:45 and :48 changed fmt.Fprint(w, "build starting at ", now, newline) to fmt.Fprintln(w.sys.Writer(), "build starting at ", w.sys.Now()) (likewise "build finished in ", duration). fmt.Fprint adds a space between operands only when neither is a string, so the old output had one space; fmt.Fprintln always adds a space between operands, so the new output is "build starting at  <time>" / "build finished in  <dur>" with two spaces — a user-visible formatting regression in watch mode.
defects.evidence: watch.go:45 `fmt.Fprintln(w.sys.Writer(), "build starting at ", w.sys.Now())`; :48 `fmt.Fprintln(w.sys.Writer(), "build finished in ", w.sys.Now().Sub(timeStart))`; base used fmt.Fprint with the same literals plus w.sys.NewLine(). Go fmt: Fprintln always separates operands with spaces.
defects.notes: Must point at watch.go 45/48 and say Fprintln adds a separator so the trailing space yields a double/extra space. Comments about the commented-out Fprintln lines in watcher.go do not count.

excluded.reason: Claims the Fprintln at internal/execute/watcher.go:83 inserts unintended spaces between arguments. That line (and :59, :91) is a commented-out statement, so it produces no output.

microsoft__typescript-go@b970689.pr_summary: Adds KindJSImportDeclaration (sharing the ImportDeclaration data struct) and makes the JS reparser turn every JSDoc `@import` tag into a synthetic type-only import statement inserted into the enclosing statement list. Checker, grammar checks, LS, printer, encoder and transformers treat the new kind like ImportDeclaration; the old JSDocImportTag special cases (GetExternalModuleName, ModuleSpecifier, IsDefaultImport, isExclusivelyTypeOnlyImportOrExport, tryGetImportFromModuleSpecifier, the text-scan branch of ForEachDynamicImportOrRequireCall) are removed. Baselines updated.

defects.title: `@import` with no import clause (`/** @import "mod" */` or a half-typed tag) dereferences a nil ImportClause and panics the parser
defects.statement: reparser.go:120 calls `importTag.ImportClause.Clone(&p.factory)` unconditionally. parseImportTag (jsdoc.go:855-868) takes the clause from tryParseImportClause, which returns nil when no identifier, `*` or `{` follows `@import` (parser.go:2195-2205) - a side-effect `@import "mod"` or any incomplete tag. Node.Clone dereferences n.data, so a nil clause panics (and lines 121-122 would deref the nil result). Any JS/JSX file whose JSDoc on a statement contains such a tag crashes parsing, taking down tsgo or the language server while the user types.
defects.evidence: reparser.go:119-122 `importTag := tag.AsJSDocImportTag(); importClause := importTag.ImportClause.Clone(&p.factory); importClause.Flags |= ast.NodeFlagsReparsed; importClause.AsImportClause().IsTypeOnly = true`. parser.go tryParseImportClause: `if identifier != nil || p.token == ast.KindAsteriskToken || p.token == ast.KindOpenBraceToken { ... } return nil`. ImportClause.Clone / Node.Clone call through n.data with no nil guard.
defects.notes: Must say the import clause can be nil (side-effect / clause-less / malformed @import) and that the unguarded Clone/deref crashes. A generic 'add nil checks' not naming the clause is a near miss.

defects.title: Synthetic import shares its bindings/specifier with the JSDoc tag; for a non-function host the binder re-parents them to the JSDocImportTag, so resolving a named or namespace @import panics (and the '/' completion trigger is lost)
defects.statement: The reparser clones only the ImportClause shell; NamedBindings, the default name, ModuleSpecifier and Attributes are the same nodes as in the JSDocImportTag (reparser.go:120-123; ImportClause.Clone reuses node.NamedBindings). parseListIndex inserts the synthetic declaration BEFORE its host statement (parser.go:477-481). bindEachStatementFunctionsFirst binds function declarations first, but for any other host (variable statement, class, export const, expression statement) the synthetic import is bound first and the host afterwards; binding the host calls setJSDocParents -> ast.SetParentInChildren(jsdoc) (binder.go:757-761), which overwrites the shared children's Parent back to the original ImportClause / JSDocImportTag. The checker then walks parents: getTargetOfImportSpecifier takes root = node.Parent.Parent.Parent (checker.go ~13800), which is now the JSDocImportTag, and ast.GetExternalModuleName no longer has a JSDocImportTag case (removed by this PR) so it panics 'Unhandled case in getExternalModuleName' (utilities.go:1678-1699); a namespace import hits getModuleSpecifierFromNode(JSDocImportTag) and panics the same way. checkImportDeclaration -> checkImportBinding -> resolveAlias runs this for every such tag, so `/** @import { Foo } from './types' */ export const x = ...` crashes type-checking. The same stale parent makes tryGetImportFromModuleSpecifier (ls/utilities.go:21-24, whose JSDocImportTag case was removed) return nil, disabling the '/' completion trigger in that tag's module specifier. All conformance tests use function hosts, which is why they pass.
defects.evidence: parser.go:477-481 `elt := parseElement(p, i); if len(p.reparseList) > 0 { list = append(list, p.reparseList...) ... } list = append(list, elt)` (reparsed nodes precede the host). binder.go:1642-1652 functions first, then others in order. binder.go:757-761 `setParent(jsdoc, node); ast.SetParentInChildren(jsdoc)`; SetParentInChildren sets node.Parent for every descendant. ast.go:4216 `NewImportClause(node.IsTypeOnly, node.Name(), node.NamedBindings)` (children shared). checker.go getTargetOfImportSpecifier: `root := node.Parent.Parent.Parent // ImportDeclaration ... c.getExternalModuleMember(root, ...)` -> `ast.GetExternalModuleName(node)`; utilities.go:1699 `panic("Unhandled case in getExternalModuleName")`.
defects.notes: Counts if a comment says the synthetic import reuses the tag's child nodes so their parent pointers end up pointing at the JSDoc tag (e.g. after the host's JSDoc is parented) and that module-specifier / import resolution then hits a JSDocImportTag and fails or panics. C11 counts as a partial hit (names the removed JSDocImportTag case in tryGetImportFromModuleSpecifier and the parent-still-JSDocImportTag consequence). Generic 'shares nodes, may be fragile' without the parent/crash consequence does not count; R1 (Node.ModuleSpecifier()) does not count.

defects.title: `@import` in JSDoc below top level becomes a block-level import: false TS1473 error, names never bound, module no longer collected for resolution
defects.statement: The synthetic JSImportDeclaration is flushed into whatever list is being parsed, so an @import in the JSDoc of a statement inside a function body or block becomes a statement of that Block. checkImportDeclaration (checker.go:4914-4925) calls checkGrammarModuleElementContext (grammarchecks.go:189-194), which reports 'An import declaration can only be used at the top level of a module' and bails out; Strada binds @import at file scope from any JSDoc. Module collection regresses too: the PR deletes the JSDocImportTag branch of ForEachDynamicImportOrRequireCall (base utilities.go:2557-2563), which found @import tags anywhere, while collectExternalModuleReferences (references.go:11-14) only visits top-level statements, so a nested @import's module is not added to file.Imports or resolved.
defects.evidence: checker.go:4917-4925 JS files get An_import_declaration_can_only_be_used_at_the_top_level_of_a_module then `return`. grammarchecks.go:190 `isInAppropriateContext := node.Parent.Kind == ast.KindSourceFile || ...ModuleBlock || ...ModuleDeclaration`. Base utilities.go:2557 `} else if includeTypeSpaceImports && node.Kind == KindJSDocImportTag {` (deleted; the deleted ForEachDynamicImportOrRequireCall branch is a base-side site). references.go:12 `for _, node := range file.Statements.Nodes { collectModuleReferences(...) }`.
defects.notes: Counts if a comment says non-top-level @import tags (inside functions/blocks) now error or go unresolved, or that removing the JSDocImportTag branch of ForEachDynamicImportOrRequireCall loses nested @import module references. Architectural 'should be handled earlier' transformer comments do not count.

excluded.reason: Claims removing KindJSDocImportTag from Node.ModuleSpecifier() may cause runtime panics on JSDocImportTag nodes. The only .ModuleSpecifier() caller (ls/completions.go:2279-2281) is guarded by IsImportDeclaration-style kind checks, so no path reaches it with a JSDocImportTag; the real crash via stale parents goes through GetExternalModuleName/getModuleSpecifierFromNode (D2), which R1 does not name.

Claims IsDefaultImport calling AsImportDeclaration() on KindJSImportDeclaration may panic if it has its own struct. Both kinds are built by newImportOrJSImportDeclaration with the same *ImportDeclaration data (ast.go:4037-4051), so the accessor is valid.

Claims calling AsImportDeclaration() on a KindExportDeclaration parent in getSymbolAtLocation panics. That ExportDeclaration disjunct and the AsImportDeclaration call are pre-existing at the base; the PR only added the correct JSImportDeclaration disjunct.

Claims directly mutating IsTypeOnly after cloning violates immutability assumptions. The clone is a fresh parser-owned node and reparser.go mutates Flags on reparsed nodes throughout; style, no consequence.
Claims emitStatement lacks a KindJSImportDeclaration case. The PR adds it at printer.go:3956, routed to emitImportDeclaration.

Claims the CommonJS module transformer should not handle JSImportDeclaration and it should be normalized earlier. Layering opinion; the type eraser already removes these type-only imports and the extra case is a harmless defensive drop.
Claims the ES module transformer should not set JSImportDeclaration to nil but handle it earlier. Same as R7: a defensive drop with no incorrect output.
Claims adding KindJSImportDeclaration to transformUsingDeclarations is misplaced. Treating it like the other import kinds (kept at top level) is correct and no failure is named.

Claims including KindJSImportDeclaration in externalModuleInfo collection adds runtime dependencies for type-only imports. Module info is collected by the module transformer after the type eraser (transformer.go:74) has already removed every JSImportDeclaration (clause IsTypeOnly, typeeraser.go:258-275), so nothing is added.
Claims grouping ImportDeclaration and JSImportDeclaration in externalmoduleinfo assumes AsImportDeclaration works for both. They share the *ImportDeclaration struct (see R2).

Claims adding JSImportDeclaration to ImportElisionTransformer.visit is incorrect because they should never reach it. Import elision is disabled for JS files (transformer.go:59), so the case is dead but harmless.
Claims the JSImportDeclaration case in importelision.go:169 is redundant. Redundancy/style with no behavioural consequence.

Claims JSImportDeclaration needs its own elide case in typeeraser rather than being grouped with ImportDeclaration. Grouping is correct: its clause is always IsTypeOnly so the shared path elides it exactly like `import type`.

Claims the importTag3.types baseline regressed from 'Foo' to 'default'. The display comes from Corsa's simplified symbolToString (checker/printer.go:37-40 prints s.Name, which is 'default' for a default-exported interface) and affects any default type import (e.g. duplicatePackage.types); the base did not bind @import at all ('Cannot find name Foo'), so this PR introduces no display regression of its own.

Claims synthetic @import declarations ignore the tag's `resolution-mode` attribute and resolve against the wrong conditional export (importTag17). Module resolution mode is hard-coded to CommonJS for every import in fileloader.go (`mode := core.ModuleKindCommonJS // !!!`, lines 369/415), unchanged at the base; the base baseline was already wrong ('Cannot find name Import'), so this is a pre-existing limitation, not introduced here.

Claims a valid `@import { Import } from 'foo' with { 'resolution-mode': 'import' }` now reports that Import does not exist because resolution ignores the requested mode. Same pre-existing hard-coded CommonJS resolution mode as C1.

Claims KindJSExportAssignment now gets a children mask but getNodeDefinedData still omits it, so IsExportEquals encodes as 0. The defined-data gap for JSExportAssignment predates this PR (base had neither mask nor data); the PR only fixed the mask and did not make the flag encoding worse.
Claims default-imported types now display as 'default' instead of 'Foo'. Pre-existing Corsa symbolToString limitation, see R15.
Claims default imported types lose their local name in displayed signatures (importTag3/importTag16). Same pre-existing display limitation as R15.
Claims the second `IsTypeOnly = true` is a redundant duplicate assignment. Style only; no behaviour.

Claims UpdateImportDeclaration and Clone rebuild via NewImportDeclaration so a visitor would convert a JSImportDeclaration into an ordinary import. Latent only: the type eraser (first transform) removes every JSImportDeclaration because its clause is always type-only, import elision is disabled for JS, and no declaration transformer exists yet, so no current path rebuilds one.
Claims Clone/UpdateImportDeclaration lose the synthetic kind and could turn a JSDoc import into a runtime import. Same latent, currently unreachable concern as C6.

Claims VisitEachChild/Clone/UpdateImportDeclaration convert a JSImportDeclaration into a regular import, e.g. via import elision. Import elision is not enabled for JS files (transformer.go:59) and the type eraser elides these nodes first, so the example path does not exist; latent as C6.

Claims externalModuleInfo counts erased synthetic imports for hasImportStar/hasImportDefault, adding an unneeded tslib import. The collector runs in the module transformer after the type eraser has removed every JSImportDeclaration, so it never sees them.

Claims inserting KindJSImportDeclaration renumbers kinds and desyncs the TS API client's SyntaxKind table. The client table was already out of sync at the base (it lacks JSTypeAliasDeclaration/JSExportAssignment/CommonJSExport; NotEmittedStatement is 345 there vs 348+ in Go), so the PR does not introduce the mismatch.
Claims IsDefaultImport's accepted-node comment should mention JSImportDeclaration. Doc-comment request; no behaviour.

microsoft__typescript-go@45c0de9.pr_summary: Refactors LanguageService.GetDocumentDiagnostics to collect diagnostic slices (syntactic, or semantic + suggestion) and adds declaration diagnostics when the program emits declarations; conversion to LSP diagnostics moves into a variadic helper toLSPDiagnostics, and the explicit Kind: StringLiteralFull{} field is dropped (its zero value still marshals to "full").

defects.title: toLSPDiagnostics passes nil converters, so every non-empty diagnostic report panics
defects.statement: The new helper calls toLSPDiagnostic(diag, nil) (diagnostics.go:44) instead of passing l.converters as the old code did. toLSPDiagnostic unconditionally calls converters.ToLSPRange for the diagnostic range (diagnostics.go:86) and for each related-information entry (:68); ToLSPRange -> PositionToLineAndCharacter calls c.getLineMap on the receiver (converters.go:207-210), a nil pointer dereference on a nil *Converters. Any file with at least one syntactic/semantic/suggestion/declaration diagnostic therefore panics the textDocument/diagnostic request instead of returning diagnostics; the comment 'converters can be nil if not needed' is false.
defects.evidence: diagnostics.go:44 `toLSPDiagnostic(diag, nil) // converters can be nil if not needed`; :86 `Range: converters.ToLSPRange(diagnostic.File(), diagnostic.Loc())`; converters.go:210 `lineMap := c.getLineMap(script.FileName())`. Base code passed `l.converters`.
defects.notes: Must identify the nil converters argument (lost l.converters) and that it crashes/panics when diagnostics exist. Removal of `Kind: StringLiteralFull{}` is NOT a defect (zero-value struct marshals "full").

excluded.reason: Asks for a regression test that declaration diagnostics appear only when declaration emit is enabled. Test-coverage request, not a defect.

microsoft__typescript-go@100dbc5.pr_summary: Ports more of Strada's `tsc --help` rendering into internal/execute/outputs.go: generateOptionOutput now prints each option's name, description, a 'type:/one of:/one or more:' candidates line and a 'default:' line, via new helpers formatDefaultValue, getValueCandidate, getPossibleValues (grouping enum synonyms) and showAdditionalInfoOutput. Only the narrow-terminal branch is implemented (terminal width is hard-coded 0). Five tsc commandLine baselines gain the new help sections.

defects.title: formatDefaultValue does not render a nil default as 'undefined' like Strada, so --lib loses its 'default: undefined' line (and non-enum options would print '<nil>')
defects.statement: Strada's formatDefaultValue returns String(undefined) = "undefined" whenever the default is undefined. The port (internal/execute/outputs.go:326-342) maps only core.TSUnknown to "undefined". A nil DefaultValueDescription on a list/enum option (--lib, declscompiler.go:300-313, which sets no DefaultValueDescription) goes to the enum branch, matches no entry and returns "", and the `if defaultValueDescription != ""` guard (outputs.go:314) drops the default line; for a non-enum option with a nil default, fmt.Sprintf("%v", nil) would print 'default: <nil>'. The ported help therefore diverges from the tsc output it ports: the help.js baseline's --lib block has no 'default: undefined' line.
defects.evidence: outputs.go:327 `if defaultValue == core.TSUnknown { return "undefined" }`; :341 `return fmt.Sprintf("%v", defaultValue)`; enum branch returns strings.Join(names, "/") which is "" when nothing matches. declscompiler.go:301-313 lib: Kind List, no DefaultValueDescription, ShowInSimplifiedHelpView true. help.js --lib entry ends after the 'one or more: ...' line with no default line, whereas --module (DefaultValueDescription core.TSUnknown) prints 'default: undefined'.
defects.notes: A comment must say a nil/undefined default is not rendered as 'undefined' (missing default line for --lib, or '<nil>' output). Comments about backticks on --declaration's default or missing trailing periods do not count.

defects.title: showAdditionalInfoOutput dereferences valueCandidates without a nil check, but getValueCandidate returns nil for object options (latent panic)
defects.statement: getValueCandidate returns nil for CommandLineOptionTypeObject (outputs.go:370-372). showAdditionalInfoOutput then reads valueCandidates.possibleValues unconditionally (outputs.go:354), whereas Strada uses `valueCandidates?.possibleValues`; the caller itself guards `valueCandidates != nil` (outputs.go:310, 313), showing nil is expected. Today only simplified-view options reach it and none is object-kind, but the --all help path (still a TODO) will feed object options such as `paths` through this formatter and panic.
defects.evidence: outputs.go:354 `if valueCandidates.possibleValues == "string" && ...` with no nil check; :370-372 `if option.Kind == tsoptions.CommandLineOptionTypeObject { return nil }`; object-kind compiler options exist (e.g. paths in declscompiler.go).
defects.notes: Must point at the missing nil check on valueCandidates in showAdditionalInfoOutput / nil candidates for object options. A comment about a nil *diagnostics.Message after the DefaultValueDescription type assertion does not count.

excluded.reason: Claims the `*diagnostics.Message` type assertion on DefaultValueDescription at outputs.go:270 needs an extra `msg != nil` check to avoid a nil dereference. No option stores a typed-nil *diagnostics.Message in DefaultValueDescription; options set either a real message pointer, a value, core.TSUnknown or nothing (untyped nil fails the assertion), so the scenario is contrived.

Claims the `if valueCandidates != nil` separator-newline check inside the default block (outputs.go:311-316) is the wrong condition. It is exactly right: the candidates line is appended precisely when valueCandidates != nil (outputs.go:310-311), mirroring Strada's `if (valueCandidates) text.push(sys.newLine)`, so the newline separates the two lines only when both exist.

Claims the --build description in Parse-watch-interval-option.js lacks a trailing period, inconsistent with other entries. The text is the verbatim diagnostic message Build_one_or_more_projects_and_their_dependencies_if_out_of_date shared with tsc; purely cosmetic baseline wording, not a defect of this PR.

Claims --declaration's default is shown with backticks (`false`, unless `composite` is set) inconsistently with other booleans. That string is the diagnostic message used as --declaration's DefaultValueDescription and is exactly what tsc prints; intentional.
Claims a description in the terminal-width baseline lacks a trailing period. Same as R4: the text comes verbatim from the shared diagnostic message; cosmetic.

Asks to remove the unreachable wide-terminal branch and alignment plumbing because terminalWidth is always zero. This is a deliberate staged-port scaffold (commented `!!!` TODOs mirroring Strada); dead-code/style preference with no behavioural consequence.
Asks to remove the `terminalWidth >= 80` branch and alignment parameters since terminalWidth is never assigned. Same as C1: intentional port scaffolding, a style preference, no defect.

Says help always uses the narrow layout because the width is always zero and asks to obtain the real terminal width. The PR explicitly ports only the narrow layout and leaves width detection as a TODO; this is missing future functionality, not a regression or bug introduced here (baselines are narrow-layout by design).

PowerShell__PowerShell@ea07b93.pr_summary: In SSHConnectionInfo.StartSSHProcess, the ssh executable lookup uses the static CommandDiscovery.LookupCommandInfo restricted to CommandTypes.Application when an ExecutionContext is on the thread, and otherwise (SDK-hosted, no Runspace) manually searches fully qualified PATH entries for ssh/ssh.exe. If nothing is found it throws CommandNotFoundException instead of starting a process with an empty file name.

excluded.reason: Asks that the new comment explain that the lookup searches PATH only and that the resolved path is needed to set WorkingDirectory. Comment-wording request; the comment already states the cwd is set to the executable's directory (used at RunspaceConnectionInfo.cs:2325).

Says skipping non-fully-qualified PATH entries makes lookup fail when ssh is only reachable through a relative PATH entry. Deliberate, security-conscious choice in a new fallback for a case that previously always failed (empty filePath); relative PATH entries holding the only ssh are a contrived setup, not a regression.

Says the no-runspace branch ignores valid relative PATH entries such as ./tools, throwing CommandNotFoundException. Same deliberate skip as R2 in a new fallback that previously never worked; contrived configuration, not a regression.

Says a relative ./bin PATH entry containing ssh is skipped in the no-runspace lookup, unlike normal command discovery. Same deliberate relative-entry skip as R2/C2; not a defect introduced by the change.
Says SDK-hosted discovery should preserve dot-relative PATH entries like the runspace path. Same deliberate relative-entry skip as R2/C2; contrived and not a regression.

Says Path.Combine/File.Exists can throw on PATH entries with invalid characters and should be wrapped in try/catch. Wrong on .NET Core: Path.Combine does not validate characters and File.Exists returns false instead of throwing.
Suggests validating that the found ssh path is not a symlink/junction. Speculative hardening; following links for a PATH executable is normal and matches the runspace CommandDiscovery route.

Says File.Exists accepts a non-executable 'ssh' earlier in PATH on Unix, stopping before a later executable one. Contrived setup (a non-executable file named ssh in a fully qualified PATH directory ahead of the real client) in a fallback that previously always failed.
Says on Unix a non-executable ssh earlier in PATH is selected and launch fails. Same contrived scenario as C3.
Says candidate selection should skip non-executable files named ssh on Unix. Same contrived scenario as C3.

Asks to reword the comment because the Unix launcher passes FileName straight to the fork/execve shim, so 'ProcessStartInfo can lookup PATH' could mislead maintainers. Comment-precision nit; the code performs the needed lookup regardless.
Asks the comment to explain that the custom launcher passes the filename directly to native process creation. Comment-precision nit, same as C4.
Points out trailing whitespace on the blank line after the else block (line 2245). Formatting only.
Asks for a test of the no-runspace fallback. Request for tests, not a defect.

libsdl-org__SDL@96dfef3.pr_summary: Fixes re-entrant command-buffer submission during Vulkan memory defragmentation. VULKAN_INTERNAL_CreateTexture gains a transitionToDefaultLayout flag, false for the cycle and defrag paths, which record the initial layout barrier on their own command buffer instead of acquiring and submitting a separate one. VULKAN_INTERNAL_DefragmentMemory now records its copies into the presenting command buffer being submitted (before EndCommandBuffer) instead of acquiring and submitting its own; a defrag failure is only logged and Submit returns true. The per-submit cleanup (fence sweep / CleanCommandBuffer, empty-allocation release, pending destroys) now runs only when the submission presents.

defects.title: Submit-time cleanup (finished command buffers, empty allocations, pending destroys) now runs only on presenting submits, so non-presenting workloads accumulate resources without bound
defects.statement: VULKAN_Submit now wraps the fence sweep that calls VULKAN_INTERNAL_CleanCommandBuffer, the checkEmptyAllocations release and VULKAN_INTERNAL_PerformPendingDestroys in `if (presenting)` (SDL_gpu_vulkan.c:10532-10570), with presenting = presentDataCount > 0 (10424). Headless/offscreen rendering, compute-only loops, and frames submitted while a window is minimized (no swapchain texture acquired, so no presentData) never recycle submitted command buffers, their fences and tracked resource references, never free empty allocations and never destroy released buffers/textures, until an explicit SDL_WaitForGPUIdle/WaitForGPUFences. submittedCommandBuffers and the command pools keep growing and GPU memory is never returned; before the PR every submit reclaimed completed work.
defects.evidence: Head 10532-10570: `// If presenting, check if we can perform any cleanups` `if (presenting) { for (Sint32 i = renderer->submittedCommandBufferCount - 1; ...) { vkGetFenceStatus ... VULKAN_INTERNAL_CleanCommandBuffer(...) } if (renderer->checkEmptyAllocations) {...} VULKAN_INTERNAL_PerformPendingDestroys(renderer); }`. Head 10424 `bool presenting = vulkanCommandBuffer->presentDataCount > 0;`. Base ran all three unconditionally on every submit. The PR body concedes headless setups would not trigger cleanup.
defects.notes: Must say cleanup / command-buffer recycling / pending destroys no longer happen on non-presenting submits, so headless/offscreen/compute (or minimized) apps accumulate or leak resources. Comments only about moving the defrag call or brace style do not count.

defects.title: CycleActiveTexture records the default-layout transition on the new texture before the NULL check, crashing on allocation failure
defects.statement: VULKAN_INTERNAL_CycleActiveTexture (SDL_gpu_vulkan.c:5876-5889) now calls VULKAN_INTERNAL_TextureTransitionToDefaultUsage(renderer, commandBuffer, UNINITIALIZED, texture) immediately after VULKAN_INTERNAL_CreateTexture and before the existing `if (!texture) return;`. CreateTexture returns NULL on image creation/memory bind failure, and TextureTransitionToDefaultUsage dereferences texture->subresourceCount (2835), so cycling a texture under memory pressure crashes instead of taking the failure path.
defects.evidence: Head 5876-5889: `texture = VULKAN_INTERNAL_CreateTexture(renderer, false, &container->header.info); VULKAN_INTERNAL_TextureTransitionToDefaultUsage(renderer, commandBuffer, VULKAN_TEXTURE_USAGE_MODE_UNINITIALIZED, texture); if (!texture) { return; }`. Head 2835 `for (Uint32 i = 0; i < texture->subresourceCount; i += 1)`. VULKAN_CreateTexture (6730-6736) checks `if (texture == NULL)` after the same call.
defects.notes: Must name the transition happening before the NULL check (ordering) in CycleActiveTexture. A generic NULL-check remark elsewhere does not count.

defects.title: isDefrag field comment still says the command buffer was created for defragging
defects.statement: DefragmentMemory now sets isDefrag on the application's presenting command buffer (SDL_gpu_vulkan.c:10608) instead of on a dedicated command buffer it acquired, but the VulkanCommandBuffer field comment at line 1070 still reads 'Whether this CB was created for defragging', which the change made wrong and which misdescribes why CleanCommandBuffer resets defragInProgress for that buffer.
defects.evidence: Head 1070 `bool isDefrag; // Whether this CB was created for defragging`. Head 10602-10608 `VULKAN_INTERNAL_DefragmentMemory(VulkanRenderer *renderer, VulkanCommandBuffer *commandBuffer) { renderer->defragInProgress = 1; commandBuffer->isDefrag = 1;` with commandBuffer being the submitted presenting buffer (10451). Base acquired a dedicated command buffer via VULKAN_AcquireCommandBuffer.
defects.notes: Must say the isDefrag comment is now inaccurate because the flag marks the presenting/app command buffer carrying defrag work.

excluded.reason: Asks to put the opening brace of `if (transitionToDefaultLayout)` on the same line. Brace style only.

Claims a defrag failure leaves defragInProgress stuck at 1 and resources inconsistent. DefragmentMemory sets isDefrag on the submitting command buffer (10608), VULKAN_Submit still submits it after logging the failure (10451-10455), and VULKAN_INTERNAL_CleanCommandBuffer resets defragInProgress for isDefrag buffers (10272-10273); the copies already recorded are valid and ride that submit.
Asks to move the `if (presenting)` opening brace to the condition line. Brace style only.

Claims the cleanup loop running CleanCommandBuffer lacks allocatorLock synchronization. The loop and allocation sweep run under submitLock with the same locking as before the PR (merely re-indented); no new race.

Claims allocationsToDefrag[count - 1] can underflow when the array is empty. The only caller invokes DefragmentMemory only when `renderer->allocationsToDefragCount > 0` under submitLock (10447-10450); unreachable.

Claims a buffer allocation failure leaves defragInProgress set forever, blocking future defrags. Same as R3: the isDefrag command buffer is always submitted by VULKAN_Submit and its cleanup resets the flag.
Says the texture failure path logs 'Failed to allocate defrag buffer!'. Cosmetic log wording with no functional impact.
Says the texture allocation failure logs 'defrag buffer' instead of texture. Cosmetic log wording.
Says the defrag texture failure message should name the texture. Cosmetic log wording.
Says the 'likely OOM' defrag failure message guesses the cause. Cosmetic log wording.
Asks for CreateTexture's boolean to be replaced by an API expressing the layout postcondition. API design preference; both current callers passing false record the needed barrier.

Says the new cycled texture's initial transition is recorded without VULKAN_INTERNAL_TrackTexture. The texture is immediately used for a write by PrepareTextureSubresourceForWrite's callers, which track it on the same command buffer; the untracked case is speculative.

Says a defrag failure is now only logged and VULKAN_Submit returns true, hiding the failure. The application's command buffer really was submitted, so returning true is correct; previously returning false for a successful submit was the wrong signal; not a defect.

Says a failed defrag drops the allocation from the defrag queue while leaving it unavailable, stranding its regions. The queue pop and early return on failure are unchanged from the base; pre-existing, not made worse (the PR actually improves the failure path by submitting the recorded copies).
Says the allocation removed from allocationsToDefrag on buffer allocation failure is never retried. Pre-existing behaviour of the unchanged pop/return logic, not introduced by this PR.

Suggests reclaiming completed work before allocating defrag replacements since defrag now runs before cleanup. Speculative ordering concern; defrag must record before EndCommandBuffer, and no concrete failure is shown.

Asks to confirm barriers when appending defrag copies after application commands in the same command buffer. The defrag path emits TransitionFromDefaultUsage barriers on sources and tracks old and new resources, so ordering and lifetime are handled; speculative.
Suggests avoiding two consecutive barriers (UNINITIALIZED->default->write) for a freshly cycled texture. Minor performance/style optimisation, not a defect.

gofr-dev__gofr@c1a26ad.pr_summary: Adds a LOG_DISABLE_PROBES config option that suppresses request logging for the /.well-known/health and /.well-known/alive probe endpoints. middleware.GetConfigs now returns a MiddlewareConfig struct (CORS header map plus the LogDisableProbes string), the logging middleware is refactored into loggingMiddleware with a shouldLog predicate plus a new LoggingWithoutProbes variant, and newHTTPServer registers the chosen logging middleware in a separate r.Use call after Tracer/CORS/Metrics. Docs, tests and go.work.sum are updated.

defects.title: Logging middleware moved behind CORS: OPTIONS/preflight requests are no longer logged and no longer get X-Correlation-ID, for every app (flag on or off)
defects.statement: Before, the chain was Tracer -> Logging -> CORS -> Metrics. The PR removes Logging from the first r.Use and appends it afterwards (http_server.go:36-46), making it Tracer -> CORS -> Metrics -> Logging. CORS (cors.go) short-circuits every OPTIONS request with `w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK); return` without calling inner, so Logging never runs for them: preflight requests silently disappear from the request log and lose the X-Correlation-ID response header that Logging sets. This behaviour change applies regardless of LOG_DISABLE_PROBES (the default `false` path also registers Logging last).
defects.evidence: http_server.go:36-40 `r.Use(middleware.Tracer, middleware.CORS(...), middleware.Metrics(c.Metrics()),)` then 42-46 `r.Use(middleware.LoggingWithoutProbes(...))` / `r.Use(middleware.Logging(c.Logger))`; base had `middleware.Tracer, middleware.Logging(c.Logger), middleware.CORS(...), middleware.Metrics(...)`. cors.go: `if r.Method == http.MethodOptions { w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK); return }`. logger.go:121 `srw.Header().Set("X-Correlation-ID", traceID)`.
defects.notes: Must point out that the logging middleware's position in the chain changed (now after CORS/Metrics) with a concrete consequence (OPTIONS not logged / correlation header missing / changed panic-recovery scope). A comment only about code style of the if/else does not count.

defects.title: With LOG_DISABLE_PROBES=true, health/alive responses also lose the X-Correlation-ID header
defects.statement: loggingMiddleware returns early for skipped requests (`if !shouldLog(r) { inner.ServeHTTP(w, r); return }`, logger.go:111-114) before `srw.Header().Set("X-Correlation-ID", traceID)` at logger.go:121. So enabling the option, documented as only suppressing probe logs, also changes probe responses: GET /.well-known/health and /.well-known/alive no longer carry X-Correlation-ID.
defects.evidence: logger.go:111-114 early return; logger.go:121 `srw.Header().Set("X-Correlation-ID", traceID)` only on the logged path.
defects.notes: Must say the skipped (probe) path no longer sets X-Correlation-ID. The OPTIONS/preflight correlation-header loss from reordering is D1, not this.

defects.title: Exported middleware.GetConfigs changes its return type from map[string]string to MiddlewareConfig, breaking external callers
defects.statement: GetConfigs in the public package gofr.dev/pkg/gofr/http/middleware previously returned map[string]string (the CORS header map, which middleware.CORS still takes). It now returns a MiddlewareConfig struct (config.go:12-17), so any user code doing `middleware.CORS(middleware.GetConfigs(conf), routes)` or ranging over the returned map no longer compiles after upgrading.
defects.evidence: base config.go: `func GetConfigs(c config.Config) map[string]string`; head config.go:17 `func GetConfigs(c config.Config) MiddlewareConfig`; cors.go `func CORS(middlewareConfigs map[string]string, routes *[]string)` unchanged.
defects.notes: Must say the exported GetConfigs signature/return type changed, breaking existing callers. R1/R3 (make LogDisableProbes a bool) do not count.

excluded.reason: Says LogDisableProbes should be a bool rather than a string. Typing LogDisableProbes as string rather than bool (config.go:14) is a design preference; the documented value 'true' works (http_server.go:42 compares to "true").
Says the config key name LOG_DISABLE_PROBES is confusing. Config-key naming preference (LOG_DISABLE_PROBES); the key is documented in docs/references/configs/page.md as controlling probe logs.
Says the config value should be parsed with strconv.ParseBool. Same bool-parsing preference as R1; not a defect — the documented 'true'/'false' values behave as documented.

Says comparing LogDisableProbes to the literal "true" misses '1'/'TRUE'. Accepting only the literal "true" (not '1'/'TRUE') matches the documented value; config values are strings (GetOrDefault), so the 'if represented as a boolean' scenario cannot occur. Robustness nit, not a defect.
Asks the docs to say precisely that only HTTP access logs for the built-in GET probe routes are suppressed. Documentation wording nit; the docs are not wrong.
Asks to share the probe path constants with the route registration in factory.go. Maintainability suggestion with no current drift (paths match).
Claims path-only suppression also hides logs of POST requests to /.well-known/health. Non-GET traffic to probe URLs is a contrived case with negligible consequence.

Claims the skipped probe path bypasses panicRecovery so a panic in downstream middleware escapes. Logging is now the last registered middleware and handler panics are recovered in handler.go:77-80 (goroutine with panicRecoveryHandler); only later user-registered middleware panicking on a probe path would be affected, which is contrived.

Claims a panic in a health/alive handler now escapes to net/http because LoggingWithoutProbes skips panicRecovery. Wrong: handler.ServeHTTP runs the handler in a goroutine with `defer panicRecoveryHandler(recover(), ...)` (handler.go:77-80) and returns ErrorPanicRecovery.
Claims suppression should check the request method so POSTs to probe URLs stay logged. Same contrived case as C4.
Asks for shared probe-path identifiers. Same maintainability suggestion as C3; no drift.

Claims skipping the wrapper skips panicRecovery so a probe panic escapes to net/http. Handler panics are recovered in handler.go:77-80 and no middleware runs after Logging by default; not a realistic failure (same as C5/C9).

gofr-dev__gofr@49ab394.pr_summary: Makes ConnectionManager.Connect synchronous (one attempt, returning the error) instead of spawning an internal retry goroutine that always returned nil. Client.Connect now, on failure, returns the error and starts a background Client.retryConnect loop that builds a new connection manager, stream manager and subscription manager once NATS is reachable. Adds a checkClient guard (nil client / nil connManager / not connected) to Publish, Subscribe and the stream/topic admin methods, an isConnected check in ConnectionManager.Publish, and changes defaultRetryTimeout from 10s to nats.DefaultTimeout (2s).

defects.title: retryConnect goroutine writes connManager/streamManager/subManager without synchronization while request paths read them: data race and a window where checkClient passes but streamManager/subManager are still nil
defects.statement: Client.Connect starts `go c.retryConnect()` (client.go:52) when the first connect fails; AddPubSub ignores the error and the app keeps serving. retryConnect assigns c.connManager (client.go:83) and only later c.streamManager and c.subManager (client.go:93-94), with no mutex/atomic, while checkClient (client.go:358-362), Publish (144), Subscribe (156-158), the admin methods (301-340), Health and Close read those fields concurrently. This is a Go data race; concretely, between line 83 and line 93 checkClient already passes (connManager set and CONNECTED) while streamManager/subManager are still nil, so a concurrent CreateTopic/CreateStream/DeleteStream/CreateOrUpdateStream or Subscribe passes the new guard and dereferences a nil manager - the panic the PR set out to prevent.
defects.evidence: client.go:52 `go c.retryConnect()`; client.go:83 `c.connManager = connManager`; client.go:93-94 `c.streamManager = newStreamManager(js, c.logger)` / `c.subManager = newSubscriptionManager(batchSize)`; client.go:358 `if c.connManager == nil` read with no lock; client.go:297-301 CreateTopic: `checkClient(c)` then `c.streamManager.CreateStream(...)`. The only mutex (subMutex, client.go:28) is used solely by SubscribeWithHandler. external_db.go:36-43 AddPubSub calls Connect (wrapper logs and swallows the error) and registers the client.
defects.notes: Counts if the comment says the background retry goroutine mutates the client's connManager/streamManager/subManager without synchronization while other methods read them (data race), or that connManager is published before the managers so a caller can pass checkClient and hit a nil manager. A comment only about the jetStream()-failure branch leaving connManager set (R2) does not count by itself; nor does a comment only about retry cancellation on Close.

defects.title: SubscribeWithHandler was left without the new guard and now nil-derefs connManager when the initial connect failed
defects.statement: Before the PR ConnectionManager.Connect always returned nil, so Client.Connect always set c.connManager and SubscribeWithHandler got an error from jetStream() while disconnected. Now a failed first connect returns before `c.connManager = connManager` (client.go:49-57), leaving it nil until retryConnect succeeds. The PR added checkClient to Publish/Subscribe/admin methods but not to SubscribeWithHandler, which calls `c.connManager.jetStream()` directly (client.go:178): a nil-interface method call panic instead of an error.
defects.evidence: client.go:178 `js, err := c.connManager.jetStream()` with no checkClient; client.go:49-55 returns before assigning c.connManager; base connection_manager.go Connect was `go cm.retryConnect(); return nil`, so base Client.Connect always assigned connManager.
defects.notes: Must name SubscribeWithHandler (or the remaining unguarded connManager use) as panicking/lacking the nil/connected guard after a failed initial connect. Exported method with no framework caller, hence low.

excluded.reason: Claims retryConnect duplicates Connect's logging and manager-initialisation logic. Refactoring/style point: the two copies are currently equivalent and nothing has drifted, so there is no behavioural defect.
