Asks Connect and retryConnect to share one setup sequence so they cannot diverge later. Same duplication/style point as R1; the copies do not currently differ (client.go:48-66 vs 75-95).
Asks for a shared successful-setup path for Connect and retryConnect. Same duplication/style point as R1; no present divergence.

Claims that when jetStream() fails in retryConnect, connManager is left set so checkClient passes with no valid JetStream context. Unreachable: ConnectionManager.Connect (connection_manager.go:80-106) returns nil only after setting cm.jStream, so connManager.jetStream() at client.go:85 cannot fail after a successful Connect; the continue branch never runs with the real manager.

Claims Subscribe ignores checkClient's error and always returns errClientNotConnected, sleeping without retrying. checkClient can only ever return errClientNotConnected (client.go:353-367), so nothing is lost; sleep-then-return mirrors the base behaviour and the framework's subscribe loop retries.

Claims the retry loop is uncancellable and can install a connection after Close or overwrite a newer one. The base code already ran an uncancellable retry goroutine (base ConnectionManager.retryConnect) that set the connection after Close; the PR moves it without making it worse, and Close runs at process shutdown (container.go:167-181).

Claims retries can reopen a closed client or replace a later successful Connect, leaking a connection. Pre-existing shape: base ConnectionManager.Connect also launched an uncancellable retry goroutine; repeated Connect is guarded by PubSubWrapper.Connect and only called once by AddPubSub.

Claims a client closed during an outage can reconnect after Close returned, leaking a live connection. Same pre-existing lifecycle gap as the base retry goroutine; Close is called at app shutdown, not made worse by this PR.

Claims repeated failing Connect calls each start a retry loop that can overwrite each other's managers. Contrived: AddPubSub calls Connect once and PubSubWrapper.Connect guards re-entry; the base code likewise spawned one goroutine per Connect.

Claims Close panics on nil subManager after a failed Connect. Pre-existing: in base, Client.Connect returned at jetStream() error (the async connect had not finished) before assigning subManager, so subManager was likewise nil and Close already called c.subManager.Close() unconditionally; the PR does not make it worse.

Asks whether disconnected publishes should still count toward app_pubsub_publish_total_count now that Publish returns before ConnectionManager.Publish. A metrics-semantics question with no stated contract that disconnected attempts must be counted; not a verifiable defect.
Asks to restore a test of the failed-Connect entry path starting the retry. Test-coverage request, not a code defect.
Asks for a regression test entering through a failed Client.Connect. Test-coverage request.
Asks the retry test to assert managers in both retry-after-failure cases. Test-quality request, not a defect of the shipped code.
Asks the retry test to assert readiness in every successful retry case since connSuccess is false for two of them. Test-quality request.
Asks to remove a 500ms sleep after a synchronous retryConnect call in the test. Test style/speed nit.

gofr-dev__gofr@b9cdcbb.pr_summary: Adds a Metadata map[string]any field to response.Response and makes the HTTP Responder serialise a Response as {data, metadata, error} instead of the handler unwrapping it to resp.Data before responding: handler.go no longer replaces result with resp.Data after setting custom headers. Responder tests are rewritten to check bodies, and the custom-response-headers doc page is rewritten to describe metadata.

defects.title: Responses without metadata now serialise `"metadata": null` instead of omitting the field (contradicting the docs)
defects.statement: pkg/gofr/http/responder.go:32 copies v.Metadata (a map[string]any, nil when unset) into the envelope's `Metadata interface{}` field with omitempty (pkg/gofr/http/responder.go:97). A nil map stored in an interface is a non-nil interface, so encoding/json does not omit it: every handler returning response.Response without Metadata (e.g. existing users who only set Headers) now gets an extra `"metadata":null` key. The new test pins this (responder_test.go:59 expects `{"metadata":null,…}`) while the docs say the body is just `{"data": …}` (docs/advanced-guide/setting-custom-response-headers/page.md:30-36, 105-114).
defects.evidence: pkg/gofr/http/responder.go:32 `resp = response{Data: v.Data, Metadata: v.Metadata, Error: errorObj}`; :97 `Metadata interface{} \`json:"metadata,omitempty"\``; response.go:9 `Metadata map[string]any`; docs/advanced-guide/setting-custom-response-headers/page.md:30 'If metadata is omitted, the response defaults to: {"data": {}}'.
defects.notes: Must identify that absent metadata is emitted as `"metadata":null` (typed-nil map in interface defeats omitempty), or that the test pins null contrary to the docs. R2 and C9 claim the opposite (that omitempty omits it and the test would fail) and do not count.

defects.title: Removing the unwrap of resp.Data makes status codes be computed on the Response wrapper: errors return 206 and POST with nil data returns 201
defects.statement: pkg/gofr/handler.go:99-102 no longer sets `result = resp.Data`, so Respond/getStatusCode receive the response.Response struct. getStatusCode (pkg/gofr/http/responder.go:57-64) returns 206 PartialContent whenever err != nil and data is non-nil — a struct value is never nil per isNil — so a handler returning `response.Response{Headers: h}, err` now gets 206 instead of the error's own status (404/400/500). handleSuccess (pkg/gofr/http/responder.go:75-80) returns 201 Created for a POST whose Response.Data is nil where it previously returned 202 Accepted.
defects.evidence: Base handler.go had `result = resp.Data` after SetCustomHeaders; head only calls `resp.SetCustomHeaders(w)`. pkg/gofr/http/responder.go:62 `if !isNil(data) { return http.StatusPartialContent, … }`; isNil (pkg/gofr/http/responder.go:108-115) is true only for nil or nil pointers; pkg/gofr/http/responder.go:76 `if data != nil { return http.StatusCreated, nil }`.
defects.notes: Must connect passing the Response wrapper (not its Data) to status selection with a wrong status code (206 on error, or 201 vs 202 on POST).

defects.title: A File or Raw payload wrapped in response.Response is no longer written in its own wire format
defects.statement: Previously the handler unwrapped response.Response to resp.Data, so `response.Response{Headers: …, Data: response.File{…}}` (e.g. to add Content-Disposition to a download) reached the File branch (pkg/gofr/http/responder.go:33-39) and wrote raw bytes with its content type, and a wrapped Raw reached the Raw branch. Now the Response case (pkg/gofr/http/responder.go:31-32) JSON-encodes the File/Raw struct under `data` with application/json, so such downloads return a JSON document (base64 content) instead of the file.
defects.evidence: pkg/gofr/http/responder.go:28-39 switch on the outer type: `case resTypes.Response: resp = response{Data: v.Data, …}` precedes and bypasses `case resTypes.File:` for a nested File; base handler.go `result = resp.Data` removed.
defects.notes: Must say nested File/Raw inside a Response lose their raw/file serialization (JSON-encoded instead).

excluded.reason: Claims the Response case ignores custom headers because SetCustomHeaders is not called in the responder. Wrong: handler.go:100-101 calls resp.SetCustomHeaders(w) before c.responder.Respond, the only path that passes a Response.

Claims nil Metadata is omitted by omitempty while tests expect null. Wrong mechanism: a nil map in an interface{} is a non-nil interface, so the output is `"metadata":null`, which is what the test expects (the real problem, null emitted contrary to the docs, is D1).

Claims omitempty omits nil Metadata so the 'without metadata' test expecting null fails. Wrong: the typed-nil map in interface{} is not omitted, so the test passes; the actual defect is the opposite (D1).
Says the doc prose spells the field `MetaData` instead of `Metadata`. Prose typo only; the code example on the same page uses the correct `Metadata` field.

gofr-dev__gofr@dc0b3e6.pr_summary: Stops logging the full MongoDB URI (which may contain credentials) in the mongo datasource: Connect calls a new generateMongoURI helper that either validates a user-supplied URI via getDBHost (net/url parse, scheme must be 'mongodb', returns the hostname) or builds one from Host/Port/Database/User/Password with net/url, and logs only the host. Adds errMissingField/errIncorrectURI/errParseHost and unit tests; the connect-error test now expects the URI-generation error.

defects.title: Credentials are double-encoded (QueryEscape then url.UserPassword), so users/passwords with special characters fail authentication
defects.statement: generateMongoURI sets `u.User = url.UserPassword(url.QueryEscape(config.User), url.QueryEscape(config.Password))` (pkg/gofr/datasource/mongo/mongo.go:156). url.UserPassword stores raw values and URL.String() (line 163) percent-encodes the userinfo itself, so the '%' produced by QueryEscape is escaped again ('a@b' -> 'a%40b' -> 'a%2540b'; spaces become '+'). The driver decodes once and authenticates with 'a%40b', so any credential containing a character outside the unreserved set fails to authenticate after this PR.
defects.evidence: mongo.go:156 `u.User = url.UserPassword(url.QueryEscape(config.User), url.QueryEscape(config.Password))`; :163 `return u.String(), u.Hostname(), nil` (URL.String escapes userinfo, including '%'); :108 `mongo.Connect(ctx, options.Client().ApplyURI(uri))`. Tests only use admin/password with no escapable characters.
defects.notes: Must say QueryEscape before url.UserPassword double-encodes credentials (or that reserved-character passwords now fail auth). A generic 'escape the password' remark does not count; database-path double-encoding (C3/C8/C17) is a different, excluded claim.

defects.title: Configured mongodb+srv:// URIs are rejected by the new scheme check, so Connect aborts and never connects
defects.statement: When Config.URI is set, generateMongoURI (mongo.go:131-137) always calls getDBHost, which returns errIncorrectURI unless `parsedURL.Scheme == "mongodb"` (lines 172-174). Valid `mongodb+srv://` connection strings (Atlas / DNS seed lists), which base code passed straight to ApplyURI, now make Connect log 'error generating mongo URI' and return (lines 93-95), leaving c.Database nil so every later operation panics. Only meant to derive a log label, the check now gates connectivity.
defects.evidence: mongo.go:172 `if parsedURL.Scheme != "mongodb" { return "", errIncorrectURI }`; :132-135 URI branch returns the error; :93-95 `if err != nil { c.logger.Errorf("error generating mongo URI: %v", err); return }`. Base Connect: `uri := c.config.URI` used unvalidated.
defects.notes: Must say mongodb+srv (SRV) URIs are rejected by the exact-scheme check, breaking connection. A remark only about multi-host log output is a near-miss that does not count alone.

defects.title: Malformed configured URI logs its credentials at error level via the url.Parse error
defects.statement: getDBHost returns the url.Parse error unchanged (mongo.go:167-169) and Connect logs it with Errorf (line 94). *url.Error's message embeds the full input (`parse "mongodb://alice:Secret@db:27017/app%ZZ": invalid URL escape ...`), so a credential-bearing URI that fails to parse (bad escape, bad port) writes the password into ERROR-level logs, the very leak this PR sets out to remove.
defects.evidence: mongo.go:167-169 `parsedURL, err := url.Parse(uri); if err != nil { return "", err }`; :94 `c.logger.Errorf("error generating mongo URI: %v", err)`; net/url Error.Error() is `fmt.Sprintf("%s %q: %s", e.Op, e.URL, e.Err)` with URL = the raw input.
defects.notes: Must say the parse error returned from getDBHost includes the raw URI (with credentials) and is logged. Only on a malformed-URI failure path, hence low.

defects.title: 'connecting to MongoDB' debug log prints an empty host for URI-based configs
defects.statement: Connect computes `host` from generateMongoURI but the debug log uses `c.config.Host` (mongo.go:98), which is empty when the config supplies URI, so the log reads 'connecting to MongoDB at  to database ...' while the later logs use `host`.
defects.evidence: mongo.go:98 `c.logger.Debugf("connecting to MongoDB at %v to database %v", c.config.Host, c.config.Database)` vs :116/:120/:127 using `host`.
defects.notes: Must point to c.config.Host vs the derived host in the debug log.

excluded.reason: Asks that errIncorrectURI say 'MongoDB' instead of 'mongo'. Wording preference in an error string; no behaviour impact.
Asks that the 'error generating mongo URI' log say 'MongoDB'. Wording preference in a log message; no behaviour impact.
Asks for 'MongoDB' capitalization instead of 'mongoDB' in a log string at mongo.go:116. Style only (and the text is pre-existing).

Claims the `User != "" && Password != ""` guard drops a username configured without a password, making it anonymous. Username-with-empty-password is a contrived configuration for the SCRAM auth this builder targets (it cannot set authMechanism), and the old code's `user:@host` / `:@host` form was not a working path; not a demonstrated regression.
Claims a User set with an empty Password now yields an anonymous connection instead of `user:@host`. Same as C1: contrived configuration, not a demonstrated regression.

Claims url.PathEscape on the database name plus URL.String double-encodes the path ('my db' -> 'my%2520db'). The encoding is doubled, but it has no consequence: authSource=admin is always set (mongo.go:160) so the path database is not used for auth, and the actual database is selected with m.Database(c.config.Database) (line 125).

Claims pre-escaping the database path double-encodes it so the URI targets a different database or is rejected. No observable effect: authSource=admin overrides the path database and m.Database(c.config.Database) picks the real one (mongo.go:125, 160).
Claims the database path is escaped twice. Same as C3/C8, and the comment itself concedes m.Database(config.Database) chooses the name independently; no consequence.

Claims url.Parse rejects comma-separated replica-set seed lists like `mongodb://node1:27017,node2:27017/db`, so Connect aborts. With the module's Go 1.22 net/url only validates the text after the LAST colon (':27017'), so the cited example parses without error (Hostname becomes a mangled label, only a log issue); the claim as stated does not hold.

Claims net/url treats `mongodb://host1:27017,host2:27017/db` as an invalid port and Connect aborts. As with C6, that URI parses in Go's net/url (only the port after the last colon is validated); the stated failure does not occur for the cited form.

Claims an IPv6 Host like '::1' produces an unbracketed authority; use net.JoinHostPort. Pre-existing: the base code built the same `%s:%d` authority with fmt.Sprintf, so this PR does not make it worse.
Asks to keep a test that reaches mongo.Connect's error path since the rewritten test stops at the missing-port check. Test-coverage request, not a defect.
Asks to restore coverage of the driver connection-error branch. Test-coverage request, not a defect.
Suggests keeping log-label host extraction separate from URI validation/construction. Design suggestion summarising other comments; the concrete breakages it alludes to are recorded as D1/D2.

gofr-dev__gofr@2c0c099.pr_summary: Adds testutil.NewServerConfigs, which picks free ports for HTTP, metrics and gRPC, sets HTTP_PORT/METRICS_PORT/GRPC_PORT via t.Setenv and returns them with host strings, and replaces the GetFreePort+Setenv boilerplate with it across pkg/gofr and example tests. It also bumps the root and ftp/s3 go.mod to go 1.22.7 / toolchain go1.23.4, deletes the sftp datasource submodule's go.mod/go.sum (sources stay), and swaps the httptest server in TestContext_WriteMessageToSocket for a real app.Run().

defects.title: sftp datasource go.mod/go.sum deleted while its sources stay: the package falls into the root module, which does not require github.com/pkg/sftp
defects.statement: The PR deletes pkg/gofr/datasource/file/sftp/go.mod and go.sum but leaves fs.go, file.go, fs_test.go etc. Without its own go.mod the directory becomes a package of root module gofr.dev; fs.go imports github.com/pkg/sftp and golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, and the root go.mod does not require github.com/pkg/sftp, so `go test gofr.dev/pkg/...` (PKG Unit Testing job) fails with 'no required module provides package github.com/pkg/sftp', and the package drops out of the per-submodule test/lint loops (`find pkg -name go.mod`).
defects.evidence: `git ls-tree <head> pkg/gofr/datasource/file/sftp/` lists file.go, fs.go, fs_test.go, interface.go, logger.go, logger_test.go, mock_interface.go, no go.mod. fs.go:8 `"github.com/pkg/sftp"`. `git grep pkg/sftp <head> -- go.mod` finds nothing. Deleted go.mod required `github.com/pkg/sftp v1.13.6`. go.yml: `go test gofr.dev/pkg/... -v -short`.
defects.notes: Deleted file: lines are base-side of sftp/go.mod. Must say removing the sftp go.mod/go.sum while its code remains breaks dependency resolution/build (or drops the package from module-based CI). Remarks only about go/toolchain version bumps do not count.

defects.title: examples/using-cron-jobs/main_test.go imports gofr.dev/pkg/gofr/testutil twice: compile error
defects.statement: The edit adds "gofr.dev/pkg/gofr/testutil" at line 4 while keeping the existing import at line 9. Importing the same package name twice in one file is a compile error ('testutil redeclared in this block'), so the example's test package fails to build and `go test gofr.dev/examples/...` fails.
defects.evidence: head main_test.go:4 `"gofr.dev/pkg/gofr/testutil"` and :9 `"gofr.dev/pkg/gofr/testutil"`.
defects.notes: Must point at the duplicate testutil import / compile failure. An import-ordering-only remark does not count.

defects.title: external_db_test.go drops the strconv import but TestApp_AddScyllaDB still calls strconv.Itoa: pkg/gofr test package does not compile
defects.statement: The PR removes `"strconv"` from pkg/gofr/external_db_test.go's imports while converting the other tests to NewServerConfigs, but TestApp_AddScyllaDB (unchanged) still does `t.Setenv("METRICS_PORT", strconv.Itoa(port))` at line 188. Go imports are per file, so this is 'undefined: strconv' and the whole gofr package test build fails, breaking `go test gofr.dev/pkg/...`.
defects.evidence: diff removes `-	"strconv"` from external_db_test.go imports; head external_db_test.go:187-188 `port := testutil.GetFreePort(t)` / `t.Setenv("METRICS_PORT", strconv.Itoa(port))`; `git grep -n strconv <head> -- pkg/gofr/external_db_test.go` shows only line 188.
defects.notes: Must say strconv is still used (Scylla test) after its import was removed, so the test file/package fails to compile.

defects.title: http-server example: _Errors and _Health tests request fresh random ports where no server listens
defects.statement: Previously all three integration tests hit http://localhost:9000, served by the main() started in TestIntegration_SimpleAPIServer. Now each test calls testutil.NewServerConfigs(t), which allocates new ports, but only the first test starts main(). TestIntegration_SimpleAPIServer_Errors (main_test.go:70, request :99) and _Health (:126, request :138) target ports nothing listens on: c.Do errors with nil resp, so Errors panics at io.ReadAll(resp.Body) (:109) and Health fails require.NoError.
defects.evidence: head main_test.go:25-27 `configs := testutil.NewServerConfigs(t); go main()`; :70 and :126 `configs := testutil.NewServerConfigs(t)` with no go main(); :99 `http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, configs.HTTPHost+tc.path, nil)`; :109 `b, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)`. port.go:43-45 picks fresh ports on every call. Base used `host := "http://localhost:9000"` in all three.
defects.notes: Must say the Errors/Health tests use new ports from NewServerConfigs on which no server runs. Generic port-allocation race remarks do not count.

defects.title: http-server example: /trace case fails because main.go still points anotherService at localhost:9000 while the server now runs on a random port
defects.statement: TestIntegration_SimpleAPIServer now starts main() on the random HTTP_PORT from NewServerConfigs (main_test.go:25) instead of 9000 from configs/.env. main.go:22 registers `anotherService` at the hard-coded http://localhost:9000, which TraceHandler calls (main.go ~79) for /redis. Nothing listens on 9000, so /trace returns an error (500) and the test's expectations for the "trace handler" case (empty data, 200) fail.
defects.evidence: main.go:22 `a.AddHTTPService("anotherService", "http://localhost:9000")`; TraceHandler `resp, err := c.GetHTTPService("anotherService").Get(c, "redis", nil); if err != nil { return nil, err }`; main_test.go:38 `{"trace handler", "/trace", ""}`; configs/.env `HTTP_PORT=9000` (godotenv.Load does not override the t.Setenv value).
defects.notes: Must connect the dynamic HTTP port to the hard-coded :9000 downstream used by the trace handler. Comments only about the Errors/Health tests belong to D4.

defects.title: TestContext_WriteMessageToSocket dials right after `go app.Run()` with no wait: racy/flaky
defects.statement: The PR replaces the synchronously listening httptest.NewServer with `go app.Run()` and dials ws://localhost:<HTTPPort>/ws on the next lines. app.Run starts the listener asynchronously, so the Dial can race ahead and get connection refused, failing require.NoError. Other tests using go app.Run() sleep 100ms first (websocket_test.go:38-39).
defects.evidence: head context_test.go:96 `go app.Run()`, :98 `wsURL := fmt.Sprintf("ws://localhost:%d/ws", configs.HTTPPort)`, :101-102 `ws, resp, err := websocket.DefaultDialer.Dial(wsURL, nil); require.NoError(t, err)`. Base dialled `server.URL` of `httptest.NewServer(app.httpServer.router)`.
defects.notes: Must identify the missing wait/readiness between go app.Run() and the Dial (or that removing httptest made it racy).

defects.title: Edited test files violate enabled golangci-lint rules (gci grouping, thelper, whitespace)
defects.statement: The root-module lint job runs golangci-lint with gci (standard/default/localmodule), thelper and whitespace enabled and no _test.go exclusion for them. The PR puts "gofr.dev/pkg/gofr/testutil" in the standard-library group in pkg/gofr/websocket_test.go:6 and context_test.go:7 (and into the third-party group in examples/grpc/grpc-server/main_test.go and using-cron-jobs), removes t.Helper() from setupTestEnvironment (gofr_test.go:862), and leaves blocks starting with a blank line (gofr_test.go:61-62, 202-203). The Code Quality lint step fails.
defects.evidence: .golangci.yml gci sections standard/default/localmodule; enable list includes gci, thelper, whitespace, wsl; exclude-rules for _test.go only gomnd/dupl/goconst. go.yml 'Lint Root Module' golangci-lint-action v1.62 on `.`. head websocket_test.go:5-7 `"fmt"` / `"gofr.dev/pkg/gofr/testutil"` / `"net/http/httptest"`.
defects.notes: Counts if a comment flags the misplaced gofr.dev testutil import grouping, the removed t.Helper(), or the leading blank lines as lint failures.

defects.title: Test_AddDuplicateHTTPService lost its METRICS_PORT isolation: New() now checks default port 2121 and Fatalf's the test binary if it is taken
defects.statement: The PR deletes the METRICS_PORT setup inside Test_AddDuplicateHTTPService (gofr_test.go:202-205) without replacing it with NewServerConfigs. New() (gofr.go:77-84) then falls back to defaultMetricPort 2121 and calls Logger.Fatalf if that port is unavailable, which exits the whole test process whenever 2121 is occupied (another gofr app or a leaked server).
defects.evidence: diff removes `metricsPort := testutil.GetFreePort(t)` / `t.Setenv("METRICS_PORT", ...)` in Test_AddDuplicateHTTPService with nothing added; gofr.go:82-83 `if !isPortAvailable(port) { app.container.Logger.Fatalf("metrics port %d is blocked or unreachable", port) }`.
defects.notes: Must say this test no longer sets an isolated metrics port so New() uses the default and can fail/abort.

defects.title: Unrelated go.mod bump to go 1.22.7 / toolchain go1.23.4 in root, ftp and s3
defects.statement: A test-helper PR changes root go.mod from `go 1.22`/`toolchain go1.22.10` to `go 1.22.7`/`toolchain go1.23.4` (ftp/s3 likewise). The go line raises the minimum Go for consumers (1.22.0-1.22.6 with GOTOOLCHAIN=local can no longer build), and the toolchain line makes GOTOOLCHAIN=auto switch CI's Go 1.22 lanes to 1.23.4, so they no longer test 1.22.
defects.evidence: go.mod diff `-go 1.22` `-toolchain go1.22.10` `+go 1.22.7` `+toolchain go1.23.4`; ftp `-go 1.22.3`, s3 `-go 1.22.4` to the same.
defects.notes: Counts if a comment questions the go/toolchain directive bump as unintended or inconsistent with supported versions/CI.

defects.title: Doc comment of exported NewServerConfigs names a nonexistent ServerConfigsProvider
defects.statement: testutil/port.go:37 begins `// ServerConfigsProvider sets up server configurations...` but the function is NewServerConfigs (line 40), so godoc does not associate the comment correctly and golint-style checks flag it.
defects.evidence: port.go:37 `// ServerConfigsProvider sets up server configurations for testing and returns a ServiceConfigs struct.`; :40 `func NewServerConfigs(t *testing.T) *ServiceConfigs {`.
defects.notes: Must point out the comment/function name mismatch. The Server vs Service naming nit alone does not count.

excluded.reason: Claims calling GetFreePort three times independently is a TOCTOU race that can make tests flaky. The close-then-reuse pattern is inherent in the pre-existing GetFreePort, which tests already called two or three times per test before this PR; nothing new or worse.

Claims the three sequential GetFreePort calls can return the same port so two services collide. Same pre-existing pattern as R7 (base tests allocated 2-3 ports the same way); the kernel does not normally hand back a just-released ephemeral port immediately; not introduced by the PR.

Claims mixing scheme-prefixed HTTP/Metrics hosts with a bare host:port GRPCHost invites misuse. Deliberate: grpc.Dial takes a target without scheme and the grpc example uses it that way; naming/design preference.

Claims the package-level `port` in examples/using-http-service is now never assigned while handler tests still build URLs with it. Those handler tests only attach the URL to a request passed to Handler, which never dials it (it calls the mocked services), so the zero value has no effect; stale-variable cleanup only.

Asks for NewServerConfigs to let callers pick only the ports they need since metrics-only tests now also set HTTP/GRPC ports. Design preference; setting extra free ports in t.Setenv has no concrete harmful effect.

gofr-dev__gofr@5e284ae.pr_summary: Adds logging.ContextLogger (pkg/gofr/logging/ctx_logger.go), which appends map{"__trace_id__": id} to every log call's args when the context carries a valid span; logger.logf strips that map via extractTraceIDAndFilterArgs and emits it as a top-level trace_id (JSON) or grey prefix (terminal). handler.ServeHTTP swaps the shared container's embedded Logger for a ContextLogger for each request and restores it in a defer; logError / panic recovery now take a logger parameter; the exported ErrorLogEntry loses its TraceID field.

defects.title: Per-request swap of the shared container.Logger races across concurrent requests: trace IDs leak between requests and a stale request logger can stay installed
defects.statement: handler.container is one *container.Container shared by every route and in-flight request (handler.go:41), and gofr.Context embeds it, so c.Logger reads the shared embedded field. ServeHTTP (handler.go:71-75) does origLogger := h.container.Logger; h.container.Logger = NewContextLogger(c.Context, origLogger); defer restore — unsynchronised writes of shared state (a data race). With overlapping requests A and B: A installs ctxA; B captures origLogger=ctxA and installs ctxB(base ctxA); A's handler logs through ctxB and gets B's trace ID; A's defer restores the base logger; B's defer then restores ctxA, leaving request A's ContextLogger installed permanently, so every later log (other requests, cron, subscribers) carries A's stale trace ID. Wrappers also nest, appending several __trace_id__ maps of which extractTraceIDAndFilterArgs (logger.go:251-267) strips only the first, so extra maps print inside messages. The developer note at :66-70 claiming the restore avoids leaking context is therefore wrong.
defects.evidence: handler.go:41 `container      *container.Container`; :71-75 `origLogger := h.container.Logger` / `h.container.Logger = ctxLogger` / `defer func() { h.container.Logger = origLogger }()`; container.go:44 Container embeds `logging.Logger`; context.go newContext sets `Container: c` (same pointer for every request); :87 and :91 read `h.container.Logger` from the handler goroutine; logger.go:256 `exists && traceID == ""` strips only the first trace map.
defects.notes: Must say the request-scoped logger is written onto the shared container (global mutable state) so concurrent requests race / log each other's trace IDs / a stale wrapper can remain installed. Saying logError/panic recovery should use the local ctxLogger because of this race also counts (R2). A bare comment about multiple trace maps in the filter without the shared-container race does not count.

defects.title: On request timeout the deferred restore removes the trace logger while the handler goroutine is still running, so its later logs and error log lose the trace ID
defects.statement: When requestTimeout fires, ServeHTTP takes the c.Context.Done() branch (handler.go:96-100), responds and returns; the defer at :75 restores the original logger while h.function is still running in the goroutine started at :85. Its subsequent c.Logger calls and h.logError(h.container.Logger, err) at :91 (and panic recovery at :87) then read the restored base logger (or another request's wrapper), so the handler error log of a timed-out request no longer carries the trace ID. Before the PR the error log captured traceID in a local at request start, so this is a regression reachable with a single request whenever REQUEST_TIMEOUT is configured.
defects.evidence: handler.go:59-63 timeout context; :75 `defer func() { h.container.Logger = origLogger }()`; :87 `panicRecoveryHandler(recover(), h.container.Logger, panicked)`; :91 `h.logError(h.container.Logger, err)`; :96-100 returns on `c.Context.Done()` without waiting for `done`. Base side captured `traceID := trace.SpanFromContext(r.Context())...` locally and passed it to logError.
defects.notes: Must describe the timeout path: ServeHTTP returns/restores before the handler goroutine finishes so its later logs/error log lack the request trace ID. The concurrent-request race alone is D1.

defects.title: Removing the exported ErrorLogEntry.TraceID field breaks callers that set or read it
defects.statement: ErrorLogEntry is an exported type in package gofr; the PR deletes its exported TraceID field (handler.go:45-47). Any downstream code constructing ErrorLogEntry{TraceID: ...} or reading entry.TraceID stops compiling against this version, with no deprecation path.
defects.evidence: Base: `type ErrorLogEntry struct { TraceID string `json:"trace_id,omitempty"`; Error string ... }`; head handler.go:45-47 `type ErrorLogEntry struct { Error string `json:"error,omitempty"` }`.
defects.notes: Must name the removal of the exported TraceID field as a public API/compile break. Comments about the JSON log schema moving trace_id (C17) do not count.

excluded.reason: Claims the formatted methods append a trace map that fmt.Sprintf then prints as %!(EXTRA ...). For every production Logger, logger.logf calls extractTraceIDAndFilterArgs before fmt.Sprintf(format, filteredArgs...) (logger.go:72-81), so the map never reaches Sprintf; no EXTRA is produced.

Claims extraction only matches exact map[string]any and keeps later trace maps. The map is only produced by ContextLogger.withTraceInfo as a literal map[string]any (ctx_logger.go:31), so the assertion always matches; multiple maps arise only from the nested-wrapper race, which is D1's root cause.
Asks the test mock to record and assert formatted-call arguments. Test-coverage request, not a defect.
Notes datasource clients hold the original logger captured at init, so their logs do not get the trace ID. Those clients never had request trace IDs before either; scope question, not a regression.

Claims the ContextLogger captures c.Context once, so a span started later by c.Trace is not reflected when the incoming request had no valid span. Incoming requests pass through gofr's tracing middleware, so the request context already carries a span; a request with no valid span but a valid c.Trace span is contrived.
Asks formatted logging tests to assert forwarded arguments. Test request.

Claims later trace-metadata maps are retained in the message after the first is extracted. Only nested ContextLoggers produce several maps, which happens only via the shared-container race (D1); the filter itself is not a separate defect.

Claims wrapping logging.MockLogger (which Sprintf's raw args) yields EXTRA artifacts. MockLogger is a test helper; no in-tree path wraps it with a context carrying a valid span in a way that affects production, and all production loggers strip the map.
Claims an application map containing the key __trace_id__ is swallowed and hijacks trace_id. Requires callers to log maps using the framework's private magic key; contrived.
Claims ContextLogger over NewMockLogger emits an extra-argument artifact for formatted calls. Same test-only MockLogger scenario as C7; production loggers strip the map.
Points out a test comment names mockTracerProvider instead of mockTracedContext. Cosmetic nit in a test.
Claims the logger misses spans created by c.Trace inside the handler. Same contrived no-incoming-span scenario as C3.

Asks how custom Logger implementations that do not understand the __trace_id__ map keep error correlation. gofr has no supported custom-logger injection point for request logging and the in-tree loggers handle the map; speculative.

Says the logError comment still mentions a traceID argument. The comment ('Log the error with traceID and errorMessage') remains broadly accurate since the supplied logger adds the trace ID; cosmetic.
Asks to document that the error log's trace_id moved from inside message to the top-level entry. This is the intended schema of the feature; a documentation request, not a defect.
Claims the wrapper should pick up a trace started by the handler via c.Trace. Same contrived scenario as C3.
Claims a caller map with __trace_id__ is taken first and makes trace_id caller-controlled. Same contrived magic-key scenario as C8.
Duplicate of C14 about the logError comment mentioning traceID. Cosmetic.
Claims any application map with a string __trace_id__ field is dropped from the message. Same contrived magic-key scenario as C8.
Asks for a test of prettyPrint with a non-empty TraceID. Test request.
Claims a caller map with __trace_id__ loses its other fields and can replace the real trace ID. Same contrived magic-key scenario as C8.

comfyanonymous__ComfyUI@4dcd698.pr_summary: Adds LoRA training to ComfyUI: comfy_extras/nodes_train.py with Train LoRA, Save LoRA Weights, Load LoRA Model, Load Image Dataset from Folder and Plot Loss Graph nodes built on the weight-adapter scheme (LoraDiff trainable module, LoRAAdapter.create_train/to_train, WeightAdapterTrainBase), gradient checkpointing via forward patching and in Cosmos blocks, out-of-place residual adds in attention.py, and folder_paths.get_input_subfolders with tests.

defects.title: lora_dtype default 'bf32' is not an offered option, so Train LoRA fails with default values
defects.statement: nodes_train.py:344-347 declares lora_dtype choices ['bf16','fp32'] but default 'bf32'. execution.py:736 combo validation rejects a value not in the list ('Value not in list'), and even if it passed, node_helpers.string_to_torch_dtype('bf32') returns None (node_helpers.py:46-52), so the adapter .to(lora_dtype) calls get None.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:345-346 `["bf16", "fp32"], {"default": "bf32", ...}`; node_helpers.string_to_torch_dtype maps only fp32/fp16/bf16.
defects.notes: Must say the default 'bf32' is invalid / not among the choices / not a recognised dtype.

defects.title: Only one random batch is ever trained on; the rest of the dataset is ignored
defects.statement: train() samples `indices = torch.randperm(num_images)[:batch_size]` and VAE-encodes that batch once (nodes_train.py:381-386) before the loop; every step at :503-514 reuses the same `encoded` tensor. With more images than batch_size (default 1) all other images are never seen.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:382-386 before the loop; :513 `{"samples": encoded.clone()}` each step.
defects.notes: Must say the batch is selected/encoded once outside the loop so remaining images are never used.

defects.title: Selecting an existing LoRA whose filename lacks the '<n>_steps_' pattern crashes with ValueError
defects.statement: existing_steps = int(existing_lora.split('_steps_')[0].split('_')[-1]) (nodes_train.py:403) is applied to any file from the full loras list (:349). Ordinary LoRA names, and this node's own output saved without steps ('{prefix}_{date}_lora.safetensors', :599), raise ValueError and abort training.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:403; options from folder_paths.get_filename_list('loras') at :349.
defects.notes: Must name the filename-based int parse of the step count failing for non-matching names.

defects.title: SaveLoRA writes to a CWD-relative 'models/loras/' path instead of the configured loras directory
defects.statement: SaveLoRA.save builds f'models/loras/{prefix}_...safetensors' (nodes_train.py:599/601) relative to the process working directory, ignoring folder_paths (models_dir derives from base_path/--base-directory, folder_paths.py:18-30). Started from another directory or with --base-directory / extra model paths, the save raises FileNotFoundError or lands where the loras list (and Train LoRA's existing_lora) never sees it.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:599-602 literal 'models/loras/'; folder_paths.py base_path from args.base_directory or dirname(__file__).
defects.notes: Must say the output path is hardcoded/relative to CWD rather than via folder_paths. Path-traversal via prefix is a separate defect (D5).

defects.title: User-supplied filename prefixes are written without path containment (SaveLoRA and Plot Loss Graph)
defects.statement: SaveLoRA interpolates the workflow STRING `prefix` into the output path (nodes_train.py:599/601) and LossGraphNode joins `filename_prefix` onto the temp dir (:680-681) with no containment check; a prefix like '../../x' writes files outside the intended directory. The repo's existing save path (folder_paths.get_save_image_path, folder_paths.py:387-391) refuses paths outside the output folder, so these nodes bypass the established guard for API-submitted workflows.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:599 `f"models/loras/{prefix}_..."`; :681 `os.path.join(self.output_dir, f"{filename_prefix}_{date}.png")`; folder_paths.py:387 commonpath check used by other save nodes.
defects.notes: Must say the prefix / filename_prefix can contain traversal components and escape the destination directory. Either site counts. Not: the hardcoded relative path (D4). Not: the folder input of Load Image Dataset (combo-validated).

defects.title: Resuming from an existing LoRA drops its trained 1-D weight diffs and bias diffs
defects.statement: When existing_lora is set only >=2-D weights are restored through the adapter loader; 1-D weight diffs ('{n}.diff') and bias diffs ('{n}.diff_b') are always recreated as zeros (nodes_train.py:443-460), so the previously trained values are discarded and the re-saved LoRA loses them.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:444-446 and :454-456 torch.zeros regardless of existing_weights; the trainer itself saves '{n}.diff'/'{n}.diff_b' (:451/:458), which comfy/lora.py:72-82 reads at inference.
defects.notes: Must say existing diff/diff_b (bias or 1-D) values are not loaded on resume.

defects.title: Resuming misreads the existing LoRA's alpha, changing its effective scale
defects.statement: Alpha is looked up as f'{key}.alpha' with key='{n}.weight' (nodes_train.py:411,414), but LoRA files and this trainer's own output store '{n}.alpha' (named_parameters 'alpha' at :437-438; comfy/lora.py:41). So a stored non-1.0 alpha is replaced by 1.0; and a LoRA with no alpha (inference scale 1.0, lora.py:169-172) resumes with scale alpha/rank = 1/rank. Either way the resumed adapter no longer reproduces the checkpoint's weights.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:414 `existing_weights.get(f"{key}.alpha", 1.0)`; comfy/lora.py:41 `alpha_name = "{}.alpha".format(x)`; weight_adapter/lora.py:169-172 alpha None -> 1.0.
defects.notes: Either the wrong key ('.weight.alpha') or the missing-alpha → 1/rank scale mismatch counts.

defects.title: Resuming a DoRA / reshape-weight LoRA ignores dora_scale and reshape
defects.statement: LoraDiff unpacks dora_scale and reshape (lora.py:18) but __call__ (lora.py:42-52) applies only w + scale*diff, unlike calculate_weight which applies weight_decompose and pad_tensor_to_shape (lora.py:163-190); in addition the trainer looks dora_scale up under '{n}.weight.dora_scale' (nodes_train.py:415-417) rather than '{n}.dora_scale'. A DoRA LoRA resumed for training therefore loses its magnitude decomposition and changes effective weights.
defects.evidence: lora.py:18 `mat1, mat2, alpha, mid, dora_scale, reshape = weights` and neither used in __call__.
defects.notes: Must say DoRA scale (or reshape) is ignored/lost in the training conversion.

defects.title: Resume looks up existing LoRA keys only by raw module name, silently starting fresh for alias-keyed files
defects.statement: The trainer calls adapter_cls.load(n, existing_weights, ...) with the raw module name n (nodes_train.py:418-421), while inference maps accepted aliases such as 'lora_unet_...' to model keys (comfy/lora.py:180-204). A LoRA in those formats matches nothing, so every module takes the fresh-init branch (:432-436) with no warning, yet existing_steps is still added to the returned step count.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:419 `adapter_cls.load(n, existing_weights, alpha, dora_scale)`; comfy/lora.py:183/193 key_map['lora_unet_...'].
defects.notes: Must say alias/kohya-style keys are not resolved so the existing LoRA is silently not loaded.

defects.title: Resuming from a conv (LoCon/tucker) LoRA crashes in LoraDiff construction
defects.statement: LoraDiff.__init__ (lora.py:21-36) picks the conv class with index mid.ndim-2 (Conv3d for a 4-D mid), constructs Conv layers without kernel_size, and calls layer(mid, rank) passing a tensor as in_channels, so any LoRA with lora_mid raises TypeError; a conv LoRA without mid has 4-D up/down tensors that cannot copy_ into the 2-D Linear weights (:30-33). The trainer calls to_train() on these (nodes_train.py:431).
defects.evidence: lora.py:35 `self.lora_mid = layer(mid, rank, bias=False)`; :22-27 `(Conv1d, Conv2d, Conv3d)[mid.ndim - 2]`; :30-31 no kernel_size.
defects.notes: Any of: tensor passed as channel count, wrong Conv class for mid dims, missing kernel_size, 4-D up/down into Linear. Not R8 (tucker reshape).

defects.title: Resuming from a non-LoRA adapter file (LoHa/LoKr/OFT/BOFT/GLoRA) raises NotImplementedError
defects.statement: The resume loop tries every registered adapter class (nodes_train.py:418-423) and unconditionally calls existing_adapter.to_train() (:431), but only LoRAAdapter implements to_train; WeightAdapterBase.to_train raises NotImplementedError (base.py:18-19).
defects.evidence: base.py:18-19; lora.py:77-78 is the only to_train.
defects.notes: Must say non-LoRA adapter types reach to_train and fail. R6 (create_train on subclasses) is a near-miss and does not count.

defects.title: TrainSampler swallows the loss RuntimeError and then crashes with UnboundLocalError
defects.statement: In TrainSampler.sample (nodes_train.py:46-51) a RuntimeError from loss_fn is caught, conditionally logged and not re-raised; loss.backward() then raises UnboundLocalError, masking the real error. The matched 'does not require grad' message comes from backward(), not the loss call.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:46-51.
defects.notes: Must say the exception is swallowed and 'loss' is then undefined.

defects.title: Plot Loss Graph divides by zero when all losses are equal (e.g. steps=1)
defects.statement: LossGraphNode.plot_loss scales by (max_loss - min_loss) (nodes_train.py:637-638); steps min is 1 (:293), so a one-step run or constant loss raises ZeroDivisionError.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:637-638; steps min 1 at :293.
defects.notes: Division by zero when min == max. The unused draw_loss_graph has the same bug but only the registered node counts.

defects.title: Resize method 'Pad' stretches the image instead of padding
defects.statement: load_and_process_images treats 'Pad' identically to 'Stretch' (nodes_train.py:107-112: both img.resize((w,h))), distorting aspect ratio despite the option name.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:108 and :112 identical resize calls.
defects.notes: Must say Pad resizes/stretches rather than pads.

defects.title: The seed input does not make training reproducible: the seeded generator is never used
defects.statement: train() creates and seeds `generator` (nodes_train.py:394-395) but never passes it anywhere: batch selection (torch.randperm :382), sigma sampling (torch.rand :506) and LoRA init (kaiming_uniform_ in lora.py:71) all use the global RNG, contrary to the seed tooltip (:337).
defects.evidence: generator referenced only at :394-395.
defects.notes: Must say the seed/generator is unused for init/batch/sigma.

defects.title: Training patches (checkpoint forwards) leak onto the shared model if setup fails before the try/finally
defects.statement: patch() replaces forward on modules of mp.model.diffusion_model (nodes_train.py:482-483); model.clone() shares the underlying model. The try/finally that unpatches starts only at :502, so an exception in load_models_gpu (:484) or guider setup (:494-496) leaves checkpoint-wrapped forwards installed for later workflows using that model.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:482-484 before `try:` at :502; unpatch only in the finally at :515-517.
defects.notes: Must say the patching happens before the try/finally so failures leave the model patched.

defects.title: Cosmos blocks take the checkpoint path during ordinary inference because the model is never in eval mode
defects.statement: GeneralDITTransformerBlock.forward checkpoints each block when self.training (blocks.py:799-800), but nn.Module defaults to training=True and ComfyUI never calls eval() on Cosmos diffusion models (model_base.py only at :650/:679 for other models), so every inference step runs torch.utils.checkpoint machinery (RNG-state stash, hooks) for nothing.
defects.evidence: model_base.py:650/679 are the only diffusion_model.eval() calls.
defects.notes: Must say self.training is True at inference so checkpointing runs there. R2 (no inference path at all) is wrong and does not count.

excluded.reason: Claims the checkpointed call passes positional args where block.forward may need keyword-only rope/adaln args. The positional order x, emb_B_D, crossattn_emb, crossattn_mask, rope_emb_L_1_1_D, adaln_lora_B_3D matches DITBuildingBlock.forward (blocks.py:670-678) and none are keyword-only, so the call is correct.
Claims checkpointing omits the forward pass for evaluation, breaking inference. Wrong: the else branch (blocks.py:801-809) runs the block normally when not training.
Suggests keeping `+=` in attention.py for in-place performance. The out-of-place add is deliberate so autograd works during training; a micro-performance preference, not a defect.
Says residual adds in BasicTransformerBlock are inconsistent (x += x_skip vs x = n + x). The PR also changed x_skip to `x = x_skip + x` (attention.py:801); style only.
Suggests typing dora_scale as Optional in WeightAdapterBase.load. Type-hint preference with no runtime consequence.

Says subclasses lack create_train so calling it raises NotImplementedError. create_train is only ever called on adapters[0] (LoRAAdapter, nodes_train.py:428-436); other algorithms are declared future work. (The to_train failure for non-LoRA resumes is D11, a different call.)

Says overriding __call__ on WeightAdapterTrainBase (an nn.Module) bypasses hooks; prefer forward. Design preference; ops.cast_bias_weight calls the wrappers directly and nothing relies on module hooks.

Says tucker_weight_from_conv's reshape(size0,size1) fails for 4-D conv up/down. Tucker up/down are 1x1 (out,rank,1,1), so the reshape is valid; the only path to it already crashes earlier in LoraDiff construction (D10).
Notes shape-convention inconsistency between tucker_weight and tucker_weight_from_conv. Documentation/readability remark; no incorrect result shown.
Says hardcoded tuple unpacking of weights in LoraDiff hurts maintainability. Style; it mirrors LoRAAdapter.weights layout.

comfyanonymous__ComfyUI@b55c224.pr_summary: DirectML fixes: adds model_management.is_directml_enabled(); Flux's rope() computes on CPU when DirectML is enabled (as for MPS/XPU); and CLIPTextModel_ builds its causal mask differently on DirectML (no fill) while other devices now fill with -inf instead of -finfo(dtype).max.

defects.title: DirectML causal mask is built from uninitialized memory, so CLIP text attention gets garbage/no causal masking
defects.statement: In CLIPTextModel_.forward (comfy/clip_model.py:107-108) the DirectML branch creates `torch.empty(x.shape[1], x.shape[1], ...)` and only calls `.triu_(1)` — without any fill. triu_ zeroes the lower triangle but leaves the strictly upper triangle as whatever uninitialized memory torch.empty returned (often 0, sometimes arbitrary values/NaN). The causal mask meant to be a large negative above the diagonal is therefore absent or random, so each token attends to future tokens (or softmax is corrupted by NaN/huge values), producing wrong text embeddings for every CLIP-based model on DirectML — the very backend the PR targets. is_directml_enabled() is a session-wide flag, so this applies even when the text encoder itself runs on CPU.
defects.evidence: clip_model.py:107-108 `if comfy.model_management.is_directml_enabled(): causal_mask = torch.empty(x.shape[1], x.shape[1], dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device).triu_(1)` vs the other branch `.fill_(float("-inf")).triu_(1)`; the mask is then added to / used as the attention mask (112-115).
defects.notes: Must say the DirectML branch never fills the tensor (torch.empty is uninitialised), so the causal mask's upper triangle is garbage/zero rather than -inf/-max.

excluded.reason: Says is_directml_enabled() is verbose (redundant `global` and if) and could just `return directml_enabled`. Style only; the function returns the correct value.

CherryHQ__cherry-studio@5644b00.pr_summary: Refactors OpenAIProvider's streaming path into a middleware pipeline: an async generator turns raw OpenAI chunks into reasoning/text-delta/finish chunks, which go through a new extractReasoningMiddleware (splits <think>…</think> content out as reasoning, adapted from vercel/ai) and a new convertLinksMiddleware (runs convertLinks on every text-delta), and are then consumed by a switch that emits THINKING/TEXT/TEXT_COMPLETE/BLOCK_COMPLETE chunks. It also adds getPotentialStartIndex and stream<->async-iterable helpers, and deletes isReasoningJustDone, the web-search-only per-provider link conversion and BaseProvider.handleThinkingTags.

defects.title: Link conversion now runs on every OpenAI-compatible response, not only web-search ones, so ordinary Markdown links (and tool-use payloads) get rewritten into citations
defects.statement: Before the PR, link conversion ran only inside `if (assistant.enableWebSearch)` (base OpenAIProvider.ts ~595-607). The PR pipes every streamed response through convertLinksMiddleware (OpenAIProvider.ts:544-546), which calls convertLinks on every text-delta with no condition (convertLinksMiddleware.ts:16-21). So in ordinary chats with web search off, every Markdown link `[label](url)` the model writes is rewritten into a numbered citation superscript (linkConverter.ts ~195-246). Because `content` is built from the converted deltas (OpenAIProvider.ts:571) and passed to processToolUses/parseAndCallTools (:639), links inside a <tool_use> payload are altered before the MCP tool call is parsed.
defects.evidence: convertLinksMiddleware.ts:20 `textDelta: convertLinks(chunk.textDelta)` inside `if (chunk.type === 'text-delta')` with no web-search check; OpenAIProvider.ts:544 `await convertLinksMiddleware<OpenAIStreamChunk>().wrapStream(...)` with no enableWebSearch guard; the deleted base branch `if (assistant.enableWebSearch) { if (delta?.annotations) { delta.content = convertLinks(delta.content || '', isFirstChunk) } ...}`.
defects.notes: Must say the conversion is now unconditional / applied to non-web-search responses (ordinary links rewritten, or tool arguments altered). A comment only about @ts-expect-error or typing of textDelta does not count; a comment only about lost provider-specific converters is D4; a comment only about the missing reset is D3.

defects.title: Text from an unmatched '[' onward is held in convertLinks' buffer and never emitted, now on every response, truncating TEXT_DELTA and TEXT_COMPLETE
defects.statement: convertLinks keeps everything from the last '[' (or '([') that does not start a complete `[text](url)` link in a module-level buffer and returns only the prefix before it (linkConverter.ts:164-192). convertLinksMiddleware has no flush() (convertLinksMiddleware.ts:14-26) and nothing drains the buffer when the 'finish' chunk arrives, so an answer containing a non-link bracket (`a[0]`, `- [ ]`, `[note]`) or ending in an incomplete link loses all text from that bracket onward: it never reaches TEXT_DELTA, and `content` (OpenAIProvider.ts:571) sent as TEXT_COMPLETE (:593) is truncated. Because D1 made the converter run on every response, this truncation now hits ordinary answers.
defects.evidence: linkConverter.ts:178-186 `} else if (buffer[i] === '[') { ... const match = /^\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)]+)\)/.exec(substring); if (!match) { safePoint = i; break } }` then :191-192 `const safeBuffer = buffer.substring(0, safePoint); buffer = buffer.substring(safePoint)`; the TransformStream in convertLinksMiddleware.ts defines only `transform`.
defects.notes: Counts if the comment says buffered/incomplete-link text is never flushed at end of stream (response truncated), or that text after an unmatched bracket is withheld. Near-miss that must not count: the missing flush in extractReasoningMiddleware (D5).

defects.title: convertLinks is never reset per response, so buffer, citation counter and URL map leak across responses (and mix between concurrent streams)
defects.statement: The old call passed `isFirstChunk` as convertLinks' resetCounter, clearing the module-level linkCounter, buffer and urlToCounterMap at the start of each response. convertLinksMiddleware.ts:20 calls `convertLinks(chunk.textDelta)` with no reset, so a new answer continues the previous answer's citation numbering, inherits any text left in the buffer (prepended to its first chunk), and the URL map grows for the renderer's lifetime; two concurrent completions interleave their buffered fragments.
defects.evidence: linkConverter.ts:2-6 module-level `let linkCounter = 1`, `let buffer = ''`, `let urlToCounterMap`; :124-128 reset only `if (resetCounter)`; base code `convertLinks(delta.content || '', isFirstChunk)`; head convertLinksMiddleware.ts:20 omits the argument.
defects.notes: Must say state is not reset / shared across responses or streams (numbering or buffered text carried over). A comment only saying conversion is unconditional is D1.

defects.title: Provider-specific web-search citation converters (OpenRouter, Zhipu, Hunyuan) are dropped
defects.statement: The old web-search branch chose convertLinksToOpenRouter, convertLinksToZhipu, or convertLinksToHunyuan (the latter resolving `[N](@ref)` against chunk.search_info.search_results) per provider. The PR removes those imports and calls only generic convertLinks (convertLinksMiddleware.ts:20), which does not understand `[ref_N]` (it treats it as an incomplete link and withholds it) or `(@ref)` citations, so Zhipu/Hunyuan search answers show unresolved references and OpenRouter citations are formatted differently.
defects.evidence: Diff deletes `import { convertLinks, convertLinksToHunyuan, convertLinksToOpenRouter, convertLinksToZhipu } from '@renderer/utils/linkConverter'` and the branch that selected them; at head, `git grep convertLinksToZhipu` finds only linkConverter.ts and its test.
defects.notes: Must name the loss of per-provider (Zhipu/Hunyuan/OpenRouter) citation conversion.

defects.title: extractReasoningMiddleware has no flush, so a partial-tag tail held in its buffer is dropped at stream end
defects.statement: When the buffer ends with a possible prefix of the next tag (e.g. text ending in '<' or '<thi'), the transform keeps it in `buffer` (extractReasoningMiddleware.ts:81-96) waiting for the next chunk. The TransformStream defines only `transform` (:56-99), and the 'finish' chunk is passed straight through (:58-60), so that literal tail is never published and the answer and TEXT_COMPLETE are truncated.
defects.evidence: extractReasoningMiddleware.ts:94-96 `} else { buffer = buffer.slice(startIndex); break }`; TransformStream literal has no flush().
defects.notes: Must mention the missing flush / buffered partial-tag text lost at stream end in the reasoning middleware.

defects.title: TEXT_COMPLETE, tool processing and BLOCK_COMPLETE now run only on a 'finish' chunk, so a stream that ends without finish_reason is never finalized
defects.statement: The old code ran processToolUses and emitted BLOCK_COMPLETE after the for-await loop unconditionally. Now the generator yields 'finish' only when finish_reason is non-empty (OpenAIProvider.ts:525-528), and processToolUses + BLOCK_COMPLETE live only inside `case 'finish'` (:638-651). A provider stream that closes without a finish_reason (or a loop exited through the pause check at :515-517) ends the consumer loop with no TEXT_COMPLETE, no tool call handling and no BLOCK_COMPLETE, leaving the message block unfinished.
defects.evidence: Base: `} // End of for await loop ... await processToolUses(content, idx) ... onChunk({ type: ChunkType.BLOCK_COMPLETE, ...})` after the loop; head: those calls only at :639-651 inside `case 'finish'`, and the generator yields finish only `if (!isEmpty(finishReason))`.
defects.notes: Must say finalization (BLOCK_COMPLETE and/or tool processing) no longer happens when the stream ends without a finish chunk / on pause. Note the pause flag is only set in commented-out code at head (TopicsTab.tsx:99), so the finish-less EOF from an OpenAI-compatible provider is the live path.

A truncated PNG, or one whose first chunk IS IHDR but with a bad length, therefore gets a misleading chunk-ordering diagnostic.
