opencv__opencv@79afad9.pr_summary: Exposes the stream-buffered VideoCapture constructor/open(Ptr<IStreamReader>, …) to Java. IStreamReader::read/seek become CV_WRAP. A new native JavaStreamReader adapter calls back into a Java IStreamReader subclass, and it is wired in through videoio's new gen_dict.json (Ptr_IStreamReader, byte[] buffer arg fix, vector_VideoCaptureAPIs). The Java generator gains 'long long' and 'byte[]' types and no longer overwrites a preconfigured Ptr_<Class> type entry. The Python header parser learns multi-word integer types ('long long', 'unsigned int'…), with a matching Python long long converter and typing-stub entry. VideoCaptureTest is re-enabled and gets a stream-constructor test.

defects.title: JavaStreamReader caches the constructing thread's JNIEnv* and reuses it on other threads; the finalizer-thread destructor or a read from a worker thread is undefined behaviour or a crash
defects.statement: JavaStreamReader stores the JNIEnv* it was constructed with (videoio_converters.hpp:18, modules/videoio/misc/java/src/cpp/videoio_converters.cpp:3) and reuses it in read() (modules/videoio/misc/java/src/cpp/videoio_converters.cpp:20-25), seek() (modules/videoio/misc/java/src/cpp/videoio_converters.cpp:33) and the destructor (modules/videoio/misc/java/src/cpp/videoio_converters.cpp:13). A JNIEnv is valid only on the thread it belongs to. The reader is created inside the VideoCapture(IStreamReader, …) / open() native call, but frames are read by whatever thread later calls capture.read()/grab(), and a Java app commonly opens on one thread and reads on another. The native reader is destroyed when the VideoCapture is released, and for a VideoCapture the user never release()s that happens from the generated finalize() -> delete(nativeObj) on the JVM finalizer thread (gen_java.py:1187-1195). In both cases the stale env pointer makes JNI calls from the wrong thread: undefined behaviour, a JVM abort under -Xcheck:jni, or a crash. The adapter should keep the JavaVM* and call GetEnv/AttachCurrentThread per call.
defects.evidence: modules/videoio/misc/java/src/cpp/videoio_converters.cpp:3 `JavaStreamReader::JavaStreamReader(JNIEnv* _env, jobject _obj) : env(_env)`; :13 `env->DeleteGlobalRef(obj);`; :23 `env->CallLongMethod(obj, m_read, jBuffer, size);`. gen_dict.json builds it inside the constructor's JNI call: `auto n_%(n)s = makePtr<JavaStreamReader>(env, source)`. gen_java.py:1191-1193 generates `protected void finalize() throws Throwable { delete(nativeObj); }` for wrapped classes, so ~VideoCapture, and with it ~JavaStreamReader, can run on the finalizer thread. There is no JavaVM/GetEnv/AttachCurrentThread anywhere in the adapter.
defects.notes: A finding must say that caching the JNIEnv* (thread-local) and using it later — from another thread or from the finalizer/destructor — is invalid, and suggest storing JavaVM* with GetEnv/Attach or an equivalent. Comments only about local-ref leaks or missing NULL checks do not count.

defects.title: Java exceptions thrown by the user's read()/seek() are never checked, so later JNI calls run with an exception pending and garbage is returned
defects.statement: JavaStreamReader::read calls the Java read() via CallLongMethod (modules/videoio/misc/java/src/cpp/videoio_converters.cpp:23) and then immediately calls GetByteArrayRegion (modules/videoio/misc/java/src/cpp/videoio_converters.cpp:24) and DeleteLocalRef without checking ExceptionCheck(). If the user's implementation throws an unchecked exception, JNI functions outside the exception-safe set are called with an exception pending (undefined behaviour; a fatal error under -Xcheck:jni). The garbage return value is passed to the backend as a byte count, and the backend's next read/seek makes more JNI calls with the exception still pending. seek (modules/videoio/misc/java/src/cpp/videoio_converters.cpp:33) has the same problem.
defects.evidence: modules/videoio/misc/java/src/cpp/videoio_converters.cpp:23-26: `jlong res = env->CallLongMethod(obj, m_read, jBuffer, size); env->GetByteArrayRegion(jBuffer, 0, static_cast<jsize>(size), ...); env->DeleteLocalRef(jBuffer); return res;` — no ExceptionCheck/ExceptionClear anywhere in the file.
defects.notes: Must name the missing exception check after the Java callback (CallLongMethod) in read/seek. An exception check after NewByteArray (R10) is a different point: NewByteArray failure is already handled by the NULL check at :21. That is a near-miss and does not count. C11 is credited for its secondary clause ('if Java throws, this JNI operation also runs with a pending exception'); its primary short-read-copy claim alone would not count.

defects.title: vector_VideoCaptureAPIs_to_List caches a FindClass local reference in a static, so later calls use a dead local ref
defects.statement: modules/videoio/misc/java/src/cpp/videoio_converters.cpp:43 stores `env->FindClass("java/lang/Integer")` (a local reference valid only for the current native frame) in a function-static jclass, and line 49 passes it to NewObject on every later call. After the first JNI call returns, the local ref is freed; the next Videoio.getStreamBufferedBackends()/getBackends()-style call that converts a backend list uses a stale handle: undefined behaviour, a fatal error under -Xcheck:jni, or a crash / wrong class. The ArrayList class two lines above is correctly promoted with NewGlobalRef by the ARRAYLIST macro (opencv_java.hpp:30).
defects.evidence: videoio_converters.cpp:39 `static jclass juArrayList = ARRAYLIST(env);` vs :43 `static jclass jInteger = env->FindClass("java/lang/Integer");`; opencv_java.hpp:30 `#define ARRAYLIST(ENV) static_cast<jclass>(ENV->NewGlobalRef(ENV->FindClass("java/util/ArrayList")))`. The same pattern exists in dnn_converters.cpp:69 (copied, per the comment at :36), which is why it is graded low.
defects.notes: Must say the cached Integer jclass is a local reference that must be promoted to a global ref (NewGlobalRef). The GetObjectClass local-ref leak in the constructor (R8, C17) is a different, harmless point.

defects.title: The new stream test's seek() ignores SEEK_CUR/SEEK_END, so the test fails when MSMF is the chosen stream backend
defects.statement: testConstructorStream's IStreamReader.seek (modules/videoio/misc/java/test/VideoCaptureTest.java:119-131) only moves the file pointer for origin 0 and otherwise returns the current position. The test picks the first available stream-buffered backend; MSMF sizes the stream with `stream->seek(0, SEEK_END)` then `seek(0, SEEK_SET)` (cap_msmf.cpp:1279-1280), gets 0 and cannot open, so assertTrue(capture.isOpened()) fails on a Windows build where FFmpeg's plugin is absent or too old and MSMF is selected. The IStreamReader contract (videoio.hpp) documents SEEK_SET/SEEK_END/SEEK_CUR.
defects.evidence: VideoCaptureTest.java:123-125 `if (origin == 0) f.seek(offset); return f.getFilePointer();`; cap_msmf.cpp:1279 `data.resize((size_t)stream->seek(0, SEEK_END));`. FFmpeg's AVIO only forwards SEEK_SET after avio_seek normalisation, so the FFmpeg path passes.
defects.notes: Must say the test reader does not implement SEEK_END/SEEK_CUR (and that a backend using them fails). Comments only about closing the RandomAccessFile (C18) do not count.

excluded.reason: Claim: Memory leak: GetByteArrayElements must be paired with ReleaseByteArrayElements. The current implementation only acquires the array elements but never releases them, causing a memory leak. Similar to the string type handling on line 80, the jni_var should include the release call. Consider: "char* n_ -- Rejected: Only the generated native wrapper for the Java IStreamReader.read (func_arg_fix read.buffer -> byte[]) ever uses the missing ReleaseByteArrayElements path, and that wrapper forwards to a native C++ IStreamReader. No API hands Java a native-backed IStreamReader (Java readers are Java subclasses built with nativeObj 0 whose read() is overridden, as in the test), so that path is unreachable in practice. The stream path that is actually used (JavaStreamReader) copies through NewByteArray/GetByteArrayRegion and is not affected.

Claim: Behavior change: previously `type_dict.setdefault("Ptr_"+name, {}).update({...})` would refresh/update an existing `Ptr_...` mapping. Now it only sets the entry when missing. If `Ptr_...` can be created earlier (e.g., multiple passes, cross-module deps, or preloaded gen_dict overrides) this can leav -- Rejected: The change exists so the gen_dict-provided Ptr_IStreamReader (videoio gen_dict.json) is not clobbered by add_class. The only wrapped class names that repeat (Feature2D, Device) are #ifdef alternatives within one module and would produce identical entries, and no other gen_dict defines a Ptr_ entry. Nothing goes stale.

Claim: The `to` function only handles `PyLong_Check(obj)` but doesn't handle `PyInt_Check(obj)`. Similar converters in this file (e.g., unsigned int, uint64_t) handle both PyInt and PyLong for Python 2 compatibility. This could cause conversion failures when the Python object is a PyInt instance. -- Rejected: OpenCV 4.x Python bindings are Python-3-only, where every int is a PyLong. The PyInt path exists only as a compatibility macro, so nothing is missed.

Claim: Logic issue: This condition allows invalid C++ type combinations. For example: -- Rejected: hdr_parser parses headers that compile, so invalid combinations like 'short char' never occur. The rule only has to accept the valid spellings, which it does. The only CV_WRAP declarations with these types are IStreamReader::read/seek.

Claim: Potential coverage issue: the generator/parser may output canonical spellings like `long long int`, `signed long long`, or `unsigned long long`. Adding only `"long long"` might not match and won’t fix the original missing-type case. Also consider whether this becomes redundant with the existing `int -- Rejected: The parser emits the type exactly as written in the header, and the only new wrapped declarations spell it 'long long' (videoio.hpp:730,739). No other spelling occurs, so the added entry covers the case.

Claim: Missing NULL check for GetObjectClass result. If GetObjectClass returns NULL (e.g., OutOfMemoryError), calling NewGlobalRef on NULL jclass will cause a crash. Also, if NewGlobalRef fails (returns NULL), the global ref is invalid but the destructor will still call DeleteGlobalRef on it. Consider addi -- Rejected: GetObjectClass on a valid global ref of a live object does not return NULL in practice (it would need OOM on a local-ref allocation); speculative hardening. m_read/m_seek NULL is already handled in read/seek.

Claim: Potential JNI local reference leak: `GetObjectClass(obj)` returns a local ref that should be `DeleteLocalRef(cls)` after `GetMethodID` calls. In long-running/native loops this can exhaust the local ref table. -- Rejected: The constructor runs once per VideoCapture construction inside a JNI native call; the local ref is freed when that native call returns. No loop accumulates it, so it is trivial.

Claim: **Missing error handling**: The code doesn't check if `GetMethodID` succeeds. If the Java class doesn't implement the required methods correctly, `m_read` or `m_seek` will be null, which could lead to crashes. -- Rejected: Already handled: read() and seek() return 0 when m_read/m_seek are null (videoio_converters.cpp:18-19, 31-32), and the Java type IStreamReader always declares both methods.

Claim: **Missing JNI exception check**: After calling `NewByteArray`, you should check for JNI exceptions. If memory allocation fails, this could throw an OutOfMemoryError that needs to be handled. -- Rejected: NewByteArray failure is handled by the `if (!jBuffer) return 0;` check at :21. The pending OOME propagates to Java when the native call returns, which is acceptable.

Claim: Size truncation risk: casting `size` (long long) to `jsize` can overflow for large values, leading to negative/incorrect allocation and memory issues. Validate `size` <= std::numeric_limits<jsize>::max() before `NewByteArray` / `GetByteArrayRegion`. -- Rejected: size comes from the videoio backend's internal I/O buffer requests (small fixed-size buffers), never from untrusted input, so exceeding 2^31 is contrived.

Claim: Const correctness: The function only reads from the vector, so the parameter should be const reference to prevent unintended modifications and enable const correctness. -- Rejected: Const-correctness style nit.

Claim: Header completeness: this header uses `std::vector` in the declaration but doesn’t include `<vector>`. Relying on transitive includes is fragile; include `<vector>` here or forward declare with `namespace std { template<class T, class Allocator> class vector; }` (including `<vector>` is preferred). -- Rejected: <vector> comes in through opencv2/core.hpp, which the header includes; a header-hygiene nit.

Claim: setUp now throws when OPENCV_TEST_DATA_PATH is unset, so every VideoCaptureTest fails. Rejected: this is the established OpenCV Java test convention (DnnTensorFlowTest.java:58, DnnListRegressionTest.java:56, BarcodeDetectorTest.java:25 throw the same way) and CI always defines the variable.
Claim: file-dependent setup makes unrelated capture tests fail without OPENCV_TEST_DATA_PATH. Rejected: same as C3, project convention with the variable always set in CI.

Claim: size is narrowed from long long to jsize without bounds, so a large request wraps. Rejected: sizes come from backend internal I/O buffer requests (small), never user input; contrived (same as R11).

Claim: the new multi-word rule lets 'unsigned char*' reach the char* -> c_string rewrite, producing 'unsigned c_string'. Rejected: before the PR 'unsigned char* x' already mis-parsed (the name absorbed 'char *'), and no CV_WRAP declaration uses signed/unsigned char*, so nothing is made worse in practice.

Claim: the new Python long long converter rejects NumPy integer scalars and accepts bools, unlike the int64 converter. Rejected: only reachable through the Python wrappers of IStreamReader.read/seek on a native IStreamReader, which Python code cannot obtain (abstract class, no wrapped factory); no concrete consequence.
Claim: on LP64 the long long converter handles IStreamReader.seek instead of int64 and rejects NumPy int64. Rejected: same as C7.

Claim: wrapping IStreamReader::read exposes char* as a Python input string that native code writes into. Rejected: Python cannot obtain a native IStreamReader instance to call read on (abstract, no constructor/factory wrapped), so the path is unreachable.

Claim: the generated native IStreamReader.read wrapper acquires byte[] elements with GetByteArrayElements and never releases them. Rejected: that wrapper is only reached for a native-backed Java IStreamReader, and none exists -- Java readers are subclasses constructed with nativeObj 0 that override read (see R1); the used path, JavaStreamReader, copies via NewByteArray/GetByteArrayRegion.
Claim: repeated generated IStreamReader.read calls pin/leak Java arrays because ReleaseByteArrayElements is missing. Rejected: same as C8, unreachable path.
Claim: GetByteArrayElements must be paired with ReleaseByteArrayElements in the generated IStreamReader.read wrapper. Rejected: same as C8.

Claim: read copies all size bytes instead of the count returned, needlessly copying the zero-filled remainder. Rejected: the backend only consumes the returned count; the extra copy of a small buffer is a negligible cost, no functional consequence.

Claim: short reads put bytes the reader did not supply into the native stream for the decoder to consume. Rejected: the caller uses only res bytes (e.g. FFmpeg's read callback returns the count), so bytes past res are never consumed; the size-narrowing part is contrived (as C4).
Claim: the enum-list converter duplicates the dnn list-conversion code and should be centralized. Rejected: refactoring preference.

Claim: gen_dict hard-codes 'source' instead of %(n)s in the Ptr_IStreamReader jni_var. Rejected: both wrapped functions (VideoCapture ctor and open) name the argument 'source', so the generated code is correct; any future mismatch fails at compile time.

Claim: the GetObjectClass local ref in the constructor is never deleted and can overflow the local ref table. Rejected: the constructor runs once inside a JNI native call and the ref is freed when it returns (same as R8).
Claim: the test does not close its RandomAccessFile. Rejected: test-hygiene nit with no effect on results.
Claim: the Java reader's byte-count/EOF contract should be documented. Rejected: documentation request.

nextcloud__server@51b5ea9.pr_summary: Refactors the public OCP layer (lib/public) to stop using the private `\OC::$server` service locator: calls become `\OCP\Server::get(...)`, ApiController reads the Origin via `IRequest::getHeader('origin')`, psalm template annotations are added (GenericEvent, ILanguageIterator), ILanguageIterator::next() gains a `: void` return type, and IQueryLogger::stopQuery is documented as void. Doc-comment usage examples in several OCP interfaces are updated to the new style, and the now-unneeded entries are removed from build/psalm-baseline-ocp.xml.

defects.title: ICrypto usage docs now show `\OCP\Server::getCrypto()`, a method that does not exist
defects.statement: lib/public/Security/ICrypto.php:16-17 replaced `\OC::$server->getCrypto()` with `\OCP\Server::getCrypto()->encrypt(...)` in both usage examples. `OCP\Server` (lib/public/Server.php) only exposes the static `get(string $serviceName)`; there is no getCrypto(). The public API documentation now tells app developers to call a method that fails with 'Call to undefined method OCP\Server::getCrypto()'. The correct form is `\OCP\Server::get(ICrypto::class)`.
defects.evidence: ICrypto.php:16 ` * $encryptWithDefaultPassword = \OCP\Server::getCrypto()->encrypt('EncryptedText');` and :17 the same with a password; lib/public/Server.php declares only `public static function get(string $serviceName)`.
defects.notes: Must say Server::getCrypto() does not exist / the example should use Server::get(ICrypto::class). The IEventDispatcher-import nit in AFilesDocument (R1, C3, C4, C6) does not count.

excluded.reason: Says the AFilesDocument doc example uses unqualified `IEventDispatcher::class` and should be fully qualified. A doc-comment snippet that, like its neighbouring unqualified `GenericEvent`, assumes the reader's own `use` imports; style of the example, not a defect.

Says adding `: void` to ILanguageIterator::next() breaks third-party classes implementing the interface with an untyped next(). ILanguageIterator is a service-produced type (IFactory::getLanguageIterator) whose only implementation already declares `void`, and the interface's other methods (current(): string, key(): int, valid(): bool) already forced typed implementations; no concrete implementer is affected, so the break is speculative.

Says the AFilesDocument listener example lacks an import for IEventDispatcher so it resolves into the Model namespace. Doc-snippet style: the example (like its unqualified GenericEvent) assumes imports; no code is affected.
Says IEventDispatcher is not imported in the AFilesDocument doc example and would resolve to the wrong namespace if copied. Doc-snippet style; same as R1/C3.
Says the AFilesDocument doc example names IEventDispatcher without qualification or import. Doc-snippet style; same as R1/C3.

Says an explicitly empty Origin header is now turned into `*` in preflightedCors while CORSMiddleware echoes the empty value. An empty Origin is not a valid CORS request and the difference has no practical consequence; contrived.

lvgl__lvgl@9cce37c.pr_summary: Reverts lv_animimg_set_src to its original three-argument signature (dropping the `bool reverse` parameter added shortly before) and adds a separate lv_animimg_set_src_reverse() that sets the animation values from num down to 0. Updates the header docs, the widget .rst, the C example and the unit tests (plus a new smoke test for the reverse setter).

excluded.reason: Says the .rst should say 'reverse' instead of 'flip playback' and show parameter types. Wording ('flip' vs 'reverse') and showing parameter types in the .rst expr are documentation style; the documented calls (animimg.rst:34,37) match the header signatures at lv_animimage.h:76,84.

Says the duplicated setup in lv_animimg_set_src and lv_animimg_set_src_reverse should be a helper. Four duplicated setup lines between lv_animimg_set_src and lv_animimg_set_src_reverse (lv_animimage.c:110-126) is a refactoring preference, not a defect.

Claims the 0..num animation range lets num==0 underflow to dsc[-1] in index_change. The num==0 underflow in index_change (lv_animimage.c:261 `idx = animimg->pic_count - 1`) and the 0..num range are pre-existing: base lv_animimg_set_src set the identical values (0,num)/(num,0) with the same clamp; the PR only splits the reverse branch into its own function and does not make it worse.

Claims removing the `reverse` parameter breaks backwards compatibility for 4-argument callers. The PR restores the original 3-argument lv_animimg_set_src; the 4-argument form was added only by #8085 (702732d) days earlier and was never the long-standing API, so dropping it restores compatibility with existing 3-arg callers (and the LV_PROPERTY_ANIMIMAGE_SRC setter table at lv_animimage.c:55). All in-repo callers (example, tests) are updated.

Says 'flip playback' and header grammar ('series images', 'images' number') are unclear. Terminology ('flip' vs 'reverse') and grammar in the header doc comment (lv_animimage.h:78-83) are wording nits.
Says test_animimg_set_src_reverse only asserts non-null and should assert the reverse start/end values. Test-quality request, not a defect.
Asks the two setters to share their validation/assignment code. Refactoring preference (same as R2); no drift.
Asks the docs to describe 'flip playback' precisely as reverse frame order. Documentation wording nit (same as R1/R5).

Claims existing callers of the four-argument lv_animimg_set_src(obj, dsc, num, reverse) no longer compile. The 4-arg form was introduced days earlier by 702732d (#8085) and never was the long-standing API; the PR restores the original 3-arg signature (which the LV_PROPERTY setter table at lv_animimage.c:55 also expects) and updates every in-repo caller.
Says the new reverse test asserts only non-null and would pass if reverse were broken. Test-quality request.
Says the new reverse test should assert animation endpoints or frame order. Test-quality request (same as C5).

Claims the 4-argument call contract is broken and old reverse callers would play forward. Same as C4: the 4-arg form was a days-old addition (702732d) being reverted to the original 3-arg API; old binaries cannot silently change direction since a 4-arg call no longer compiles, and all in-repo callers are updated.

lvgl__lvgl@e526b2a.pr_summary: Assorted XML fixes and additions: lv_switch XML parser/schema, a tabview tab_button element (new lv_tabview_get_tab_button), grid column/row dsc_array props for inline object styles and named styles, span text binding (lv_spangroup_bind_span_text plus new lv_span_set_text_fmt / lv_spangroup_set_span_text_fmt), scale section min/max bindings; consolidates duplicate free-user-data callbacks into lv_event_free_user_data_cb, makes grid_update return early when calc() fails, fixes scale rotation parsing, and edits several schema XMLs and docs.

defects.title: Grid dsc_array parsers under-allocate by one int: heap overflow on every value
defects.statement: Both new grid descriptor parsers count spaces (n tokens -> n-1 spaces) and allocate (item_cnt + 1) ints, then write all n tokens plus LV_GRID_TEMPLATE_LAST, i.e. n+1 ints into n slots. Every well-formed value, even a single track like "100", writes one int past the malloc block (src/others/xml/parsers/lv_xml_obj_parser.c:903/920, src/others/xml/lv_xml_style.c:293/309), corrupting the heap.
defects.evidence: for(i = 0; value[i] != '\0'; i++) if(value[i] == ' ') item_cnt++;  int32_t * dsc_array = lv_malloc((item_cnt + 1) * sizeof(int32_t)); ... while(sub_value) { dsc_array[item_cnt] = ...; item_cnt++; } dsc_array[item_cnt] = LV_GRID_TEMPLATE_LAST; (obj_parser.c:903-920, style.c:293-309). lv_xml_split_str returns every token.
defects.notes: Must say the allocation is one element short (counts separators, not tokens, so no room for the terminator) and overflows. Either site counts. Generic 'validate bounds'/'sub_value[1] out of bounds' remarks (R14) do not count.

defects.title: Span *_text_fmt setters never free the previous owned text: leak per call / per bound-subject update
defects.statement: lv_span_set_text_fmt and lv_spangroup_set_span_text_fmt free the old text only when `span->txt == NULL && span->static_flag` (lv_span.c:216, 274), which never frees a real allocation; the owned previous string is then overwritten. The new span_text_observer_cb calls lv_spangroup_set_span_text_fmt on every subject notification, so every update leaks one string.
defects.evidence: if(span->txt == NULL && span->static_flag) { lv_free(span->txt); } span->static_flag = 0; span->txt = text;  Compare lv_spangroup_delete_span (lv_span.c:150): if(cur_span->txt && cur_span->static_flag == 0) lv_free(cur_span->txt).
defects.notes: Must identify the wrong/inverted free condition leaking the previous text. A comment only about va_end is D3. C41 (share the two copies) is a refactor suggestion, excluded.

defects.title: Span *_text_fmt return on allocation failure without va_end
defects.statement: In lv_span_set_text_fmt and lv_spangroup_set_span_text_fmt, `if(text == NULL) return;` precedes va_end(args) (lv_span.c:212, 270), so the va_start'ed list is not ended on the OOM path: undefined behaviour per the C standard.
defects.evidence: va_start(args, fmt); char * text = lv_text_set_text_vfmt(fmt, args); LV_ASSERT_MALLOC(text); if(text == NULL) return; va_end(args);
defects.notes: Must mention va_end skipped on the early return. R25 also raises this point but is filed under D2 (its more severe half).

defects.title: Textarea schema renamed to placeholder_text but the parser only accepts placeholder
defects.statement: xmls/lv_textarea.xml:9 now advertises `placeholder_text` (was `placeholder`), while lv_xml_textarea_apply only handles `placeholder` (src/others/xml/parsers/lv_xml_textarea_parser.c:59). XML written against the schema silently leaves the placeholder unset.
defects.evidence: xmls/lv_textarea.xml:9 <prop name="placeholder_text" .../> (base: name="placeholder"); textarea_parser.c:59 else if(lv_streq("placeholder", name)) lv_textarea_set_placeholder_text(item, value);
defects.notes: Must say schema and parser now disagree on the attribute name (either fix direction counts).

defects.title: Grid dsc_array parsers cast away const and destructively split the caller's attribute string
defects.statement: Both new parsers do `char * value_buf = (char *)value;` and call lv_xml_split_str, which writes '\0' over each separator. The attribute value is `const char *` owned by the caller: lv_xml_create() with string-literal attrs writes into read-only memory (crash), and any reused attribute value is truncated to its first token (lv_xml_obj_parser.c:905, lv_xml_style.c:295).
defects.evidence: char * value_buf = (char *)value; ... const char * sub_value = lv_xml_split_str(&value_buf, ' ');  lv_xml_split_str writes *src_next = '\0'.
defects.notes: Must point at mutating the const input (read-only literal crash / corrupting the attribute).

defects.title: grid_update early return leaks row arrays when calc_cols fails
defects.statement: calc() allocates c->y/c->h in calc_rows then returns LV_RESULT_INVALID if calc_cols finds no column descriptor (lv_grid.c:237-244). The new `if(res != LV_RESULT_OK) return;` (lv_grid.c:193-194) skips calc_free, leaking both arrays on every layout pass of a grid with rows but no column template.
defects.evidence: calc_rows: c->y = lv_malloc(...); c->h = lv_malloc(...); calc: if(calc_cols(cont, calc_out) == LV_RESULT_INVALID) return LV_RESULT_INVALID; grid_update: lv_result_t res = calc(cont, &c); if(res != LV_RESULT_OK) return;
defects.notes: Must say the early return skips calc_free and leaks partially allocated calc arrays. The empty-grid stale-size regression of the same line is D12.

defects.title: Tabview tab_button XML element crashes when the index attribute is omitted
defects.statement: lv_xml_tabview_tab_button_create passes lv_xml_get_value_of(attrs, "index") straight into lv_xml_atoi (lv_xml_tabview_parser.c:99-100); lv_xml_get_value_of returns NULL for a missing attribute and lv_xml_atoi dereferences it, so <lv_tabview-tab_button/> without index is a NULL dereference.
defects.evidence: const char * index_str = lv_xml_get_value_of(attrs, "index"); int32_t index_int = lv_xml_atoi(index_str);
defects.notes: Must mention a missing/NULL index attribute leading to a crash.

defects.title: Span text binding keeps a raw span pointer; deleting the span leaves a dangling observer (UAF)
defects.statement: lv_spangroup_bind_span_text stores the span in the observer user_data but ties the observer only to the spangroup object (lv_observer.c:831-836). lv_spangroup_delete_span frees the span (lv_span.c:155) while the group lives; the next subject notification calls lv_spangroup_set_span_text[_fmt] on freed memory.
defects.evidence: user_data->element = span; lv_observer_t * observer = lv_subject_add_observer_obj(subject, span_text_observer_cb, obj, user_data); nothing unsubscribes in lv_spangroup_delete_span.
defects.notes: Must mention span deletion while bound -> dangling pointer / use-after-free.

defects.title: New label doc notes wrongly say the fmt setters ignore LV_USE_ARABIC_PERSIAN_CHARS
defects.statement: The PR adds `@note It ignores LV_USE_ARABIC_PERSIAN_CHARS` to lv_label_set_text_fmt/vfmt (lv_label.h:100, 117), but both go through lv_text_set_text_vfmt, which runs lv_text_ap_proc when the option is enabled (lv_text.c:493-510). The new docs are false.
defects.evidence: lv_text.c:493 #if LV_USE_ARABIC_PERSIAN_CHARS ... lv_text_ap_proc(raw_txt, text);
defects.notes: The note on lv_label_set_text_static (line 126) is correct; only the fmt/vfmt notes count.

defects.title: lv_spangroup_bind_span_text declared under LV_USE_LABEL but defined under LV_USE_SPAN
defects.statement: lv_observer.h:548-564 wraps the declaration in #if LV_USE_LABEL while lv_observer.c defines it under #if LV_USE_SPAN. With LV_USE_SPAN=1 and LV_USE_LABEL=0, lv_xml_spangroup_parser.c:102 calls an undeclared function (build error under strict C / -Werror); with LV_USE_LABEL=1, LV_USE_SPAN=0 the API is declared but not defined (link error if called).
defects.evidence: lv_observer.h:548 #if LV_USE_LABEL ... lv_observer_t * lv_spangroup_bind_span_text(...); lv_observer.c:795 #if LV_USE_SPAN.
defects.notes: Must name the wrong preprocessor guard. A comment only saying the doc text says Label (R6/C26) is D14, not this.

defects.title: Named-style grid branch matches the prefixed names, so the schema's grid_*_dsc_array style props are ignored
defects.statement: lv_xml_style_register matches unprefixed property names (SET_STYLE_IF uses #prop, lv_xml_style.c:45) and globals.xml:315-316 declares `grid_column_dsc_array`/`grid_row_dsc_array` for styles, but the new branch (lv_xml_style.c:284-285) only accepts `style_grid_column_dsc_array`/`style_grid_row_dsc_array`. A <style> using the advertised names falls to the 'style property is not supported' warning and the grid template is never set.
defects.evidence: lv_xml_style.c:45 #define SET_STYLE_IF(prop, value) if(lv_streq(name, #prop)) ...; :284 else if(lv_streq(name, "style_grid_column_dsc_array") || lv_streq(name, "style_grid_row_dsc_array")); globals.xml adds <prop name="grid_column_dsc_array" .../>. Compare the obj parser whose macro prefixes "style_" (lv_xml_obj_parser.c:64).
defects.notes: Must say the named-style parser checks the style_-prefixed name while styles (and the schema) use unprefixed names, so the feature does not work in named styles.

defects.title: grid_update early return also skips the size refresh and LAYOUT_CHANGED for an empty grid
defects.statement: calc() returns LV_RESULT_INVALID (after zeroing the result) when the container has no children (lv_grid.c:233-236). Previously grid_update carried on, refreshed a content-sized container (lv_obj_refr_size) and sent LV_EVENT_LAYOUT_CHANGED; the new `if(res != LV_RESULT_OK) return;` (lv_grid.c:194) skips both, so a LV_SIZE_CONTENT grid whose last child is deleted/cleaned keeps its stale size and layout listeners are not notified.
defects.evidence: calc: if(lv_obj_get_child(cont, 0) == NULL) { lv_memzero(calc_out, ...); return LV_RESULT_INVALID; } (same at base); grid_update tail: if(w_set == LV_SIZE_CONTENT || h_set == LV_SIZE_CONTENT) lv_obj_refr_size(cont); lv_obj_send_event(cont, LV_EVENT_LAYOUT_CHANGED, NULL); now unreachable when res != OK.
defects.notes: Must say the early return also bypasses the empty-grid size refresh / LAYOUT_CHANGED. A comment only about leaking calc arrays is D6.

defects.title: Named-style grid descriptor arrays are never freed
defects.statement: The named-style branch lv_mallocs dsc_array and stores only the pointer in the style (lv_xml_style.c:311-316). Scope teardown calls lv_style_reset (lv_xml_component.c:294), which frees the style's property storage, not the pointed-to array, and nothing else owns it, so every registered grid style leaks its arrays (unlike the object path, which frees on LV_EVENT_DELETE).
defects.evidence: lv_style_set_grid_column_dsc_array(style, dsc_array); no free anywhere; lv_xml_component.c:294 lv_style_reset(&style->style); obj parser path adds lv_obj_add_event_cb(obj, lv_event_free_user_data_cb, LV_EVENT_DELETE, dsc_array).
defects.notes: Must say the array is never released (on style reset/replacement/teardown). Freeing it immediately after setting (R12's suggested fix) would be a use-after-free, but R12 does identify the leak at this site.

defects.title: lv_spangroup_bind_span_text doc copied from the label binding is wrong
defects.statement: The new declaration's doc (lv_observer.h:550-559) says it binds a Subject 'to a Label' and that `fmt == NULL` can only be used with string/pointer subjects, but the function binds a spangroup's span and, like the implementation shows (lv_observer.c:802-812), defaults to "%d"/"%0.1f" for int/float subjects when fmt is NULL.
defects.evidence: lv_observer.h: "Bind an integer, string, or pointer Subject to a Label." / "@note fmt == NULL can be used only with string and pointer Subjects."; lv_observer.c: if(fmt == NULL) { if(subject->type == LV_SUBJECT_TYPE_INT) fmt = "%d"; ... }
defects.notes: Either the 'Label' mistake or the wrong NULL-fmt note counts. A comment about the #if guard is D10.

lvgl__lvgl@a0067e3.pr_summary: Adds an early return to lv_text_utf8_next (src/misc/lv_text.c:652-653) that returns 0 without advancing the index when txt is NULL or txt[*i] is the terminating '\0' (previously the ASCII branch returned 0 and incremented *i), plus five unit tests for lv_text_encoded_letter_next_2 (NULL, empty, single ASCII, single 2-byte UTF-8, two characters).

defects.title: Not advancing the index at '\0' makes length-bounded scans that include the terminator loop forever (e.g. tapping the last line of a centred/right-aligned label or roller)
defects.statement: lv_text_utf8_next now returns without incrementing *i when txt[*i] == '\0' (lv_text.c:653); before, NUL took the ASCII branch and advanced *i. Loops that iterate `while(i < length)` calling lv_text_encoded_letter_next_2 — lv_text_get_width (lv_text.c:399-402) and lv_text_get_width_with_flags (:432-435) — therefore make no progress once i reaches a NUL that lies inside `length`. lv_label_get_letter_on deliberately includes the NUL terminator in the last line (lv_label.c:446-450 `new_line_start++`), computes length = new_line_start - line_start (:477) and passes it to calculate_x_coordinate (:478), which for LV_TEXT_ALIGN_CENTER/RIGHT calls lv_text_get_width_with_flags(txt, length, ...) (lv_label.c:1285-1291). So hit-testing the last line of a centre/right-aligned label spins forever: this is a normal path — lv_roller's click handler calls lv_label_get_letter_on (lv_roller.c:758) on a label that inherits the default theme's text_align_center (lv_theme_default.c:965), and textarea click/cursor code calls it too (lv_textarea.c:887, 913, 1297, 1361). A tap on the last roller option freezes the UI thread.
defects.evidence: lv_text.c:653 `if(txt == NULL || txt[*i] == '\0') return result;`; lv_text.c:540-541 letter_next_2 = `*letter = lv_text_encoded_next(txt, ofs); *letter_next = *letter != '\0' ? ... : 0;` (ofs unchanged at NUL); lv_text.c:432-435 `while(i < length) { ... lv_text_encoded_letter_next_2(txt, &letter, &letter_next, &i);`; lv_label.c:446-450 `/*Include the NULL terminator in the last line*/ ... if(letter != '\n' && txt[new_line_start] == '\0') new_line_start++;`; :477-478 `uint32_t length = new_line_start - line_start; calculate_x_coordinate(&x, align, bidi_txt, length, ...)`; :1285-1291 calls lv_text_get_width_with_flags for CENTER/RIGHT; lv_roller.c:758 `letter_i = lv_label_get_letter_on(label, &p, true);`; lv_theme_default.c:965 roller gets text_align_center. Base lv_text_utf8_next: NUL is LV_IS_ASCII so `result = txt[*i]; (*i)++;`.
defects.notes: Must say the early return at NUL leaves *i unadvanced so a caller looping on a byte length / index that reaches or passes the terminator never terminates (hang / infinite loop). Naming lv_text_get_width(_with_flags), lv_label_get_letter_on or get_char_id as the stuck caller all count. A vague 'callers might expect *i to be incremented' (R2) is a weak match. Comments that only ask for logging on NULL (R1) or about test style do not count.

excluded.reason: Asks that the new NULL check log an error/warning (LOG_ERR/LOG_WRN). Style/policy request: neighbouring encode helpers do not log and LOG_ERR is Zephyr's API, not LVGL's; no defect.

No test configuration sets LV_TXT_ENC (git grep TXT_ENC under tests/ finds nothing), so tests always build with the UTF-8 default; the alternate-build crash is not reachable in this repo's test runs. Its style nits are formatting preferences.
Asks to split combined variable declarations in the new tests per the coding style. Formatting nit.
Suggests initialising letter/letter_next to non-zero sentinels so the NULL/empty tests actually verify the outputs are cleared. Test-strength request, not a defect in the code.

cline__cline@419534c.pr_summary: Makes non-attempt-completion checkpoint creation in Task.saveCheckpoint non-blocking: the 'checkpoint_created' message is now said immediately, and CheckpointTracker.commit() runs in the background via a floating .then() that later writes the resulting hash onto the last 'checkpoint_created' message. A long comment explains that the attempt-completion path stays synchronous.

defects.title: Floating commit() promise has no rejection handler: a failed checkpoint commit becomes an unhandled rejection and leaves a hash-less checkpoint row in the chat
defects.statement: CheckpointTracker.commit() rethrows every failure (CheckpointTracker.ts:189-195 `throw new Error("Failed to create checkpoint: ...")`). At src/core/task/index.ts:1322 the promise is started with `.then(async ...)` and neither awaited nor given a `.catch`, so any git failure (lock contention, add/commit error, shadow repo missing) becomes an unhandled promise rejection in the extension host instead of reaching the caller. In addition, `await this.say("checkpoint_created")` (1321) now runs BEFORE the commit and unconditionally, whereas before it ran only when a commitHash came back; a failed/empty commit therefore leaves a checkpoint_created message with no lastCheckpointHash that the UI presents as a real checkpoint but restore/compare cannot use (restore paths at index.ts:407/418/429 require lastCheckpointHash).
defects.evidence: index.ts:1321 `await this.say("checkpoint_created")`; 1322 `this.checkpointTracker.commit().then(async (commitHash) => {` ... 1334 `})` with no catch. CheckpointTracker.ts:189 `} catch (error) {` ... `throw new Error(`Failed to create checkpoint: ...`)`. Base side awaited commit() and only said checkpoint_created `if (commitHash)`.
defects.notes: Must say the background commit promise is unhandled (no catch / not awaited) so failures become unhandled rejections and/or leave a checkpoint message with no hash. A generic 'consider error handling' without tying it to the floating promise is borderline.

defects.title: Background commit races with later work: hash can land on the wrong checkpoint message and the snapshot can include later edits or collide with the next commit
defects.statement: Because saveCheckpoint now returns before the git commit finishes (index.ts:1322), the task proceeds to the next API request/tool while `git add`/`git commit` is still running on the shadow repo. (a) When the commit resolves, the hash is written to `findLastIndex(... m.say === "checkpoint_created")` evaluated at completion time (1324-1327), not to the message created for this commit; if another saveCheckpoint has said a newer checkpoint_created in the meantime, this hash is attached to the newer message and the older one never gets a hash (or gets overwritten out of order). (b) The staged snapshot is taken whenever `addCheckpointFiles` actually runs, so file writes by the next tool can be included in the earlier checkpoint, making 'restore' to it incorrect. (c) A second commit() (another checkpoint or the synchronous attempt_completion commit at 1363) can run concurrently on the same shadow git index, failing on index.lock.
defects.evidence: index.ts:1324 `const lastCheckpointMessageIndex = findLastIndex(this.messageStateHandler.getClineMessages(), (m) => m.say === "checkpoint_created")` inside the .then callback; saveCheckpoint is called from ~30 sites in ToolExecutor.ts (233, 247, 458, ...), each after which execution continues immediately; the comment at 1319 states the commit 'can take multiple seconds for large shadow git repos'.
defects.notes: Count if the comment identifies that the async commit is not tied to its own message (index captured at resolve time) OR that it races with subsequent checkpoint/commits/file edits. Should capture the index before the commit or serialize commits.

defects.title: Checkpoint row is shown (with Restore/Compare) before its hash exists; Restore in that window silently resets to an older checkpoint
defects.statement: saveCheckpoint now says 'checkpoint_created' (index.ts:1321) before commit() has produced a hash, and the webview renders its checkpoint controls immediately. While the background commit is running (seconds on large shadow repos, per the PR's own comment at 1319) the row has no lastCheckpointHash: Compare logs 'No checkpoint hash found' and does nothing (index.ts:566-570), and Restore takes the fallback branch `!offset && lastMessageWithHash.lastCheckpointHash` (index.ts:429-431, 'falling back to previous checkpoint') and resets the workspace to the PREVIOUS checkpoint, not the one the user clicked. Before the PR the row only appeared once the hash was known.
defects.evidence: index.ts:1321 `await this.say("checkpoint_created")` before 1322 `this.checkpointTracker.commit().then(...)`; index.ts:429-431 `} else if (!offset && lastMessageWithHash.lastCheckpointHash && this.checkpointTracker) { // Fallback: restore to most recent checkpoint when target message has no checkpoint hash`; index.ts:566-570 `if (!hash) { console.error("No checkpoint hash found") ...`.
defects.notes: Must say the checkpoint UI/actions are available before the hash exists (pending window), leading to a wrong/older restore or a no-op compare. The permanent hashless row after a FAILED commit belongs to D1; the hash being written to the wrong (newer) row belongs to D2.

excluded.reason: Says the new checkpoint comment is overly verbose and should be restructured. Comment style preference; the comment is accurate.
Asks whether the first-request checkpoint (index.ts ~2156-2171), which still awaits commit(), is outside this fix. Scope question; leaving another path unchanged introduces no defect.

cline__cline@f098af0.pr_summary: Adds terminal telemetry: three enums (TerminalOutputFailureReason, TerminalUserInterventionAction, TerminalHangStage) and four capture methods on TelemetryService, re-exported from services/telemetry. Task.executeCommandTool starts a 30s 'buffer stuck' timer around each command_output ask, records a STREAM_TIMEOUT hang when the ask throws, records 'Proceed while running' clicks, and starts a 60s 'waiting for completion' timer. TerminalProcess records output failures (empty shell-integration output, no shell integration) and whether output was captured via shell integration, clipboard, or not at all, calling getLatestTerminalOutput a second time to decide.

defects.title: Every superseded command_output ask is logged as a STREAM_TIMEOUT terminal hang
defects.statement: flushBuffer's `this.ask("command_output", chunk)` (src/core/task/index.ts:1518) waits until the user answers or lastMessageTs changes; ask() then throws "Current ask promise was ignored" (index.ts:845-846), which its own comment names as the expected outcome for command_output. Because flushBuffer returns early while chunkEnroute (index.ts:1498-1504), the first chunk's ask normally stays open for the whole command and is superseded when the task posts its next message. The PR's catch (index.ts:1531-1533) records `captureTerminalHang(STREAM_TIMEOUT)` for that rejection (and for 'Cline instance aborted'), so nearly every command that produces output and is not clicked through emits a hang event; no stream timeout is measured anywhere.
defects.evidence: index.ts:842-846 `await pWaitFor(() => this.taskState.askResponse !== undefined || this.taskState.lastMessageTs !== askTs ...); if (this.taskState.lastMessageTs !== askTs) { throw new Error("Current ask promise was ignored") // could happen if we send multiple asks in a row i.e. with command_output`; index.ts:1531-1533 `} catch { Logger.error("Error while asking for command output"); telemetryService.captureTerminalHang(TerminalHangStage.STREAM_TIMEOUT)`; say() sets lastMessageTs (index.ts:889,920,935).
defects.notes: Must say the catch labels an ordinary ask rejection (superseded/ignored ask or abort) as STREAM_TIMEOUT, i.e. false hang telemetry on the normal path. Timer-leak comments (R2/R4) do not count; the BUFFER_STUCK user-wait issue is D2.

defects.title: BUFFER_STUCK timer clocks the pending user prompt, so any command-output ask open for 30s is reported as a stuck buffer
defects.statement: The 30s bufferStuckTimer (index.ts:1511-1515) is started after outputBuffer has already been drained (index.ts:1505-1508) and spans `await this.ask("command_output", chunk)`, which waits for the user (or supersession). As the first ask normally stays open for the whole command run, any command that streams output for more than 30s without the user clicking emits a BUFFER_STUCK hang, even though the buffer is not stuck. The metric measures prompt/command duration, not a buffer stall.
defects.evidence: index.ts:1505-1507 `const chunk = outputBuffer.join("\n"); outputBuffer = []; outputBufferSize = 0`; 1511-1514 `bufferStuckTimer = setTimeout(() => { telemetryService.captureTerminalHang(TerminalHangStage.BUFFER_STUCK) ...}, BUFFER_STUCK_TIMEOUT_MS)`; 1518 `await this.ask("command_output", chunk)`; timer cleared only in finally when the ask settles.
defects.notes: Must say the BUFFER_STUCK timer covers the time spent waiting on the ask/user response (or a healthy long run), producing false stuck-buffer events.

defects.title: WAITING_FOR_COMPLETION hang is emitted for every command that legitimately runs longer than 60s
defects.statement: completionTimer (index.ts:1577-1582) fires `captureTerminalHang(WAITING_FOR_COMPLETION)` if 'completed' has not arrived 60s after the command started, with no notion of progress. Builds, test suites, installs and dev servers that are running normally (and producing output) are all counted as terminal hangs, so the hang metric is dominated by healthy long commands.
defects.evidence: index.ts:1575 `const COMPLETION_TIMEOUT_MS = 60000`; 1578-1581 `completionTimer = setTimeout(() => { if (!completed) { telemetryService.captureTerminalHang(TerminalHangStage.WAITING_FOR_COMPLETION) ...`; only cleared on 'completed' or after `await process`.
defects.notes: Must say the 60s completion timer flags normal long-running commands as hangs (elapsed time rather than lack of progress).

defects.title: Unguarded second getLatestTerminalOutput() call can reject and leave the command (and task) waiting forever
defects.statement: returnCurrentTerminalContents wraps getLatestTerminalOutput in try/catch (TerminalProcess.ts:30-40). The PR adds a second, unguarded `await getLatestTerminalOutput()` for telemetry (TerminalProcess.ts:198 in the empty-output shell-integration path, :229 in the no-shell-integration path). getLatestTerminalOutput reads/writes the clipboard via host RPC and runs terminal commands, all documented to throw (utils/env.ts readTextFromClipboard/writeTextToClipboard). If it rejects, run() (not awaited by TerminalManager.runCommand) aborts before emitting 'completed'/'continue'/'no_shell_integration'; the promise TerminalManager returns settles only on 'continue' or 'error' (TerminalManager.ts:181-188), so executeCommandTool's `await process` never resolves. A failure that was previously swallowed now hangs the task.
defects.evidence: TerminalProcess.ts:31-39 `try { const terminalSnapshot = await getLatestTerminalOutput() ... } catch (error) { console.error(...) }`; :198 and :229 `const terminalSnapshot = await getLatestTerminalOutput()` with no try; :216-217 / :237-239 emit completed/continue only afterwards; TerminalManager.ts:181-188 `new Promise((resolve, reject) => { process.once("continue", () => resolve()); process.once("error", ...) })`; utils/env.ts readTextFromClipboard `@throws Error if the operation fails`.
defects.notes: Must say the new second capture is not error-guarded so a rejection skips completed/continue and strands the command. Merely noting the call is duplicated/slow (D5) does not count.

defects.title: Telemetry re-runs the clipboard/select-all terminal capture and classifies a different snapshot than the one delivered
defects.statement: returnCurrentTerminalContents() already calls getLatestTerminalOutput(), which saves the clipboard, runs terminal selectAll/copySelection/clearSelection and restores the clipboard. Purely to choose a telemetry event, the PR calls getLatestTerminalOutput() again (TerminalProcess.ts:198 for empty shell-integration output; :229 for every command in a terminal without shell integration). That repeats the visible select-all and clipboard overwrite/restore and adds latency before 'completed'/'continue' are emitted, and the success/method flag is computed from a second, independent snapshot that can differ from the output actually emitted to the model. The first call's result should be returned and reused.

Asks for the multi-field update path to be timed too. Completeness of debug instrumentation, not a defect.

cline__cline@ca7f02b.pr_summary: Renames the task identifier used for telemetry and API-handler options from taskId to ulid: ApiHandlerOptions.taskId becomes ulid, providers (Cline X-Task-ID header, Gemini telemetry, LiteLLM session id, Vertex) and controller call sites pass task.ulid, BrowserSession.setTaskId becomes setUlid, TelemetryService methods drop the taskId parameter in favour of ulid (two unused capture methods deleted), captureOptionSelected is wired into the follow-up/plan handlers, and the proto conversion helpers map `ulid`.

browser-use__browser-use@0b21e50.pr_summary: Adds BrowserConfig.chrome_remote_debugging_port (int | None, default CHROME_DEBUG_PORT=9222) and uses it instead of the hard-coded 9222 when probing/connecting to a user-provided Chrome over CDP and when launching the built-in browser; the '--remote-debugging-port' flag moves out of CHROME_ARGS into a CHROME_DEBUGGING_ARG template. defects.title: chrome_remote_debugging_port is typed int | None but None is never handled: builtin launch crashes with TypeError and URLs become localhost:None
defects.statement: BrowserConfig declares `chrome_remote_debugging_port: int | None = CHROME_DEBUG_PORT` (browser.py:111), so pydantic accepts an explicit None (e.g. a user trying to disable the debugging port). No code path handles None: _setup_builtin_browser formats '--remote-debugging-port=None' (:277) and then calls `s.connect_ex(('localhost', self.config.chrome_remote_debugging_port))` (:291), which raises TypeError for a None port, so the browser never launches; _setup_user_provided_browser builds 'http://localhost:None/json/version' and passes '--remote-debugging-port=None' to Chrome (:202, :220, :255), so it can never connect.
defects.evidence: browser.py:111 `chrome_remote_debugging_port: int | None = CHROME_DEBUG_PORT`; :277 `CHROME_DEBUGGING_ARG % {'chrome_remote_debugging_port': self.config.chrome_remote_debugging_port}`; :291 `if s.connect_ex(('localhost', self.config.chrome_remote_debugging_port)) == 0:`; chrome.py:97 `CHROME_DEBUGGING_ARG = '--remote-debugging-port=%(chrome_remote_debugging_port)s'`. defects.notes: Must say that the Optional/None port is not handled (TypeError in connect_ex or a 'None' port in URLs/args), or that the field should be a plain int. R2 counts. Comments that only ask for range validation (out-of-range ints) without the None case are near-misses; C16 counts because it names None -> TypeError.

defects.statement: test_user_provided_browser_launch_on_custom_chrome_remote_debugging_port (tests/test_browser.py:160-233) monkeypatches requests.get (:173-180), but _setup_user_provided_browser probes with httpx.AsyncClient.get (browser.py:199-213, :238-247). The mock is dead: on a machine where nothing listens on 9223 the real pre-probe fails, the mocked create_subprocess_exec runs, then all ten real post-launch probes fail with ~1 s sleeps (≈10 s added to the suite) before the dummy connect_over_cdp succeeds; if anything answers 200 on 9223, the reuse branch is taken and create_subprocess_exec (which holds the only port-argument assertion) is never called, yet the test passes. Its DummyResponse returning 200 for the custom URL would, if it were effective, also route to the reuse branch — the test cannot verify the launch it documents.
defects.evidence: tests/test_browser.py:180 `monkeypatch.setattr(requests, 'get', dummy_get)`; browser.py:200-203 `async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client: response = await client.get(f'http://localhost:{self.config.chrome_remote_debugging_port}/json/version', timeout=2)`; :238-247 ten-attempt httpx loop with `await asyncio.sleep(1)`; the port assertion lives only inside dummy_create_subprocess_exec (:190-195) and nothing asserts it was called.
defects.notes: Must say the test patches requests.get while the code uses httpx (so the mock is ineffective / the test depends on the real port), or that the launch assertion may never run because nothing checks the subprocess mock was called. Generic 'add more tests' does not count.

defects.evidence: browser.py:84-85 `Also, makes it possible to launch new user provided chrome browser without closing already opened chrome instances, by providing non-default chrome debugging port.`; chrome.py:102 `# f'--user-data-dir={CHROME_PROFILE_PATH}',     # managed by playwright arg instead`; launch args at browser.py:217-227 contain no user-data-dir.

defects.title: thinking_budget hardcoded to -1: the caller's configured budget is ignored
defects.statement: ainvoke checks `if self.thinking_budget is not None` but then always sends `{'thinking_budget': -1}` (chat.py:201-203); the base sent `self.thinking_budget`. A caller who sets thinking_budget=0 to disable thinking, or a positive token cap, now silently gets dynamic (unbounded) thinking, increasing latency and token cost, and the public field no longer has any effect beyond None vs not-None.
defects.evidence: chat.py:202 `thinking_config_dict: types.ThinkingConfigDict = {'thinking_budget': -1}`; diff: `-{'thinking_budget': self.thinking_budget}` -> `+{'thinking_budget': -1}`.
defects.notes: Must say the configured thinking_budget value is ignored/overridden by the hardcoded -1. Comments only about the default changing to 0 and older models receiving a thinking config belong to D3.

defects.title: Retry/backoff removed on the false premise that the genai client retries
defects.statement: The 10-attempt retry loop with exponential backoff for rate-limit/5xx/connection errors was deleted and replaced by one `_make_api_call()` (chat.py:381-384) with the comment 'Let Google client handle retries internally'. get_client() builds genai.Client from only the user's params (chat.py:102-127) with no retry_options, and google-genai does not retry by default, so a transient 429/503 now surfaces immediately as ModelProviderError and counts toward the agent's failure limit.
defects.evidence: Diff removes `for attempt in range(10)`, `_is_retryable_error`, `await asyncio.sleep(delay)`; head 382-384 `# Let Google client handle retries internally ... return await _make_api_call()`; _get_client_params passes api_key/vertexai/credentials/project/location/http_options only.
defects.notes: Must say removing the retry loop drops resilience to rate limits/transient errors because the client is not configured to retry.

defects.title: Default thinking_budget=0 makes every request carry thinking_config, including non-thinking models
defects.statement: Changing the default from None to 0 (chat.py:78) makes the `is not None` guard (201) always true, so every default request now includes thinking_config (with -1), including requests to the listed Gemini 2.0 and Gemma models (chat.py:24-37) that do not support thinking; previously default requests sent no thinking config. Those models can reject the request with an invalid-argument error, breaking callers that never set the parameter (e.g. examples and tests using gemini-2.0-flash / -exp).
defects.evidence: diff `-thinking_budget: int | None = None` / `+thinking_budget: int | None = 0`; 201 `if self.thinking_budget is not None:`; VerifiedGeminiModels includes 'gemini-2.0-flash', 'gemma-3-27b-it' etc.; callers ChatGoogle(model='gemini-2.0-flash-exp') in examples/apps and browser_use/llm/tests.
defects.notes: Must say the new non-None default sends a thinking config on every request, including to models without thinking support. Saying only that the user's value is overridden by -1 is D1.

excluded.reason: Asks the native and fallback branches to share fence stripping/JSON parsing. Duplication refactor suggestion; both copies are identical today, no drift.

Says raw response text should not be logged on parse failures because it may contain sensitive data. It is a DEBUG-level log of the model's own output, consistent with the library's debug logging; no concrete leak beyond what debug logging is for.
Says the debug log of the first 200 response chars can echo private content into logs. Same as C2: debug-level diagnostic of model output, not a security defect.

Says asyncio.CancelledError derives from BaseException so the 504 cancellation branch under `except Exception` is unreachable. True but the only consequence is a dead diagnostic branch; cancellation still propagates correctly, so no behavioural defect.
Says the cancellation diagnostic branch cannot run because CancelledError bypasses `except Exception`. Same as C3: dead code with no functional consequence.
Asks to consolidate the inner log-and-rethrow handler into the outer one and to word parse failures differently from API failures. Logging/style suggestion, no defect.

electron__electron@c486457.pr_summary: Pure refactor: replaces the 'declare a local with its default, then dict.Get(key, &local)' pattern with gin_helper::Dictionary::ValueOrDefault(key, default) across WebContents (constructor, LoadURL, Print), ElectronBrowserContext display-media selection, the download save-dialog callback, the URL loader factory's statusCode, SimpleURLLoader options, the WebMouseWheelEvent converter and the macOS touch bar; adds an equivalent ValueOrDefault template to gin_helper::PersistentDictionary for the touch bar code.

excluded.reason: Says scaleFactor, pagesPerSheet, copies and custom margins are not range-validated and ValueOrDefault passes negative/zero values to Chromium. Pre-existing: the old code (`int scale_factor = 100; options.Get("scaleFactor", &scale_factor);`) passed the same unvalidated values; ValueOrDefault returns exactly what Get produced, so the refactor is behaviour-preserving.
Prefers explicit types over `auto` for device_name/duplex_mode. Style preference; the default argument (std::u16string{}, DuplexMode::kSimplex) fixes the deduced type.

Prefers an explicit FetchCacheMode type and asks whether ValueOrDefault silently falls back on a wrong-typed value. Style; the wrong-type fallback is identical to the old opts.Get() into a pre-initialised default.
Suggests inlining the canScroll ValueOrDefault call instead of a local. Style; `!ValueOrDefault("canScroll", true)` is logically equal to the old `Get(...) && !can_scroll`.

Says PersistentDictionary::ValueOrDefault requires default-constructible T, copies default_value, and misbehaves for pointer T. Hypothetical API concerns: it mirrors the existing gin_helper::Dictionary::ValueOrDefault and every call site uses small value types (bool/int).
Asks the new helper's comment to say the default also applies when conversion fails. Documentation nit; behaviour matches the old Get-with-default pattern and the sibling Dictionary helper's comment.

Says persistent_dictionary.h uses std::string_view without including <string_view> (plus comment wording and duplication questions). Include-hygiene/doc nits; the header compiles via existing includes and no build break is shown.
Says ValueOrDefault is duplicated between PersistentDictionary and Dictionary and may drift. Two identical 4-line helpers on different classes; maintainability suggestion without existing drift.

Says the touch-bar slider now reads maxValue/value after assigning minValue, so a JS getter with side effects could observe a different order. Contrived: settings are plain option objects from the TouchBar JS wrapper; no realistic path depends on getter ordering.
Asks to name the selected color model instead of inlining the ternary in settings.Set. Readability preference, no defect.

electron__electron@6084595.pr_summary: Reworks lifetime management of ClearDataTask / ClearDataOperation in shell/browser/api/electron_api_session.cc (session.clearData). ClearDataTask is now a raw-new'd gin_helper::CleanedUpAtExit that owns its operations in a std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ClearDataOperation>> and deletes itself at the end of OnTaskFinished; operations hold a raw_ptr back to the task and are erased from the vector when they report completion via OnOperationFinished(operation, failed_types). At process exit CleanedUpAtExit::DoCleanup deletes any still-pending task (and with it its operations) before the isolate and browser contexts are torn down.

defects.title: New class comment says ClearDataTask's lifetime is managed through CleanedUpAtExit, but it actually deletes itself on completion
defects.statement: The rewritten header comment (electron_api_session.cc:202-203) states the type 'manages its own lifetime through gin_helper::CleanedUpAtExit, ensuring it's destroyed before the node environment shuts down'. The normal destruction path is the `delete this` at the end of OnTaskFinished (:358); CleanedUpAtExit only deletes tasks still pending at shutdown (DoCleanup, called from JavascriptEnvironment::DestroyMicrotasksRunner). The PR removed the accurate sentence ('deleting itself once the task finishes completely') and replaced it with one that describes only the exit path, so a reader is misled about who frees the object.
defects.evidence: head :202 `// This type manages its own lifetime through gin_helper::CleanedUpAtExit,` ; :358 `delete this;` in OnTaskFinished; base comment was `This type manages its own lifetime, deleting itself once the task finishes completely.` cleaned_up_at_exit.cc: DoCleanup deletes remaining registrants only at teardown.
defects.notes: Must say the new ClearDataTask comment is inaccurate/incomplete because the task self-deletes on completion (CleanedUpAtExit only covers shutdown). Suggestions to replace `delete this` with CleanedUpAtExit (R6) do not count.

excluded.reason: Says allocating the task with a raw `new` without smart-pointer ownership may leak if an exception occurs. Chromium/Electron builds without exceptions; nothing between `new ClearDataTask` (:215) and the final OnOperationFinished can throw, and the task is deliberately self-owned (deleted in OnTaskFinished, or by CleanedUpAtExit at exit).

Suggests replacing the OnOperationFinished(nullptr, std::nullopt) bookkeeping call with a dedicated method. Style suggestion; OnOperationFinished guards the nullptr with `if (operation)` (:321) and the fallback call is documented.

Claims erasing the operation's unique_ptr inside OnOperationFinished is a use-after-free because the call originates from that operation's OnBrowsingDataRemoverDone. Erasing the unique_ptr inside OnBrowsingDataRemoverDone is equivalent to the base `delete this`: after task_->OnOperationFinished(this, ...) returns, OnBrowsingDataRemoverDone touches no members and simply returns. The lambda only compares the pointer before destruction. No use-after-free.

Says the remove_if erase in OnOperationFinished is O(n) per completion and O(n^2) overall. A task starts at most two operations (cookies + the rest), so the vector has <=2 elements; the O(n) erase is irrelevant.

Suggests using the CleanedUpAtExit mechanism instead of `delete this` in OnTaskFinished. CleanedUpAtExit only deletes objects at isolate teardown; ~CleanedUpAtExit erases the object from the doomed list, so `delete this` on completion is the correct and necessary normal path.

Says the operation must be pushed into operations_ before Start because a synchronous completion leaves a stale registered observer that could be notified again and decrement the count twice. Even if RemoveWithFilterAndReply ever replied synchronously, the only effect is that the finished ClearDataOperation stays in operations_ until the task finishes and ~ClearDataTask clears the vector (electron_api_session.cc:296): it is still freed. operations_running_ is decremented exactly once per operation (the static Run holds its own count, so the task cannot be deleted mid-Run), and BrowsingDataRemover delivers OnBrowsingDataRemoverDone only to the observer passed for that specific removal task, so a completed operation receives no further notification. No incorrect count, leak or crash results.

Says an operation should be tracked before calling Start since a synchronous reply would leave the completed observer in operations_ until the task's other operations finish. Even if RemoveWithFilterAndReply ever replied synchronously, the only effect is that the finished ClearDataOperation stays in operations_ until the task finishes and ~ClearDataTask clears the vector (electron_api_session.cc:296): it is still freed. operations_running_ is decremented exactly once per operation (the static Run holds its own count, so the task cannot be deleted mid-Run), and BrowsingDataRemover delivers OnBrowsingDataRemoverDone only to the observer passed for that specific removal task, so a completed operation receives no further notification. No incorrect count, leak or crash results.

Says that if RemoveWithFilterAndReply completes synchronously the operation is stored after OnOperationFinished already ran and cannot be erased. Even if RemoveWithFilterAndReply ever replied synchronously, the only effect is that the finished ClearDataOperation stays in operations_ until the task finishes and ~ClearDataTask clears the vector (electron_api_session.cc:296): it is still freed. operations_running_ is decremented exactly once per operation (the static Run holds its own count, so the task cannot be deleted mid-Run), and BrowsingDataRemover delivers OnBrowsingDataRemoverDone only to the observer passed for that specific removal task, so a completed operation receives no further notification. No incorrect count, leak or crash results.
Asks for a regression test that tears down the environment while session.clearData() is pending. A test request, not a defect.
Says the explicit `~ClearDataTask() { operations_.clear(); }` is redundant with the vector's own destruction. Style/cleanup only; behaviour is identical.
Suggests std::erase_if instead of the erase/remove_if idiom. Style preference, no behavioural difference.

electron__electron@100ad24.pr_summary: Fixes Linux file-dialog filters in GetFilterInfo (shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_linux.cc). Previously a description override was pushed for every filter but no extension group was pushed for a '*' filter, so labels after a '*' filter were shifted onto the wrong extensions. The PR pushes the description override only for non-wildcard filters; a '*' filter only sets include_all_files.

defects.title: Mis-indented edited block is not clang-format clean and fails Electron's C++ lint step
defects.statement: In GetFilterInfo the lambda continuation line uses a 6-space indent (file_dialog_linux.cc:48; Chromium style needs the 4-space continuation, 8 columns here, as before the PR) and `if (has_all_files_wildcard) {` is indented 6 spaces instead of 4 (line 50), so it no longer lines up with its own `} else {` (line 52). Electron's lint job (pipeline-electron-lint.yml `node script/yarn lint` -> script/lint.js) runs script/run-clang-format.py over every shell/**/*.cc file without --fix and fails on any formatting diff, so the PR turns the lint check red; the misleading indentation also obscures the if/else structure.
defects.evidence: head file_dialog_linux.cc:47-52 `    const bool has_all_files_wildcard = std::ranges::any_of(` / `      extension_group, [](const auto& ext) { return ext == "*"; });` / (blank) / `      if (has_all_files_wildcard) {` / `      file_type_info.include_all_files = true;` / `    } else {`. script/lint.js:102-110 cpp linter roots ['shell'], *.cc, `spawnAndCheckExitCode('python3', ['script/run-clang-format.py', ...clangFormatFlags, ...chunk])`; .github/workflows/pipeline-electron-lint.yml:75 `node script/yarn lint`.
defects.notes: Counts if the comment flags the wrong indentation of the `if` or of the any_of continuation line, whether it cites clang-format/lint or only readability. Comments only about the dropped label for the '*' filter do not count.

excluded.reason: Asks for a regression test with an All Files ('*') filter before a named filter. Test request, not a defect.

electron__electron@2cc5656.pr_summary: Ports Chromium's Bluetooth-adapter handling into Electron's SerialChooserController: device enumeration is posted as a task (GetDevices); when every filter targets a Bluetooth service class (and extra service class ids are allowed), the controller first acquires and observes the BluetoothAdapter, and re-enumerates ports on AdapterPoweredChanged(powered=true). OnGetDevices now clears ports_ before refilling, and the class becomes a public BluetoothAdapter::Observer.

defects.title: Adapter power-on re-runs OnGetDevices, re-emitting select-serial-port for an already-emitted (or already-resolved) request
defects.statement: AdapterPoweredChanged(powered=true) (serial_chooser_controller.cc:165-170) calls GetDevices -> OnGetDevices (221-244), which unconditionally clears/replaces ports_ and emits 'select-serial-port' again with a fresh OnDeviceChosen callback, with no check that this is the first enumeration or that callback_ is still pending. Chromium's controller only refreshes its own chooser list here; Electron's event-based API was not adapted. While a request is pending the app receives a second select-serial-port for the same requestPort() (two pickers / competing callbacks), and the list replacement emits no serial-port-added/removed for the differences. The controller stays in ElectronSerialDelegate's map (only replaced on the next RunChooser, electron_serial_delegate.cc:34-40) and stays an adapter observer after its callback ran, so later power toggles re-emit the event for a finished request, and an app handler that picks a port reaches OnDeviceChosen, which calls chooser_context_->GrantPortPermission (line 213) with no pending request.
defects.evidence: cc:167-168 `if (powered) { GetDevices(); }`; cc:236-239 `prevent_default = session->Emit("select-serial-port", ports_, web_contents_.get(), base::BindRepeating(&SerialChooserController::OnDeviceChosen, ...))` with no guard; cc:213 `chooser_context_->GrantPortPermission(origin_, *it->get(), rfh);`; cc:273 `adapter_observation_.Observe(adapter_.get());` never reset when the callback runs.
defects.notes: Must say the Bluetooth power-on refresh re-enters OnGetDevices and re-emits select-serial-port (duplicate selection event / second prompt), or that the refresh silently replaces the port list without added/removed events for an open picker. Generic observer-lifetime or 'refresh on power-off too' (R3) remarks do not count.

excluded.reason: Claims there is no error handling if Bluetooth adapter retrieval fails. BluetoothAdapterFactory::GetAdapter always calls back with an adapter (OnGetAdapter CHECKs it, as upstream Chromium does); no failure path exists to handle.

Claims GetDevices dereferences chooser_context_ without a null check and may run after context shutdown. chooser_context_ is the browser context's keyed service, alive for the BrowserContext's lifetime; OnDeviceChosen dereferences it the same way and upstream Chromium's GetDevices is identical. No concrete reachable trigger.

Claims the posted GetDevices task or adapter callback can dereference chooser_context_ after context shutdown. Same as R2: only reachable during browser-context teardown, pre-existing pattern mirrored from upstream; speculative.

Claims the chooser keeps stale Bluetooth ports when the adapter powers off because only power-on refreshes. On power-off the Bluetooth ports are removed via the port manager's OnPortRemoved notifications (cc:185-194), matching upstream; not a defect.
Suggests passing base::OnceClosure by rvalue reference to avoid copies. OnceClosure is move-only and passing by value is Chromium style; no copy occurs.
Generic reminder to ensure initialization/cleanup of the adapter_ scoped_refptr. adapter_ is released automatically and adapter_observation_ is declared after it so it unobserves first; no defect.
Suggests marking IsWirelessSerialPortOnly() const. Const-correctness style; no behaviour change.
Suggests marking IsWirelessSerialPortOnly const in the header. Same style preference as R6.

Claims the promised Bluetooth status hints never reach the app because adapter state is not exposed via select-serial-port. Feature request: this PR ports upstream's internal refresh behaviour and Electron has no built-in chooser UI; not a defect in the change.
Asks which Bluetooth status changes should be exposed (initial state, power-off). Clarification / feature request, not a defect.

Claims IsWirelessSerialPortOnly returns false when allowed_bluetooth_service_class_ids_ is empty even though SPP is allowed by default, skipping adapter observation. This early return is copied verbatim from upstream Chromium's IsWirelessSerialPortOnly, and the only consequence is no power-on refresh for that request (the pre-PR behaviour); not a regression.
Claims Bluetooth-only (SPP) requests with an empty allowed-ID list skip the adapter observation. Same as C2: mirrors upstream exactly and only means no extra refresh, as before the PR.
Claims wireless-only detection ignores the default-allowed Serial Port Profile. Same as C2/C12: upstream behaviour, no regression.

Claims ports_.clear() in OnGetDevices drops a port announced by OnPortAdded while GetDevices was pending if the snapshot predates it. Requires a device to be plugged in during the enumeration window with cross-pipe reordering; before the PR the same race produced a duplicate entry instead. Contrived timing race, not a demonstrated defect.
Claims the posted-task enumeration lets OnPortAdded append a port that the later snapshot then clears. Same narrow race as C3; contrived.
Asks for a regression test for the Bluetooth power refresh path. Test request, not a defect.
Suggests OnGetAdapter call GetDevices directly instead of taking a one-use closure. Simplification nit; mirrors upstream structure.

nodejs__node@e8b6c18.pr_summary: Test-only change: drops the TODO about custom-eval tests from lib/repl.js and replaces test/parallel/test-repl-eval.js with a node:test based test/parallel/test-repl-custom-eval.js covering custom eval output and errors, the context passed to eval (custom, global with useGlobal, non-global otherwise), preservation of the original input (issue 9743), and previews being off by default for custom evals but on with preview: true.

defects.title: Preview test assumes previews are available; fails under TERM=dumb and on --without-inspector builds
defects.statement: The 'does show previews if `preview` is set to `true`' test (test/parallel/test-repl-custom-eval.js:95-109) asserts the `// 'Hello custom eval World!'` preview line, but setupPreview returns no-op preview handlers when process.env.TERM === 'dumb' (lib/internal/repl/utils.js:141-144) and showPreview returns immediately when !process.features.inspector (utils.js:363-366). The new file neither resets TERM nor calls common.skipIfInspectorDisabled(), so this test fails in those supported test configurations even though custom eval works; the existing preview suites guard exactly these (test-repl-preview.js:10-13, test-repl-preview-without-inspector.js).
defects.evidence: utils.js:141-144 `if (process.env.TERM === 'dumb' || !active) { return { showPreview() {}, clearPreview() {} }; }`; utils.js:365 `if (inputPreview !== null || !repl.isCompletionEnabled || !process.features.inspector) { return; }`; test-repl-preview.js: `common.skipIfInspectorDisabled();` and `process.env.TERM = '';`; many repl tests skip on TERM=dumb. New test asserts `new RegExp(`${escapedInput}\n// 'Hello custom eval World!'`)` with no such guard.
defects.notes: Must say the preview assertion fails when previews are unavailable (TERM=dumb and/or no inspector) and needs a skip/guard. Comments only about eval() usage or global cleanup do not count.

excluded.reason: Claim: the suite should run with concurrency: true and avoid the shared global.foo to prevent races. node:test runs the its of a describe sequentially by default, so the shared global cannot race; enabling concurrency is a preference, not a defect.
Claim: getReplOutput is defined after its use and should be moved above the tests. A hoisted function declaration is valid and common in Node tests; style only.

Claim: the preview tests call JavaScript eval() on REPL input, a code-injection risk; return a fixed string instead. The input is a hard-coded literal in a test file; there is no untrusted input and no behavioural defect.

Claim: if the global-context assertion fails, global.foo is not deleted, polluting later tests; use try/finally. Cleanup only matters after a test has already failed; test-hygiene suggestion, not a defect.
