sveltejs__svelte@44bec4c.pr_summary: Adds a `maybe_runes` flag to ComponentAnalysis — true for non-runes components not compiled with runes:false that reference neither $$props/$$restProps nor export a `let` — and makes client build_expression skip the legacy coarse-grained dependency wrapper for them, so templates reading runes state from external .svelte.js modules update fine-grained. Adds four runtime-runes test samples and a changeset.

defects.title: `Map.keys().some()` needs Iterator helpers: compiling any non-runes component throws on Node 18/20 (supported, and in CI)
defects.statement: analyze_component (packages/svelte/src/compiler/phases/2-analyze/index.js:441) evaluates `module.scope.references.keys().some(...)` whenever `!runes && options.runes !== false`. Map.prototype.keys() returns an iterator; Iterator.prototype.some only exists from Node 22 (V8 12.x). packages/svelte/package.json declares engines node >=18 and CI runs `pnpm test` on Node 18 (three OSes) and 20. On those runtimes every compile of an ordinary legacy/undecided component throws `TypeError: ...keys(...).some is not a function` — the runtime-legacy suite fails, and users on Node 18/20 (or older browsers running the compiler) cannot compile legacy components. Line 409 in the same function uses the portable `Array.from(module.scope.references.keys()).some(is_rune)`.
defects.evidence: index.js:441 `!module.scope.references.keys().some((name) => ['$$props', '$$restProps'].includes(name)) &&`; index.js:409 `const runes = options.runes ?? Array.from(module.scope.references.keys()).some(is_rune);`; package.json `"engines": { "node": ">=18" }`; .github/workflows/ci.yml matrix node-version 18 (windows/macOS/ubuntu), 20, 22, 24.
defects.notes: Must say `.some` is called on a Map iterator, which is unavailable on supported Node versions / needs Array.from — i.e. compilation throws. Generic remarks about the condition's logic do not count.

defects.title: Legacy-prop detection misses `export var` / `var x; export { x }` (a second copy of the prop rule that already drifted), so such legacy components lose coarse-grained template tracking
defects.statement: maybe_runes (index.js:442-452) treats a component as explicitly legacy only if it exports a `let` declaration or an export specifier whose binding's declaration_kind is 'let'. The existing export analysis (index.js:514-526 marks every non-const exported VariableDeclaration as bindable_prop; 538-541 accepts declaration_kind 'var' or 'let') also makes `var` exports props. A legacy component whose props are `var`-declared therefore gets maybe_runes=true and build_expression (shared/utils.js:373) skips the legacy wrapper that `$.deep_read_state`s bindable props, so template calls/member expressions over such props stop updating when the parent mutates them in place. The prop classification now lives in two independent scans that already disagree.
defects.evidence: index.js:447 `node.declaration.kind === 'let'` and 451 `?.declaration_kind === 'let'` vs 522-526 (non-const → `binding.kind = 'bindable_prop'`) and 538-541 `(binding.declaration_kind === 'var' || binding.declaration_kind === 'let')`; utils.js:390-398 deep_read_state for bindable_prop, skipped when maybe_runes.
defects.notes: Must name `var`-declared exported props (export var / var + export {}) as a missed legacy signal, or say the maybe_runes export scan duplicates/diverges from the existing prop classification. A generic 'other legacy signals such as $: are missed' (R1) does not count.

defects.title: The new regression samples run under runtime-runes' forced `runes: true`, so they never evaluate maybe_runes and pass without the fix
defects.statement: All four samples live in tests/runtime-runes, whose suite is `runtime_suite(true)` (tests/runtime-runes/test.ts:4); common_setup (tests/runtime-legacy/shared.ts:~150-162) spreads config.compileOptions and then sets `runes` last, so every sample compiles with runes: true and `!runes` short-circuits maybe_runes (index.js:437-438). The legacy-runes-ambiguous sample therefore passes with the compiler change reverted, and the export-let sample asserts '1' — the forced-runes result — whereas under automatic mode its `export { x }` of a `let` makes maybe_runes false and the legacy untrack wrapper applies. The PR's regression coverage is vacuous and would mask a broken or reverted fix.
defects.evidence: tests/runtime-runes/test.ts `const { test, run } = runtime_suite(true);`; shared.ts common_setup `const compileOptions = { ..., ...config.compileOptions, immutable: ..., accessors: ..., runes }`; index.js:437 `maybe_runes: !runes && ...`.
defects.notes: Must say the new tests run with runes forced on (runtime-runes suite) so they never reach the maybe_runes path / pass without the fix (or that the export-let fixture's expectation reflects forced-runes behaviour). A mere 'add more tests' request, or the btn?.click optional-chaining nit (C1), does not count.

excluded.reason: Claims maybe_runes should also exclude components with `$:` reactive statements or they are misclassified. `$:` statements do not rely on the template's coarse-grained wrapper — fine-grained template tracking still reads every signal the expression touches — and the comment names no concrete breakage.

Claims build_expression does not account for maybe_runes and should check both flags. Wrong: the changed line is exactly `if (context.state.analysis.runes || context.state.analysis.maybe_runes)` (utils.js:373).
Claims `var getter` should be `let`. Pre-existing line untouched by the PR; style.
Claims the new maybe_runes property lacks a JSDoc comment. Documentation request; not a defect.
Claims making maybe_runes a required ComponentAnalysis field may break producers that do not set it. The only producer, analyze_component, sets it; no type error or consumer breakage.
Claims the explicit-false test can pass without clicking because of `btn?.click()`. The button exists in main.svelte; a robustness nit on a test assertion, not a defect.
Claims the comment 'fallback to the runic behavior' overstates what maybe_runes does. Comment wording nit; the comment describes the intent and misleads no caller.
Claims the comment should say maybe_runes only selects fine-grained template tracking rather than runes mode. Same wording nit as C2.

alibaba__spring-ai-alibaba@3555a95.pr_summary: Refactors the alitranslate tool-calling starter onto the shared tool-calling-common module: AliTranslateProperties now extends CommonToolCallProperties (access key id/secret mapped to apiKey/secretKey, defaults read from ACCESS_KEY_ID/ACCESS_KEY_SECRET env vars, old setters deprecated), the prefix comes from CommonToolCallConstants, and the alimt SDK is bumped to 1.0.3. AliTranslateService stops closing the shared client after every call (it becomes Closeable and the bean gets destroyMethod=close), reads the typed response body instead of round-tripping through Gson, logs and returns null on failure instead of throwing, and adds an optional sourceLanguage request field replacing the hard-coded 'zh'.

defects.title: Omitting the optional sourceLanguage makes apply() return null instead of defaulting to zh
defects.statement: The new Request component sourceLanguage is declared optional (@JsonProperty(required = false)) and described to the model as 'default is zh' (AliTranslateService.java:141-142), but apply() now returns null whenever sourceLanguage is blank (AliTranslateService.java:84-87). Tool-call JSON is deserialised through the record's canonical 3-arg constructor, so an omitted field is null; the defaults exist only in the 1-arg convenience constructor (:147-149), which that path does not use. Before the PR the source language was hard-coded to 'zh', so a call with only text+targetLanguage worked; now a model that follows the schema and omits the optional parameter gets a null result and the tool silently stops translating.
defects.evidence: AliTranslateService.java:84-86 `if (request == null || !StringUtils.hasText(request.text) || !StringUtils.hasText(request.sourceLanguage) || !StringUtils.hasText(request.targetLanguage)) { return null; }`; :141-142 `@JsonProperty(required = false, value = "sourceLanguage") @JsonPropertyDescription("Source language of the text, default is zh") String sourceLanguage`; base used `.sourceLanguage(LANGUAGE_CODE)` with LANGUAGE_CODE = "zh".
defects.notes: Must say an omitted optional sourceLanguage (or languages generally) is not defaulted and the request returns null, contradicting required=false / the documented default.

defects.title: Adding the sourceLanguage record component removes the public two-argument Request(text, targetLanguage) constructor
defects.statement: AliTranslateService.Request is a public record; before the PR its canonical constructor was Request(String text, String targetLanguage). Inserting sourceLanguage as the middle component (AliTranslateService.java:137-145) replaces it with a 3-arg canonical constructor, and the only other constructor takes just text (:147-149). Any external Java caller doing `new AliTranslateService.Request(text, "fr")` no longer compiles after upgrading the starter.
defects.evidence: Base: `public record Request(String text, String targetLanguage) { public Request(String text) { this(text, "en"); } }`; head :137-149 `public record Request(String text, String sourceLanguage, String targetLanguage) { public Request(String text) { this(text, LANGUAGE_CODE_ZH, LANGUAGE_CODE_EN); } }`.
defects.notes: Must point out that the previous public 2-arg Request constructor is gone, breaking source compatibility for callers.

defects.title: InterruptedException from response.get() is swallowed without restoring the interrupt flag
defects.statement: apply() now catches every Exception from response.get() and returns null after logging (AliTranslateService.java:99-107). When the calling thread is interrupted, InterruptedException is caught here and the interrupt status (cleared by the throw) is not restored, so cancellation/shutdown of the caller is silently lost; before the PR the exception propagated (wrapped in RuntimeException) and aborted the call.
defects.evidence: AliTranslateService.java:99-107 `try { TranslateGeneralResponse resp = response.get(); ... } catch (Exception e) { logger.error("Failed to invoke alitranslate caused by:{}", e.getMessage()); return null; }` — no Thread.currentThread().interrupt().
defects.notes: Must mention the lost interrupt status. Merely objecting that failures now return null instead of throwing is a design complaint and does not count.

excluded.reason: Asks to drop the 'Function' suffix from the aliTranslateFunction bean method name. Naming preference on a name this PR does not change.

Says the ACCESS_KEY_ID/ACCESS_KEY_SECRET env var names should be service-prefixed and set via System.getenv directly. Naming/design preference; setPropertiesFromEnv only supplies a default when nothing is configured and explicit properties override it, so no concrete misbehaviour.

Asks that credentials be managed via CommonToolCallProperties apiKey/secretKey instead of local fields. The PR already does exactly this (getAccessKeyId/getAccessKeySecret delegate to getApiKey/getSecretKey; old setters kept as deprecated).

Claims the new tool-calling-common dependency uses a SNAPSHOT version via ${revision}. It is a sibling module of the same reactor versioned with the project's own ${revision}, as every other internal dependency is; not a defect.
Asks to validate response fields without throwing exceptions just to be caught and logged. Style preference; behaviour is correct.
Suggests reusing CommonToolCallUtils.handleServiceError instead of the local catch. Refactoring preference; no drift with a concrete consequence.
Suggests using CommonToolCallUtils.isInvalidateRequestParams for request validation. Refactoring preference; the defaulting bug itself is D1.
Asks to include resp.getStatusCode() in the error message. Diagnostic nicety, not a defect.
Asks for regression tests for source-language propagation and defaults. Test-coverage request.

Claims SDK/upstream failures now return null, indistinguishable from invalid requests, and logging getMessage() loses the cause. Returning null on failure is the PR's deliberate 'optimize exception handling' design for a tool function (the model receives an empty result); a design objection, not a defect.
Claims callers cannot distinguish an upstream failure (null) from an invalid request (null). Same deliberate design change as C10; not a defect.
Asks to log the exception object instead of only getMessage(). Logging-quality suggestion; ExecutionException's message already carries the cause's description.

Notes that client.translateGeneral(...) runs outside the try, so a synchronous SDK exception still propagates. The call was outside the try before the PR as well; not made worse, and the SDK returns failures through the future.

google-gemini__gemini-cli@77ea28a.pr_summary: Adds MCP prompt support: core mcp-client discovers each server's prompts via prompts/list during connectAndDiscover, stores them in a module map (getMCPServerPrompts), adds invokeMcpPrompt (prompts/get), and drops the 'No enabled tools found' error from discoverTools. The CLI's new promptCommands.ts turns every discovered prompt into a slash command (with a help subcommand, --key=value argument parsing and completion) that reconnects to the server, invokes the prompt and submits the first message's text to Gemini; BuiltinCommandLoader registers them. /mcp now lists prompts and prompt counts alongside tools.

defects.title: Prompt text is JSON.stringify'd before submission, so Gemini receives a quoted, escaped string literal instead of the prompt
defects.statement: The prompt action returns `{ type: 'submit_prompt', content: JSON.stringify(result.messages[0].content.text) }` (promptCommands.ts:144-147). content.text is already a string; JSON.stringify wraps it in double quotes and escapes newlines, quotes and backslashes, so every invoked MCP prompt is sent to the model as e.g. `"Review this code:\n..."` — literal surrounding quotes and `\n` sequences instead of line breaks. This is on the only success path of the feature.
defects.evidence: promptCommands.ts:146 `content: JSON.stringify(result.messages[0].content.text),`; line 135 already requires `.text` to be truthy (a string per MCP TextContent).
defects.notes: Must identify that JSON.stringify on the already-string text wraps/escapes it (quotes, \n) in the submitted prompt.

defects.title: MCP prompt slash commands are named by bare prompt name and appended after built-ins, so they silently override built-in commands and each other
defects.statement: createPromptCommands names each command `${prompt.name}` (promptCommands.ts:28) and BuiltinCommandLoader appends them after all built-ins (BuiltinCommandLoader.ts:70). CommandService.create de-duplicates with a Map where the last command with a given name wins (CommandService.ts: `commandMap.set(cmd.name, cmd)`). So an MCP server exposing a prompt called e.g. `help`, `clear`, `quit`, `memory` or `mcp` replaces that built-in command, and when two servers expose the same prompt name only the later one is reachable. The PR description claims collisions are handled by appending the server name, but no such code exists.
defects.evidence: promptCommands.ts:28 `const commandName = `${prompt.name}`;`; BuiltinCommandLoader.ts:70 `...createPromptCommands(this.config),` after `toolsCommand`; CommandService.create: `for (const cmd of allCommands) { commandMap.set(cmd.name, cmd); }` ('The last one found with a given name wins').
defects.notes: Count a comment that prompt command names can collide with built-in commands or across MCP servers (no namespacing / no conflict handling). Generic 'naming' remarks without the collision consequence do not count.

defects.title: /mcp no longer shows the '/mcp auth <server>' hint for a disconnected OAuth server that has no tools and no prompts
defects.statement: The listing's footer was restructured (mcpCommand.ts:270-281). When serverTools and serverPrompts are both empty it prints only '  No tools or prompts available' and never checks `status === DISCONNECTED && needsAuthHint`. That is exactly the state of an unauthenticated OAuth server (it fails to connect, so it has no tools or prompts), which in the base code printed 'No tools available (type: "/mcp auth <server>" to authenticate this server)'. The auth hint is now shown only when there are tools, or prompts but no tools.
defects.evidence: mcpCommand.ts:270-271 `if (serverTools.length === 0 && serverPrompts.length === 0) { message += '  No tools or prompts available\n'; } else if (serverTools.length === 0) { ... needsAuthHint ... }`; base mcpCommand.ts:225-229 printed the hint whenever tools were empty and the server was disconnected with needsAuthHint.
defects.notes: Must name the both-empty case (no tools and no prompts) losing the auth hint. R5's claim (hint missing when there are only prompts) is wrong — that case still shows the hint — and does not count.

defects.title: Prompt-only MCP servers (no tools capability) still fail discovery: tools/list errors, the client is closed and the server is marked DISCONNECTED while its prompts stay registered
defects.statement: connectAndDiscover calls discoverPrompts and then discoverTools (mcp-client.ts:424-432). discoverTools calls mcpToTool(mcpClient).tool(), i.e. tools/list, and rethrows any error as 'Error discovering tools' (mcp-client.ts:465-492). A server that only offers prompts answers tools/list with 'Method not found', so the catch at 434-437 closes the client and the outer catch logs 'Error connecting to MCP server' and sets DISCONNECTED — yet mcpServerPromptsInternal keeps the prompts just stored, so /mcp shows a red Disconnected server listing prompts and an error on every startup. The PR removed the 'No enabled tools found' throw to support prompt-only servers but did not tolerate a missing tools capability, so that support is incomplete.
defects.evidence: mcp-client.ts:424 `await discoverPrompts(mcpServerName, mcpClient);` 426 `const tools = await discoverTools(...)`; 434-437 `} catch (error) { mcpClient.close(); throw error; }`; discoverTools 490-492 `} catch (error) { throw new Error(`Error discovering tools: ${error}`); }` — no Method-not-found tolerance, unlike discoverPrompts (513-527).
defects.notes: Must say a server without tools (tools/list unsupported) still errors/disconnects even though prompts were discovered; mentioning only the removed 'No enabled tools' check without this consequence is a near-miss.

defects.title: mcp-client JSDoc describes behaviour the code does not have: 'throws if no enabled tools', 'cleans up if no tools found', and discoverPrompts 'logs their names'
defects.statement: The PR removed the `if (discoveredTools.length === 0) throw Error('No enabled tools found')` check, so a server with zero enabled tools now stays connected with its client open. The JSDoc of discoverTools (mcp-client.ts:457) and of connectAndDiscover (mcp-client.ts:380-382, '...and cleaning up resources if no tools are found') still describe the removed behaviour. The new discoverPrompts JSDoc (mcp-client.ts:496-498) likewise says it 'retrieves prompt declarations from the client and logs their names', but it never logs them; it caches them in mcpServerPromptsInternal (line 514).
defects.evidence: mcp-client.ts:457 ` * @throws An error if no enabled tools are found or if the server provides invalid function declarations.`; 382 ` * and cleaning up resources if no tools are found.`; the throw was deleted in this diff (base ~462-464).
defects.notes: Count a comment pointing out any of the inaccurate JSDoc: discoverTools '@throws if no enabled tools', connectAndDiscover 'cleaning up resources if no tools are found', or discoverPrompts 'logs their names' (it caches, never logs).

defects.title: Invoking a prompt submits only the first message's text; multi-message results are truncated and a non-text first message is rejected
defects.statement: The action checks `result.messages?.[0]?.content?.text` and submits only `result.messages[0].content.text` (promptCommands.ts:135-147). MCP prompts/get returns an array of messages (user/assistant turns, text/image/resource content); every message after the first is silently dropped, and a valid prompt whose first message is an image/resource (with text later) is rejected as 'empty or invalid prompt response'.
defects.evidence: promptCommands.ts:135 `if (!result.messages?.[0]?.content?.text) {` ... 146 `content: JSON.stringify(result.messages[0].content.text)`; GetPromptResultSchema has `messages: z.array(PromptMessageSchema)`.
defects.notes: Must say that messages beyond the first are dropped (or non-text first message rejected). A pure 'check content.type' null-safety remark (R13) does not count: the optional chain already guards the access.

defects.title: Prompt discovery reads only the first page of prompts/list and ignores nextCursor
defects.statement: discoverPrompts sends one `prompts/list` request with empty params and caches `response.prompts` (mcp-client.ts:508-514). ListPromptsResult is paginated (`nextCursor`); on a server that paginates, every prompt after the first page never appears in /mcp and never becomes a slash command.
defects.evidence: mcp-client.ts:508-514 `mcpClient.request({ method: 'prompts/list', params: {} }, ListPromptsResultSchema); const prompts = response.prompts; mcpServerPromptsInternal.set(...)`; no cursor loop.
defects.notes: Must mention pagination / nextCursor being ignored. R20 (normalise undefined prompts to []) does not count.

defects.title: Prompt slash commands are snapshotted once at command load; prompts discovered by /mcp refresh or /mcp auth never become commands
defects.statement: BuiltinCommandLoader calls createPromptCommands(this.config) (BuiltinCommandLoader.ts:70), which reads the prompt cache at that moment. slashCommandProcessor rebuilds commands only when `config` changes (useEffect deps `[config]`). `/mcp auth` and `/mcp refresh` re-run discovery (mcpCommand.ts ~403-409, 503) without changing config, so prompts of a server that only connects after OAuth or refresh are listed by /mcp but are never invocable as slash commands for the session (and removed prompts stay registered).
defects.evidence: BuiltinCommandLoader.ts:70 `...createPromptCommands(this.config),`; slashCommandProcessor.ts useEffect `load()` with `}, [config]);`; mcpCommand.ts:503 `await toolRegistry.discoverMcpTools();` on refresh.
defects.notes: Must say prompt commands are not rebuilt after re-discovery (refresh/auth), so newly discovered prompts are missing as commands.

defects.title: Cached prompts are not cleared when connectAndDiscover fails, so a server that failed to (re)connect keeps advertising stale prompts
defects.statement: The prompt cache is cleared only in mcpClient.onerror (mcp-client.ts:408) and when prompts/list itself fails (515). The outer failure path of connectAndDiscover (mcp-client.ts:437-445) marks the server DISCONNECTED but leaves mcpServerPromptsInternal untouched, so after a failed reconnect (/mcp refresh) or a tool-discovery failure after prompts were stored, /mcp lists prompts for a disconnected server and createPromptCommands registers them as commands that fail when invoked.
defects.evidence: mcp-client.ts:437-445 outer catch: console.error + `updateMCPServerStatus(mcpServerName, MCPServerStatus.DISCONNECTED);` with no `mcpServerPromptsInternal.delete`; contrast 408 and 515.
defects.notes: Must say the prompt cache is not invalidated on connection/discovery failure (stale prompts shown/offered).

defects.title: Prompt argument completion produces invalid input for a partially typed option and never runs after the first argument
defects.statement: The completion callback returns `${partialArg}--${arg.name}=""` (promptCommands.ts:170). useCompletion replaces the last partial token with the suggestion, so for `/prompt --fi` the suggestion `--fi--field=""` yields `/prompt --fi--field=""`. And once one argument is typed followed by a space, useCompletion's command-tree traversal treats `--a="x"` as a sub-command name, finds none, sets leafCommand=null and never calls completion again.
defects.evidence: promptCommands.ts:170 `suggestions.push(`${partialArg}--${arg.name}=""`)`; useCompletion.ts argument branch passes `rawParts.slice(depth).join(' ')`; InputPrompt.tsx `basePath = ... parts.slice(0, -1); newValue = `/${[...basePath, suggestion].join(' ')}``.
defects.notes: Must identify that completion concatenates onto the partial token (producing e.g. `--fi--field=""`) or does not work past the first argument. R15 (substring(2) with multiple dashes) does not count.

excluded.reason: Claims `getMCPServerPrompts(serverName) || []` may hide an error state and the getter should return []. getMCPServerPrompts returns undefined for a server with no prompts by design and `|| []` handles it correctly; API-style preference.
Claims the DISCONNECTED status line shows only the tools count, not the prompts count. Cosmetic: prompts are still listed in full below; no functional consequence.
Suggests extracting repeated pluralization logic into a helper. Refactoring preference.
Claims `if (descLines)` is always truthy so the else branch is dead. True but harmless: this branch is only entered when prompt.description is truthy, so output is unaffected.

Claims the /mcp auth hint is shown only when there are tools, not when there are only prompts. Wrong: with prompts but no tools, the `serverTools.length === 0` branch (mcpCommand.ts:272-276) prints the hint; the real gap is the both-empty case (D3), which R5 does not describe.
Suggests an early return instead of nesting in createPromptCommands. Style.
Suggests extracting hard-coded error messages to constants/i18n. Style.
Asks for positional-argument support in the prompt argument parser. Feature request; the --key=value syntax is what help and completion advertise.
Says the argument regex may not handle all edge cases. Vague, no concrete failing input.

Claims `if (value)` drops an explicitly passed empty string for optional args. Dropping an empty optional value lets the server apply its default; rejecting an empty required value is defensible; not a defect.
Asks for an explicit `Client | null` type on mcpClient. TypeScript infers the type; style.

Claims `result.messages[0].content.text` is accessed without checking the content type. The optional-chain guard at promptCommands.ts:135 already returns an error for non-text content, so the access at 146 is safe. (Truncation of later messages is a separate defect, D6.)
Claims `substring(2)` in completion may misbehave with multiple dashes. Matches of /--([^=]+)/ always start with '--', so substring(2) strips exactly that; no bug shown.
Suggests renaming mcpServerStatusesInternal/mcpServerPromptsInternal. Naming preference consistent with existing code.
Claims the module-level prompts map can grow without bound. It is keyed by configured server names, a small fixed set; not realistic.
Suggests renaming getMCPServerPrompts to getPrompts. Naming preference; mirrors getMCPServerStatus.
Suggests running discoverPrompts and discoverTools in parallel. Optimization suggestion with no concrete regression.
Suggests normalising `response.prompts ?? []`. ListPromptsResultSchema requires prompts to be an array, so it is never undefined after validation.
Says the 'Method not found' filter is duplicated in invokeMcpPrompt. Refactoring preference.
Says matching the substring 'Method not found' is brittle vs the JSON-RPC code. The check only controls whether a log line is printed; robustness nit.
Suggests making promptParams optional. API-style preference; the sole caller always passes an object.
Says `${promptParams}` logs as [object Object]. Trivial logging nit with no functional effect.
Asks the discovery test to assert getMCPServerPrompts after success and failure. Test request, not a defect.

Claims `--key=""`/`--key=` are treated as absent, so a required argument errors as missing and an optional one is dropped. Rejecting an empty value for a required argument and omitting an empty optional one (server default applies) is reasonable behaviour, not a bug.

Claims the argument regex keeps backslashes of escaped quotes and lets a key absorb whitespace (`--first --second=value`). `--first` without `=` is not a supported syntax, and escaped quotes inside values are an edge case; no realistic failure.
Claims a prompts-only server prints its prompts then 'No tools available', looking empty. The line is accurate (there are no tools) and prompts are listed right above; cosmetic wording.
Claims a server that stalls on prompts/list delays tool registration. Speculative: servers without prompts answer Method not found immediately; no concrete regression.
Claims `split('\n')` always returns a non-empty array so the else branch is dead. True but harmless (same as R4): description is non-empty in this branch.
Claims prompts/get uses the SDK's 60s default timeout instead of the configured server timeout. A prompt template fetch exceeding 60s is contrived; no realistic consequence.
Claims a prompts-only server showing 'No tools available' makes it look empty. Same cosmetic wording point as C16; the statement is accurate.
Claims logging `${promptParams}` renders [object Object]. Trivial logging nit (same as R24).
Asks for a test exercising a real prompt command instead of mocking the factory. Test request.

Claims server-supplied prompt names/descriptions can inject terminal escape sequences into /mcp output. Tool names/descriptions from the same trusted configured servers were already printed this way; not newly introduced and the server is user-configured.
Claims completion treats `--lang` inside a quoted value as an already-used argument. Contrived input (an argument value containing `--name=`), only affects a suggestion list.

google-gemini__gemini-cli@d64b61e.pr_summary: Rewrites the extension enablement rules engine (packages/cli/src/config/extensions/extensionEnablement.ts) around an `Override` class: input paths are normalized to leading/trailing forward slashes, `*` becomes an optional `(/.*)?` group, `disable` is `enable` with a `!` rule, and enabling/disabling at a path drops conflicting, equal and child rules. The `extensions enable|disable` commands drop yargs `choices` for `--scope`, validate it case-insensitively via a custom `.check`, and map 'workspace' to SettingScope.Workspace and everything else to SettingScope.User. Docs and tests are updated.

defects.title: `--scope system|systemdefaults` now passes validation and silently acts at user scope
defects.statement: The new `.check` in disable.ts:47-63 and enable.ts accepts any lowercased `Object.values(SettingScope)`, which includes 'system' and 'systemdefaults', and even lists them as valid in its error message. handleDisable/handleEnable (disable.ts:17-23, enable.ts:17-23) then map anything other than 'workspace' to SettingScope.User. So `gemini extensions disable foo --scope=system` disables the extension for the whole user (homedir rule) and prints 'successfully disabled for scope "system"'. Before the PR, `choices: [User, Workspace]` rejected it, and disableExtension/enableExtension's explicit 'System and SystemDefaults scopes are not supported.' guard (extension.ts:709-711, 724-726) is now unreachable from the CLI.
defects.evidence: disable.ts:49-52 `argv.scope && !Object.values(SettingScope).map((s) => s.toLowerCase()).includes((argv.scope as string).toLowerCase())`; SettingScope has User, Workspace, System, SystemDefaults; disable.ts:19-22 `if (args.scope?.toLowerCase() === 'workspace') {...} else { disableExtension(args.name, SettingScope.User); }`; base disable.ts had `choices: [SettingScope.User, SettingScope.Workspace]`.
defects.notes: Must say that unsupported scopes (System/SystemDefaults) are accepted by validation and silently applied at user scope (or reported as success for a scope not changed). Comments only about duplicated scope parsing (R1, R3, C6) or about an explicitly empty `--scope=` (C3, C8) do not count.

defects.title: Previously saved Windows rules (backslash paths) stop matching because only the looked-up path is slash-normalized
defects.statement: isEnabled now normalizes the current path with ensureLeadingAndTrailingSlash (extensionEnablement.ts:132), which converts backslashes to '/' and prepends '/', so on Windows `C:\Users\me\proj` becomes `/C:/Users/me/proj/`. Rules already persisted by the previous version were written from the raw path (`!C:\Users\me*`), and fromFileRule (32-40) does not normalize them, so their regex `^C:\\Users\\me(.*)?$` no longer matches anything. After upgrading, an extension a Windows user disabled is silently enabled again, and new enable/disable calls cannot dedupe against the old rules (base differs).
defects.evidence: head :82 `let result = dirPath.replace(/\\/g, '/');` :83-85 prepend '/'; :132 `override.matchesPath(ensureLeadingAndTrailingSlash(currentPath))`; :32-39 fromFileRule only strips '!' and '*'. Base isEnabled tested the raw currentPath against the raw rule, and base enable/disable wrote `${scopePath}*` from the raw os.homedir()/cwd (extension.ts:715-717).
defects.notes: Must say persisted (pre-upgrade) rules are not normalized while the looked-up path now is, specifically for Windows backslash / drive paths, so saved disables stop applying. The POSIX exact-path variant (legacy `!/home/user/project` with no `*`) does not count on its own: production code never wrote such rules. C16 counts because it names the mechanism (fromFileRule leaves persisted rules un-normalized while the lookup path is slash-normalized, including Windows separators); C11, which argues only the POSIX exact-path case, does not.

defects.title: Docs still say a user-level disable disables the extension everywhere, contradicting the new workspace-enable guidance
defects.statement: docs/extension.md:39 (edited by this PR) still says `gemini extensions disable extension-name` 'will disable the extension at the user level, so it will be disabled everywhere', while the new text at 43-45 (and the new engine) lets `enable --scope=workspace` re-enable it in a workspace despite the user-level disable. The PR removed the old caveat that made the two statements consistent, so the doc now contradicts itself.
defects.evidence: docs/extension.md:39 `... will disable the extension at the user level, so it will be disabled everywhere.`; :43 `You can also enable an extension for a specific workspace using ... --scope=workspace`; :45 `This is useful if you have an extension disabled at the top-level and only enabled in specific places.`; base had `Note that if an extension is disabled at the user-level, enabling it at the workspace level will not do anything.`
defects.notes: Must point at the 'disabled everywhere' wording being contradicted by the workspace-enable override.

excluded.reason: Suggests mapping the scope string directly to the SettingScope enum instead of conditional checks. Refactoring preference; it does not identify that System scopes are accepted and silently mapped to User (D1).
Points out the typo 'extenison' in the --scope describe string. Pre-existing on the base side and harmless.
Suggests extracting the scope parsing into a shared helper to avoid duplication. Maintainability preference; names no wrong behaviour.
Asks for an explicit boolean return type on isChildOf. Style: the inferred type is already boolean.
Claims ensureLeadingAndTrailingSlash('') returns '//'. Wrong: '' gets '/' prepended and then already ends with '/', so it returns '/'; callers pass cwd/homedir, never empty.
Says conflictsWith||isEqualTo is just a same-base comparison and should be collapsed. Simplification preference; behaviour is correct.

Says the test at extensionEnablement.test.ts:147 passes '/*', producing '/*/*' instead of a root rule. The resulting regex `^(/.*)?(/.*)?$` still matches every absolute path, so the test exercises a root-wide rule as intended; test-style only.
Says an explicitly empty `--scope=` on enable skips the check and enables at User scope. Contrived input; User is the documented default scope, so no user-visible harm.

Says legacy inclusive rules like `!/home/alice*` are not replaced when the same scope is changed, so a sibling such as /home/alice-other stays disabled. New rules are always appended last and last-match wins, so every path under the changed scope takes the new setting; the only residue is on prefix-sibling directories outside the scope, which the base glob already mis-matched. Contrived and not a regression of the scope's own behaviour.

Asks to share the duplicated scope validation between enable.ts and disable.ts. Duplication preference; it only parenthetically hints at admitting unhonoured scopes without stating the System→User behaviour of D1.
Says passing a '!'-prefixed path into enable() hides polarity in the path argument. API naming/design preference; behaviour is correct.
Says an explicitly empty `--scope=` on disable skips validation and disables at User scope. Contrived input; User is the default scope anyway.
Says the last Override test duplicates the output assertion instead of testing a disabled path. Test-quality request, not a defect in shipped code.

Says persisted exact-path rules like `!/home/user/project` stop matching because the lookup path now has a trailing slash. Production code (extension.ts:717, 732) always wrote rules with includeSubdirs=true (`...*`), which still match; exact-path rules only exist if hand-edited, so the scenario is contrived.
Asks to rename the test 'should handle'. Test naming style.
Asks to rename the test 'should handle'. Test naming style.
Says enabling a parent should not delete child overrides. Deliberate design of this PR (pruning child rules, covered by tests); with last-match-wins the child rule would be shadowed anyway.
Says the last test duplicates the serialization assertion instead of checking matchesPath/isEnabled. Test-quality request, not a defect.

google-gemini__gemini-cli@e7ed0a4.pr_summary: Refactor in packages/core: LS, ReadFile, Grep, Glob and ReadManyFiles tools drop their separate targetDir/rootDirectory constructor argument and read config.getTargetDir() on each use; the private isWithinRoot copies in edit.ts, write-file.ts, glob.ts and ls.ts are replaced by the shared fileUtils.isWithinRoot (now using path.resolve instead of path.normalize); config.createToolRegistry and tests are updated.

defects.title: glob.test.ts reassigns the shared tempRootDir to its 'sub' child, so afterEach deletes only the child and leaks the mkdtemp'd root on every run
defects.statement: To give GlobTool a deeper root now that it reads config.getTargetDir(), the test at packages/core/src/tools/glob.test.ts:228 does `tempRootDir = path.join(tempRootDir, 'sub')` instead of using a separate config/local. afterEach (glob.test.ts:57-60) then runs `fs.rm(tempRootDir, ...)` on the mutated value, removing only `<tmp>/glob-tool-root-XXXX/sub`; the parent directory with fileA.txt, FileB.TXT, older/newer.sortme is left in os.tmpdir() on every test run. The base used a local `deeperRootDir` and did not mutate the shared variable.
defects.evidence: glob.test.ts:228 `tempRootDir = path.join(tempRootDir, 'sub');`; glob.test.ts:59 `await fs.rm(tempRootDir, { recursive: true, force: true });`; beforeEach glob.test.ts:30 `tempRootDir = await fs.mkdtemp(...)`. Base: `const deeperRootDir = path.join(tempRootDir, 'sub'); new GlobTool(deeperRootDir, mockConfig)`.
defects.notes: Must say that mutating tempRootDir breaks cleanup (leaks the temp dir/fixtures). Disliking the reassignment for style alone does not count.

excluded.reason: Claims registerCoreTool's `ToolClass: any` removes constructor type-checking after the signature changes. The `any` parameter predates this PR (with an existing eslint-disable); every call site passes arguments matching the new constructors, so this is a typing-hygiene suggestion, not a defect.

Claims calling this.config.getTargetDir() three times in grep.ts hurts readability/performance. getTargetDir is a trivial getter of an immutable field set once in the Config constructor (config.ts:200,343); style only.

Claims repeated getTargetDir() calls in read-file.ts are redundant and could make messages inconsistent if config were mutable. targetDir is readonly and set once, so values cannot diverge; style only.

Claims read-many-files should keep one local root snapshot instead of repeated getTargetDir() calls. Readability preference: targetDir is a private readonly field, so every call returns the same value.
Claims read-many-files should capture getTargetDir() once per execution. Same readability preference as C2; no behavioural difference.

Claims read-many-files' `startsWith` containment check accepts same-prefix sibling directories and should use isWithinRoot. The prefix check is unchanged from the base (it only switched from toolBaseDir to getTargetDir(), the same value), so this is a pre-existing weakness not introduced or worsened by the PR.
Claims read-many-files can read a same-prefix sibling directory's files because its glob-result check is a bare prefix match. Pre-existing check, unchanged in substance by this PR (see C3).

Claims grep's `startsWith` root check lets `../project-private` search a same-prefix sibling. grep.ts's prefix check is identical at the base (this.rootDirectory, which was path.resolve'd, vs the equally resolved getTargetDir()); pre-existing, not made worse.
Claims grep's root check accepts sibling directories sharing the root prefix. Same pre-existing check as C6.

Claims isWithinRoot's @param doc should say relative paths are now resolved against the process cwd. Documentation request; every caller (edit.ts:133, ls.ts:113, read-file.ts:85, write-file.ts:103, glob.ts resolves first) checks path.isAbsolute before calling, so no behaviour changes.
Claims the `searchDirAbsolute || this.config.getTargetDir()` fallback in glob.ts is unreachable and should be removed. Pre-existing dead fallback and a style point; no consequence.

google-gemini__gemini-cli@6fd8269.pr_summary: Refactors SubAgentScope.create to take a SubAgentOptions object (toolConfig, outputConfig, onMessage), builds a per-subagent ToolRegistry that can hold BaseTool instances, and reports each turn's text and each tool call through onMessage. Adds an opt-in planning_tool (usePlanningTool setting, registered directly in createToolRegistry) that runs a gemini-2.5-pro sub-agent with read-only file tools (ReadFile, ReadManyFiles, Grep, Glob, LS instances) to produce a JSON execution plan, plus tests and a tools/index.ts barrel.

defects.title: Tool instances are sent to the model as raw FunctionDeclarations, so the planner's tool declarations are malformed
defects.statement: ToolConfig.tools now accepts tool instances, but runNonInteractive still pushes every non-string entry straight into toolsList (subagent.ts:379-383), which is sent as `tools: [{ functionDeclarations: toolsList }]` (subagent.ts:418). A tool instance is not a FunctionDeclaration: its declaration is `tool.schema` (parameters live under parameterSchema). The planning tool passes only instances (planning-tool.ts:187-195), so its sub-agent is advertised declarations without valid parameter schemas (plus stray fields), and it cannot reliably call its code-reading tools.
defects.evidence: subagent.ts:379-383 if (typeof tool === 'string') { toolsToLoad.push(tool); } else { toolsList.push(tool); } with toolsList: FunctionDeclaration[] (compiles because FunctionDeclaration's fields are all optional); tools.ts DeclarativeTool: get schema(): FunctionDeclaration { return { name, description, parameters: this.parameterSchema } }.
defects.notes: Must say tool instances are pushed into the function-declaration list instead of their schema / names. Comments only about unknown string tool names being skipped (R3) are a near-miss; the instanceof/registration failure is D2.

defects.title: ReadFile/Grep/Glob are BaseDeclarativeTool, fail `instanceof BaseTool`, and are never registered in the sub-agent registry
defects.statement: SubAgentScope.create registers non-string tools only if `tool instanceof BaseTool` (subagent.ts:308). ReadFileTool, GrepTool and GlobTool extend BaseDeclarativeTool, not BaseTool (read-file.ts:165, grep.ts:539, glob.ts:244), so three of the planner's five tools fall into the 'FunctionDeclaration' branch and are never registered. They are still advertised to the model (D1), but processFunctionCalls executes through the private this.toolRegistry (subagent.ts:451, executeToolCall), so every read_file/grep/glob call the planner makes fails as an unknown tool.
defects.evidence: subagent.ts:308 } else if (tool instanceof BaseTool) { subagentToolRegistry.registerTool(tool); } else { // FunctionDeclaration ... }; read-file.ts:165 export class ReadFileTool extends BaseDeclarativeTool<...>; tools.ts: BaseDeclarativeTool extends DeclarativeTool, BaseTool extends DeclarativeTool (siblings).
defects.notes: Must say the declarative tools are not BaseTool instances, so they are not registered/executable in the child registry. A claim that this breaks TypeScript compilation (C12) is wrong: the instances are assignable to the all-optional FunctionDeclaration member of the union.

defects.title: Planning tool ignores the abort signal: cancelling leaves a 10-minute, 100-turn sub-agent running
defects.statement: PlanningTool.execute receives `signal` (planning-tool.ts:127-132) but never uses it; runNonInteractive creates its own never-triggered AbortController (subagent.ts:372). Cancelling the tool call leaves the gemini-2.5-pro sub-agent issuing model requests and file reads until it finishes or hits max_time_minutes 10 / max_turns 100, burning quota and still pushing updateOutput for a cancelled call.
defects.evidence: async execute(params, signal: AbortSignal, updateOutput?) { const plan = await this.createPlan(params.user_request, updateOutput); ... subagent.ts:372 const abortController = new AbortController();
defects.notes: Must say the AbortSignal is not propagated so cancellation does not stop the sub-agent.

defects.title: Running the planner permanently switches the parent session's model to gemini-2.5-pro
defects.statement: SubAgentScope.createChatObject calls `this.runtimeContext.setModel(this.modelConfig.model)` (subagent.ts:629), and Config.setModel mutates the shared contentGeneratorConfig.model (config.ts:418-421). The planning tool hands the main session's Config to the sub-agent (planning-tool.ts:196-202) and is the first production caller of SubAgentScope, so after one planning_tool call every subsequent main-session turn runs on gemini-2.5-pro instead of the user's selected model; nothing restores it.
defects.evidence: subagent.ts:629 this.runtimeContext.setModel(this.modelConfig.model); config.ts:418 setModel(newModel) { if (this.contentGeneratorConfig) this.contentGeneratorConfig.model = newModel; }; planning-tool.ts modelConfig.model = 'gemini-2.5-pro'; grep shows planning-tool.ts is the only non-test SubAgentScope caller.
defects.notes: Must say the sub-agent's setModel on the shared Config changes the parent session's model after planning.

defects.title: planning_tool registration (and its child tools) bypass coreTools / excludeTools
defects.statement: Every built-in tool is registered through registerCoreTool, which honours the coreTools allowlist and excludeTools (config.ts:724-754), but the planning tool is registered directly with `registry.registerTool(getPlanningTool(this))` when usePlanningTool is on (config.ts:767-770). Excluding planning_tool (or restricting coreTools) does not remove it; likewise the planner constructs its own ReadFile/Grep/Glob/LS/ReadManyFiles instances (planning-tool.ts:187-195) even if those tools are excluded in the configuration.
defects.evidence: config.ts:767-770 // Manually register the planning tool ... if (this.getUsePlanningTool()) { registry.registerTool(getPlanningTool(this)); } vs registerCoreTool's excludeTools?.includes(className) checks.
defects.notes: Must say the planning tool (or its sub-tools) ignore the coreTools/excludeTools restrictions.

excluded.reason: Claims usePlanningTool should get a default in the CLI config to avoid propagating undefined. The core Config constructor already does `params.usePlanningTool ?? false`, so undefined is handled.
Asks for a JSDoc comment on the new usePlanningTool setting. Documentation request.

Claims unknown tool names are silently skipped when building the sub-agent registry. Missing names were already silently filtered by getFunctionDeclarationsFiltered before this PR; not introduced here.
Claims onMessage fires once per model turn instead of per streamed chunk. Per-turn delivery (plus per tool call) is the design; it is still incremental and not a defect.
Claims the sub-agent delivers text only after each response stream ends, not during it. Per-turn progress is the chosen granularity; a design preference, not a defect.
Claims no text progress is shown during a single long model response. Same per-turn design choice as C2; not a defect.
Claims accumulating textResponse for a whole response grows a buffer without bound. One model response is bounded by the model's output limit; contrived.
Claims each onMessage call replaces the tool's live display so earlier progress disappears. Showing the latest progress line is a UX choice, not a correctness defect.
Claims untruncated tool arguments in the progress messages are too long and lack markdown. Log/display formatting preference.

Claims forwarding raw tool arguments to onMessage leaks sensitive data to the display. The arguments are the planner's own read-only tool calls shown to the same local user; verbosity preference, not a security defect.

Claims ${user_request} in the planning prompt is never interpolated. It is escaped in the template literal on purpose and SubAgentScope's templateString substitutes it from the ContextState that createPlan sets.
Claims the hardcoded 'gemini-2.5-pro' should use a models.ts constant. Style/configurability preference.
Asks for max_time_minutes/max_turns to be configurable. Configurability request, not a defect.
Asks for validation that user_request is non-empty. The schema marks it required; input-validation request.
Claims returning the raw non-JSON plan as returnDisplay may be large and should be truncated. Intentional (commented) behaviour; preference.
Claims console.error in library code bypasses logging. Consistent with subagent.ts; style.
Claims createPlan swallows errors and returns null, losing the reason. Errors are logged and a failure result is returned; error-reporting preference.
Claims the new tools/index.ts barrel is unused. Dead-code tidy-up, no behavioural consequence.
Asks the planning test fixture to contain a real plan array and a rejection case. Test request.
Asks the subagent test to register a real list_files tool. Test-quality request.
Claims the external-tool subagent test can pass while the tool is not available to the child. Test-quality request; the product defects are D1/D2.

Claims ToolConfig.tools only admits BaseTool so the planner's declarative tools make the PR fail to type-check. The union includes the all-optional FunctionDeclaration, to which these instances are assignable, so it compiles; the real consequence (not registered) is D2.
Claims any parseable JSON (e.g. {}) is reported as a successful plan without checking the plan array. Output-shape validation request; not a defect of the code's stated contract.
Claims JSON.parse accepts null/[]/objects without a plan array yet success is reported. Validation request; not a defect.
Claims parsed JSON should be validated as a plan before reporting success. Validation request; not a defect.
Claims giving the planner read_many_files allows unbounded aggregate reads. read_many_files's limits are pre-existing and the same tool is available to the main agent; not introduced here.
Claims the subagent deadline is only checked after a stream completes. That loop structure predates this PR.
Asks for usePlanningTool to be documented in docs/cli/configuration.md. Documentation request.
Claims thought parts are filtered out of resp.text so 'thinking' is not streamed. The sub-agent never requests thoughts (no includeThoughts), so there are no thought parts to lose; speculative.

google-gemini__gemini-cli@0fa1bd7.pr_summary: Fix for #8077 (saving settings rewrote the whole settings.json, dropping comments and writing env-var references out as resolved plaintext). Adds comment-json and utils/commentJson.ts: updateSettingsFilePreservingFormat parses the existing file, deep-merges the in-memory settings into it (applyUpdates), restores recorded $VAR references (restoreEnvVarReferences) and stringifies with 2-space indent; trackEnvVarMappings records settings paths whose original value was exactly a $VAR/${VAR}. loadSettings records mappings per scope around resolveEnvVarsInObject and LoadedSettings.setValue passes them to saveSettings, which (after the existing migrateSettingsToV1 conversion) writes through the new helper.

defects.title: Merge-only save never deletes keys: removed MCP servers (and replaced fields) persist on disk
defects.statement: applyUpdates (commentJson.ts:52-80) starts from the parsed file and only adds/overwrites keys present in the in-memory settings, recursing into nested objects; keys deleted in memory are never removed from the file. `gemini mcp remove` does `delete mcpServers[name]; settings.setValue(scope, 'mcpServers', mcpServers)` (commands/mcp/remove.ts:30-32), so the server stays in settings.json and reappears on restart while the CLI reports it removed; re-adding a server with a different transport merges into the old object, leaving stale command/args beside httpUrl. Before the PR the whole object was written with JSON.stringify, so deletions took effect.
defects.evidence: commentJson.ts:56 `const result = current;` then :58-77 loop over `Object.entries(updates)` assigning `result[key] = ...`; nothing deletes keys absent from updates. remove.ts: `delete mcpServers[name]; settings.setValue(settingsScope, 'mcpServers', mcpServers);`. Base saveSettings wrote `JSON.stringify(settingsToSave, null, 2)`.
defects.notes: Must say the new save merges and never removes keys that were deleted in memory (mcp remove / replaced nested objects). R11 (arrays replaced wholesale) and R9 (mutating the parsed object) do not count.

defects.title: Env references embedded in a larger string ("Bearer $TOKEN") are not tracked and are written back resolved
defects.statement: resolveEnvVarsInString (utils/envVarResolver.ts:20-28) substitutes $VAR/${VAR} anywhere inside a string, but trackEnvVarMappings records a mapping only when the whole original string matches the anchored /^\$(?:(\w+)|{([^}]+)})$/ (commentJson.ts:152). A value like an MCP header "Authorization": "Bearer $API_TOKEN" or "${BASE_URL}/api" is resolved at load, not tracked, and the next save of that scope (any setValue, e.g. /settings theme toggle) writes the resolved secret into settings.json - the leak #8077 is about, left open for the common header/URL case.
defects.evidence: commentJson.ts:152 `const envVarPattern = /^\$(?:(\w+)|{([^}]+)})$/;` vs envVarResolver.ts `const envVarRegex = /\$(?:(\w+)|{([^}]+)})/g;` used with value.replace, doc example `resolveEnvVarsInString("Token: $API_KEY")`. saveSettings passes the resolved settingsFile.settings as updates.
defects.notes: Must say partial/embedded references are resolved but not tracked/restored, so they are saved in plaintext. R13 (support default-value/nested syntax) does not count. Graded medium, not high: before the PR every value (whole or embedded reference) was written back resolved, so the embedded case is a gap in the fix, not a regression, the same class and grade as D3 and D4.

defects.title: Env references inside arrays (e.g. MCP args) are tracked but never restored, so they are saved resolved
defects.statement: trackEnvVarMappings recurses into arrays (for...in yields index keys, commentJson.ts:146,162-168) and resolveEnvVarsInObject resolves array items, but restoreEnvVarsRecursive only descends into non-array objects (commentJson.ts:117-123) and applyUpdates replaces arrays wholesale with the resolved in-memory array (:76). "args": ["--api-key", "$API_KEY"] is therefore written back with the secret in plaintext on the next save of that scope.
defects.evidence: commentJson.ts:117-121 `} else if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)) { restoreEnvVarsRecursive(...) }`; :162 `else if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null)` includes arrays when tracking; envVarResolver.ts maps arrays item by item.
defects.notes: Must say env references inside arrays are not restored (leak). C16 also mentions arrays but is filed under D2 (its lead point). R11 on array merge granularity does not count.

defects.title: Env mappings are recorded on V2 paths but the saved object is converted to V1, so references for migrated keys leak
defects.statement: loadAndMigrate migrates V1 files to V2 in memory (settings.ts:576-600) before the mappings are captured on the V2 object (:663-683). With MIGRATE_V2_OVERWRITE = false (:60), saveSettings always runs migrateSettingsToV1 (:731-735) before calling the updater, so every key in MIGRATION_MAP is written under its V1 name while the mapping paths are V2 (e.g. ['tools','discoveryCommand'] vs top-level toolDiscoveryCommand, ['model','name'] vs model). restoreEnvVarsRecursive never matches them, and saving any setting writes the resolved env value in plaintext. Only mcpServers (same path in both shapes) is protected.
defects.evidence: settings.ts:60 `const MIGRATE_V2_OVERWRITE = false;`; :731-735 `if (!MIGRATE_V2_OVERWRITE) { settingsToSave = migrateSettingsToV1(...) }`; MIGRATION_MAP :117 `toolDiscoveryCommand: 'tools.discoveryCommand'`; mappings built from the migrated objects at :663-683; commentJson.ts:112-115 looks up `fullPath.join('.')` of the V1 structure.
defects.notes: Must say the mapping paths (V2) do not match the V1-converted structure written by saveSettings, so env references for non-mcpServers keys are lost/leaked.

defects.title: Saving into a V2-format file adds V1 keys beside the old nested values, and the old value wins on reload
defects.statement: saveSettings converts to V1 (settings.ts:731-735) and the updater now MERGES into the parsed file instead of replacing it. For a hand-written V2 file with {"ui": {"theme": "A"}}, changing the theme writes a top-level "theme": "B" but leaves ui.theme = "A". On reload needsMigration sees the V1 key, migrateSettingsToV2 sets ui.theme = B and then carries over the unrecognized original `ui` object (settings.ts:251-254), overwriting it with {theme: "A"}; the edit is lost. Before the PR the whole file was rewritten in V1 so no duplicate existed.
defects.evidence: migrateSettingsToV2: `for (const [oldKey, newPath] of Object.entries(MIGRATION_MAP)) { if (flatKeys.has(oldKey)) { setNestedProperty(v2Settings, newPath, ...); flatKeys.delete(oldKey); } }` then `for (const remainingKey of flatKeys) { v2Settings[remainingKey] = flatSettings[remainingKey]; }` - `ui` remains in flatKeys and replaces the freshly set ui object. applyUpdates merges `theme` without touching `ui`.
defects.notes: Must say V1-converted save merged into a V2 file leaves the old nested value, which overrides the edit on next load (or duplicates V1/V2 keys with the stale one winning). Plain 'keys are not deleted' (D1) is a different defect.

defects.title: A deliberately changed value at an env-backed path is silently reverted to the $VAR reference on save
defects.statement: restoreEnvVarsRecursive (commentJson.ts:114-116) restores the recorded reference whenever the path matches and the current value is any string, never comparing with mapping.resolvedValue (recorded at :159, read nowhere), and the mappings captured at load are reused by every setValue (settings.ts:421-422). If a user replaces an env-backed value (e.g. `gemini mcp add` re-adding a server with `-e API_KEY=newkey` where the file had "$API_KEY"), the file keeps "$VAR" and the new value is lost on restart.
defects.evidence: commentJson.ts:115 `if (envVarReference && typeof value === 'string') { (obj as Record<string, unknown>)[key] = envVarReference; }`; EnvVarMapping.resolvedValue set at :159 and unused.
defects.notes: Must say restoration ignores whether the value was changed (resolvedValue unused / stale mappings). R3 (non-string resolved values) does not count.

defects.title: Comments inside arrays are still dropped on every save
defects.statement: applyUpdates replaces every array in the parsed file with the plain in-memory array (commentJson.ts:63-76, arrays take the `result[key] = value` branch). comment-json stores comments on array items as symbol properties of the parsed CommentArray, so any comment inside an array (e.g. a commented-out arg or excluded tool) is removed whenever any setting in that scope is saved - the comment preservation the PR claims is incomplete for arrays.
defects.evidence: commentJson.ts:66 `!Array.isArray(value)` excludes arrays from the merge branch; :76 `result[key] = value;` assigns the plain resolved array from settingsFile.settings (built via JSON.parse(stripJsonComments(...)) and resolveEnvVarsInObject, so it carries no comment metadata).
defects.notes: Must say comments attached to array elements are lost because arrays are replaced wholesale. R11 (arrays replaced instead of element-wise merge, no mention of comments) does not count.

excluded.reason: Claim: the constructor parameter `migratedInMemorScopes` is misspelled. The identifier pre-exists this PR (only context lines here); a naming nit, not a defect.
Claim: define a named type alias instead of `ReturnType<typeof trackEnvVarMappings>` in the Map. Readability preference with no functional consequence.

Claim: restoration only happens for string values, so env vars resolving to numbers/booleans/objects would be saved resolved. resolveEnvVarsInString always returns a string and tracking requires both values to be strings, so a resolved env value is never a non-string; the premise is unreachable.

Claim: updateSettingsFilePreservingFormat should validate that filePath is a string and updates an object. It is a typed internal helper with a single caller passing a path and the settings object; a runtime-validation request, not a defect.

Claim: add type checking before casting the parsed file to Record<string, unknown>. loadSettings already rejects non-object settings files, so on reachable paths the parsed content is an object; speculative.

Claim: on parse failure the function logs and returns instead of throwing. A file that fails comment-json parsing would already have failed loadSettings; only an external edit between load and save reaches it, and saveSettings itself only logs errors as before.
Claim: stringify(..., null, 2) forces 2-space indentation, changing tab/4-space files. The previous code also wrote JSON.stringify(settingsToSave, null, 2), so formatting is not made worse; cosmetic.
Claim: writeFileSync lacks handling for EACCES/ENOENT. The only caller saveSettings wraps the call in try/catch and logs, exactly as before.
Claim: applyUpdates mutates the object passed in rather than a deep copy. The mutated object is the freshly parsed file content local to updateSettingsFilePreservingFormat; no side effect escapes.

Claim: Object.entries in applyUpdates introduces prototype-pollution risk. applyUpdates explicitly skips __proto__/constructor/prototype and Object.entries yields only own enumerable keys; no pollution path exists.

Claim: applyUpdates replaces arrays wholesale instead of updating individual elements. Replacing a settings array with the saved array is the correct save semantics; element-wise merge would be wrong. It names neither the env-var leak (D3) nor the comment loss (D7).

Claim: joining mapping paths with '.' is ambiguous when a key contains a dot. Tracking and restoring use the same join, so a mis-restore needs both a dotted key and a nested path spelling the identical string with an env reference; contrived.

Claim: the env pattern should support default values or nested references. The resolver itself supports only $VAR/${VAR}, so there is nothing more to track; it does not state the real gap (embedded references, D2).
Claim: forcing 2-space indentation reformats tab/4-space files on an unrelated edit. The base code already rewrote the file with JSON.stringify(..., null, 2), so this is not a regression; cosmetic.

Claim: an unrelated setting edit reserializes and reformats the whole file (fixed indent, LF). Same as base behaviour (full JSON.stringify rewrite); formatting preference, not a defect introduced here.
Claim: the single-setting save writes a fully reserialized snapshot, reformatting unchanged content. Same root as C24; base also rewrote the entire file; cosmetic.

Claim: if the settings file disappears between load and save, the new-file branch writes resolved updates without restoring references. Mappings exist only for files that existed at load, so this needs the file deleted mid-session; contrived, and base behaviour wrote resolved values too.
Claim: the !existsSync branch bypasses envVarMappings, so recreating a deleted file writes the resolved token. Same contrived deleted-between-load-and-save scenario as C5.

Claim: the new-file branch writes settingsToSave with JSON.stringify before applying mappings, persisting resolved secrets if the file was removed or config was in-memory migrated. Migrated-in-memory scopes still have their file on disk (existing-file branch); only a mid-session deletion reaches this; contrived.
Claim: the parse-error log should include filePath. Diagnostic-message improvement; the parse-failure path is only reachable if the file is corrupted after a successful load.

Claim: returning on parse failure reports success to setValue although nothing was written. Only reachable if the file became unparseable after loadSettings parsed it; contrived, and saveSettings only ever logged failures.

Claim: the prototype-pollution test builds `__proto__` via an object literal, so it sets the prototype rather than an own key and never exercises the guard. A test-quality observation; the guard itself is correct and no runtime defect results.
Claim: same as C19 - the malicious update's object-literal `__proto__` is not an own key so the test would pass without the guard. Test-coverage request, not a defect in shipped behaviour.

infiniflow__ragflow@f189316.pr_summary: GraphRAG support for the Infinity doc engine. graphrag/utils.py: get_graph falls back to rebuild_graph when no stored graph row is found; rebuild_graph is fixed (asserts 'entity' in the entity loop, json.loads in place of json.load, unwraps list-valued *_kwd fields from Infinity, stops paging on an empty page, returns None only when there are no nodes). rag/utils/infinity_conn.py: field_keyword becomes a module function; conditions on keyword fields turn into filter_fulltext(...) clauses; update() implements 'remove' for both the string form (reset a column to its default) and the dict form (remove one value from a '###'-joined list, done as per-row updates before the main update).

defects.title: Infinity update(): the string 'remove' branch leaves the 'remove' key in newValue and writes '' to integer columns, so resetting a KB's pagerank fails
defects.statement: In InfinityConnection.update the `elif k == "remove":` branch (infinity_conn.py:574-584) handles the string form (`{"remove": PAGERANK_FLD}`, sent by kb_app.py:122 when pagerank is set back to 0) by writing `newValue[v] = de` but never runs `del newValue[k]`. The base code deleted it. So `table_instance.update(filter, newValue)` at line 609 is called with a column named 'remove' that does not exist in the table, and the update raises. Secondarily, the default computation is also wrong. `ty.lower().find("cha")` returns -1, which is truthy, for non-char types such as pagerank_fea's 'integer' (conf/infinity_mapping.json: `"pagerank_fea": {"type": "integer", "default": 0}`). The default 0 is falsy, so de becomes '' and an empty string is written into an integer column. The base code wrote 0. Result: on Infinity, setting a knowledge base's pagerank back to 0 now errors, and the pagerank values are never cleared.
defects.evidence: infinity_conn.py:575-580 `if isinstance(v, str): ty, de = clmns[v]; if ty.lower().find("cha"): if not de: de = ""; newValue[v] = de`. There is no `del newValue[k]` on this path; only the dict branch at :584 deletes it. Base: `del newValue[k]; if v in [PAGERANK_FLD]: newValue[v] = 0`. The caller is kb_app.py:122 `settings.docStoreConn.update({"exists": PAGERANK_FLD}, {"remove": PAGERANK_FLD}, ...)`.
defects.notes: The comment must say that the 'remove' key is not deleted on the string path, or that pagerank_fea gets '' instead of 0 (the find('cha') truthiness or the integer default). Either one counts. The same find('cha') idiom in exists() is pre-existing and does not count.

defects.title: rename_tag on Infinity now loses the tag: the new remove updates commit before the main update, which then fails on the unsupported 'add' key
defects.statement: The new dict-'remove' support runs per-row `table_instance.update(...)` calls (infinity_conn.py:605-607) that strip the old value from the list, and only then runs the main `table_instance.update(filter, newValue)` (:609). rename_tags (kb_app.py:281-282) sends `{"remove": {"tag_kwd": from}, "add": {"tag_kwd": to}}`. update() has no 'add' handling: it falls to `else: newValue[k] = v` (:585-586), so the main update is sent with a non-existent 'add' column and a dict value, and it fails. Before this PR the whole call failed without changing anything. Now the old tag has already been removed from every matching chunk, and the new tag is never added. The tags are silently lost.
defects.evidence: kb_app.py:281-282 `settings.docStoreConn.update({"tag_kwd": req["from_tag"], ...}, {"remove": {"tag_kwd": req["from_tag"].strip()}, "add": {"tag_kwd": req["to_tag"]}}, ...)`. infinity_conn.py:605-607 performs the remove updates first, then :609 `table_instance.update(filter, newValue)` with newValue still containing 'add'. es_conn.py:376-380 shows 'add' is a list-append operation that only the ES backend implements.
defects.notes: The comment must connect the new remove-first sequencing to the unhandled 'add' key or to rename_tag, as a partial/non-atomic update that loses data. Just saying 'add is not supported on Infinity' without the new partial-write consequence is a near-miss (that part is pre-existing). A comment that ties the unhandled 'add' key to this PR's reworked update loop on the rename_tag path (e.g. C4, which says the loop handles only 'remove' and forwards 'add' to the update at :609) counts.

defects.title: Keyword-field conditions become full-text token matches, so deletes and updates by entity/tag name hit non-identical values
defects.statement: equivalent_condition_to_str now turns every condition on a keyword field (field_keyword: source_id and *_kwd except docnm_kwd/knowledge_graph_kwd) into `filter_fulltext('<k>', '<v>')` (infinity_conn.py:72-84). Before, it was an exact `k IN (...)` or `k='v'`. These columns use the `whitespace-#` analyzer (conf/infinity_mapping.json:13,35-39), so the filter matches any row whose value contains the query's tokens, not only the exact member. The same builder feeds delete() (:624) and update() (:554). So set_graph's `delete({"knowledge_graph_kwd": ["entity"], "entity_kwd": sorted(change.removed_nodes)})` (graphrag/utils.py:436) removing entity `JOHN` also deletes the stored chunk for `JOHN SMITH`. Relation deletes by from/to entity (:441) and tag updates by `tag_kwd` (kb_app.py:262, 281) likewise reach unrelated rows. The result is silent loss of knowledge-graph entities and relations on Infinity.
defects.evidence: infinity_conn.py:78 `inCond.append(f"filter_fulltext('{k}', '{item}')")` and :84 `cond.append(f"filter_fulltext('{k}', '{v}')")` replace the base `k IN (...)` / `k='v'` for keyword fields. conf/infinity_mapping.json:37 `"entity_kwd": {..., "analyzer": "whitespace-#"}`. Entity names are multi-word upper-cased strings (graphrag/utils.py:240 `clean_str(record_attributes[1].upper())`). delete() uses the same builder (:624).
defects.notes: The comment must say that filter_fulltext is a token/full-text match rather than exact membership, so conditions on keyword fields (entity, tag, source_id) can select rows with a different value. Comments only about quote escaping in these filters do not count.

excluded.reason: The claim is that `if not res.total == 0:` should read `if res.total != 0:` for clarity. `not res.total == 0` vs `!= 0` is a readability preference. The behaviour is correct.

The claim is that the inverted `if not res.total == 0:` guard leaves the for loop outside the block, which breaks get_graph. Wrong: the for loop IS inside the `if not res.total == 0:` block (utils.py:417-425). The fall-through to rebuild_graph is the intended fix.

The claim is that switching the rebuild_graph paging stop from getTotal() to len(es_res) terminates the loop prematurely. Breaking on an empty page (len of the current page) is the correct paging termination. getTotal returns the overall hit count, which never becomes 0 while paging past the end, so the old check could not stop the loop correctly. No premature termination: a page is empty only when the offset is past the results.
The claim is that field_keyword uses 8-space indentation. 8-space indentation inside a function body is style only. It is valid Python.

The claim is that the scalar keyword branch interpolates v into filter_fulltext without escaping quotes, which allows SQL injection. This is pre-existing: the base's scalar-string branch `cond.append(f"{k}='{v}'")` also interpolated v without escaping. The PR moves the same pattern into filter_fulltext without widening it. The values are internal ids and tag names from authenticated KB owners.

The claim is that clmns[v] in the string 'remove' branch may raise KeyError. The only string 'remove' caller passes PAGERANK_FLD (kb_app.py:122), and conf/infinity_mapping.json:32 defines pagerank_fea as a table column. A KeyError needs a column that does not exist, which is speculative.

The claim is that table_instance may be None in the remove path and that old_v[k] may not be a list. table_instance comes from db_instance.get_table, and the pre-existing update already called table_instance.update unconditionally, so None is no new exposure. old_v[k] is always a list, because getFields splits keyword fields (field_keyword) on '###' into lists (infinity_conn.py:661-662).

The claim is that an empty filter makes `filter + ' AND id in (...)'` start with AND. equivalent_condition_to_str never returns an empty string: it returns '1=1' when there are no conditions (infinity_conn.py:108).

The claim is that concatenating ids into the update filter is SQL injection. The ids concatenated into the filter are chunk ids read back from the table itself (row_to_opt), not user input. There is no injection path.

The claim is that scalar keyword values are interpolated into filter_fulltext without escaping apostrophes. This is pre-existing: the base scalar branch `cond.append(f"{k}='{v}'")` (still at infinity_conn.py:103) interpolated the same values unescaped, and the PR only moved keyword scalars into a different unescaped template.

The claim is that get_graph should log when a stored graph fails to deserialize before falling back to a rebuild. That is an observability request, not a defect; the silent `except: continue` is pre-existing.

The claim is that removal-only updates now finish with `table_instance.update(filter, {})`, which Infinity may reject. This is pre-existing: the base branch `del newValue[k]` for a dict 'remove' also left newValue empty and called `table_instance.update(filter, newValue)` with {} for the same callers (document_service.py:106-107, kb_app.py:262-263). Whether Infinity rejects it is not shown.

The claim is that does_graph_contains still checks only graphs with removed_kwd='N', so after a removal every document is treated as absent and re-extracted. That was already the base behaviour (base get_graph returned None and everything was re-extracted). After the first set_graph writes a fresh removed_kwd='N' graph chunk (graphrag/utils.py:447-455), the check works again. There is no new concrete defect.
The claim is that the commented-out getTotal lines are dead code to remove. That is style.
The claim is that the `if not res.total == 0` guard is redundant nesting. That is style; the behaviour is correct.

The claim is that `to_df()` returns a (DataFrame, meta) tuple that getFields cannot handle, so the source-ID removal crashes. getFields unwraps tuples (`if isinstance(res, tuple): res = res[0]`, infinity_conn.py:645-646), so the call works.
The claim is that tags with apostrophes break the scalar filter_fulltext expression. This is pre-existing: the base scalar branch `{k}='{v}'` was equally unescaped (see C3).
The claim is that the list-vs-scalar identifier unwrapping is duplicated three times and should be a shared accessor. That is a refactoring preference.

The claim is that stored ids interpolated into the per-row update filter are unescaped. The ids are uuid chunk ids read back from the table itself (row_to_opt), not attacker- or user-shaped strings, so there is no reachable failure.
The claim is that removing a tag named O'Brien builds an invalid filter because scalar keyword values are unescaped. This is pre-existing: the base scalar branch was equally unescaped (see C3).
The claim is that a list-element removal ends with an empty update that Infinity may reject. This is pre-existing, as for C7: base also called update with an empty dict for these callers.
The claim is that removal-only calls execute `update(filter, {})` after the per-row updates. This is pre-existing, as for C7.

The claim is that a rebuilt graph keeps a removed document's provenance because node and edge attributes come from unchanged content_with_weight. document_service never rewrote content_with_weight on removal, before or after the PR; the graph-level source_id the system actually uses is derived from the updated field (graphrag/utils.py:576, 596, 606). The claimed consequence is attribute-level staleness with no demonstrated user-visible effect.

The claim is that an empty entity_kwd list makes `d["entity_kwd"][0]` raise IndexError. Entity and relation chunks are always written with non-empty entity names (graph_node_to_chunk/graph_edge_to_chunk, graphrag/utils.py:307, 357-358), so the input is contrived.

The claim is that removed-document provenance returns through rebuilt node/edge attributes and graph_merge. This is the same stale-attribute concern as C19; the graph-level source_id is derived from the updated fields, and no concrete wrong outcome is shown.

infiniflow__ragflow@a63caa1.pr_summary: Attempts to fix crashes in the knowledge-graph 'Entity Resolution' path (#6653): entity_resolution.py uses list(component) instead of component.nodes for the sets from nx.connected_components; extractor._merge_graph_nodes stops assigning the None result of list.extend (and drops the nonexistent node 'keywords' merge), extending then deduplicating source_id/keywords in place; graphrag/utils.set_graph deletes removed relation chunks with await trio.to_thread.run_sync instead of passing a sync lambda to nursery.start_soon.
