defects.title: Entity resolution still crashes: change.removed_nodes is a set but _merge_graph_nodes calls .extend on it
defects.statement: With the connected-components fix, every selected merge group now reaches Extractor._merge_graph_nodes, whose first real statement after the length check is `change.removed_nodes.extend(nodes[1:])` (graphrag/general/extractor.py:196). GraphChange.removed_nodes is declared as a set (graphrag/utils.py:41, default_factory=set), and sets have no extend, so every merge raises AttributeError before touching the graph and the Entity Resolution action still fails - the fix for #6653 is incomplete.
defects.evidence: extractor.py:196 `change.removed_nodes.extend(nodes[1:])`; utils.py:41 `removed_nodes: Set[str] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=set)`; entity_resolution.py:114-115 now passes `list(sub_connect_graph)` to `_merge_graph_nodes`, the only caller.
defects.notes: Must say removed_nodes is a set and .extend fails (should be update), so resolution still crashes. Comments about edge bookkeeping in the else branch (C1/C7) or attribute overwrite (C3/C5) are different.

excluded.reason: Claim: accessing .nodes on the sets from nx.connected_components raises AttributeError; use the set directly. That is the pre-PR bug this PR fixes; head line 114 already reads `merging_nodes = list(sub_connect_graph)`.

Claim: the lambda passed to nursery.start_soon captures merging_nodes by reference so all tasks merge the last component. trio's start_soon calls the async function synchronously inside spawn_impl (coroutine_or_error(async_fn)) to create the coroutine, so the lambda runs and binds the current merging_nodes in the same loop iteration; no late-binding bug, and the line is unchanged context.

Claim: start_soon defers the lambda, so every task reads the final merging_nodes and components are merged twice / missed. Same as R2: trio invokes the lambda immediately in start_soon to obtain the coroutine, capturing the current list.
Claim: node1_attrs['source_id'] may raise KeyError; use .get. tidy_graph (graphrag/utils.py:164-176) purges every node lacking description or source_id, so merged nodes always carry source_id.
Claim: build a new combined keywords list instead of mutating in place, for consistency. Style preference; behaviour is correct.

Claim: edge keywords/source_id use list(set(...)) giving nondeterministic order, and existence/list-ness should be checked. Edges always carry list keywords/source_id (tidy_graph sets keywords=[] and purges edges without source_id), nothing depends on their order, and the base already used list(set(...)); speculative.

Claim: replacing nursery.start_soon with an awaited to_thread call serializes relation deletions, degrading performance. The base never ran concurrently: start_soon on a lambda wrapping the synchronous delete raises TypeError (not an async function); the sequential awaited delete is the working minimal fix, not a regression.

Claim: awaiting each thread-backed delete inside an unused nursery serializes deletions; schedule them as tasks or drop the nursery. Same as R6: the baseline crashed rather than running concurrently; slower-than-ideal deletion and an idle nursery are not a defect introduced here.
Claim: the loop serializes all edge deletions (one round trip per edge); schedule via start_soon with bound endpoints or batch. Same as R6/C6 - optimisation request over a previously crashing path.

Claim: in _merge_graph_nodes the else branch adds the redirected edge nodes[0]-neighbor without recording it in change.added_updated_edges, so the relation disappears from the search index. The else branch is unchanged pre-existing code, and at head it is still unreachable because the merge crashes earlier at extractor.py:196 (D1); not introduced or exposed by this PR.

Claim: a transferred relationship created in the else branch (extractor.py:222) is not added to added_updated_edges and vanishes from the relation index. Same as C1: unchanged pre-existing logic that remains unreachable at head because of the removed_nodes.extend crash.

Claim: node0_neighbors is captured once, so when two removed nodes share a neighbor the second add_edge overwrites the first transferred edge's weight/description/keywords. Unchanged pre-existing logic in the else branch, still unreachable at head because the merge crashes at extractor.py:196; not caused by this PR.

Claim: with A lacking an edge to C but B and D both having one, merging D overwrites the A-C edge created from B instead of aggregating. Same pre-existing, still-unreachable else-branch behaviour as C3.
Claim: the repeated extend-and-dedupe lines for keywords and source_id should be a loop. Style/duplication preference with no drift or consequence.
Claim: add regression tests for component merging, attribute merging and relation deletion. A request for tests, not a defect.

appwrite__appwrite@710b8bd.pr_summary: Replaces reads of _APP_DOMAIN with _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN (falling back to _APP_DOMAIN) across the HTTP router/init in app/controllers/general.php, console variables, error view, site template, function/build/execution API endpoint variables, the proxy rule-creation denied-domain lists, VCS comments, the Executor default host header and one e2e test, so a deployment with a separate console domain uses it as the main host (dropping the region. prefix).

defects.title: With a distinct console domain, _APP_DOMAIN is no longer in the rule deny lists and now goes through the router, so a project can claim/hijack the platform's API hostname
defects.statement: The four proxy rule Create actions now deny only the console domain (e.g. Rules/API/Create.php:79-80, Function/Create.php:84-85, Redirect/Create.php:87-88, Site/Create.php:84-85), dropping _APP_DOMAIN when both env vars are set and differ. At the same time general.php:812-814 skips the router only for the console domain, so requests whose Host is _APP_DOMAIN enter router(), which looks up a rule purely by host (general.php:66-75). A project user can create an API/function/site/redirect rule for _APP_DOMAIN and have traffic to the platform's own API hostname served by their project. The e2e test was changed to the same fallback expression, so it no longer checks _APP_DOMAIN.
defects.evidence: Rules/API/Create.php:79-80 `$mainDomain = System::getEnv('_APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN', System::getEnv('_APP_DOMAIN', '')); $deniedDomains[] = $mainDomain;` (base denied _APP_DOMAIN). general.php:812-814 `$mainDomain = System::getEnv('_APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN', ...); if ($host !== $mainDomain || !empty($previewHostname)) { if (router(...))`. router() general.php:66-75 finds the rule by `Query::equal('domain', [$host])`.
defects.notes: Must say _APP_DOMAIN is no longer denied (or reserved) for project rules when a distinct console domain is configured, so the API host can be claimed. Suggesting to deny both domains counts. Reachable only when the two env vars differ. A pure 'add a test' request does not count.

defects.title: With router protection on and a distinct console domain, every request to the _APP_DOMAIN API hostname is now rejected with 'Router protection does not allow accessing Appwrite over this domain'
defects.statement: general.php:812-814 now bypasses router() only for the console domain, so requests addressed to _APP_DOMAIN (the regional API host that SDKs and functions still use) enter router(). With no project rule for that host, router() reaches the protection check at general.php:100-104, which allows only localhost, the internal hostname and _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN, and throws GENERAL_ACCESS_FORBIDDEN. Before the PR the _APP_DOMAIN host never entered router(), so in a split-domain deployment with _APP_OPTIONS_ROUTER_PROTECTION=enabled the whole API on _APP_DOMAIN becomes unreachable.
defects.evidence: general.php:100-101 `if (System::getEnv('_APP_OPTIONS_ROUTER_PROTECTION', 'disabled') === 'enabled') { if ($host !== 'localhost' && $host !== APP_HOSTNAME_INTERNAL && $host !== System::getEnv('_APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN', '')) { throw new AppwriteException(AppwriteException::GENERAL_ACCESS_FORBIDDEN, ...` reached after `$rule->isEmpty()`; general.php:812 main domain is now the console domain.
defects.notes: Must connect the changed main-domain guard with router protection rejecting the _APP_DOMAIN host (API hostname becomes blocked/forbidden). Saying only that _APP_DOMAIN now goes through the router, without the protection/forbidden consequence, is the D1 symptom, not this.

defects.title: Incomplete migration: Certificates worker, OPTIONS and robots/humans handlers still treat _APP_DOMAIN as the main domain, disagreeing with the changed init
defects.statement: general.php:861 now treats the console domain as the main domain when auto-issuing its TLS certificate, but the Certificates worker still identifies the main domain from _APP_DOMAIN only (src/Appwrite/Platform/Workers/Certificates.php:271-279); on an ordinary renewal the console hostname is then validated as a custom domain requiring the CNAME/A targets, so renewal can fail for a valid console DNS setup, and the _APP_DOMAIN host's certificate is no longer auto-issued from the init hook. Likewise the OPTIONS init (general.php:1093-1096) and the /robots.txt and /humans.txt handlers (general.php:1400-1402, 1432-1434) still use _APP_DOMAIN for the same router-bypass decision the PR changed at 812, so preflights and requests on the same host take different routing paths.
defects.evidence: Certificates.php:273 `$envDomain = System::getEnv('_APP_DOMAIN', '');` vs general.php:861 `$envDomain = System::getEnv('_APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN', System::getEnv('_APP_DOMAIN', ''));`; general.php:1093 and 1401 `$mainDomain = System::getEnv('_APP_DOMAIN', '');`.
defects.notes: Counts if a comment names a remaining _APP_DOMAIN main-domain use (Certificates worker main-domain identity, OPTIONS handler, robots/humans handlers) as inconsistent with the change. A bare 'rename everywhere' with no site is a near miss.

excluded.reason: Claims console.php domain validation should use _APP_DOMAIN because _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN is reserved for admin frontend contexts. The check only decides whether the configured main (console) domain is a real public domain to enable the domains UI; validating the console domain is the PR's intent and no such reservation contract exists in the code.
Claims the getEnv fallback is computed twice on consecutive lines in console.php. Style/micro-efficiency with no behavioural consequence.

Claims building APPWRITE_FUNCTION_API_ENDPOINT from _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN points functions at the wrong API. Using the console domain for endpoints is the PR's stated purpose; Vcs/Comment.php already built API/console links from it at the base, and the console domain serves the same Appwrite HTTP app, so no concrete failure is shown.
Claims the build worker's API endpoint may break if the console domain does not serve the API. Same as R3: intended, and nothing in the repo configures a console domain that does not serve /v1.

Claims changing $mainDomain at general.php:812 risks router failures in untested contexts and should be reverted. No mechanism is named; the concrete consequences are D1 and D2, which this note does not state.

Claims an empty fallback in error.phtml yields a malformed 'https://' URL. Only when both variables are unset/empty, a misconfigured install in which the base produced the same URL from an empty _APP_DOMAIN.
Claims empty console and app domains make the execution endpoint 'https:///v1'. Same pre-existing misconfiguration case as R6.
Suggests a more descriptive default for an empty hostname in Builds.php. Same misconfiguration case as R6; not a defect.
Claims Functions worker builds 'https:///v1' when both variables are unset. Same misconfiguration case as R6.

Claims Comment.php's '' default can produce malformed URLs. Comment.php already used the same _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN/_APP_DOMAIN fallback at the base; an explicit '' instead of null concatenates identically.

Claims an empty mainDomain is appended to $deniedDomains unconditionally and domains should be normalised. The unconditional append predates the PR (base did it with _APP_DOMAIN) and an empty entry cannot block a valid non-empty domain; normalisation is a style suggestion.

Claims an explicitly blank _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN yields an empty mainDomain instead of falling back. Setting the variable to an empty string is an operator misconfiguration; _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN is not defined in the shipped env/compose files, so on a normal install it is unset and falls back.

Claims a blank _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN adds '' to $deniedDomains and blocks valid user domains. '' in the deny list only matches an empty domain, which the Domain validator already rejects; and a blank variable is a misconfiguration (see R12).
Claims a defined-but-empty _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN sets an empty Host header in Executor. Misconfiguration case as R12; base had the same behaviour for an empty _APP_DOMAIN.
Asks to confirm that defaulting the executor Host header to the console domain is intended. It is consistent with the PR's endpoint change and names no concrete failure.
Asks for a two-domain e2e configuration checking that both the console hostname and _APP_DOMAIN are rejected as rules. Request for a test; the underlying defect is D1.

Claims docker-compose/compose.phtml do not forward _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN to the builds worker, so the override silently falls back to _APP_DOMAIN. With the variable absent every read falls back to _APP_DOMAIN, i.e. exactly the base behaviour; the variable was already consumed without compose wiring before this PR (router protection, Vcs/Comment.php) and is not a documented self-host setting, so nothing regresses.
Claims the builds worker service does not receive _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN in docker-compose.yml. Same as C4: absent variable falls back to base behaviour; no regression.

Claims supplied Compose configs omit _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN so operators cannot activate the override. Same as C4: deployment wiring gap that leaves base behaviour intact, pre-existing for this variable.
Claims the appwrite service does not forward _APP_CONSOLE_DOMAIN, so executions still get the old endpoint domain. Same as C4.

laravel__framework@0a5238a.pr_summary: In MigrateMakeCommand::writeMigration, the path returned by the migration creator is rewritten to use backslashes on Windows before it is printed in the 'Migration [...] created successfully.' message, matching the GeneratorCommand-based make: commands. Only the console output changes; the file has already been written at that point.

Design preference: the replacement only affects the display string after the file is created (MigrateMakeCommand.php:111-119) and mirrors the existing GeneratorCommand pattern; no incorrect behaviour results.
Asks for a regression assertion on the Windows success-message path. Test-coverage request, not a defect.
Asks for a command-output assertion on the Windows path format since existing tests use NullOutput. Test-coverage request, not a defect.

laravel__framework@180c25f.pr_summary: Test-only PR: rewrites tests/Validation/ValidationEmailRuleTest.php — renames Rule::email() tests, uses named arguments, adds failure messages naming the input, and adds large tables of emails asserting which pass/fail under rfcCompliant(), rfcCompliant(strict: true) and withNativeValidation(), to document behaviour for a docs PR. No production code changes.

defects.title: Escaped-quote fixtures do not contain an escaped quote (PHP single-quote escaping), and a valid IPv6 literal is commented as invalid
defects.statement: In PHP single-quoted strings `\\` becomes one backslash and `\"` stays as two characters, so '"escaped\\\"quote"@example.com' (ValidationEmailRuleTest.php:331, :543) and '"test\\\"quote"@example.com' (:703) evaluate to an address with TWO backslashes before the inner quote: an escaped backslash that closes the quoted local part early, followed by an unquoted `quote"`. The comment 'Escaped quote inside quoted local part' therefore describes an address that is never tested, so the behaviour table this PR adds to document validator behaviour (and back a docs PR) records the wrong case. Likewise 'user@[IPv6:::]' (:337) is commented 'invalid shorthand IPv6' while it is asserted to PASS rfcCompliant(); `::` is the valid unspecified address. Consequence: misleading regression documentation; readers draw wrong conclusions about escaped-quote handling.
defects.evidence: :331 `'"escaped\\\"quote"@example.com',       // Escaped quote inside quoted local part`; :543 same literal and comment; :703 `'"test\\\"quote"@example.com',     // Escaped quote in quoted local part`; :337 `'user@[IPv6:::]',  // invalid shorthand IPv6` inside $emailsThatPassOnRfcCompliantButFailOnStrict, asserted passes(Rule::email()->rfcCompliant()) at :341-345. PHP single-quote strings only unescape \\ and \'.
defects.notes: A comment counts if it says the escaped-quote literal actually yields two backslashes / the quote is not escaped / the fixture does not test what its label says (at :331, :543 or :703), or that the [IPv6:::] comment contradicts the pass assertion. Comments that additionally predict the test will FAIL still count for identifying the mis-encoded fixture, though that prediction is unsupported (the PR's author derived the tables empirically and the PR merged). Generic 'use a data provider' / 'fixtures file' comments do not count.

excluded.reason: Claims testRfcCompliantStrict should be refactored to a data provider instead of hardcoded examples. This is a style preference; the test at :104-143 is correct and nothing behaves wrongly.
Claims the large inline email arrays (:327-339) should move to external fixture files. Style/organisation preference; inline arrays are the convention in this suite and cause no defect.

Claims $emailsThatPassNativeFailRfc is empty so its loop never asserts and should be removed or populated. The empty list is deliberate and labelled (`// none I could find`, :517) in a documentation-style test; an empty loop is harmless and gives no false coverage in the assertions — a style point, not a defect.
Claims the empty native-passes/RFC-fails list and loop (:516) should be removed because it runs no assertions. Same as C1: deliberate, commented, harmless; style only.

Claims withNativeValidation() (filter_var FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL) accepts '"has space"@example.com' so the fails-native assertion at :542/:551-556 will fail. Wrong: PHP's FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL regex restricts quoted-string content to [\x01-\x08\x0B\x0C\x0E-\x1F\x21\x23-\x5B\x5D-\x7F] (excludes \x20 space), so the address is rejected natively and the fixture is in the right group.

At src/valkey-benchmark.c:1998 the free is immediately followed by `return 0;` (idle/test mode exit) and at :2205 by `return 0;` at the end of main, so the pointer is never reused; the PR only renamed the field. valkey-io__valkey@36f37c0.pr_summary: Makes setProtocolError in src/networking.c honour hide-user-data-from-log: when server.hide_user_data_from_log is on, the query-buffer sample logged on a protocol error is replaced by a redaction marker (short buffers) or a marker plus the byte count (long buffers).

defects.title: Long-buffer branch uses the comma operator inside a ternary, so snprintf gets a size_t or a client-controlled buffer pointer as its format string (build break / crash / format-string injection)
defects.statement: At src/networking.c:2771-2776 the author tried to pick between two whole argument lists with `cond ? ("fmt1", a) : ("fmt2", b, c, d, e, f)`. In C these parenthesised lists are comma expressions: the first evaluates to `sdslen(c->querybuf) - c->qb_pos` (size_t), the second to `c->querybuf + sdslen(c->querybuf) - PROTO_DUMP_LEN / 2` (char*). snprintf is called with just that value as its format and no varargs. The conditional mixes integer and pointer (a hard error on modern GCC/clang, at least warnings under -Wall/-Werror); if it builds, the redacted path passes an integer as the format pointer and crashes, and the non-redacted path uses the tail of the client's query buffer as the format string, so a malformed long request containing %s/%n can read garbage, crash or write memory. Both redaction and the original sampled output are lost. Reached on any protocol error with >=128 unconsumed bytes when the error is logged (verbose logging or primary link).
defects.evidence: src/networking.c:2771-2776 `snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), server.hide_user_data_from_log ? ("...Redacted %zu bytes", sdslen(c->querybuf) - c->qb_pos) : ("...'%.*s' (... more %zu bytes ...) '%.*s'", PROTO_DUMP_LEN / 2, ..., c->querybuf + sdslen(c->querybuf) - PROTO_DUMP_LEN / 2));` - the format strings are discarded left operands of the comma operator.
defects.notes: Must identify that the parenthesised groups are comma expressions / the ternary cannot select argument lists (format string lost, wrong args, type mismatch, crash, format-string vulnerability or compile failure). A comment only about redaction wording or ordering does not count. The short-buffer branch (2768-2769) is correct.

excluded.reason: Claims the query buffer is processed before the hide_user_data_from_log check so sensitive data may be exposed, and the check should move earlier. In the short branch the ternary substitutes the redaction string before anything is written or logged; measuring querybuf is not exposure. There is no ordering bug (the real long-branch problem is D1, which this note does not describe).
Asks for regression tests asserting the server log contains no payload for short and long protocol errors. Request for tests, not a defect in itself.

valkey-io__valkey@1379171.pr_summary: Adds a --rdma option to valkey-cli and valkey-benchmark (compiled only under USE_RDMA): it calls libvalkey's valkeyInitiateRdma() and makes valkeyConnectWrapper (cli_common.c) set VALKEY_OPTIONS_SET_RDMA instead of TCP when its new rdma argument is set. valkey-benchmark, because RDMA has no POLLOUT, calls writeHandler directly instead of registering AE_WRITABLE in createClient/resetClient when config.rdma is set. Build plumbing: deps/Makefile builds libvalkey with USE_RDMA=1, src/Makefile links libvalkey_rdma.a (into FINAL_LIBS for BUILD_RDMA=yes, via RDMA_CLIENT_LIBS for module), and CMake sets ENABLE_RDMA for libvalkey and links valkey::valkey_rdma into binaries/modules.

defects.title: valkey-benchmark gates write scheduling on the global config.rdma, so non-RDMA connections (cluster mode, -s unix socket) never get AE_WRITABLE and stall after a partial write
defects.statement: createClient (valkey-benchmark.c:832-838) and resetClient (:395-399) skip aeCreateFileEvent(AE_WRITABLE) and call writeHandler directly whenever config.rdma is set, regardless of the transport the client actually uses. But cluster clients are connected with rdma=0 (:654-674 only sets rdma for the non-cluster branch) and -s clients use valkeyConnectUnixWrapper, i.e. plain TCP/unix sockets. On those sockets writeHandler can do a partial write (`c->written += nwritten; return;` at :613-615) expecting the AE_WRITABLE event to resume it — which is never registered, so the client never finishes its request and the benchmark hangs; and for a non-blocking TCP connect still in progress, the direct call spins in writeHandler's while(1) on EAGAIN.
defects.evidence: :395 `if (config.rdma) { writeHandler(el, c->context->fd, c, 0); ...} else { aeCreateFileEvent(el, ..., AE_WRITABLE, writeHandler, c); }`; :654 `int rdma = 0;` and only `rdma = config.rdma;` in the `!is_cluster_client` branch (:661); writeHandler :613 `} else if (nwritten > 0) { c->written += nwritten; return; }` relies on a later AE_WRITABLE callback.
defects.notes: Must say that the direct-writeHandler path is keyed on config.rdma rather than on whether this client's connection is RDMA, so cluster/unix-socket clients with --rdma lose AE_WRITABLE (hang on partial write / busy loop). Merely saying 'RDMA is not used in cluster mode' is D2, not this.

defects.title: valkey-benchmark --rdma is silently ignored for cluster mode and for the fcall test's setup connection
defects.statement: All cluster-path connections pass rdma=0 (fetchClusterConfiguration :1104, fetchClusterSlotsConfiguration :1217, per-node getServerConfig :1832, and cluster clients in createClient :654-674), and the fcall test's FUNCTION LOAD connection hard-codes 0 (:2079) even in standalone mode. With --rdma the user gets TCP connections without any warning (cluster benchmarks run entirely over TCP), and against a server that only accepts RDMA on that port the fcall test exits with 'Could not connect'. The fcall test is part of the default suite (test_is_selected returns 1 when no -t is given, :1713-1717), so a plain `valkey-benchmark --rdma` against an RDMA-only endpoint aborts mid-suite.
defects.evidence: :2079 `valkeyContext *ctx = getValkeyContext(config.conn_info.hostip, config.conn_info.hostport, NULL, 0);` while the standalone CONFIG fetch at :1842 passes config.rdma.
defects.notes: Must point at a connection that ignores --rdma (fcall ctx, or cluster connections). R7 (document port requirement) does not count. Comments about the cluster discovery/slot refresh/per-node/cluster-worker connections using TCP despite --rdma, or the FCALL FUNCTION LOAD connection passing 0, all count.

defects.title: valkey-cli --rdma --pipe hangs: pipeMode waits for AE_WRITABLE on the RDMA completion-channel fd, which never reports POLLOUT
defects.statement: With --rdma, cliConnect connects via valkeyConnectWrapper(..., config.rdma) (valkey-cli.c:1645) and libvalkey sets context->fd to the RDMA completion channel fd (deps/libvalkey/src/rdma.c:744). pipeMode (valkey-cli.c:8518ff) only writes stdin data when aeWait(context->fd, AE_READABLE|AE_WRITABLE, 1000) reports AE_WRITABLE; libvalkey documents that RDMA has no POLLOUT (rdma.c:617) and the completion channel only ever signals readable. So pipe mode never sends anything, never reaches EOF, and loops forever. The PR itself works around this in valkey-benchmark (direct writeHandler call, comment 'can't be invoked by AE_WRITABLE') but accepts --rdma with --pipe in valkey-cli unchanged.
defects.evidence: valkey-cli.c pipeMode: `if (!eof || obuf_len != 0) mask |= AE_WRITABLE; mask = aeWait(context->fd, mask, 1000);` and writes only under `if (mask & AE_WRITABLE)`; rdma.c:744 `c->fd = ctx->comp_channel->fd;`; rdma.c:617 `/* RDMA has no POLLOUT event supported ... */`; valkey-benchmark.c:396 comment `RDMA context always writable, but it can't be invoked by AE_WRITABLE`.
defects.notes: Must say that --rdma combined with --pipe (pipe mode) cannot write/hangs because the RDMA fd never becomes writable (no POLLOUT). Keepalive-on-RDMA-fd comments (C8) do not count.

defects.title: BUILD_RDMA=module links the RDMA client libs into the TLS module (valkey-tls.so)
defects.statement: src/Makefile:519 appends $(RDMA_CLIENT_LIBS) (= libvalkey_rdma.a plus -lrdmacm -libverbs, :352) to the valkey-tls.so link line. The TLS module uses no RDMA code; the change only adds an unneeded dependency on librdmacm/libibverbs to the TLS module (a load-time dependency where the linker does not use --as-needed). A copy-paste of the cli/benchmark change onto the wrong target.
defects.evidence: :519 `$(QUIET_CC)$(CC) -o $@ tls.c -shared -fPIC $(TLS_MODULE_CFLAGS) $(TLS_CLIENT_LIBS) $(RDMA_CLIENT_LIBS)`; :352 `RDMA_CLIENT_LIBS = ../deps/libvalkey/lib/libvalkey_rdma.a $(RDMA_LIBS)`.
defects.notes: Must identify the TLS module target getting RDMA libs. The duplicate $(RDMA_LIBS) in FINAL_LIBS (R4) is a different, harmless issue.

defects.title: With --rdma, benchmark clients send their first request at creation time, before config.start, skewing first-request latency
defects.statement: In createClient (:832-835) the RDMA path calls writeHandler immediately, which stamps c->start (:597) and sends the request while benchmark() is still creating the remaining clients (createMissingClients, :999-1000) and before config.start (:1002). The reply is only read once aeMain runs, so each early client's first latency includes the connection setup of all later clients (RDMA connects are slow), inflating reported latency percentiles/max; on TCP the first write happens from the event loop after config.start.
defects.evidence: writeHandler :597 `c->start = ustime();`; readHandler :478 `if (c->latency < 0) c->latency = ustime() - (c->start);`; benchmark(): createClient/createMissingClients then `config.start = mstime();` then aeMain.
defects.notes: Must say the RDMA direct write in createClient happens before the event loop / benchmark start, distorting latency or timing.

defects.title: RDMA path in createClient calls writeHandler before the client is added to config.clients, so a write error frees an unlisted client (assert abort / use-after-free)
defects.statement: createClient (valkey-benchmark.c:832-835) now calls writeHandler synchronously when config.rdma is set, before listAddNodeTail(config.clients, c) and the liveclients increment (:842-843). If the first write fails with a non-EAGAIN error, writeHandler calls freeClient(c) (:609-611), which frees c, decrements liveclients and then does `ln = listSearchKey(config.clients, c); assert(ln != NULL);` (:381-383) — the client is not in the list, so the benchmark aborts; were the assert compiled out, createClient would go on to add and dereference the freed pointer (:842-845). In the base code the first write always ran from the event loop after the client was listed, so a write error just dropped the client.
defects.evidence: createClient: `if (config.rdma) { writeHandler(el, c->context->fd, c, 0); } ...` followed by `listAddNodeTail(config.clients, c);`; writeHandler: `if (nwritten == -1 && errno != EAGAIN) { ... freeClient(c); return; }`; freeClient: `ln = listSearchKey(config.clients, c); assert(ln != NULL);`.
defects.notes: Must say the immediate writeHandler call happens before the client is registered in config.clients so the error path's freeClient asserts / uses a freed client. Error-path only, hence low.

excluded.reason: Asks for a comment/TODO explaining why valkey_rdma is linked before valkey in CMake. Request for an explanatory comment/TODO on the link order; no defect.

Says valkey_build_and_install_module is unused and the RDMA logic added to it should be removed. valkey_build_and_install_module is indeed unused (only its definition at ValkeySetup.cmake:110), but that is pre-existing; adding RDMA linkage to it has no effect. Cleanup suggestion, not a defect.

Says the ENABLE_RDMA cache description 'Should we test RDMA connections' is misworded. Cache-variable help string copied from the ENABLE_TLS pattern; the variable is unset from the cache right after (deps/CMakeLists.txt:38). Wording only.
Says $(RDMA_LIBS) is added to FINAL_LIBS twice and may cause link problems. Listing -lrdmacm -libverbs twice on a link line is harmless (shared libs, no duplicate-symbol or ordering problem).

Says the rdma parameter of valkeyConnectWrapper is silently ignored when USE_RDMA is not compiled in. rdma can only be non-zero when --rdma was parsed, which exists only under #ifdef USE_RDMA, and cli_common.c is compiled with the same flags; the non-USE_RDMA fallthrough is unreachable.
Says getValkeyContext's rdma parameter is redundant and config.rdma should be used instead. Design preference; passing rdma explicitly is what lets callers choose TCP for cluster/fcall connections.
Asks to document that RDMA cluster operation requires the TCP port to equal the RDMA port. Documentation request, not a code defect.
Says config.rdma in valkey-cli is not explicitly initialised. config is a file-scope `static struct config {...} config;` (valkey-cli.c:217-290), zero-initialised by the C standard.

Says passing --rdma multiple times calls valkeyInitiateRdma() repeatedly. valkeyInitiateRdma just calls valkeyContextRegisterFuncs and returns VALKEY_OK (deps/libvalkey/src/rdma.c:994-998); repeated calls are idempotent.

Says calling valkeyInitiateRdma() and exiting inside option parsing is too rigid. Exiting on option errors during parsing matches the rest of parseOptions; valkeyInitiateRdma cannot fail. Design preference.
Says the usage text 'a RDMA connection' should read 'an RDMA connection'. Grammar nit in usage text ('a RDMA'); trivial.
Asks for tests exercising valkey-cli --rdma in command and pipe modes. A test request, not a defect (the pipe-mode hang itself is D3).
Asks for RDMA test coverage of valkey-benchmark. A test request, not a defect.
Asks for README examples of CLI/benchmark RDMA invocation. A documentation request, not a defect.

Asks to remove the RDMA linkage added to the unused valkey_build_and_install_module CMake macro. The macro has no callers (only its definition in ValkeySetup.cmake), so the addition has no effect; cleanup only.

Says cliConnect/clusterManagerNodeConnect pass the RDMA completion-channel fd to anetKeepAlive, which sets TCP socket options and will fail. anetKeepAlive's return value is ignored at valkey-cli.c:1679 and :4013, so setsockopt failing with ENOTSOCK has no effect on the connection; TCP keepalive is irrelevant to RDMA. No observable defect.

Says --rdma and --tls can be combined and TLS initialisation then fails because privctx is occupied, so the option combination should be rejected. TLS over an RDMA context is a nonsensical user configuration; libvalkey's TLS init returns an error when privctx is already set (deps/libvalkey/src/tls.c:357) and valkey-cli/benchmark report 'Could not negotiate a TLS connection' and exit. A clearer up-front error is a usability suggestion, not a defect.

Says resetClient calls writeHandler before clearing c->written/c->pending so the handler sees the previous request as already written and reused RDMA clients stop sending. writeHandler never advances c->written on a complete write (valkey-benchmark.c:616-619 only registers the read handler), so after a fully written request c->written is still 0 and the handler re-initialises and sends the next request; pending is only consumed later by readHandler, after it has been reset. RDMA writes are never partial (valkeyRdmaWrite loops until all data is written, rdma.c:573-615), so the claimed stall does not occur.

Says that after a partially written request, the direct writeHandler call in resetClient runs with a stale nonzero c->written and sends an incomplete next request. A nonzero c->written can only persist after a partial write that was later resumed; with config.rdma no AE_WRITABLE event is ever registered to resume one, so the client stalls first (that stall is D1), and RDMA writes themselves are never partial (rdma.c:573-615). The described corrupted-request outcome is unreachable.

valkey-io__valkey@ecb3abd.pr_summary: Fixes an ACL regression from the dict-to-hashtable conversion: server.commands and server.orig_commands shared the serverCommand struct and both keyed on cmd->fullname, so rename-command changed the key under orig_commands and ACL rules by original name stopped resolving. Adds serverCommand.current_name (aliasing fullname until renamed), keys server.commands on current_name and orig_commands on fullname, makes rename-command update only current_name, marks many acl.c helpers static and removes dead ACL code, and adds a tcl test with renamed commands.

defects.title: Renamed commands are now reported under their ORIGINAL name in COMMAND INFO/LIST/DOCS, INFO commandstats/latencystats and module APIs
defects.statement: Before this PR rename-command replaced cmd->fullname with the new name (base config.c: `sdsfree(cmd->fullname); cmd->fullname = sdsdup(argv[2]);`), so every path printing fullname showed the callable name. Now rename only sets current_name (config.c:545-552) and fullname keeps the original, while all user-facing sites still read fullname: addReplyCommandInfo (server.c:5017), COMMAND LIST with/without FILTERBY PATTERN (server.c:5206,5219), COMMAND DOCS, INFO commandstats/latencystats `cmdstat_%s` (server.c:5455,5490), LATENCY HISTOGRAM, VM_GetCurrentCommandName. After `rename-command SET VSET`, discovery advertises `set` (not executable), `COMMAND LIST FILTERBY PATTERN vset` misses it, and metrics move from cmdstat_vset to cmdstat_set; clients building their command table from COMMAND no longer find the renamed command.
defects.evidence: head config.c:552 `cmd->current_name = sdsdup(argv[2]);` with fullname untouched vs base `cmd->fullname = sdsdup(argv[2]);`. server.c:5017 `addReplyBulkCBuffer(c, cmd->fullname, sdslen(cmd->fullname));`; server.c:5455 `getSafeInfoString(c->fullname, ...)`. current_name is read only in config.c, module.c:1406, server.c:524/3217.
defects.notes: Must say that after a rename, introspection (COMMAND INFO/LIST/DOCS, pattern filter), stats/metrics or the module current-command API still use fullname, i.e. the original rather than the renamed/callable name. Comments about the ACL fix itself, current_name memory, or the acl.c cleanup do not count.

defects.title: A module registering a builtin's original name after that builtin was renamed now aborts the server
defects.statement: VM_CreateCommand checks availability only against server.commands (module.c:1364 lookupCommandByCString), which after `rename-command SET VSET` no longer contains `set`; it then does `serverAssert(hashtableAdd(server.orig_commands, cp->serverCmd))` (module.c:1373). orig_commands is now correctly keyed on fullname (server.c originalCommandSetType), so the builtin still occupies `set` there and the add fails, hitting serverAssert and crashing at module load. At the merge base the stale key let this add succeed, so this PR newly exposes the abort (e.g. renaming a builtin to replace it with a module implementation).
defects.evidence: module.c:1364 `if (lookupCommandByCString(name) != NULL) return VALKEYMODULE_ERR;`; :1373 `serverAssert(hashtableAdd(server.orig_commands, cp->serverCmd));`; server.c `originalCommandSetType = {.entryGetKey = hashtableCommandGetOriginalName, ...}`.
defects.notes: Must identify that the module name check consults only the active table while orig_commands still holds the original builtin name, so the orig_commands insert assert fails/crashes.

excluded.reason: Points out the typo 'its' vs 'it's' in the new config.c comment. Comment spelling only; no functional or maintainability consequence.
Asks to split the long Tcl rename list in the new test across lines. Formatting preference, not a defect.

Claims renaming a command and then disabling it with an empty name leaks the separately allocated current_name. The serverCommand stays alive in server.orig_commands and still references current_name, and rename-command runs once at config load; nothing unreachable accumulates.

Claims the '-ping' test is vacuous because the user never had PING. The regression made `ACL setuser ... -ping` fail to resolve the original name (erroring the command), so the test does exercise the fix; test-quality opinion.
Asks to drop GETUSER compaction cases duplicated from earlier in acl.tcl. Test duplication/style, not a defect.

Claims native subcommands leave current_name NULL, contradicting the new field comment. Subcommands are never renamed nor keyed by current_name (they use subcommandSetType on declared_name), so no current reader is affected; speculative future risk.

valkey-io__valkey@8b2137d.pr_summary: Offloads writes to ONLINE replica clients to IO threads: writeToReplica is split into a write step (runnable in an IO thread, bounded by io_last_reply_block/io_last_bufpos captured in trySendWriteToIOThreads, and using writev across multiple replication buffer blocks) and postWriteToReplica (main thread: refcount/ref_block_pos advance, stats, backlog trim). Primary-client reads/writes are no longer excluded from IO-thread offload (READ_FLAGS_PRIMARY skips query-buffer trimming in the IO thread), replicationCachePrimary waits for in-flight IO and resets IO state, client.nwritten becomes ssize_t, the multibulk parser uses memchr instead of strchr, and unit + integration tests are added.

defects.title: writeToReplica submits a zero-length first iovec when the replica sits at the end of a full block, breaking TLS (and iovcnt==1) connections
defects.statement: postWriteToReplica (src/networking.c:2010-2040) only advances ref_repl_buf_node when a next node exists, so a replica that has sent everything leaves ref_block_pos == used on the (full) tail block. feedReplicationBuffer (src/replication.c:445-472) then appends a new block without moving already-attached replicas. On the next write the multi-block loop in writeToReplica (src/networking.c:2078-2089) builds iov[0] with start = ref_block_pos and len = used - start = 0, i.e. an empty first vector, and there is no skip of empty blocks (the old per-block loop skipped them via `if (o->used > c->ref_block_pos)`). For a TLS replica, connTLSWritev (src/tls.c:923-931) writes each iov separately when the batch exceeds NET_MAX_WRITES_PER_EVENT and returns on the first non-positive SSL_write; SSL_write of 0 bytes returns <= 0, so writeToReplica sets WRITE_FLAGS_WRITE_ERROR and makes no progress (replica disconnected via freeClientAsync, or stalled if reported as EAGAIN) every time. On a connection with iovcnt == 1 the loop stops after the empty vector, total_bytes == 0 and the function returns without writing, so the replica never progresses. Affects both the main-thread and IO-thread paths since both go through writeToReplica.
defects.evidence: networking.c:2080-2085 `size_t start = (cur_node == first_node) ? c->ref_block_pos : 0; size_t len = (cur_node == last_node) ? bufpos : cur_block->used; len -= start; iov[iovcnt].iov_base = ...; iov[iovcnt].iov_len = len;` with no len==0 skip; postWriteToReplica `while (nwritten >= o->used) { next = listNextNode(curr); if (!next) break; ...}` leaves ref_block_pos == used at the tail; replication.c:445-472 creates a new tail node and only attaches replicas whose ref_repl_buf_node == NULL; tls.c:926-927 `ssize_t sent = connTLSWrite(conn_, iov[i].iov_base, iov[i].iov_len); if (sent <= 0) return tot_sent > 0 ? tot_sent : sent;`.
defects.notes: A comment must identify that an exhausted first block (ref_block_pos == used) yields an empty/zero-length iovec in writeToReplica and that this stalls or errors replication (TLS per-iov write, or iovcnt==1 no-progress loop). Generic remarks about partial-iovec bookkeeping duplication, or about ssize_t/int widths, do not count.

excluded.reason: Claims that putting READ_FLAGS_PRIMARY into the per-read read_flags bitmask conflates persistent client state with transient flags. This is a design opinion: READ_FLAGS_PRIMARY already exists and processInputBuffer already sets it per-parse (networking.c:3219 `c->read_flags = c->flag.primary ? READ_FLAGS_PRIMARY : 0;`); the PR only sets it on the IO-thread path too. No behavioural defect.

Claims listLast(server.repl_buffer_blocks) may be NULL and is dereferenced at io_threads.c:397. Unreachable: trySendWriteToIOThreads returns early unless clientHasPendingReplies(c), which for a replica requires a non-NULL ref_repl_buf_node, i.e. a non-empty repl_buffer_blocks list.
Questions the need for the `if (!last_node) return;` NULL check in writeToReplica's main-thread branch. Harmless defensive redundancy, not a defect.

Claims postWriteToReplica may dereference a NULL ref_repl_buf_node and add a negative nwritten. It returns immediately when c->nwritten <= 0 (networking.c:2011), and a positive nwritten only arises from writing bytes starting at a non-NULL ref_repl_buf_node, so neither case is reachable.

Claims bufpos - c->ref_block_pos in the single-block path can underflow into a huge write length. ref_block_pos only advances by bytes actually written up to the captured bufpos, and a block's used never shrinks, so bufpos >= ref_block_pos always holds; with no pending bytes clientHasPendingReplies prevents the call.

Claims `int nwritten = connWritev(...)` should be ssize_t, totals may overflow, and conn->iovcnt should be asserted >0. connWritev itself returns int (same pattern as writevToClient), a single non-blocking writev cannot approach INT_MAX in practice, and iovcnt is initialised to IOV_MAX (or >=1 for RDMA) for every connection. Robustness nit, no reachable failure.

Suggests guarding `sdslen(c->querybuf) - c->qb_pos` against underflow if qb_pos > sdslen before memchr. qb_pos <= sdslen is an invariant asserted elsewhere (trimClientQueryBuffer); the scenario requires prior corruption and the memchr change is an improvement.
Asks to rename 'master' to 'primary' in the new tcl test. Inclusive-naming style preference, not a defect.

Asks to share the partial-iovec advancement loop between writeToReplica and writevToClient to avoid future divergence. Refactoring/duplication preference; the two loops are currently both correct and no rule has drifted.
Asks to share or document the duplicated partial-write iovec advancement between the replica and ordinary client writers. Same refactoring preference as C1; no present defect.

Claims test_postWriteToReplica leaves server.repl_backlog / server.repl_buffer_blocks dangling so later tests or createReplicationBacklog will crash. No later unit test in the binary touches these globals (the remaining networking tests exercise argv rewriting), so the dangling pointers are never used; test hygiene only.

Claims the unit test overwrites server.repl_buffer_blocks without saving/releasing a prior list, leaking it. In the unit-test binary the server struct is zero-initialised and nothing creates that list beforehand, so nothing is leaked or lost; test hygiene only.

Claims the tcl test's io_threaded_writes_processed >= old+3 assertion can pass without the replica write being offloaded because it counts all clients. Between the two INFO captures the master performs exactly the first INFO reply, the SET reply and the replica propagation write, so the +3 lower bound does depend on the replica write; test-strength suggestion, not a defect in the PR's code.

Same claim as C4: the new replication test cannot distinguish replica write offload from ordinary client writes. As for C4, the +3 bound requires the replica write; a request for a stronger test is not a defect.
Suggests extracting a common fixture for the repeated mock-connection setup in the new unit tests. Test-code style preference.

Asks whether writes to the upstream primary should really be offloaded now that the primary exclusion was removed. Deliberate scope: the PR adds waitForClientIO/resetClientIOState in replicationCachePrimary to support it; a scope question, no concrete failure shown.

Asks whether offloading reads from the upstream primary is intended given the description says replica reads stay on the main thread. The description refers to replica clients; primary read offload is deliberately supported via READ_FLAGS_PRIMARY and main-thread repl_applied trimming. Scope question, not a defect.

Asks to make writeToReplica's write boundary an explicit caller contract instead of switching on inMainThread(). Design preference mirroring the existing _writeToClient pattern (networking.c:2241-2250); no defect.

Asks to update the server.h comments on io_last_reply_block/io_last_bufpos since they now also hold a replication buffer node, and to make the variant explicit. The comments still describe the last block/position captured for the IO thread and the variant is disambiguated by client type/WRITE_FLAGS_IS_REPLICA; documentation nit, no behavioural consequence.

Claims replica writes in an IO job are unbounded (no NET_MAX_WRITES_PER_EVENT cap) and can starve other clients on the worker. The pre-PR writeToReplica loop was equally unbounded (it wrote until EAGAIN on the main thread); moving it to a worker does not make fairness worse. Not a regression.

Claims an offloaded primary read can keep the IO worker's thread_shared_qb because trimming is skipped for READ_FLAGS_PRIMARY. The primary client always owns a private query buffer (replication.c:1917 `server.primary->querybuf = sdsempty();`, never set to NULL for primaries — server.c:882 excludes primaries), so readToQueryBuf never assigns thread_shared_qb to it; unreachable.

facebook__react@b045f18.pr_summary: Introduces a dedicated REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE symbol ('react.activity') and ActivityComponent work tag 31 so unstable_Activity is no longer an alias of REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE. The reconciler creates an ActivityComponent fiber wrapping an internal Offscreen child (updateActivityComponent), completeWork bubbles it like a plain wrapper, Fizz renders Activity through the Offscreen path, isValidElementType accepts it, getComponentNameFromFiber names it, and React DevTools learns the tag (named 'Activity', filtered from the tree).

defects.title: DevTools imports the reconciler's ActivityComponent constant instead of using its version-aware ReactTypeOfWork map, leaving the new map entries dead
defects.statement: react-devtools-shared supports many React versions and maps work tags per version through getInternalReactConstants().ReactTypeOfWork, which the PR extends with `ActivityComponent: 31` / `-1` in every version branch (renderer.js:389,426,463,500,537). But those entries are never destructured; instead renderer.js:149 adds a runtime import `import {ActivityComponent} from 'react-reconciler/src/ReactWorkTags'` (the only non-type reconciler import in the DevTools backend) and uses that constant in the display-name switch (renderer.js:631) and shouldFilterFiber (renderer.js:1491). The tag is hard-coded to the current reconciler's numbering for every attached renderer regardless of version, bypassing the -1 guards the PR itself wrote for older versions; any renderer whose tag 31 means something else would be named/hidden as Activity, and the map entries are dead code.
defects.evidence: renderer.js:149 `import {ActivityComponent} from 'react-reconciler/src/ReactWorkTags';`; renderer.js:389 `ActivityComponent: 31,` and :426/463/500/537 `ActivityComponent: -1`; the destructurings `} = ReactTypeOfWork;` at renderer.js:581 and :928 do not include ActivityComponent. git grep of react-devtools-shared/src for 'react-reconciler' shows every other hit is `import type`.
defects.notes: A comment must say DevTools should take ActivityComponent from the version-specific ReactTypeOfWork map (destructure it) rather than importing the reconciler's constant / crossing the package boundary into reconciler internals. Saying Activity should be visible in DevTools (R2) or asking for a comment on the tag does not count.

excluded.reason: Claims ActivityComponent must be visible in DevTools and should not be added to the hidden-fiber list. Before this PR unstable_Activity created an Offscreen fiber, which shouldFilterFiber already hid (OffscreenComponent case at renderer.js ~1493); hiding the new wrapper preserves prior DevTools behaviour of this refactor, a product preference rather than a regression.

Claims the Offscreen case in createFiberFromTypeAndProps is now redundant and should be removed. REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE remains a distinct internal type still used by createFiberFromOffscreen, Suspense/LegacyHidden, Fizz and isValidElementType; nothing is redundant.

Claims setting fiber.elementType = REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE in createFiberFromActivity overrides the element's real type (e.g. lazy) and breaks reconciliation. createFiberFromActivity is only reached from `case REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE` in createFiberFromTypeAndProps (ReactFiber.js:600), so elementType equals the element type; the same pattern is used by createFiberFromOffscreen/Suspense, and lazy resolves to the symbol before this point.

Claims createFiberFromActivity's pendingProps typed as OffscreenProps weakens type safety. Activity's props are exactly {mode, children}, matching OffscreenProps; a typing nit with no incorrect behaviour.

Claims createFiberFromActivity should initialize stateNode with an OffscreenInstance like createFiberFromOffscreen. The Activity fiber is a plain wrapper; its Offscreen child is created by mountWorkInProgressOffscreenFiber -> createFiberFromOffscreen, which sets the instance; the wrapper needs none.
Suggests extracting a shared helper because updateActivityComponent duplicates Offscreen mounting logic. Refactor preference mirroring the Suspense primary-child pattern; no defect.

Asks whether updateActivityComponent needs a feature flag and whether always creating an Offscreen child is intended. Questions only; wrapping Offscreen is the stated design and no enableActivity flag exists.
Objects to the `(current.child: any)` cast in updateActivityComponent. Flow cast identical to updateSuspensePrimaryChildren's pattern; style only.
Asks for a comment explaining ActivityComponent in ReactWorkTags.js. Documentation request; other tags carry no comments either.
Suggests reusing a shared constant instead of hardcoding 'Activity' in getComponentNameFromFiber. Style; neighbouring cases hardcode 'Cache', 'Offscreen' etc.

Asks to confirm that rendering REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE via renderOffscreen in Fizz is intended. It is identical to prior behaviour when unstable_Activity was REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE; a confirmation request, no defect.
Claims REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE is unnecessary and should be removed. It is still used by Fizz, createFiberFromOffscreen elementType and isValidElementType, and this PR does not change that; wrong.

Asks to double-check the symbol's stability and that other codepaths expecting Offscreen do not break, plus add tests. Generic verification/test request; the relevant paths (Fizz, isValidElementType, reconciler) were updated and no breakage was found.
Suggests placing REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE before REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE alphabetically. Ordering style; the file is not alphabetical.

Claims the REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE check in isValidElementType should be gated by an enableActivity flag. No such flag exists in shared/ReactFeatureFlags.js and REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE, which Activity previously aliased, was accepted unconditionally; no behaviour change.

Claims shared/getComponentNameFromType has no case for REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE so type-based diagnostics lose the Activity name. Pre-existing: before the PR unstable_Activity was REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE, for which getComponentNameFromType (shared/getComponentNameFromType.js:73-96) also returned null; the PR makes nothing worse.

Asks for an Activity built-in frame in ReactFiberComponentStack and DevToolsFiberComponentStack. Before the PR the Activity element was an Offscreen fiber, which describeFiber also rendered as '' (default case); no regression, a feature request.

Claims shared getComponentNameFromType should recognise REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE since Fizz uses it for element names. Same pre-existing gap as for REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE, which unstable_Activity aliased before the PR and which also returned null; not introduced by this change.

Claims Fizz replay loses Activity identity because getComponentNameFromType returns null, so replayElement's name-mismatch check (ReactFizzServer.js:2441) is skipped. Before the PR unstable_Activity was REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE whose name was likewise null, so the replay check behaved identically; pre-existing, not newly exposed.
Asks for a reconciler test pinning that an Activity fiber wraps a distinct Offscreen child. Test request, not a defect.

facebook__react@be58f26.pr_summary: Changes ensureFormComponentIsStateful in ReactFiberHooks.js so a host form fiber whose memoizedState exists but has no second (reset-state) hook is treated as not yet upgraded and gets a fresh two-hook list (avoiding the null `.next` crash in requestFormReset on rapid double submission). Adds a ReactDOMForm test that submits a form twice in rapid succession and expects the action to run twice.

defects.title: New test committed as `it.only`, skipping every other ReactDOMForm test (and failing lint)
defects.statement: packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMForm-test.js:1673 declares the new test with `it.only(...)`, so Jest runs only this test in the file and the other ReactDOMForm tests are skipped in CI; regressions in them go unnoticed. The repo's ESLint config enables jest/no-focused-tests for __tests__ files (turned off only for setup/helper files), so lint fails as well.
defects.evidence: packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMForm-test.js:1673 `it.only('multiple form submissions in rapid succession do not throw', async () => {`; .eslintrc.js extends plugin:jest/recommended and disables 'jest/no-focused-tests' only for setupTests/setupEnv/helper files.
defects.notes: Must point out the leftover `.only` (focused test) and that it skips the rest of the file / fails lint.

defects.title: Fix replaces a partial form hook list wholesale, discarding the existing transition-status hook and its queue
defects.statement: With the new condition at packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberHooks.js:3264, a form fiber whose memoizedState holds the transition-status hook but whose `.next` is null (the partial list left when TransitionAwareHostComponent suspends in useThenable after its first useState, packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberHooks.js:868-876) is treated as never upgraded: a brand-new stateHook/resetStateHook pair is assigned to both fiber and alternate (packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberHooks.js:3318-3323). The existing hook's memoizedState (the pending thenable of the earlier submission) and its queue — into which the earlier startHostTransition dispatches its completion — are orphaned, so that submission's pending status/updates can be lost. The crash symptom is masked instead of repairing only the missing reset hook.
defects.evidence: packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberHooks.js:3264 `if (existingStateHook !== null && existingStateHook.next !== null) { return existingStateHook; }`; otherwise :3318 `formFiber.memoizedState = stateHook;` and `alternate.memoizedState = stateHook;` overwrite the existing hook unconditionally; startHostTransition captures `stateHook.queue` for the transition.
defects.notes: Must say the new condition ignores/discards the existing single-hook state (pending status / queue) rather than reusing it or only adding the missing reset hook. A generic 'is this the right fix?' without the state-discard mechanism does not count; R1 counts.

excluded.reason: Says the test may not actually make the two submissions overlap because the action timer and the resubmit delay are both 1 ms and act flushes timers, so it only proves both actions ran. Test-effectiveness speculation that cannot be verified by reading (ordering depends on act/timer and transition-commit scheduling); a request for a stronger test, not a defect in shipped code.

bitcoin__bitcoin@4ba2e48.pr_summary: Makes BLOCK_FAILED_CHILD and m_best_header always correct: InvalidateBlock caches non-main-chain blocks by fork point and by work so that, per disconnected block, it marks side-branch descendants BLOCK_FAILED_CHILD (replacing a pre-existing BLOCK_FAILED_VALID) and recomputes m_best_header; AcceptBlock calls InvalidChainFound when a block fails CheckBlock/ContextualCheckBlock. With descendants now always marked, the m_failed_blocks set and its AcceptBlockHeader descendant walk are removed, and CheckBlockIndex gains asserts that m_best_header is not failed, that every descendant of an invalid block carries a failure flag, and that no non-failed block has more work than m_best_header.

defects.title: InvalidateBlock changes nStatus of side-branch descendants without adding them to m_dirty_blockindex, so the change is never flushed to disk
defects.statement: The new loop at validation.cpp:3767-3772 rewrites `it->second->nStatus = (nStatus & ~BLOCK_FAILED_VALID) | BLOCK_FAILED_CHILD` for every cached descendant but, unlike every other status write in this function (3757, 3764, 3817), never calls `m_blockman.m_dirty_blockindex.insert(...)`. In-memory and on-disk block index diverge: the FAILED_CHILD marking is not persisted, and where a pre-existing BLOCK_FAILED_VALID was replaced by BLOCK_FAILED_CHILD the disk still holds FAILED_VALID, so after a restart the block reloads with the old flag. (FAILED_CHILD itself is re-derived at load, which limits the impact.)
defects.evidence: validation.cpp:3771 `it->second->nStatus = (it->second->nStatus & ~BLOCK_FAILED_VALID) | BLOCK_FAILED_CHILD;` with no dirty insert; compare :3763-3764 `to_mark_failed->nStatus = ... | BLOCK_FAILED_CHILD; m_blockman.m_dirty_blockindex.insert(to_mark_failed);`.
defects.notes: Must say the modified descendant entries are not added to m_dirty_blockindex / the status change is not persisted.

defects.title: Headers accepted while InvalidateBlock has released cs_main are missing from the one-time caches, so the new CheckBlockIndex asserts can fire before the final InvalidChainFound sweep
defects.statement: cand_invalid_descendants and best_header_blocks_by_work are built once under cs_main (validation.cpp:3698-3720), but the disconnect loop re-acquires cs_main per iteration (3729-3731), so AcceptBlockHeader can add a header in between (e.g. a child of a still-active block that will be disconnected later, or a competing valid header). Such a header is never marked BLOCK_FAILED_CHILD when its parent is disconnected, nor considered by the best-header fallback (3775-3788). m_chainman.CheckBlockIndex() (3795) runs before the final InvalidChainFound/SetBlockFailureFlags sweep (3819-3829) and now asserts that every descendant of an invalid block has BLOCK_FAILED_MASK (5395-5396) and that no unfailed block exceeds m_best_header's work (5410-5411), so with block-index consistency checks enabled (default on regtest/test chains) invalidateblock can abort the node.
defects.evidence: validation.cpp:3729 `LOCK(cs_main);` inside the while loop; :3795 `m_chainman.CheckBlockIndex();` before the final `InvalidChainFound(to_mark_failed);` at :3829; the existing comment at :3820 already acknowledges 'If any new blocks somehow arrived while we were disconnecting'. CheckBlockIndex is gated on m_options.check_block_index (5253), defaulted from chainparams DefaultConsistencyChecks (6302).
defects.notes: Must say headers/blocks arriving during InvalidateBlock (cs_main released between disconnects) are absent from the precomputed caches, leaving descendants unmarked or m_best_header stale when CheckBlockIndex's new asserts run. A claim that lower-work pre-existing descendants are excluded by the work filter (C2/C14) does not count.

excluded.reason: Claims off-chain headers forking from a disconnected block but with less work than pindex->pprev are excluded from the cache and never marked FAILED_CHILD. Impossible: any block forking from a disconnected block descends from pindex, so its nChainWork strictly exceeds pindex->pprev's (each block adds positive work), and it passes the `!CBlockIndexWorkComparator()(candidate, pindex->pprev)` filter at validation.cpp:3715-3716.

Claims the work cutoff excludes lower-work off-chain descendants so CheckBlockIndex aborts invalidateblock on a short side branch. Same as C2: every descendant of pindex has more work than pindex->pprev, so none is excluded; branches forking below pindex are not descendants.

Asks whether clearing BLOCK_FAILED_VALID on a side-branch block that was independently invalid loses its provenance. Intentional (commented at validation.cpp:3768) and without consequence: the block stays failed, and reconsiderblock's ResetBlockFailureFlags clears both flags on descendants alike.

Claims the assignment clears an independently established BLOCK_FAILED_VALID, unlike SetBlockFailureFlags. Same as C7: documented intent, the block remains failed, and no code path distinguishes the two flags for these descendants.

Claims repeated best-header fallback scans cost depth x cache-size under cs_main on deep invalidations. Speculative performance concern on an RPC-only path; the scan runs only when the current best header became failed and erases failed entries, and no concrete harmful bound is shown.
Claims the best-header loop rescans remaining headers for each disconnected block while holding cs_main. Same speculative RPC-only performance point as C4.
Claims the cached best-header selection duplicates RecalculateBestHeader's rule and could drift. Maintainability suggestion; the two currently agree (unfailed, most work), no drift.
Asks to document that FindFork must run against the pre-disconnect chain. Documentation request; the cache is built before any disconnection, as required.
Asks for a regression test covering off-chain descendants and best-header changes across invalidate/reconsider/restart. Test request.

bitcoin__bitcoin@e98c51f.pr_summary: Allows -proxy to be given per network with a '=<network>' suffix (ipv4, ipv6, tor/onion, cjdns), including '-proxy=0=<net>' to remove one. AppInitMain iterates args.GetArgs("-proxy") and assigns per-network Proxy objects (ipv4/ipv6 also set the name proxy); CheckHostPortOptions strips the suffix for -proxy and newly validates -bind; DEFAULT_TOR_SOCKS_PORT moves to torcontrol.h; doc/tor.md and feature_proxy.py are updated.

defects.title: -proxy precedence inverted: a config-file proxy now overrides the command-line (and settings.json) proxy
defects.statement: The old code used args.GetArg("-proxy"), where the command line wins over settings.json and bitcoin.conf. The new loop (init.cpp:1598-1637) applies every value of args.GetArgs("-proxy") with last-assignment-wins, and GetSettingsList returns command-line values first, then read-write settings, then config-file values (common/settings.cpp MergeSettings/GetSettingsList). So `bitcoind -proxy=B` with `proxy=A` in bitcoin.conf now routes through A (and config can undo a command-line `-proxy=0=cjdns`). doc/tor.md:60-61, added in this PR, claims 'command line overrides the config file', which the code contradicts.
defects.evidence: init.cpp:1598 `for (const std::string& param_value : args.GetArgs("-proxy"))`, later assignments overwrite; settings.cpp GetSettingsList appends COMMAND_LINE, RW_SETTINGS, then CONFIG_FILE sections; GetSetting takes the command line first.
defects.notes: Must say config-file (lower-priority) values are applied after and override command-line values, or that the new tor.md precedence sentence is wrong for this reason. A bare 'multiple -proxy are order-dependent' (R1) does not count.

defects.title: A unix: proxy path containing '=' is now misparsed as a network suffix and rejected
defects.statement: The '=<network>' suffix is split at rfind('=') unconditionally (init.cpp:1599-1605, and in CheckHostPortOptions at 1223-1224), so a previously valid `-proxy=unix:/run/a=b.sock` yields net_str 'b.sock' and startup fails with 'Unrecognized network in -proxy'.
defects.evidence: init.cpp:1599 `const auto eq_pos{param_value.rfind('=')};`; the else-branch InitError for an unknown net_str.
defects.notes: Must mention an '=' inside a unix socket path (or value) being taken as a network suffix.

defects.title: Privacy parameter interaction reads a different -proxy value than the proxies actually installed
defects.statement: InitParameterInteraction still decides -listen/-natpmp/-discover defaults from the single args.GetArg("-proxy") (init.cpp:753-766), while AppInitMain now installs proxies from every GetArgs("-proxy") value with last-wins. GetArg takes the FIRST config-file value, so a config with `proxy=0` then `proxy=A` leaves listening/discovery on while proxy A is installed; conversely a lone `-proxy=0=cjdns` (or `-proxy=0=ipv4`) is a non-empty, non-'0' string, so listening and discovery are disabled although no proxy is set.
defects.evidence: init.cpp:753 `std::string proxy_arg = args.GetArg("-proxy", ""); if (proxy_arg != "" && proxy_arg != "0")`; settings.cpp GetSetting reverse_precedence for config sources.
defects.notes: Must say the -proxy parameter-interaction (listen/discover/natpmp defaults) uses GetArg and no longer matches the effective per-network proxy configuration.

defects.title: Removing one network's proxy also removes the DNS name proxy while other networks stay proxied
defects.statement: Per-network assignments write name_proxy too: `ipv4_proxy = name_proxy = proxy` and `ipv6_proxy = name_proxy = proxy` (init.cpp:1627-1630). With `-proxy=A -proxy=0=ipv4` (or `-proxy=A=ipv4 -proxy=0=ipv6`) name_proxy becomes invalid, SetNameProxy is skipped, and hostname connections fall back to local DNS resolution (net.cpp / netbase Lookup when !HaveNameProxy()) even though another network is still routed through the proxy.
defects.evidence: init.cpp:1628 `ipv4_proxy = name_proxy = proxy;`, :1630 `ipv6_proxy = name_proxy = proxy;` with proxy default-constructed (invalid) for '0'.
defects.notes: Must say that a '0=ipv4'/'0=ipv6' removal clears the name/DNS proxy, leaking DNS while other networks remain proxied. R4 claims the opposite (name proxy stays active) and does not count.

defects.title: -proxy=...=tor is not honoured by Tor-control SOCKS discovery the way -onion is
defects.statement: doc/tor.md presents `-proxy=ip[:port]=tor` as an alternative to `-onion=ip[:port]`, but TorController::auth_cb only skips SOCKS discovery when -onion is set (torcontrol.cpp:469) and get_socks_cb then calls SetProxy(NET_ONION, discovered) (torcontrol.cpp:410). With onion listening enabled, an explicit `-proxy=A=tor` is replaced by the discovered proxy, and `-proxy=0=tor` does not keep onion disabled the way `-onion=0` does.
defects.evidence: torcontrol.cpp:469 `if (gArgs.GetArg("-onion", "") == "")` then GETINFO net/listeners/socks; :410 `SetProxy(NET_ONION, addrOnion);`.
defects.notes: Must say Tor control discovery can override/re-enable the onion proxy despite an explicit =tor setting or removal.

excluded.reason: Suggests adding examples to the -proxy help and clarifying that multiple -proxy entries are order-dependent. Help-text/UX suggestion; the '=network' syntax is documented in the help string (init.cpp:567-572) and doc/tor.md, and it does not identify the command-line-vs-config precedence inversion.

Says `-proxy==ipv4` (empty proxy with suffix) silently unsets the ipv4 proxy and should be disallowed. Empty-string removal is the documented semantics (init.cpp:1596-1597, '-proxy="" can be used to remove the proxy setting'), consistent with -proxy=0=<net>; a design preference, not a bug.

Says disabling a network proxy such as -proxy=0=ipv6 leaves name-resolution proxying active. Wrong: net_str 'ipv6' assigns `ipv6_proxy = name_proxy = proxy` (init.cpp:1630), so the name proxy is cleared too.
Asks the -onion help '(default: -proxy)' to clarify that ipv4/ipv6-only proxies are not inherited for onion. Documentation-clarity request; the behaviour matches doc/tor.md.

wavetermdev__waveterm@90a57d5.pr_summary: Moves per-block environment (the block's "env" file plus cmd:env) and a new per-shell cmd:initscript[.sh/.bash/.zsh/.pwsh/.fish] (optionally under a "[conn]" override) into the swap token that Wave's shell-integration rc files unpack with `wsh token`, and removes CommandOptsType.Env so shellexec no longer sets env vars on the process (local UpdateCmdEnv, ssh session.Setenv, WSL JWT prefix). Refactors blockcontroller connection handling into a ConnUnion (conn type, wsh enabled, shell path/type via RemoteGetInfo or local settings), moves BlockFile_* constants to wavebase, adds cmd:allowconnchange meta, and drops unused ctx/flags parameters from conncontroller.GetConn and wslconn.GetWslConn.

defects.title: cmd blocks (wsh run, cmd:env) lose their environment and WAVETERM_JWT: env now travels only in the swap token, which a `shell -c cmd` process never unpacks
defects.statement: resolveEnvMap's result (env file written by `wsh run` + cmd:env) and the JWT are now placed only in swapToken.Env (blockcontroller.go:354-360, 529/558/581), and the PR deletes the code that applied them to the process: `shellutil.UpdateCmdEnv(ecmd, cmdOpts.Env)` in StartLocalShellProc, the `session.Setenv` loop in StartRemoteShellProc and the `WAVETERM_JWT=...` prefix in StartWslShellProc. The swap token is decoded only by `wsh token "$WAVETERM_SWAPTOKEN" <shell>` inside Wave's rc files (shellutil.go:57-61,115-117,143-145,155), which are loaded only on the interactive path (cmdStr == ""). A cmd block runs `shellPath -c cmdStr` (shellexec.go:507, 394, 247) with no rc file, so the variables never reach the command: `wsh run` (which snapshots the caller's environment into the block's env file, wshcmd-run.go:136-145) runs its command without that environment, cmd:env is ignored for cmd blocks on local, ssh and wsl, and `wsh` invoked from a cmd block has no WAVETERM_JWT.
defects.evidence: Removed base lines: shellexec.go:560 `shellutil.UpdateCmdEnv(ecmd, cmdOpts.Env)`, :429-431 `session.Setenv(envKey, envVal)`, :260 `jwtToken, ok := cmdOpts.Env[wshutil.WaveJwtTokenVarName]`. Head StartLocalShellProc cmd path: `shellOpts = append(shellOpts, "-c", cmdStr)` (507) and only WAVETERM_SWAPTOKEN is set (517). `git grep WAVETERM_SWAPTOKEN` finds only the rc snippets in pkg/util/shellutil/shellutil.go. Base createCmdStrAndOpts filled cmdOpts.Env from the env file and cmd:env.
defects.notes: Must say that env vars (env file / cmd:env and/or the JWT) are no longer applied to the spawned process for command (non-interactive, `-c`) blocks because they live only in the swap token that only interactive rc files redeem. Saying merely 'CommandOptsType.Env was removed' without the consequence does not count. A claim limited to interactive shells (which never received cmd:env in base) does not count.

defects.title: Local blocks with cmd:nowsh ignore term:localshellpath because ShellPath is resolved only when wsh is enabled
defects.statement: getRemoteInfoAndShellType returns immediately when !union.WshEnabled (blockcontroller.go:401), so for a local connection with cmd:nowsh=true union.ShellPath stays "". The local branch sets `cmdOpts.ShellPath = connUnion.ShellPath` (583) and StartLocalShellProc falls back to DetectLocalShellPath() (shellexec.go:472-474). Previously the local branch read term:localshellpath from meta/settings regardless of cmd:nowsh. A user with a custom local shell who disables wsh now gets the detected default shell, while getLocalShellOpts (584) still passes the custom shell's term:localshellopts to it.
defects.evidence: blockcontroller.go:401 `if !union.WshEnabled { return nil }` precedes :414 `union.ShellPath = getLocalShellPath(blockMeta)`; :454 `rtn.WshEnabled = wshEnabled`; :583 `cmdOpts.ShellPath = connUnion.ShellPath`; shellexec.go:473-474 fallback to DetectLocalShellPath. Base set cmdOpts.ShellPath from settings/meta unconditionally in the local branch.
defects.notes: Must identify that the local shell path is not computed when wsh is disabled (cmd:nowsh), so the configured local shell is lost.

defects.title: A RemoteGetInfo failure in getConnUnion now aborts SSH/WSL terminal start instead of reaching the existing no-wsh fallback
defects.statement: getConnUnion calls getRemoteInfoAndShellType, which for wsh-enabled SSH/WSL connections issues RemoteGetInfoCommand with a 2s timeout and returns an error on failure (blockcontroller.go:404-410); setupAndStartShellProcess returns that error (481-484). In base the RemoteGetInfo call happened inside StartRemoteShellProc/StartWslShellProc, whose failure was caught by the caller's `attempting install without wsh` fallback (blockcontroller.go:559-568, 530-539). Now a slow or unresponsive connserver makes the terminal fail to open at all rather than falling back to a plain shell.
defects.evidence: blockcontroller.go:406-409 `remoteInfo, err := wshclient.RemoteGetInfoCommand(...); if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("unable to obtain remote info from connserver: %w", err) }`; :456-459 propagate; shellexec.go:330-332 StartRemoteShellProc's own RemoteGetInfo failure feeds the fallback at blockcontroller.go:560-565.
defects.notes: Must say that the new up-front remote-info lookup fails the whole start and bypasses the no-wsh fallback. A comment only about the 2s timeout value does not count.

defects.title: SSH branch ignores the block's cmd:nowsh: it tests conn.WshEnabled instead of connUnion.WshEnabled and now hands the block a JWT
defects.statement: getConnUnion folds cmd:nowsh into rtn.WshEnabled (blockcontroller.go:451) and the WSL branch uses connUnion.WshEnabled (515), but the SSH branch tests the raw connection flag `if !conn.WshEnabled.Load()` (544). A block with cmd:nowsh=true on a wsh-enabled SSH connection takes the wsh path, and unlike base (which only minted a JWT when !cmd:nowsh) now mints a JWT into the swap token (550-558), so the per-block opt-out is fully ignored. Its ShellType is also empty (getRemoteInfoAndShellType returned early), so only the generic init script is selected.
defects.evidence: blockcontroller.go:544 `if !conn.WshEnabled.Load() {` vs :515 `if !connUnion.WshEnabled {`; base SSH branch wrapped JWT creation in `if !blockMeta.GetBool(waveobj.MetaKey_CmdNoWsh, false)`.
defects.notes: Must say the SSH dispatch checks the connection's WshEnabled rather than the union's/block's cmd:nowsh-aware flag.

defects.title: Init-script shell type is derived from remoteInfo.Shell, not the shell the launcher actually runs (conn:shellpath)
defects.statement: For SSH/WSL, union.ShellPath = remoteInfo.Shell (blockcontroller.go:412) and ShellType is computed from it (416) to choose the cmd:initscript.<shell> key (makeSwapToken, 361). But StartRemoteShellProc/StartWslShellProc prefer conn.GetConfigShellPath() over remoteInfo.Shell (shellexec.go:340-348, 188-196). When conn:shellpath names a different shell (e.g. zsh configured on a bash-default host) the token carries the bash/sh script to a zsh/fish session, which may fail or misbehave.
defects.evidence: blockcontroller.go:411-412 `// TODO allow overriding remote shell path` / `union.ShellPath = remoteInfo.Shell`; shellexec.go:340-343 `configShellPath := conn.GetConfigShellPath(); if shellPath == "" && configShellPath != "" { shellPath = configShellPath }`.
defects.notes: Must say the init-script (shell-type) selection uses the detected remote shell while the launched shell honours conn:shellpath.

defects.title: cmd:env and cmd:cwd are documented as nestable under "[conn]" but the code never reads the connection override for them
defects.statement: wtypemeta.go:54 adds `// these can be nested under "[conn]"` above CmdEnv, CmdCwd and the initscript keys, but only getCustomInitScript consults meta.GetConnectionOverride. resolveEnvMap takes connName and ignores it (blockcontroller.go:252-283), and cmd:cwd is read only from the top-level meta (293, 491). A per-connection cmd:env or cmd:cwd is silently ignored, contrary to the documented contract.
defects.evidence: `git grep GetConnectionOverride` at head: only metamap.go and getCustomInitScript; resolveEnvMap reads `blockMeta.GetMap(waveobj.MetaKey_CmdEnv)` only; connName unused.
defects.notes: Must say per-connection ([conn]) env and/or cwd overrides are not honoured although the struct comment/init-script lookup implies they are. A comment only about unused parameters (C9/C31) or dotted JSON keys (R4) does not count.

defects.title: An env-file read error is now logged and ignored; the command starts without its configured environment instead of failing
defects.statement: Base createCmdStrAndOpts returned `error reading command env file` and the block failed to start. Now makeSwapToken calls resolveEnvMap and on error only logs (blockcontroller.go:354-357), then starts the process with none of the env-file/cmd:env variables (resolveEnvMap returns nil map on error), silently dropping variables the command may depend on.
