defects.evidence: blockcontroller.go:354-357 `envMap, err := resolveEnvMap(...); if err != nil { log.Printf("error resolving env map: %v\n", err) }`; :259-260 returns nil on read error (2s filestore timeout); base returned the error from createCmdStrAndOpts.
defects.notes: Must say the env read error is swallowed so the block starts with an incomplete environment rather than reporting the error.

excluded.reason: Claims `err == fs.ErrNotExist` should be `errors.Is` to catch wrapped errors. The comparisons are pre-existing (only the constant name changed) and filestore returns the sentinel unwrapped; the PR does not change behaviour.

Claims the space check for cmd:shell=false is insufficient validation and allows command injection. Moved verbatim from base createCmdStrAndOpts; args are shell-quoted and cmd is the user's own block config, not a trust boundary.

Claims the new debug log in StartWslShellProc outputs the sensitive swap token. conn.Debugf logs via blocklogger with a plain context.WithTimeout(Background) ctx that carries no log-block, so it emits nothing; the app log already recorded the WAVETERM_JWT credential in base's `full combined command` line.

Claims `log.Printf("full combined command")` now logs the redeemable swap token in plaintext for every WSL session. Base logged the same line with `WAVETERM_JWT=<jwt>` embedded, an equally sensitive credential, so this is a pre-existing logging practice not made materially worse.
Claims the packed WSL swap token is logged via log.Printf and is redeemable. Same as C8: base already logged the combined command carrying the JWT; not a new exposure class.

Claims dotted JSON tags like cmd:initscript.sh could be ambiguous if a layer interprets dots as nesting. Speculative: all lookups use literal map keys; the real [conn] gap is D6, which this comment does not state.
Claims the new WslConn.Debugf calls blocklogger.Infof instead of Debugf. Its only caller (shellexec.go:262) passes a ctx without log-block data, so nothing is emitted at any level; inert.
Claims WslConn.Debugf using Infof writes WSL debug messages to the block log even when not verbose. Same as R5: the only caller's ctx has no block logger attached, so nothing is written.

Claims interactive local shells with cmd:nowsh lose their cmd:env/env-file values. Base never applied cmd:env or the env file to interactive shell blocks (base shell branch set cmdOpts.Env to an empty map plus the JWT only), so nothing regressed; the command-block loss is D1.
Claims StartWslShellProcNoWsh ignores cmdStr so a no-wsh WSL command block opens a shell instead. Pre-existing: StartWslShellProcNoWsh (shellexec.go:152-171) is unchanged by this PR.
Asks to remove unused blockId/connName parameters of createCmdStrAndOpts. Style/unused-parameter point; the missing [conn] resolution is D6.
Asks to remove unused blockId and connName from createCmdStrAndOpts. Style/unused-parameter point.
Asks to remove the never-populated ConnUnion.ShellOpts field. Dead-field style point with no behavioural consequence.
Asks to remove the unused ConnUnion.ShellOpts field. Same style point as C17.

wavetermdev__waveterm@61b0fb4.pr_summary: Adds a token-swap mechanism for shell startup: Wave registers a one-time TokenSwapEntry (UUID, env vars incl. WAVETERM_JWT/BLOCKID/TABID/..., socket name, rpc context, 5-minute expiry) in an in-memory map and passes it packed as WAVETERM_SWAPTOKEN to local and SSH shells; the bash/zsh/fish/pwsh rc files run a new hidden `wsh token <token> <shell>` that redeems it over the domain socket via a new `authenticatetoken` RPC and prints shell code exporting the env. The inline `WAVETERM_JWT=... cmd` prefix for SSH shells is removed. The SSH connserver startup now just execs `wsh connserver`, which installs rc files itself, prints HAVE-JWT/NEED-JWT and reads the JWT from stdin. Also conndebug block logging, WAVETERM_WSHFORCEUPDATE, and ds.NewSyncMap -> MakeSyncMap.

defects.title: PowerShell rc passes multi-line `wsh token` output as an array to Invoke-Expression, so the token-swap env script never runs
defects.statement: In PwshStartup_wavepwsh (pkg/util/shellutil/shellutil.go:156-159) the output of the native `wsh token ... pwsh` call is captured into $waveterm_swaptoken_output. PowerShell captures multi-line native output as an array of lines; passing that array to Invoke-Expression's [string] -Command parameter joins the lines with spaces, producing `$env:A = '...' $env:B = '...' ...`, which is a parse error. `wsh token` always prints several lines (TERM_PROGRAM, WAVETERM_BLOCKID, WAVETERM_VERSION, WAVETERM, JWT, ... one `$env:K = V` per line from encodeEnvVarsForPowerShell, plus the init-script line), so for every pwsh shell the swap fails with an error printed in the terminal and none of the env vars are set. For SSH pwsh shells this also means WAVETERM_JWT is no longer delivered (the old inline prefix was removed), so wsh loses its socket auth there. The same file already uses `| Out-String | Invoke-Expression` for completions (line 164), which is the working pattern.
defects.evidence: shellutil.go:156 `$waveterm_swaptoken_output = wsh token $env:WAVETERM_SWAPTOKEN pwsh 2>$null`; :158 `Invoke-Expression $waveterm_swaptoken_output`; tokenswap.go encodeEnvVarsForPowerShell emits `fmt.Sprintf("$env:%s = %s\n", ...)` per var; blockcontroller.go makeSwapToken always sets >=4 env vars; wshcmd-token.go:35-36 WriteStdout env script then InitScriptText on separate lines. Contrast shellutil.go completion line `wsh completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`.
defects.notes: Must say that the pwsh token output is multi-line and is captured as an array / not joined with newlines, so Invoke-Expression fails or evaluates it wrongly. Comments only about suppressing stderr (2>$null) or about Remove-Item errors do not count.

defects.title: Connserver handshake reads the JWT status line from a stream that merges stderr, so an rc-install error line makes the client skip sending the JWT and connserver startup times out
defects.statement: StartConnServer points the SSH session's Stdout and Stderr at the same pipe (pkg/remote/conncontroller/conncontroller.go:297-298), then takes the next line after the version as the JWT status (conncontroller.go:333-339) and writes the JWT only if that line equals NEED-JWT; any other line is silently treated like HAVE-JWT. The connserver's serverRun now calls wshutil.InstallRcFiles() first and on failure does log.Printf(...) to stderr (cmd/wsh/cmd/wshcmd-connserver.go:253-256) before askForJwtToken prints NEED-JWT and blocks on stdin. When rc installation fails (e.g. unwritable ~/.waveterm), the client consumes the error line as the status, never sends the JWT, the connserver blocks forever on Fscanln, and StartConnServer fails with 'timeout waiting for connserver to register' (conncontroller.go:392), so wsh is disabled for that connection. Before the PR the JWT was written unconditionally and an rc-install failure surfaced as a direct error.
defects.evidence: conncontroller.go:297-298 `sshSession.Stdout = pipeWrite` / `sshSession.Stderr = pipeWrite`; :333 `jwtLine, err := wshutil.ReadLineWithTimeout(linesChan, 3*time.Second)`; :339 `if strings.TrimSpace(jwtLine) == wavebase.NeedJwtConst {` with no else. wshcmd-connserver.go:253-255 `installErr := wshutil.InstallRcFiles(); if installErr != nil { log.Printf("error installing rc files: %v", installErr) }` then :257 `askForJwtToken()` which prints NEED-JWT and reads stdin. No log.SetOutput in cmd/wsh, so log goes to stderr.
defects.notes: Must say the status-line read can pick up something other than NEED-JWT/HAVE-JWT (stderr/log output on the same pipe, e.g. the rc-install error) and that the JWT is then not sent / connserver waits on stdin. The older-connserver compatibility claim (R7), a pure 3-second-timeout concern (C31) and 'rc install errors are only logged' without the handshake consequence (C11) do not count.

defects.title: SSH command blocks (and shells without a Wave rc file) no longer receive WAVETERM_JWT because the inline prefix was replaced by a swap token only rc files redeem
defects.statement: Before the PR, StartRemoteShellProc always prefixed the remote command with `WAVETERM_JWT=<jwt>` regardless of cmdStr. The PR removes that and prefixes only `WAVETERM_SWAPTOKEN=<packed>` (pkg/shellexec/shellexec.go:403-409). The swap token is redeemed only by the Wave bash/zsh/fish/pwsh rc files, which are not used when cmdStr != "" (shellexec.go:360-363 runs `-c cmdStr`) or for other shell types. For those, the JWT now reaches the process only via session.Setenv (shellexec.go:393-396), whose errors are ignored and which default sshd configs (AcceptEnv LANG LC_*) reject. So wsh inside remote command blocks loses its JWT/domain-socket auth and falls back to terminal-OSC mode.
defects.evidence: Base shellexec.go (deleted lines ~443-449): `jwtToken, ok := cmdOpts.Env[wshutil.WaveJwtTokenVarName]` ... `cmdCombined = fmt.Sprintf(`%s=%s %s`, wshutil.WaveJwtTokenVarName, jwtToken, cmdCombined)`. Head :395 `session.Setenv(envKey, envVal)` with comment 'these might fail depending on server settings'; :408 prefixes only WaveSwapTokenVarName. wshcmd-root.go preRunSetupRpcClient falls back to SetupTerminalRpcClient when WAVETERM_JWT is empty.
defects.notes: Must say that remote command-mode (cmdStr / -c) shells, or shells that do not source the Wave rc, no longer get WAVETERM_JWT because the inline JWT prefix was removed and Setenv may be rejected. Saying only that command blocks do not get the NEW block/workspace env vars (C25) does not count, since those vars were never delivered before.

defects.title: WSL path builds a swap token but never packs or registers it, so WSL shells cannot redeem the new startup env
defects.statement: setupAndStartShellProcess creates the swap token for every block and, on the WSL branch, even adds the JWT to swapToken.Env (pkg/blockcontroller/blockcontroller.go:363-364, 383), but sets no SockName/RpcContext and calls StartWslShellProc, which never calls PackForClient/AddTokenSwapEntry nor sets WAVETERM_SWAPTOKEN. The WSL shells source the same updated rc files, whose `wsh token "$WAVETERM_SWAPTOKEN" ...` therefore always fails silently, so WSL shells never get the new WAVETERM_BLOCKID/TABID/WORKSPACEID/CLIENTID variables the PR delivers to local and SSH shells.
defects.evidence: blockcontroller.go:383 `swapToken.Env[wshutil.WaveJwtTokenVarName] = jwtStr` then :386 `shellexec.StartWslShellProc(ctx, rc.TermSize, cmdStr, cmdOpts, wslConn)`; StartWslShellProc still only passes `WAVETERM_JWT=...` via wsl.exe args and has no reference to SwapToken. wshcmd-root.go setupRpcClientWithToken rejects `token.SockName == ""`.
defects.notes: Must say WSL shells do not get/redeem the swap token (not packed/registered, or no sockname), so the token-provided env is missing on WSL. A claim that WSL loses the JWT or wsh entirely is wrong (JWT is still passed inline).

excluded.reason: Claims askForJwtToken leaks token presence by printing HAVE-JWT on stdout and mishandles EOF. HAVE-JWT/NEED-JWT is the handshake protocol parsed by conncontroller.go:339 and reveals no secret; EOF already surfaces as a wrapped Fscanln error.
Claims using wavebase.WaveJwtTokenVarName instead of wshutil.WaveJwtTokenVarName is inconsistent. wshutil.go:49 now defines the latter as the former; same constant, style only.

Claims wshcmd-root.go:156 logs the authentication token in plaintext. It logs the single-use swap UUID to wsh's stderr, which every rc file discards (2>/dev/null), and the same call redeems it (GetAndRemoveTokenSwapEntry deletes it); no usable credential is exposed.
Asks for JSDoc on the generated CommandAuthenticateRtnData type. gotypes.d.ts is generated; documentation request, not a defect.

Claims logging the swap token at blockcontroller.go:365 exposes sensitive data. blocklogger.Infof only writes when a conn-debug log ctx is attached, into the user's own block, and the UUID is redeemed by the shell within milliseconds; debug output, not an exploitable leak.
Claims debugLog's differing prefixes between blocklogger and log are confusing. Cosmetic.

Claims an older connserver that does not print NEED-JWT/HAVE-JWT will time out the handshake. This path only runs when IsWshVersionUpToDate is true (remote wsh >= app version), so the remote binary always has the new protocol; older ones are reinstalled first.

Claims shellexec.go:324 logs SwapToken.Token in plaintext. It goes to the user's own app log/conn-debug block; the UUID is single-use and redeemed at shell start; reading it requires access to the user's own data dir, where the JWT is equally reachable. Not a concrete vulnerability.
Claims cmdOpts.SwapToken may be nil at shellexec.go:324. The only caller sets cmdOpts.SwapToken = swapToken unconditionally (blockcontroller.go:363-364) before any branch.
Claims the packed swap token is logged in debug output. blocklogger.Debugf only writes in verbose conn-debug mode into the user's own block; single-use UUID; not a concrete leak.

Claims duplicate PATH manipulation and 2>/dev/null in the zsh rc is a security problem. Adding the bin dir before `wsh token` and conditionally after the user rc is deliberate (the user rc can clobber PATH); stderr suppression keeps shells quiet when no token exists. No security impact.
Claims redirecting stderr of `wsh token` hides errors. Intentional so shells without a token stay quiet; diagnosability preference.
Suggests a value sync.Mutex and simpler map init in tokenswap.go. Go style preference, no behavioural effect.
Suggests URL-safe base64 for the packed token. The token travels only as an env assignment and a quoted CLI arg, where + / = are safe; Pack and Unpack both use StdEncoding.
Suggests fallback decoding and field validation in UnpackSwapToken. Only relevant if R14 were applied; sockname/rpccontext/token emptiness are already checked (wshcmd-root.go:144-150, wshproxy.go).
Claims entries with zero Exp would be evicted immediately. The only producer, makeSwapToken, always sets Exp = now + 5 minutes.
Claims adding Env/InitScriptText fields to CommandAuthenticateRtnData breaks older consumers. Fields are omitempty and ignored by Go/TS decoders; both ends ship together.
Claims wshproxy.go:144 logs the authentication token from msg.Data. The logged swap UUID is removed from the map in the same call, so it cannot be replayed; debug noise, not a credential exposure.

Claims the empty AuthenticateToken branch in HandleClientProxyAuth must be removed or implemented. It falls through to 'connection not authenticated' like before and is not reached in practice: swap tokens carry the SSH-forwarded /tmp socket or the local socket, both served by HandleAuthentication in the Wave process. Code cleanliness only.
Claims `wsh token` should validate shellType before consuming the one-time token. The only callers are the generated rc files, which always pass zsh/bash/fish/pwsh; an unsupported type is contrived.

Claims local shells still receive the JWT directly in their environment, bypassing the swap. This is unchanged from before the PR (cmdOpts.Env always carried WAVETERM_JWT) and the PR states no goal of removing it; not a regression.
Claims removeExpiredTokens scanning the whole map under a mutex is a performance problem. The map holds at most a handful of short-lived entries per shell launch; no concrete consequence.
Claims wshcmd-root.go:156 logs the one-time credential in plaintext. stderr is discarded by all rc files and the token is consumed by the same call; not an exploitable leak (see R3).
Claims every redemption writes its live bearer credential to logs at wshcmd-root.go:156. Same as R3: stderr discarded, token consumed immediately.

Claims shellexec.go:324 writes the bearer swap token into the block's terminal output. Only with a conn-debug log ctx, into the user's own block, and the token is redeemed at shell start; not a concrete vulnerability.

Claims conn.Infof always logs the swap UUID to the app log where a reader can race to redeem it. The app log is in the user's own data dir (same trust boundary as the JWT itself) and the shell redeems the token within milliseconds; not a concrete vulnerability.
Claims wshproxy.go:144 logs incoming authentication credentials. The swap UUID is consumed in the same call; see R18.
Claims the swap entry is consumed before its RpcContext is validated, preventing retry. The producer always sets a valid RpcContext when SockName is set; the failure scenario is contrived.
Claims a direct `wsh token` invocation prints the redeemable UUID to stderr. It is consumed by the same invocation; see R3.

Claims rc-file installation failures are now only logged, so shells start with missing integration files instead of failing. In reality such a failure breaks the JWT handshake first (the log line is read as the status line, see D2) and wsh is disabled for the connection; the stated consequence does not occur and the comment does not identify the handshake problem.
Asks for a visible diagnostic when token redemption fails in the bash rc. Stderr suppression is intentional; diagnosability preference.
Claims a failed pty start leaves the swap entry redeemable until expiry. The entry is an unguessable UUID in process memory that expires in 5 minutes; no concrete consequence.

Claims remote shells' `wsh token` hits the connserver's empty AuthenticateToken branch and cannot redeem because the registry is local. The token's SockName is conn.GetDomainSocketName(), a /tmp socket opened via client.ListenUnix and served by RunWshRpcOverListener -> HandleAuthentication in the local Wave process, where the registry lives; the connserver branch is not on this path.
Claims the shared 2-second ctx may expire before makeSwapToken's DB lookups. Speculative; a few local SQLite reads after a file create, and failures only omit optional env vars with a log.
Claims the empty proxy branch means remote shell initialization cannot redeem tokens. Wrong: remote swap tokens use the SSH-forwarded socket handled by HandleAuthentication locally (see C15).
Claims wshproxy.go:144 exposes the bearer credential in the app log. Consumed in the same call; see R18.
Claims remote `wsh token` sends authenticatetoken to the connserver, which rejects it. Wrong: the socket in the token is the forwarded one served by the local Wave process (see C15).
Claims blockcontroller.go:365 records the redeemable swap UUID in block output under conndebug. Debug-only, user's own block, single-use and redeemed at startup; see R5.

Claims command blocks do not receive the new token-provided block/workspace env because `-c` bypasses the rc files. Those variables were never delivered to command blocks before; not a regression (the JWT loss for remote command blocks is D3).
Claims a user cmd:env entry can override WAVETERM_SWAPTOKEN. A user deliberately setting that internal variable is contrived.
Claims the swap token is a bearer credential written into block output at blockcontroller.go:365. Debug-only, user's own block; see R5.
Claims remote shells still receive the JWT directly via Setenv, bypassing the one-use exchange. Pre-existing behaviour (the JWT was even inlined before); the PR does not claim to remove it.
Claims wshproxy.go:144 logs the token-swap credential. Consumed in the same call; see R18.

Claims local shells' WAVETERM changes from the executable path to "1". Nothing in the repo reads WAVETERM as a path; it is a presence flag and the new value is consistent across local/remote; no demonstrable consequence.

Claims InstallRcFiles running before NEED-JWT can exceed the client's 3-second status-line window on a slow home dir. Writing seven small files taking >3 s is speculative, and it is not the stderr-merge defect (D2).
Claims a failed launch should remove its registered swap token. Same as C14; no concrete consequence.
Claims unredeemed entries linger indefinitely without later activity. They are tiny, in-memory, and purged on the next add/redeem; no concrete consequence.
Claims rc files deleted while the connserver runs are no longer repaired per shell. Deleting integration files mid-session is contrived.
Asks to remove or implement the empty AuthenticateToken branch in HandleClientProxyAuth. It falls through to the same rejection as before and is not reached (see R19); cleanliness only.

wavetermdev__waveterm@4b7637f.pr_summary: Reworks copy/move for prefix filesystems (S3, wavefile). A new fsutil.DetermineCopyDestPath centralizes destination resolution (appends the source basename only when the destination is a directory, or is missing and the source is a directory) and the overwrite/merge conflict checks. PrefixCopyInternal/PrefixCopyRemote use it. CopyInternal/CopyRemote (and the remotefilecopy RPC) now return whether the source was a directory, so moves delete the source recursively only when it was a directory. It also changes GetParentPathString to return "" for top-level paths and CleanPathPrefix to accept an empty path, removes the recursive pre-check in the cross-host fileshare.Move, moves S3 recursive delete to the paginated listFilesPrefix, appends '/' to the source URI when renaming a directory in the UI, and adds many log.Printf calls.

defects.title: Copying a single file to a not-yet-existing 'dir/' destination on S3/wavefile writes it to key 'dir' instead of 'dir/<name>'
defects.statement: DetermineCopyDestPath (fsutil.go:137-160) computes destHasSlash but uses it only in the source-is-directory case: the basename is appended only when `destInfo.IsDir || (!destExists && !destHasSlash && srcInfo.IsDir)`. CleanPathPrefix drops the trailing slash (fsutil.go:196-206, fspath.Join of the split parts). So for a single file copied to a destination like `s3://bucket/newdir/` that does not exist yet (the normal way to 'copy into a folder' on a prefix store), destPath becomes `newdir`. PrefixCopyInternal copies to that key (fsutil.go:85), and PrefixCopyRemote overrides fileName with destPath for single files (fsutil.go:114-116). The file is stored as object `newdir` instead of `newdir/a.txt`. The old code was also wrong here (it produced `newdira.txt`), so the PR's rewrite of this logic leaves the trailing-slash file case broken. The wsh backend handles this case explicitly (wshremote.go `if singleFile && !destHasSlash`), so the prefix backends now disagree with it.
defects.evidence: fsutil.go:139 `destHasSlash := strings.HasSuffix(destConn.Path, fspath.Separator)`; :156 `if destInfo.IsDir || (!destExists && !destHasSlash && srcInfo.IsDir) { destPath = fspath.Join(destPath, fspath.Base(srcConn.Path)) }`. There is no branch for a file source with destHasSlash. CleanPathPrefix returns `fspath.Join(newParts...)`, which strips the trailing slash. S3 Stat of a missing 'newdir/' returns NotFound (s3fs.go:572-577), so destInfo.IsDir is false.
defects.notes: The comment must say that a trailing-slash (directory-intent) destination that does not exist is ignored for single-file copies, so the file lands at the directory name. General remarks about DetermineCopyDestPath complexity do not count, and neither does R4 (destPathPrefix ordering).

defects.title: Cross-connection move no longer enforces the recursive flag: a directory is copied and then recursively deleted even without -r
defects.statement: The PR removes the pre-check in fileshare.Move that refused `cannot move directory ... without recursive flag` for cross-host moves (base fileshare.go:132-139). Now Move calls CopyRemote and then `srcClient.Delete(ctx, srcConn, srcIsDir)` (fileshare.go:132-136), passing the returned is-directory flag as `recursive`. So `wsh file mv somedir s3://bucket/x` without `-r` (the flag is declared at cmd/wsh/cmd/wshcmd-file.go:106 and forwarded at :440) now copies the whole tree and recursively deletes the source directory. A same-host move still refuses (wshremote.go:742-743 `cannot move directory %q, recursive option not specified`). The -r safety contract is silently dropped for one route only, which contradicts the PR's stated intent ('adds better error for move without recursive').
defects.evidence: Base fileshare.go: `recursive := data.Opts != nil && data.Opts.Recursive; if finfo.IsDir && data.Opts != nil && !recursive { return fmt.Errorf("cannot move directory %q to %q without recursive flag", ...) }` followed by `srcClient.Delete(ctx, srcConn, recursive)`. Head fileshare.go:132-136 `srcIsDir, err := destClient.CopyRemote(...)` ... `return srcClient.Delete(ctx, srcConn, srcIsDir)`, with no Opts.Recursive check anywhere on this path.
defects.notes: The comment must say that the recursive check for moving directories between connections was removed (or that Delete now uses srcIsDir regardless of opts.Recursive), so directories are moved/deleted without -r. Comments about the same-host wavefs/s3 MoveInternal paths alone do not count. C2 counts: it states cross-host directory moves now proceed without -r, even though it frames the fix as a help-text update.

defects.title: Recursive S3 delete now sends every listed key in one DeleteObjects call, which S3 rejects above 1,000 keys
defects.statement: The PR switches S3Client.Delete's recursive branch to the paginated listFilesPrefix (s3fs.go:719-727), so it now accumulates ALL keys under the prefix, then sends them in a single DeleteObjects request (s3fs.go:737-742). S3's DeleteObjects accepts at most 1,000 keys per request, so for any prefix with more than 1,000 objects the request fails and nothing is deleted. That breaks `wsh file rm -r`, overwrite-deletes in DetermineCopyDestPath, and every S3 directory move (MoveInternal and cross-host Move delete the source after copying). The copy has already been done, so the move returns an error and leaves the data duplicated. Before the PR, a single ListObjectsV2 page (≤1,000 keys) was deleted, which was incomplete but did not fail; the PR's pagination change needs batching to be a real fix.
defects.evidence: s3fs.go:719-727 `objects := make(...); err := c.listFilesPrefix(ctx, &s3.ListObjectsV2Input{...}, func(obj *types.Object) (bool, error) { objects = append(objects, types.ObjectIdentifier{Key: obj.Key}); return true, nil })`; :737 `c.client.DeleteObjects(ctx, &s3.DeleteObjectsInput{Bucket: ..., Delete: &types.Delete{Objects: objects}})` with no chunking. listFilesPrefix (s3fs.go:756-779) iterates every page via NewListObjectsV2Paginator. Base used a single `c.client.ListObjectsV2` call (one page, max 1000 keys).
defects.notes: The comment must say that recursive delete now sends more than 1,000 keys in one DeleteObjects request (the S3 per-request limit), so large prefixes fail to delete or move. Comments only about checking output.Errors for per-key failures (C9) do not count, and neither do comments about per-object logging.

defects.title: PrefixCopyInternal no longer cleans the source path, so a bucket- or zone-root copy lists prefix '/' and silently copies nothing
defects.statement: Before the PR, PrefixCopyInternal ran the source through CleanPathPrefix, and a root source such as `s3://bucket/` (connparse Path "/") became "", so listing with prefix "" enumerated the whole bucket. DetermineCopyDestPath now returns the raw `srcPath = srcConn.Path` (fsutil.go:138). PrefixCopyInternal uses it as the listing prefix (fsutil.go:53-59). For `s3://bucket/` the prefix is "/". For `s3://bucket`, Path "" gets the separator appended at fsutil.go:55 and also becomes "/". Ordinary S3 keys have no leading slash, so the listing is empty, tree.Walk visits nothing, and the copy (or move) returns success having copied nothing. The same holds for any source path with a leading slash or `.` segments, which the old cleaning normalised. Worse, on a move the success is followed by a delete of the source.
defects.evidence: Head fsutil.go:138 `srcPath = srcConn.Path` (no CleanPathPrefix); base PrefixCopyInternal had `srcPath, err := CleanPathPrefix(srcConn.Path)`. connparse.ParseURI parseGenericPath sets remotePath = "/" for `s3://bucket/`. S3 Stat treats ""/"/" as the bucket and returns IsDir: true (s3fs.go:501-526). s3fs CopyInternal lists with `Prefix: aws.String(prefix)` (s3fs.go:683-686).
defects.notes: The comment must say that the source path is no longer normalised/cleaned before the prefix listing, so a root or leading-slash source lists nothing and the copy succeeds empty. Comments about the destination-path cleaning do not count.

defects.title: GetParentPathString now returns "" for top-level paths, so an S3 bucket-root listing loses its '..' entry back to the bucket list
defects.statement: GetParentPathString previously returned "/" when the path had no inner slash (base fsutil.go:30-35). It now returns "" (fsutil.go:30-31, 40-41). S3 ListEntriesStream builds the '..' row from `parentPath := fsutil.GetParentPath(conn)` and emits it only `if parentPath != ""` (s3fs.go:456-457). For a listing of `s3://bucket` (GetPathWithHost = "bucket"), parentPath was "/", pointing to the bucket list. It is now "", so the '..' row is no longer sent and the directory view gives no way to click back up from a bucket root to the list of buckets.
defects.evidence: Head fsutil.go:30-31 `if hostAndPath == "" || hostAndPath == fspath.Separator { return "" }` and :40-41 `if lastSlash <= 0 { return "" }` (base returned fspath.Separator in both). s3fs.go:456-457 `parentPath := fsutil.GetParentPath(conn); if parentPath != "" {` emits the `Name: ".."` entry. connparse GetPathWithHost returns c.Host when Path is empty.
defects.notes: The comment must connect the GetParentPathString return-value change to a caller, e.g. the missing '..' entry at the bucket root or a Dir field now empty instead of '/'. Just noting that the function changed does not count.

excluded.reason: The claim is that updateName's useCallback has an empty dependency array and may capture stale model/setter references. The empty useCallback dependency array is pre-existing; the PR only added a parameter. model and the jotai setter are stable for the component's lifetime, so there is no concrete stale-capture bug.

The claim is that lastIndexOf in the rename path replacement targets the wrong segment when a name repeats in the path. Wrong and pre-existing: lastIndexOf finds the LAST occurrence, so '/folder/doc/doc' correctly replaces the final segment (directorypreview.tsx:302-303, untouched by the PR).

The claim is that the rename should also add a trailing slash to the destination URI when the source is a directory. The trailing slash on the source deliberately means 'contents of' (srcHasSlash in DetermineCopyDestPath), so the renamed directory's contents land at the new name. Adding a slash to the destination is not needed for the rename to work.

The claim is that destPathPrefix is computed from destConn.Path before DetermineCopyDestPath rewrites the destination, so directory copies land in the wrong place. Deliberate, per the comment at fsutil.go:90. For a source without a trailing slash the tar entry names already include the source directory name (ReadTarStream includeDir), so destPathPrefix + next.Name yields the same location as the extended destPath. Only single files use destPath (:114-116). Verified: PrefixCopyRemote only uses destPathPrefix for multi-file tars, whose entry names already include the source directory when the source has no trailing slash (ReadTarStream includeDir, s3fs.go:191), so destPathPrefix + next.Name equals the extended destPath subtree.

The claim is that the new NewTree warning for a path without a trailing delimiter may spam logs. The only production caller that can pass a path without a trailing delimiter is s3 ReadTarStream. This is a warning log line, which is logging noise/style, not a defect.

The claim is that the per-path relativePath debug log in Tree.Add floods logs and hurts performance. Leftover debug logging is style/noise. Tree.Add already logged every call before the PR (pathtree.go:52 `tree.Add: path`), and the copy path already logs per file, so there is no new concrete consequence.
The claim is that the 'path already in tree' debug log should be removed. Debug-log removal request. This is style; see R6.

The claim is that logging invalid path components is a log-injection vector. Log-injection concern about logging a path component to the local app log. The paths are the user's own object keys, so there is no security boundary.
The claim is that the invalid-component debug log should be removed. Debug-log removal request. This is style; see R6.
The claim is that the ReadTarStream tarPathPrefix log is leftover debug output. Debug-log removal request. This is style.
The claim is that the per-entry 'writing' log in ReadTarStream is leftover debug output. Debug-log removal request. This is style.

The claim is that `return true, nil` in the recursive delete callback is a merge leftover. `return true, nil` is the correct continue-listing result for listFilesPrefix's (bool, error) callback (s3fs.go:620-624), not a merge leftover.
The claim is that the many log.Printf calls in S3 Delete are leftover debug output. Debug-log removal request. This is style.

The claim is that the destination-parse error in RemoteFileCopyCommand prints srcUri instead of destUri. The wrong variable (srcUri) in the destination-parse error message is pre-existing. The base line was identical except for the return arity; the PR did not introduce it.

The claim is that S3 Delete logs one line per deleted object key, flooding logs and exposing filenames. This is leftover diagnostic logging to the local app log, a noise/style concern with no functional consequence, so it is not counted as a defect.

The claim is that PrefixCopyRemote checks conflicts on destination/source but writes trailing-slash-source tar entries directly into the destination directory. When the source has a trailing slash, DetermineCopyDestPath does not append the basename (fsutil.go:155), so the checked path and the written prefix (destPathPrefix, fsutil.go:91-95) are the same directory. When the source has no trailing slash, the tar names include the source dir (ReadTarStream includeDir), so writes land under the checked destination/source. There is no mismatch.
The claim is that the new per-entry logs in pathtree.Tree.Add flood output during large copies. This is debug logging noise (Tree.Add already logged each call before the PR), not a functional defect.

The claim is that NewTree now logs a warning for supported inputs without a trailing delimiter, producing false alarms. This is a log-noise/style issue; behaviour is unchanged (the delimiter is still appended at pathtree.go:39-40).

The claim is that copying a file onto itself with overwrite deletes the source before the copy reads it. This is pre-existing: the base PrefixCopyInternal/PrefixCopyRemote also deleted the resolved destination on overwrite before copying (base fsutil.go overwrite branch `c.Delete(ctx, destConn, true)`), and self-targeting inputs (e.g. `cp -f b/dir/a b/dir`) reached it in base too. It needs an explicit -f self-copy by the user.

The claim is that S3 Delete ignores per-key failures in DeleteObjectsOutput.Errors. That is pre-existing: the base code discarded the DeleteObjects output identically (`_, err = c.client.DeleteObjects(...)`), and the PR did not make it worse.

The claim is that DetermineCopyDestPath hides destructive destination deletion behind a path-determination name. That is naming/design preference: the overwrite delete existed inline before the PR and behaves the same.

The claim is that an older remote wsh that returns no boolean from remotefilecopy makes Move delete a directory non-recursively and leave the source behind. Mixed-version remotes are speculative here: waveterm installs the matching wsh on connect, and even then the outcome is a failed delete error, not data loss.

The claim is that an empty source directory with a trailing slash returns srcIsDir=false, so the move's non-recursive delete fails. For a wsh source, RemoteFileDeleteCommand uses os.Remove, which removes an empty directory without the recursive flag (wshremote.go:841). Prefix filesystems cannot hold an empty directory. The delete therefore succeeds.

The claim is that internal directory copies write b/a/a/x because the leaf path keeps the source name. For source `a` without a slash, srcPath becomes `a/` and prefixToRemove = fspath.Dir("a/")+"/" = "a/" (path.Dir("a/") is "a"), so `a/x` becomes `x` and the write goes to `b/a/x` (fsutil.go:72-81). There is no duplication.
The claim is that DetermineCopyDestPath mutating destConn.Path should be documented or avoided. That is API-style preference: the base code mutated destConn.Path the same way, and callers rely on it.
The claim is that the per-entry logging in Tree.Add should be removed or debug-gated. This is logging noise/style, not a defect.
The claim is that an older remote worker's missing boolean makes directory moves leave the source behind. This is speculative mixed-version operation; the same reasoning as C12 applies.

The claim is that a destination like `s3://bucket//key` is conflict-checked as `/key` but written to `key`, which bypasses overwrite protection. This needs a hand-written double-slash URI and is a contrived input.
The claim is that NewTree's new warning mislabels normal bare-root inputs as suspicious. This is log noise only; behaviour is unchanged.

The claim is that overwrite deletes the destination before the copy starts, so a failed copy loses the original destination. The base code had the same delete-before-copy order in both PrefixCopyInternal and PrefixCopyRemote, so the PR did not introduce it.
The claim is that logging every added path in Tree.Add generates huge logs and exposes names. This is debug-log noise/style, not a functional defect.
The claim is that ReadTarStream logs every walked tar entry. This is debug-log noise/style, not a functional defect.

The claim is that remote destination resolution should happen in one place instead of destPathPrefix plus DetermineCopyDestPath. That is a refactoring preference; the two are consistent (see C4), so there is no behavioural defect.

excluded.reason: Claims withUser creates a browser context with no cleanup, leaking memory. The extra context lives only until the worker's browser is torn down and is used by two tests; no concrete failure or measurable leak results in this test-only helper.
Claims the secondBrowser in the change-email test should be closed to avoid resource leaks. Same as R1: one bounded, test-scoped extra context in test code with no concrete consequence.

Claims the non-null assertion on page.context().browser() is unsafe. browser() is null only for persistent/Android contexts; the fixture context (fixtures/base.ts:128) comes from the regular browser fixture, so it is non-null on every reachable path.
Claims the cast of this.n8n.constructor to `new (page: Page) => n8nPage` is unsafe. n8nPage's constructor takes a Page, so the cast is correct; type-style preference.

Claims login in withUser lacks try/catch so failed auth does not propagate meaningful errors. loginAndSetCookies (api-helper.ts:235-252) already throws TestError with the response text, which fails the test as desired.
Claims SettingsPersonalPage locator methods lack the `get` prefix convention. Naming style only.
Claims `changePassword-modal` test id may be a typo and fail. The modal key is 'changePassword' (constants.ts:51) and the removed Cypress test used the same selector; no selector failure is shown.
Claims getAccountType lacks an explicit Locator return type. Inferred type is correct; style.

Link labels ('More info' -> 'more info', 'Learn more', 'Example', 'See docs', 'View metric examples') and whole sentences after a link are now lowercased: 'Choose from the list, or specify IDs using ...' -> 'choose from the list, or specify ids using ...' n8n-io__n8n@f523897.pr_summary: Splits the user list item schema into userMemberSchema (id, firstName, lastName, email, role) and userAdminSchema (member fields plus isPending, isOwner, signInType, settings, personalizationAnswers, projectRelations, mfaEnabled, lastActiveAt, inviteAcceptUrl) and exports both from @n8n/api-types. UsersController.removeSupplementaryFields now parses each listed user with userAdminSchema when the caller has the global user:create scope or the row is the caller's own user, and with userMemberSchema otherwise, so members get only the basic fields of other users from GET /users. Schema unit tests and integration tests are added/updated.

defects.title: Members no longer receive isPending, so the editor treats invited (pending) users as active for members
defects.statement: userMemberSchema (packages/@n8n/api-types/src/schemas/user.schema.ts:25-31) omits isPending, and zod strips unknown keys, so GET /users for a caller without user:create returns other users without isPending (users.controller.ts:99-105). The editor's users store derives isPendingUser from it (`const _isPendingUser = (user) => !!user?.isPending;`, users.store.ts:35, used in addUsers :137 after fetchUsers :323-325), so for a member every invited-but-not-signed-up user becomes isPendingUser=false. Consequences: ProjectNavigation's hasMultipleVerifiedUsers (`allUsers.filter((user) => !user.isPendingUser).length > 1`, ProjectNavigation.vue:30-32) counts pending invites, showing the 'Shared with you' menu item (:111-121) to a member whose only other 'user' is a pending invite; design-system UserInfo/UsersList lose the pending badge and pending-last sorting. isPending is not sensitive (it only says an invite is outstanding) and it was part of the member-visible response before; the PR even deletes the assertion `expect(nonPendingUser!.isPending).toBe(false)` from users.api.test.ts rather than keeping the field.
defects.evidence: user.schema.ts:25-31 member schema has only id/firstName/lastName/email/role; :33-34 `export const userAdminSchema = userMemberSchema.extend({ isPending: z.boolean().optional(),`; users.controller.ts:104 `return userMemberSchema.parse(user);`; users.store.ts:35 `const _isPendingUser = (user: IUserResponse | null) => !!user?.isPending;`, :323-325 `fetchUsers` -> `usersApi.getUsers(...)` -> `addUsers(items)`; ProjectNavigation.vue:30-32 and :111-114 `v-if="(...) && hasMultipleVerifiedUsers"`; ProjectNavigation.vue:89 calls usersStore.fetchUsers() for every user.
defects.notes: Must say that isPending is dropped for members (member schema lacks it) and that this changes how pending users are shown/treated for members. A generic 'the member schema removes fields' without naming isPending or the pending-user consequence does not count; R2's schema-typing point does not count.

defects.title: Hidden admin fields still leak to members through the list filter/sort (mfaEnabled filter, mfaEnabled/lastActiveAt sort)
defects.statement: The PR hides mfaEnabled and lastActiveAt from callers without user:create, but GET /users still accepts, for any caller with user:list, `filter={"mfaEnabled": true|false}` and `sortBy=mfaEnabled:*|lastActiveAt:*` (users-list-filter.dto.ts:16-19, :41). A member can therefore recover (e.g. filter by a colleague's email plus mfaEnabled and read `count`, or filter mfaEnabled:true and read the returned ids) exactly which users have MFA enabled (filter and compare the ids returned) and the order of last activity, so the information restriction the PR introduces (and its tests at users.api.test.ts assert 'mfaEnabled'/'lastActiveAt' are absent) is bypassable. listUsers applies no scope check to the filter/sort options (users.controller.ts:109-118).
defects.evidence: users-list-filter.dto.ts:16-19 `'mfaEnabled:asc', 'mfaEnabled:desc', 'lastActiveAt:asc', 'lastActiveAt:desc'`, :41 `mfaEnabled: z.boolean().optional(),`; users.controller.ts:110 `@GlobalScope('user:list')` then :116 `this.userRepository.buildUserQuery(listQueryOptions)` with no restriction by caller scope; existing test users.api.test.ts:230-259 exercises `filter={ "mfaEnabled": true }`.
defects.notes: Must say that members can still filter or sort by the now-hidden fields (mfaEnabled / lastActiveAt) and so infer them. Complaints about user:create being the wrong scope (R4) do not count.

excluded.reason: Suggests renaming userMemberSchema/userAdminSchema to userBaseSchema/userDetailSchema because the names are misleading. Naming preference; the schemas behave correctly.

Claims usersListSchema.items typed as userAdminSchema mismatches the member-shaped items the controller returns. Every field userAdminSchema adds is .optional() (user.schema.ts:33-43), so member items validate and the inferred type already marks those fields optional; no runtime or type error.

Claims removeSupplementaryFields assumes currentUser is present and would throw without auth. listUsers is behind @GlobalScope('user:list') on an AuthenticatedRequest and req.user is already dereferenced unconditionally (users.controller.ts:122/127); speculative.

Claims user:create is the wrong scope for deciding detail visibility and a dedicated scope should exist. Design preference; user:create already gates inviteAcceptUrl in the same handler and is held by owner/admin; no concrete exposure.

immich-app__immich@9032c7e.pr_summary: Extends the web service worker to precache SvelteKit's `build` and `files` on install and serve them cache-first via appResources(), and adds an ssr() handler that answers GETs whose path matches a hard-coded regex of app route prefixes with the cached '/' document, fetching and caching it on a miss. Asset thumbnail/original caching is unchanged.

defects.title: Entry-point route regex lists `maps` but the route is `/map`, so the map page never gets the cached app shell
defects.statement: The fetch handler decides which GETs are answered with the cached index via a hand-maintained regex of top-level routes (index.ts:40-46). It lists `maps`, but the SvelteKit route is web/src/routes/(user)/map and AppRoute.MAP = '/map' (web/src/lib/constants.ts:35), so `/map` and `/map/...` never match and are not served from the cache, unlike every other user route. The duplicated route list has already drifted from the routes tree.

defects.notes: Must point out `maps` vs the real `/map` route (or that the list misses /map). A generic 'hard-coded list may drift' without naming the mismatch is a near miss. The '/libraries' part of C17 is wrong (no such route directory) but its /map part counts.

defects.title: The app shell ('/') is never precached, so a first offline visit to an entry point fails
defects.statement: addFilesToCache precaches only `build` and `files` (index.ts:14-17, 57-60); '/' is not among them and is not matched by the entry-point regex. ssr() (index.ts:62-77) only stores '/' after a successful online fetch triggered by an earlier controlled navigation to a matched route. If the worker installs and the next navigation to e.g. /photos happens offline, cache.match('/') misses, fetch('/') rejects, and the navigation fails even though all static resources are cached — the 'cache all entry points' goal is only met lazily.
defects.evidence: index.ts:14-17 APP_RESOURCES = [...build, ...files]; :64-69 `new URL('/', origin)`, cache.match then fetch(url).
defects.notes: Must say the '/' shell/index document is not cached at install so an offline first navigation to a route fails. Not: generic 'fetch in ssr has no try/catch' (R5/C8), whose Response.error() alternative is the same network error.

excluded.reason: Says APP_RESOURCES must reference `files` instead of `build` because build excludes static resources. Wrong: APP_RESOURCES already spreads both `build` and `files` (index.ts:14-17); `files` is the $service-worker export for static/.

Says calling event.waitUntil() twice in the install handler may not extend the event lifetime. ExtendableEvent.waitUntil may be called multiple times during dispatch and each promise extends the lifetime; the activate handler already used the same pattern.
Says the URL is parsed twice (url and new URL(...).origin in the ssr call). Trivial micro-optimisation, not a defect.

Says cache.addAll(APP_RESOURCES) rejects the whole install if any resource fails, preventing installation. Failing install when precaching fails is the standard service-worker contract (old worker stays, install retried); no build/static resource is shown to fail.

Says ssr() lacks try/catch around fetch so an offline failure throws unhandled. A rejected respondWith promise produces a network error, the same outcome as returning Response.error(); nothing is lost (the missing-shell problem is D2).
Says appResources duplicates logic from ssr and should share a helper. Duplication/refactoring preference.
Asks to remove the unreachable `!(response instanceof Response)` branch and its comment in appResources. Dead defensive code copied from the existing immichAsset pattern; no behavioural consequence.

Says shared-link navigations lose link-specific metadata because ssr() fetches '/' instead of /share/<key>. The server's per-link tags (api.service.ts ssr) serve link-preview crawlers, which never run this service worker; in a controlled browser the SPA renders its own page, so there is no concrete user-visible consequence.

Says a cross-origin fetch whose pathname matches a build/static path would be answered from the local cache. Contrived: the app issues no cross-origin GETs whose path coincides with its hashed build/static paths.

Asks whether /share/<key> navigations should keep the server's link metadata instead of the cached '/'. Same as C2; the metadata matters to crawlers that do not run the worker, and the candidate itself notes client-side loading restores the page.

Says the inner APP_RESOURCES.includes check in appResources is redundant and the network-first path unreachable. Dead-code/maintainability remark; the cache-miss path still falls through to fetch, so behaviour is correct.
Asks to remove the duplicate APP_RESOURCES.includes guard inside appResources. Same as C6: redundancy, no behavioural effect.

Says an uncached entry-point navigation offline makes fetch(url) reject in ssr(), leaving respondWith rejected. A rejected respondWith yields a network error, identical to Response.error(); the real gap (no precached shell) is D2.

Says the shell fallback should be limited to navigations and same-origin, else data/cross-origin GETs under matched paths get HTML. The web app has no +page.server/+server routes (no __data.json requests) and makes no cross-origin GETs under these paths, so the scenario is not reachable.
Says a cross-origin request to another origin's /share/... is intercepted and answered with that origin's '/'. Contrived: the app does not fetch cross-origin resources under these paths.
Asks to reword the 'for everything else' comment in appResources as a cache-miss fallback. Comment wording nit.
Asks to rename `ssr` since it serves the root shell rather than rendering. Naming preference.
Says non-document GETs under a matched prefix receive root HTML; check navigation mode. Same as C9: no such non-navigation same-origin requests exist in this app.
Says a cross-origin resource whose path coincides with a precached path such as /manifest.json would be served from Immich's cache. Contrived cross-origin scenario with no such request in the app.
Requests a regression test for install followed by a first offline navigation. Test request.

Says /share/[key] direct visits and crawlers get generic metadata because the worker fetches '/'. Crawlers never run the service worker, so they still get the server's per-link tags; controlled-browser users see the SPA-rendered page.

immich-app__immich@d38f1f5.pr_summary: Adds a SvelteKit service worker (web/src/service-worker/index.ts) that intercepts GET /api/assets/<id>/original|thumbnail, serves them from a Cache Storage cache named per deployment version, and tracks in-flight fetches in a URL-keyed AbortController map so pages can cancel them. A BroadcastChannel helper (web/src/lib/utils/sw-messaging.ts) lets image-thumbnail.svelte cancel its URL on destroy and photo-viewer.svelte cancel on unmount and preload neighbours via the worker instead of `new Image()`. Also excludes the service-worker dir from one eslint config object, adds a `prod-down` Makefile target, and removes/adjusts some e2e tests.

defects.title: Service worker caches every thumbnail/original with no expiry or size bound: ignores Cache-Control, serves stale images and grows storage with every original viewed or downloaded
defects.statement: immichAsset (web/src/service-worker/index.ts:43-67) answers from `cache.match(url)` whenever an entry exists and `cache.put`s every 200 response (59-60) into `cache-${version}`; entries are only removed when a new build activates (deleteOldCaches, 35-41). The server's `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400` is ignored, so (a) thumbnail URLs built without a cacheKey (e.g. album-cover.svelte:18) show a stale image indefinitely after regeneration instead of for at most a day, and (b) every original that is viewed, zoomed, preloaded or downloaded (downloadFile's `<a href=/api/assets/<id>/original download>` in asset-utils.ts:262 also matches the route, including videos) is stored in full in Cache Storage with no eviction, growing origin storage until the next release. The un-awaited `cache.put` turns quota failures into unhandled rejections.
defects.evidence: index.ts:45-48 `let response = useCache ? await cache.match(url) : undefined; if (response) { return response; }`; :59-60 `if (response.status === 200) { cache.put(url, response.clone()); }`; :12 `const CACHE = `cache-${version}``; route test :30 `/^\/api\/assets\/[a-f0-9-]+\/(original|thumbnail)/`; asset-utils.ts:262 `downloadUrl(getBaseUrl() + `/assets/${id}/original` ...)`.
defects.notes: Count a comment that says the SW cache never expires / ignores HTTP caching headers (stale thumbnails), or that it caches originals/all assets without size limit or eviction (unbounded storage / quota errors). A comment only about hardcoding `useCache` (R12, C6) or about logging in the catch does not count. The authorization/logout angle is D2.

defects.title: Cached private media is served by URL without re-checking authorization, surviving logout, account switches and revoked shares
defects.statement: Because immichAsset returns `cache.match(url)` (index.ts:45-48) before any request reaches the authenticated asset endpoint, and entries are keyed only by URL within `cache-${version}`, an image fetched under one session is served to any later request for the same URL from that browser: after logout (handleLogout in web/src/lib/utils/auth.ts:100-115 does not clear Cache Storage), after another account signs in, or after a shared link or album access is revoked. The server's per-request access check is bypassed for anything already cached.
defects.evidence: index.ts:45 `let response = useCache ? await cache.match(url) : undefined; if (response) { return response; }`; handleLogout clears only in-memory stores (resetSavedUser, foldersStore.clearCache, ...), never `caches`.
defects.notes: Must say that cached images are served without the server's authorization check, i.e. they remain available after logout/account switch/revocation. Staleness or storage-growth comments belong to D1.

defects.title: pendingLoads keyed only by URL: concurrent same-URL loads overwrite/delete each other's AbortController, so a cancel can abort another consumer's request or fail to abort at all
defects.statement: Every immichAsset call does its own fetch and `pendingLoads.set(url, controller)` (index.ts:50-54), overwriting any existing entry, and its `finally` unconditionally deletes the key (66). There is no in-flight dedupe, so a preload racing the viewer's , two tabs sharing the one worker, or duplicate thumbnails download the same URL twice. A cancel message (78-84) aborts whichever request registered last — possibly one a still-visible image or another tab needs, which then gets Response.error() and renders broken — while the other request is unregistered and cannot be cancelled; whichever finishes first also deletes the survivor's entry.
defects.evidence: index.ts:54 `pendingLoads.set(url.toString(), cancelToken);`, :66 `pendingLoads.delete(url.toString());`, :80-83 `const pending = pendingLoads.get(url.toString()); if (pending) { pending.abort(); ... }`; sw-messaging.ts:4 posts only `{ type: 'cancel', url }`.
defects.notes: Must identify that same-URL requests share one map entry (overwritten or deleted by another request), so cancellation hits the wrong request / cannot identify the owner / breaks another consumer. Comments about cancelling superseded URLs of one component (R7, C23, C31, C46) or about the cache-lookup window (C9, C19) do not count.

defects.title: Neighbour preloading silently stops whenever no running service worker receives the BroadcastChannel message (insecure origins, first visit, idle-terminated worker)
defects.statement: photo-viewer.svelte:72-78 replaced `new Image().src = ...` with preloadImageUrl, which only posts a BroadcastChannel message (sw-messaging.ts:6-8). The message does nothing unless a service worker is installed and currently running: on non-secure origins (e.g. self-hosted http://<lan-ip>:2283, where no worker can register), on a first visit before the worker controls the page, or after the browser has stopped an idle worker (BroadcastChannel messages do not wake or extend a service worker; the preload promise at index.ts:85-88 is not tied to any extendable event), the next/previous image is no longer preloaded. The PR states that without a secure context 'you don't lose any function', but the pre-existing preload is lost.
defects.evidence: base photo-viewer.svelte `let img = new Image(); img.src = getAssetUrl(preloadAsset.id, targetSize, preloadAsset.thumbhash);` → head :75 `preloadImageUrl(getAssetUrl(...))`; sw-messaging.ts:6-7 `broadcast.postMessage({ type: 'preload', url });`; index.ts:85-88 `} else if (event.data.type === 'preload') { ... immichAsset(url); }` with no waitUntil.
defects.notes: Must say preloading now depends on an active service worker and is lost without one (insecure context / before install / worker not running), or that the broadcast-triggered preload is not kept alive by an extendable event so it can be dropped. Generic 'BroadcastChannel may be undefined' comments (R4, R10, C13) do not count.

excluded.reason: Suggests the new prod-down target consider volume flags/parity with prod. `down --remove-orphans` is a correct, intentional choice; preference only.

Says ignoring the service-worker directory bypasses all linting and suggests overrides. Lint-configuration preference; in flat config the `ignores` only excludes that object, the file is still linted by the recommended configs and the lint step passes.
Asks to confirm the `**/service-worker/**` glob matches the actual folder and to narrow it. The folder is exactly web/src/service-worker/, so it matches as intended; no other code is excluded.
Says importing sw-messaging throws where BroadcastChannel is unavailable. BroadcastChannel exists in every browser immich supports and the web app disables SSR; no reachable environment lacks it.

Says SW preloading may not warm the browser decode cache like `new Image()`. Speculative performance remark; the response is cached and served from Cache Storage on navigation. (The real loss of preloading without a worker is D4, which this does not describe.)

Says reading the $derived imageLoaderUrl in the onMount cleanup may be stale or undefined. In Svelte 5 it returns its last value, always a string, and PhotoViewer is keyed by asset id, so the right URL is cancelled.
Says a thumbnail whose url prop changes never cancels the old request. A mounted thumbnail's url only changes on a thumbhash change; the superseded request is a negligible edge, not a leak.
Suggests guarding cancelImageUrl(url) for empty/loaded URLs. url is a required string and cancelling a finished URL is a no-op in the worker.
Suggests extracting the 'immich' channel name to a constant. Style.
Says top-level BroadcastChannel crashes SSR. The web app sets `ssr = false` (web/src/routes/+layout.ts) and Node ≥18 has a global BroadcastChannel anyway.
Suggests a TypeScript type for the message payload. Style.
Says the hardcoded `useCache` constant should be configurable. Configurability preference; does not describe the caching consequences (D1/D2).
Says the '// ignore POST requests etc' comment is redundant. Comment style.
Suggests extracting the URL regex into a constant. Style.
Says the catch block swallows errors without logging. Logging preference; returning Response.error() on abort is intended.
Says `new URL(urlstring, event.origin)` can throw on malformed input. URLs come from getAssetUrl/createUrl and are always valid relative paths; unreachable.
Claims event.origin is undefined on BroadcastChannel MessageEvents. Wrong: BroadcastChannel message events carry the sender's origin in `event.origin`, so the URL resolves correctly.
Says the preload branch's un-awaited immichAsset can cause an unhandled rejection. Fetch failures are caught inside immichAsset; only a caches.open failure could reject, which is contrived.
Says URL parsing is duplicated between the cancel and preload branches. Style.
Says the matcher `[a-f0-9-]+` misses uppercase UUIDs. Immich asset ids are generated lowercase by the database and all URL builders use them verbatim; unreachable.
Asks whether cancellation limited to original/thumbnail paths matches the description. Scope clarification, not a code defect.
Says `useCache` only gates reads while writes still happen. Dead-toggle naming issue on a hardcoded `true` constant; no behaviour consequence.
Says the description promises app precaching on activation but the worker does not implement it. PR-description mismatch; no existing behaviour regresses.

Says a cancel arriving during caches.open/cache.match is lost because the controller is registered only afterwards. The window is milliseconds and the consequence is just an uncancelled fetch, i.e. pre-PR behaviour; negligible.
Says the `instanceof Response` check is redundant. Style.

Says fetch(url) drops the original request's headers, so Range requests become full fetches. No caller of these routes sends Range or other headers (img tags, anchor downloads and the panorama viewer send plain GETs with cookies, which same-origin fetch still includes); speculative.

Says constructing BroadcastChannel at import breaks rendering where the API is absent, including jsdom specs. Supported browsers have it, and the vitest jsdom environment inherits Node's global BroadcastChannel; not reachable.

Says the discarded cache.put promise may not complete before the worker's lifetime ends. The fetch event's response stream keeps the worker alive while the tee'd clone is written; speculative (quota-rejection handling is covered under D1 via C42).

Says cache.put is not awaited or tied to the event lifetime so the preload may not be cached. Speculative lifetime concern; the concrete preload-lifetime problem is D4 (C3/C29) and quota handling is D1.

Says deleteOldCaches deletes every Cache Storage cache on the origin, including other apps'. Nothing else on the immich origin uses Cache Storage (the only `caches.` use is this worker); not reachable.
Says the thumbnail's destroy only cancels the final url when the url prop changes while mounted. Same negligible edge as R7.
Says the worker does not precache the app despite the description's claim. PR-description mismatch, not a regression.

Asks to keep an end-to-end loading-spinner assertion after the test's removal. Request for tests; page.route cannot intercept worker-handled requests, so the removal is a test-infrastructure consequence.
Says ignoring the worker directory removes lint coverage. Lint-configuration preference; the file is still linted by the recommended configs and lint passes.
Says a preview URL superseded by zoom before unmount is never cancelled. The preview has normally loaded before the user zooms; negligible edge.
Says intercepted requests lose Authorization/Range headers. No caller sends these headers to the matched routes (auth is by cookie or `key` query param, which fetch(url) preserves); speculative.
Says the matcher misses deployments under a URL prefix. Immich's web app serves the API at `/api` on its own origin; no prefixed deployment is supported.
Asks whether the prod-down Makefile target belongs in this PR. Scope/process remark, not a defect.
Asks to distinguish aborts from unexpected fetch failures in the catch. Logging/diagnostics preference.
Asks to share the 'immich'/'cancel'/'preload' protocol strings between page and worker. Maintainability preference; the two copies currently agree.

Says the `ignores` entry only applies to its own config object, so the worker is still linted by the earlier configs without this object's globals/type-aware rules. Accurate description of flat-config semantics, but lint still passes (typescript-eslint turns off no-undef for .ts files) and the author's eslint-disable comment shows it was run; no broken step.
Says caches.keys() is origin-wide so activation deletes other features' caches. Nothing else on the origin uses Cache Storage; not reachable.
Says activation erases unrelated offline caches on the origin. Nothing else on the immich origin uses Cache Storage; not reachable.
Asks to share the asset-route matcher with the SDK URL builders. Maintainability preference; the paths currently agree.
Says cleanup cancels only the current imageLoaderUrl, leaving superseded preview fetches running. Same negligible edge as C31.

Says a cancel sent while caches.open/cache.match is pending is lost and the fetch then starts anyway. The window is milliseconds and the consequence is one uncancelled fetch, i.e. pre-PR behaviour; negligible (same as C9).

immich-app__immich@b7a1255.pr_summary: Upgrades bullmq ^4.8.0 -> ^5.51.0 and splits album-update notifications from one job per album (merged recipientIds) into one job per recipient: AlbumService.addAssets emits one 'album.update' event per recipient, the NOTIFY_ALBUM_UPDATE jobId becomes `${albumId}/${recipientID}`, onAlbumUpdate removes any pending job for that pair and re-queues it (debounce), and handleAlbumUpdate emails the single recipient. JobRepository.removeJob takes (name, jobID), returns void and no longer swallows 'Missing key for job'. Specs and mocks updated.

defects.title: handleAlbumUpdate no longer checks the recipient is still an album member/owner, so removed members still get the update email
defects.statement: The old handler built recipients from album.albumUsers plus the owner and filtered by recipientIds, so anyone removed from the album during the 5-minute delay was dropped. The new handler (server/src/services/notification.service.ts:293-341) loads the album and owner but emails userRepository.get(recipientID) with no membership check. A user removed from a shared album (or whose share was revoked) within the delay window still receives an email with the album name, link and thumbnail attachment of an album they can no longer access.
defects.evidence: Base (removed): `const recipients = [...album.albumUsers.map((user) => user.user), owner].filter((user) => recipientIds.includes(user.id));`. Head :309 `const user = await this.userRepository.get(recipientID, { withDeleted: false });` then straight to preferences, renderEmail and SEND_EMAIL queue (:332-341) with no albumUsers/owner check.
defects.notes: Must say the album-membership filter was dropped so a recipient removed from the album (during the delay) can still be emailed. Comments that merely say the owner lookup is unused do not count.

defects.title: removeJob dropped its error handling; a remove failure now throws out of the album.update event and fails addAssets (and skips remaining recipients)
defects.statement: removeJob (server/src/repositories/job.repository.ts:233-240) used to catch 'Missing key for job' from existing.remove() (the job finished/was removed between getJob and remove). It now propagates every remove failure. onAlbumUpdate awaits it (notification.service.ts:98) and EventRepository.onEvent awaits handlers without catching (event.repository.ts:236-245), so the rejection propagates into AlbumService.addAssets' per-recipient loop (album.service.ts:173-175): the request fails after the assets were already added, and the later recipients in the loop are never queued. The same propagation applies when BullMQ refuses to remove a locked active job.
defects.evidence: Head: `const existingJob = await ...getJob(jobID); if (existingJob) { await existingJob.remove(); }`. Base had `try { await existingJob.remove(); } catch (error) { if (error.message?.includes('Missing key for job')) return; throw error; }`. event.repository.ts:244 `await handler(...event.args);`; album.service.ts:173-175 `for (const recipientID of allUsersExceptUs) { await this.eventRepository.emit('album.update', ...) }`.
defects.notes: Must point at the removed Missing-key try/catch or an unhandled remove failure (race/locked/active job) propagating to addAssets / aborting the remaining recipients. Note the locked-active-job rejection was already rethrown in base; a comment only about that case is a near-miss but is accepted because it describes the same propagation path. Pure latency comments about the serial loop do not count.

defects.title: Album-update jobs already queued in the old shape are silently dropped on upgrade
defects.statement: Delayed NOTIFY_ALBUM_UPDATE jobs queued before the deploy carry `{id, recipientIds}` under jobId=albumId. After upgrade handleAlbumUpdate destructures `recipientID` (notification.service.ts:293), which is undefined, so userRepository.get(undefined) finds no user and the job is SKIPPED: those pending emails are never sent. The new removeJob/queue use `${albumId}/${recipientID}` (job.repository.ts:210, notification.service.ts:98) and never match the old albumId jobIds, so updates during rollout do not replace them either.
defects.evidence: types.ts INotifyAlbumUpdateJob now `recipientID: string`; no fallback for `recipientIds` anywhere in head (git grep). Base jobId for NOTIFY_ALBUM_UPDATE was `item.data.id`.
defects.notes: Must mention in-flight/queued jobs with the old payload shape or old jobId being lost/skipped/not replaced after deploy.

excluded.reason: Asks to rename `recipientID` to `recipientId` for naming consistency. Naming preference; the field is used consistently across the event map, job type and handlers.

Claims `item.data.recipientID` may be undefined when composing the jobId, producing ids like `abc/undefined`. recipientID is a required string in INotifyAlbumUpdateJob and the only producer (onAlbumUpdate) always sets it from AlbumService's user id list; unreachable for newly queued jobs (old-format jobs are D3, which this comment does not describe).
Asks to use a JSDoc @deprecated tag on removeJob instead of a plain comment. Documentation-style preference.
Suggests Promise.all instead of sequential per-recipient emits in addAssets for performance. A handful of Redis round trips per album member; no concrete consequence, micro-optimisation.

Questions removing and immediately re-queueing the same job as inefficient. Remove-then-requeue is the intentional debounce: it resets the 5-minute delay for the same jobId, which BullMQ would otherwise ignore as a duplicate add.
Generic advice to wrap external calls in defensive try/catch in handleAlbumUpdate. Names no concrete failure; job failures are handled by the job framework.

Claims user.email may be null/empty for some accounts and should be guarded before SEND_EMAIL. email is a required user column and the old code also emailed recipient.email without a guard; speculative and pre-existing.
Notes INotifyAlbumInviteJob uses recipientId while INotifyAlbumUpdateJob uses recipientID. Naming inconsistency with no functional effect.

Asks whether per-recipient event emission serializes Redis work on the asset-add request path, growing latency with recipient count. A few sequential Redis round trips per member; no concrete user-visible consequence demonstrated, performance preference.
Suggests dispatching per-recipient emits with Promise.all so notification scheduling does not scale linearly. Same as C1/R4: micro-optimisation without concrete consequence.
Asks for the spec to set up an actual pending job to test replacement. Test-coverage request, not a defect.

Asks whether retaining pending-job removal contradicts the PR's stated goal of moving away from it. A question; the removal is kept deliberately (marked deprecated) as the per-recipient debounce and behaves correctly.
Asks to rename a spec title that still mentions adding new recipients. Test naming nit.
Asks to reword the TODO from 'asset notifications' to 'album-update notifications'. Comment wording nit with no consequence.
Asks the spec to establish a pending job and trigger a second update, plus rename the title. Test-coverage request and naming nit.
Asks to centralize the album-recipient jobId format shared by onAlbumUpdate and getJobOptions. The two sites currently agree; a refactoring preference, not a drifted rule.
Same as C18: share the jobId encoding between removal and enqueueing. The two constructions currently match; maintainability preference only.
Says thumbnail lookup and uncached config loading happen before the recipient/preference checks, wasting work per skipped job. Minor efficiency ordering with no concrete failure shown; not a defect.

vllm-project__vllm@075f1b5.pr_summary: Merges KVCacheManager.append_slots (decode) into allocate_slots (prefill) in vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py: allocate_slots(request, num_tokens, new_computed_blocks) touches prefix-cache hits first, checks free capacity, and on failure reverses the touch with a new _untouch helper; req_to_blocks becomes a defaultdict(list). The scheduler's running path calls allocate_slots(request, n, []), num_tokens == 0 now raises for decode too, and tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py is updated.

defects.title: Failed allocation touches then untouches prefix-hit blocks, moving them to the MRU tail of the free queue and changing LRU eviction order
defects.statement: allocate_slots now calls _touch(new_computed_blocks) before the capacity check (vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py:147-148); _touch removes every ref_cnt==0 hit from its position in free_block_queue (:421-422). When the check fails (:163-166), _untouch (:425-438) re-appends those blocks at the tail in forward order. The old code only counted evictable hits and never moved them. Since eviction pops from the head (_get_new_blocks :358) and free() appends in reverse so tail blocks are evicted first (:229-237), every failed attempt (repeated each step for the head waiting request under memory pressure) makes an unscheduled request's cached prefix look most-recently-used and inverts its order, so other prefixes are evicted instead and the chain's first block is evicted before its tail. Eviction policy changes as a side effect of a refactor billed as no functional change.
defects.evidence: kv_cache_manager.py:147-148 `if self.enable_caching: self._touch(new_computed_blocks)`; :163-166 `if num_new_blocks > self.free_block_queue.num_free_blocks: self._untouch(new_computed_blocks); return None`; :437-438 `if block.ref_cnt == 0: self.free_block_queue.append(block)`; :232 `ordered_blocks = reversed(blocks)`; :358 `self.free_block_queue.popleft()`. Base computed num_evictable_computed_blocks and returned None without touching.
defects.notes: Must say that on allocation failure the touch/untouch changes the free-queue position or order of the prefix-hit blocks (appended to the tail, not restored to original position, LRU order changed). Docstring typos in _untouch do not count.

excluded.reason: Suggests making new_computed_blocks default to None so callers need not pass []. API-shape preference.
Points out the 'cacheing' typo in a comment. Typo, not a defect.
Says the _untouch docstring should say 'Untouching' and 'blocks to untouch' instead of 'blocks to touch'. Docstring wording; trivial.
Asks to change the _untouch argument description from 'blocks to touch' to 'blocks to untouch'. Docstring wording; trivial.
Suggests 'Untouch blocks decrease' grammar in the _untouch docstring. Trivial wording.

Claims running requests should pass get_computed_blocks() results instead of [] to allocate_slots. A running request already owns its computed prefix in req_to_blocks; new_computed_blocks is only for fresh prefix-cache hits at admission, so [] matches the old append_slots behaviour.
Suggests sharing the decrement-and-enqueue release logic between _untouch and free(). Duplication/style suggestion with no drift shown.

Asks the allocate_slots docstring to describe running requests rather than a 'new decode request'. Docstring wording; the docstring says 'a new prefill or a new decode request', which is not wrong enough to mislead.
Asks the docstring to describe extension of running requests and to document the None return. Documentation request, not a defect.

vllm-project__vllm@a800045.pr_summary: Adds AIMODataset (AI-MO/aimo-validation-aime, NuminaMath-1.5, NuminaMath-CoT) support to benchmarks/benchmark_throughput.py: get_requests selects AIMODataset for those hf dataset paths with the train split, and validate_args requires the vllm backend. The benchmarks README gains a HuggingFace-AIMO row and serving/throughput examples for AI-MO/aimo-validation-aime.

defects.title: New online AIMO example requests Qwen/QwQ-32B from a section whose documented server serves Qwen/Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct
defects.statement: The AIMO serving example (README.md:196-205) sits under 'Other HuggingFaceDataset Examples', whose only server command is `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct` (README.md:166), yet it passes `--model Qwen/QwQ-32B` with no matching `vllm serve` step. benchmark_serving.py sends that model name in its initial test request and aborts when the server rejects an unserved model, so following the documentation as written fails.
defects.evidence: README.md:166 `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct --disable-log-requests`; :199-200 `python3 vllm/benchmarks/benchmark_serving.py \ --model Qwen/QwQ-32B \`.
defects.notes: Counts: the new serving example's model does not match the server the section starts (needs its own vllm serve QwQ-32B). Script path prefix (vllm/benchmarks vs benchmarks) comments do not count.

excluded.reason: Says the serving example's vllm/benchmarks/ script prefix is inconsistent with the throughput example's benchmarks/ prefix. The README already mixes both cwd-relative spellings (e.g. README.md:156 `python3 benchmarks/benchmark_serving.py`); both name the real script, doc-style consistency only.

Says AIMO hardcodes dataset_split='train' instead of args.hf_split. Matches how VisionArena/InstructCoder are handled in the same function (benchmark_throughput.py:322-330) and how benchmark_serving.py handles AIMODataset; the AI-MO datasets are used with their train split. Consistency preference.
