vllm-project__vllm@6217b0c.pr_summary: Adds a shutdown() override to MultiConnector that calls shutdown() on every wrapped KV connector, logging each failure with logger.exception and re-raising the first exception after all connectors have been attempted. Previously MultiConnector inherited the base no-op shutdown, so wrapped connectors were never shut down.

excluded.reason: Claims logger.exception duplicates the exception text because the message also formats str(e). Cosmetic log duplication (multi_connector.py:96-97); no functional consequence.

Claims re-raising a child's shutdown failure propagates through the worker/executor shutdown so EngineCore.shutdown skips scheduler.shutdown. That propagation is the existing contract for any connector whose shutdown raises (a single connector configured directly behaves identically via ensure_kv_transfer_shutdown -> multiproc_executor shutdown -> core.py shutdown); MultiConnector now matches it after attempting every child, so the PR does not make the unguarded teardown chain worse.

Claims the re-raise leaves _KV_CONNECTOR_AGENT set and skips message-queue clearing and distributed teardown in the worker. Same pre-existing teardown chain as C1: ensure_kv_transfer_shutdown and WorkerProc.shutdown already abort on any connector shutdown exception; MultiConnector merely forwards its children's errors like a directly configured connector.
Suggests keeping only the first exception instead of a list. Style/simplification; behaviour identical.
Asks for tests of shutdown delegation and continuation after a failure. Request for tests.

astral-sh__uv@61b521f.pr_summary: Adds an integration test `install_remote_requirements_txt` to crates/uv/tests/it/pip_install.rs that serves a requirements.txt from a wiremock MockServer behind basic auth, asserting failure without credentials and success with credentials in the URL, then mounts a second mock intended to serve updated contents (Jinja2) and re-runs the install. Adds `wiremock` (workspace dep) to the uv crate's [dev-dependencies] and Cargo.lock.

defects.title: The 'updated requirements.txt' step is dead: the original mock still wins and the assertion cannot tell the two bodies apart
defects.statement: wiremock selects among matching mocks by priority then mount order, and all mocks here have the default priority. The Flask mock with basic_auth (pip_install.rs:504-509) was mounted first and matches every authenticated GET /requirements.txt, so the later 'Update the mock server to serve the new requirements.txt' mock (pip_install.rs:561-573) is never selected (the server is never reset). Even if it were, the third invocation's expected output 'Audited 1 package' (pip_install.rs:575-585) is identical for 'Flask' and for 'Jinja2' (already installed as a Flask dependency), and the final check is again `import flask`. The step therefore verifies nothing about re-fetching changed remote contents while its comment claims it does.
defects.evidence: pip_install.rs:504-509 `Mock::given(method("GET")).and(path("/requirements.txt")).and(basic_auth(username, password)).respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200).set_body_string(requirements_txt))` with requirements_txt = "Flask", mounted first; :563 `// Update the mock server to serve the new requirements.txt` mounts an identical matcher without server.reset(); :584 expects `Audited 1 package`; :587 `context.assert_command("import flask").success();`. The second install (:537-555) already installed jinja2==3.1.3.
defects.notes: Counts if the comment says the updated/second mock does not take effect (first-mounted mock still matches / server not reset) or that the final assertion cannot distinguish the new body from the old, so the step does not test the changed remote file. Generic 'add more tests' does not count.

excluded.reason: Claims wiremock should be a dev-dependency rather than a regular dependency shipped in production binaries. It is added under [dev-dependencies] in crates/uv/Cargo.toml (the section containing reqwest/similar/tar/tempfile/zip); Cargo.lock lists dev-deps too, so nothing ships.

Claims the test will hang because #[tokio::test]'s current-thread runtime is blocked by uv_snapshot!'s synchronous Command::output() so wiremock cannot answer. wiremock's MockServer runs its HTTP server on its own dedicated thread and runtime, independent of the test's runtime, so the blocking wait does not starve it; the same pattern is used by uv's other wiremock tests.
Claims the mock server cannot serve requests while uv_snapshot! blocks the current-thread runtime, so the test hangs. Same as C1: wiremock serves from its own thread.
Claims a single-threaded tokio test runtime deadlocks with blocking Command::output() while wiremock needs the runtime. Same as C1: wiremock's server does not run on the test's runtime.

dbeaver__dbeaver@ed40132.pr_summary: Lets navigator object filters match overloaded objects (functions/procedures, Postgre aggregates/dependencies) by their overloaded name with arguments as well as by plain name: DBSObjectFilter.matches(String) becomes matches(String... names), where an include or exclude pattern applies if any of the names matches, and DBNDatabaseNode passes both getName() and getOverloadedName() for DBPOverloadedObject children, which also makes the navigator's 'hide'/'show only' actions (which store the node display name) work for functions.

defects.title: Signature-aware matching applied only in the navigator; SQL completion and Go-to-object still filter by bare name
defects.statement: Only DBNDatabaseNode (DBNDatabaseNode.java:726-736) passes the overloaded name to DBSObjectFilter.matches. The same per-type object filters are reused by SQLCompletionAnalyzer (SQLCompletionAnalyzer.java:694 `filter.matches(proposal.getObject().getName())`) and GotoObjectDialog (GotoObjectDialog.java:214 `filter.matches(ref.getName())`), which still pass only the bare name. Now that a signature filter such as 'show only foo(integer)' (the display name stored by the navigator action) actually shows the function in the tree, those other consumers reject the same function because 'foo' does not match 'foo(integer)', so the object is visible in the navigator but missing from completion and Go-to-object.
defects.evidence: DBNDatabaseNode.java:729-733 `if (childItem instanceof DBPOverloadedObject overloadedObject) { isMatchingFilter = filter.matches(objectName, overloadedObject.getOverloadedName()); }`; SQLCompletionAnalyzer.java:694 and GotoObjectDialog.java:214 call matches with getName() only; NavigatorUtils.java:444-446 stores `node.getNodeDisplayName()` via addExclude/addInclude.
defects.notes: Must say other consumers of the same object filter (SQL completion, Go-to-object) still match only the plain name, so signature filters behave inconsistently between the navigator and those paths. Generic 'add tests' or binary-compat remarks do not count.

excluded.reason: Says objectName or getOverloadedName() may be null and cause an NPE in matches. DBPOverloadedObject.getOverloadedName() is declared @NotNull and the implementations return non-null values; a null getName() would have NPE'd identically in the old matches(String).
Asks whether the project's Java level supports instanceof pattern matching. DBeaver already builds on Java 17+, so this compiles.
Suggests renaming matches to matchesAny. Naming preference.

Says a null element in names NPEs inside matchesPattern. Pre-existing: the old matchesPattern(pattern, name) would NPE the same way on a null name; callers pass object names and the added overloaded name is @NotNull.

Says changing matches(String) to matches(String...) changes the JVM descriptor, so precompiled plugins calling the old method get NoSuchMethodError. All in-tree callers recompile against the varargs signature (source-compatible); DBeaver does not promise binary compatibility for this internal model API and no concrete prebuilt consumer is shown.

Says the new varargs signature breaks binary compatibility for compiled plugins calling matches(String). Same as C1: source-compatible change inside a monorepo built together; no demonstrated consumer.
Asks for regression tests for signature include/exclude and bare-name matching. Test request, not a defect.

Claims a filter for `f(integer, text)` can never match because SQLUtils.splitFilter splits the entered text at the argument comma. Wrong for the paths this PR serves: the filter dialog stores entries as a list (EditObjectFilterDialog.java:187-188 collectStringValues), the navigator hide/show-only actions call addInclude/addExclude with the whole display name, and the modern serializer stores lists; splitFilter is only used by the legacy string constructor.
Asks to document that any name matching an exclude vetoes the object. Documentation request; the behaviour is intended.
Says single-name callers now allocate a varargs array. Negligible micro-performance.
Suggests a loop instead of Arrays.stream per pattern. Micro-performance/style, no measurable consequence.

dbeaver__dbeaver@dc67ca7.pr_summary: Adds a basic SAP HANA table-partition view: a new HANAPartition model (extends HANATable, implements DBSTablePartition) loaded by a PartitionCache in HANATable that joins TABLE_PARTITIONS with M_CS_TABLES, a 'Partitions' navigator folder under tables in plugin.xml, and property labels in bundle.properties. To hide table-level properties on partition rows it overrides getName/getTableType/getSchema/getDescription in HANATable with new @Property annotations guarded by a HANANotPartitionedTable visibleIf validator.

defects.title: Re-annotating getName/getSchema/getDescription in HANATable drops the inherited editable/optional/label attributes for every HANA table
defects.statement: plugins/org.jkiss.dbeaver.ext.hana/src/org/jkiss/dbeaver/ext/hana/model/HANATable.java:70-98 overrides getName, getTableType, getSchema and getDescription with fresh @Property annotations that only carry viewable/order/visibleIf. Method annotations are not inherited and DBeaver reads the most-derived annotated method, so for ALL HANA tables (not just partitions): the name loses `editable = true` (AbstractTable.java:81), so it can no longer be edited in the properties editor / new-table editor; getDescription loses editableExpr/updatableExpr and MULTILINE (GenericTableBase.java:304), so comments are no longer editable; getSchema loses `optional = true` and the SchemaNameTermProvider label (GenericTableBase.java:181); orders change too.
defects.evidence: plugins/org.jkiss.dbeaver.ext.hana/src/org/jkiss/dbeaver/ext/hana/model/HANATable.java:72 `@Property(viewable = true, order = 1, visibleIf = HANANotPartitionedTable.class) public String getName()` vs AbstractTable.java:81 `@Property(viewable = true, editable = true, order = 1)`; plugins/org.jkiss.dbeaver.ext.hana/src/org/jkiss/dbeaver/ext/hana/model/HANATable.java:94 vs GenericTableBase.java:304 `@Property(viewable = true, editableExpr = "object.dataSource.metaModel.tableCommentEditable", updatableExpr = …, length = PropertyLength.MULTILINE, order = 100)`; plugins/org.jkiss.dbeaver.ext.hana/src/org/jkiss/dbeaver/ext/hana/model/HANATable.java:87 vs GenericTableBase.java:181 `optional = true, labelProvider = GenericSchema.SchemaNameTermProvider.class`. HANAMetaModel.java:106 creates every table as `new HANATable(...)`.
defects.notes: Must say the overriding @Property annotations lose the original attributes (editable name, editable description, optional/labelProvider schema) and thus affect ordinary tables. Comments only about the visibleIf validator's name (R4, C4, C6) do not count.

defects.title: Partitions are HANATable objects named by PART_ID under the schema, so inherited table operations target a non-existent table SCHEMA."<partId>"
defects.statement: plugins/org.jkiss.dbeaver.ext.hana/src/org/jkiss/dbeaver/ext/hana/model/HANAPartition.java:44,65 makes each partition a HANATable via `super(table.getContainer(), String.valueOf(partId), ...)`: container = schema, name = partition number. The object inherits all table behaviour (data container, DDL, columns, row count, getTableSize via the schema statistics) whose SQL/lookup uses the table name, so opening a partition from the new Partitions folder (plugin.xml:42-45) shows Data/DDL/column tabs and statistics that query or look up SCHEMA."1" and fail or show nothing.
defects.evidence: plugins/org.jkiss.dbeaver.ext.hana/src/org/jkiss/dbeaver/ext/hana/model/HANAPartition.java:44 `public class HANAPartition extends HANATable implements DBSTablePartition`; :65 `super(table.getContainer(), String.valueOf(partId), table.getTableType(), dbResult);`. GenericTableBase builds its fully-qualified name from container + name.
defects.notes: Must say the partition object is exposed as a table named by its PART_ID so inherited table operations (data/DDL/row count/attributes) run against the wrong/non-existent name. A bare 'should not extend HANATable' remark without the consequence is a near-miss.

defects.title: HANATable exposes getPartitions but does not implement DBSPartitionContainer, so generic path lookup cannot resolve HANA partitions
defects.statement: plugins/org.jkiss.dbeaver.ext.hana/src/org/jkiss/dbeaver/ext/hana/model/HANATable.java:44,137-140 adds getPartitions without implementing DBSPartitionContainer, unlike the other drivers' partitioned tables (MySQLTable, DB2Table, OracleTablePhysical). DBUtils.findObjectByPath (DBUtils.java:610-617) only searches partitions when the entity implements DBSPartitionContainer, so a partition shown in the navigator cannot be resolved by object path (returns null) — e.g. when a saved navigator/editor reference to a partition is restored.
defects.evidence: DBUtils.java:610 `if (finalEntity instanceof DBSPartitionContainer partitionContainer) { … partitionContainer.getPartitions(monitor) …}`; HANATable.java:44 `public class HANATable extends GenericTable implements DBPObjectStatistics` (no DBSPartitionContainer).
defects.notes: Must say HANATable should implement DBSPartitionContainer / generic partition lookup cannot find these partitions.

defects.title: Multi-level range partitions show only the first populated level's bounds
defects.statement: plugins/org.jkiss.dbeaver.ext.hana/src/org/jkiss/dbeaver/ext/hana/model/HANAPartition.java:70-79 takes LEVEL_1 range min/max and only falls back to level 2/3 when level 1 is empty. For a RANGE-RANGE (multi-level range) table every second-level partition shares the same level-1 bounds, so distinct partitions display identical Range Start/End and the level-2 bounds that distinguish them are never shown.
defects.evidence: plugins/org.jkiss.dbeaver.ext.hana/src/org/jkiss/dbeaver/ext/hana/model/HANAPartition.java:70-75 `this.rangeStart = …LEVEL_1_RANGE_MIN_VALUE…; if (CommonUtils.isEmpty(this.rangeStart)) { …LEVEL_2… }`.
defects.notes: Must say that populated lower-level bounds are ignored when level 1 is non-empty (multi-level partitions display incomplete/identical ranges). R7 (claims level 3 overwrites level 2) and R8 (rangeEnd not checked) do not count.

excluded.reason: Asks to Title-Case 'Last delta merge'/'Last log replay' labels. Cosmetic label style.

Claims the folder type should be HANATable rather than HANAPartition or the partitions property will never resolve. Wrong: in DBeaver navigator configs the folder type is the child object type (GenericTableIndex for Indexes at plugin.xml:37, CubridPartition in ext.cubrid), and `property="partitions"` resolves on the parent HANATable (getPartitions, HANATable.java:138).
Asks for a self-closing <items/> tag. XML style.
Says HANANotPartitionedTable is misnamed because it tests for partition objects, not partitioned tables. Naming only; behaviour works as intended (the real problem with those overrides is D1).

Asks to rename the validator since it excludes HANAPartition instances. Naming preference.
Lists unused imports in HANAPartition. Compiles fine; cleanliness only.
Says @NotNull on primitive int partId is redundant. Harmless style.
Claims a level-3 value can overwrite a level-2 value. Wrong: level 3 is read only if rangeStart is still empty after level 2 (HANAPartition.java:76).
Says rangeEnd is not checked so a start without an end may appear. A range with only a min value is a legitimate HANA state; showing an empty Range End is correct.
Asks for real statistics logic instead of hasStatistics() false. Design choice; partition sizes are exposed as dedicated properties.
Asks to make PartitionCache private. Encapsulation style.
Says the dbResult null check comes after dbResult is used. Dead code only: JDBCObjectCache calls fetchObject with a non-null, positioned result set, so there is no NPE path.
Says the dbResult null branch is unreachable and should be removed. Dead-code cleanup, no functional impact.
Asks to remove the unreachable result-set null check. Dead-code cleanup.
Asks to remove the unreachable null guard. Dead-code cleanup.
Says HANAPartition.getStatProperties duplicates the inherited null-returning method. Redundant override; no behaviour change.

Claims table refresh leaves the partition cache stale. Wrong: GenericTableBase.refreshObject reloads via the table cache, and AbstractObjectCache.deepCopyCachedObject (lines 335-338) clears every DBSObjectCache field (including partitionCache) on the refreshed object, or loadObjects recreates the table objects.
Says partitionCache is never cleared on refreshObject. Wrong: the refresh path's deepCopyCachedObject clears DBSObjectCache fields such as partitionCache (AbstractObjectCache.java:335-338).
Says RECORD_COUNT as int overflows above 2^31 rows. Unreachable: a HANA column-store partition is limited to about 2 billion rows, the int range.

Says M_CS_TABLES may have several host rows per partition, duplicating PART_IDs. Speculative: a partition lives on one index server; no concrete duplicate case in normal setups.
Asks to translate the new labels into other locale bundles. i18n fallback to English is standard; not a defect.
Asks for a singular 'Partition' item label instead of reusing the plural. Cosmetic label choice.
Asks for tests of the partition mapping. Test request, not a defect.

dbeaver__dbeaver@8224826.pr_summary: Adds a Databricks-specific execution context (DatabricksExecutionContext) that tracks the active catalog by querying SELECT CURRENT_CATALOG() in refreshDefaults, overrides getDefaultCatalog to return that catalog, and overrides setDefaultCatalog to record the new active catalog (swallowing DBCException). DatabricksDataSource creates this context and overrides initializeContextState to refresh defaults for a new context or copy the default catalog from the initFrom context; refreshDefaults also fills the runtime bootstrap default-catalog name from CURRENT_CATALOG() when none is configured.

defects.title: setDefaultCatalog swallows DBCException, so a failed catalog switch is reported as success
defects.statement: DatabricksExecutionContext.setDefaultCatalog (DatabricksExecutionContext.java:59-71) wraps super.setDefaultCatalog in try/catch(DBCException) and only logs at debug level, though it still declares throws DBCException. GenericExecutionContext.setDefaultCatalog throws on SQLException or when the catalog cannot be changed. Callers — the active-catalog selector in the UI, initializeContextState for new contexts (DatabricksDataSource.java:93), and DatabricksMetaModel.prepareTableLoadStatement (which catches DBCException around its temporary switch before running SHOW VIEWS) — now see silent success: the user gets no error when a switch fails (permission, dropped catalog) and the metadata code proceeds as if the catalog were active.
defects.evidence: DatabricksExecutionContext.java:65-70 `try { super.setDefaultCatalog(monitor, catalog, schema); activeCatalogName = catalog.getName(); } catch (DBCException e) { log.debug("Error setting default catalog for Databricks", e); }`. GenericExecutionContext.setDefaultCatalog: `catch (SQLException e) { throw new DBCException(e, this); }` and `throw new DBCException("Active catalog can't be changed ...")`. DatabricksMetaModel.java:125-146 `contextDefaults.setDefaultCatalog(...)` inside `try { ... } catch (SQLException | DBCException e)`.
defects.notes: Must say the exception is swallowed / not rethrown so callers or users are not told the catalog change failed. A comment only asking for more logging detail or a different log level does not count.

excluded.reason: Asks for initializeContextState parameters on separate lines. Formatting style only.

Asks to replace the casts to DatabricksExecutionContext in initializeContextState with getContextDefaults. createExecutionContext always returns a DatabricksExecutionContext (DatabricksDataSource.java:98-100) and GenericDataSource uses the same cast pattern; style preference.

Claims getDefaultCatalog can return null from getCatalog(activeCatalogName) and cause NPEs. The method is @Nullable per the DBCExecutionContextDefaults contract, callers handle null, super can also return null, and activeCatalogName comes from CURRENT_CATALOG() so it names an existing catalog.

Claims refreshDefaults must not write bootstrap.setDefaultCatalogName. getBootstrapSettings() returns the runtime resolved connection configuration (a deep copy while connected), and the write only fills an empty value; no concrete misbehaviour follows.

Claims initializing a context from another copies only the catalog and passes a null schema, losing the user's schema selection. The replaced initDefaultsFrom also copied only the catalog whenever catalog change is supported (Databricks has catalogs and no datasource-level schemas, so supportsCatalogChange is true); not a regression of this PR.

Claims secondary contexts no longer inherit the source context's schema, which initDefaultsFrom used to copy when no catalog was selectable. For Databricks the catalog branch was already taken (supportsCatalogChange true) and getDefaultCatalog is non-null after the CURRENT_CATALOG refresh, so the schema-only fallback is effectively unreachable.

Claims getCachedDefault (used by query-manager records) is derived from selectedEntityName and can disagree with the CURRENT_CATALOG-based getDefaultCatalog. The cached value is computed exactly as before the PR, so QM history is not made worse; a cosmetic inconsistency in history records, not a defect of the change.
Asks to include the requested catalog name in the debug log on failure. Logging nicety.

Says getDefaultCatalog returns null if CURRENT_CATALOG's name is missing from the cached catalog list. Contrived (the name comes from the server's own catalog) and the method is @Nullable; super would not find an unlisted catalog either.

filamentphp__filament@d47632c.pr_summary: In generate_search_column_expression (packages/support/src/helpers.php), when search is forced case-insensitive on MySQL/MariaDB and the column uses Laravel's JSON arrow syntax (data->field), the column is rewritten via the grammar's wrapJsonFieldAndPath into json_extract(`data`, '$."field"') before being wrapped in lower(), so the SQL is valid instead of lower(data->field).

defects.title: The new branch uses bare json_extract without json_unquote, so the search matches the JSON-encoded value (quotes/escapes) rather than the field's text
defects.statement: helpers.php:187 builds `json_extract({$field}{$path})`, whereas Laravel's own MySQL JSON selector (used for data->field when search is not forced case-insensitive) is json_unquote(json_extract(...)). json_extract returns a JSON value, so a string field is compared in its serialized form with surrounding double quotes and backslash escapes. The forced case-insensitive search then compares `lower("...")` LIKE '%term%': a term containing a double quote, backslash or other JSON-escaped character (e.g. value a"b serialized as "a\"b") no longer matches, and a lone `"` term matches every string value. Plain alphanumeric terms still work, so the impact is limited to terms with escaped characters.
defects.evidence: helpers.php:184-190 `if (in_array($driverName, ['mysql', 'mariadb'], true) && str_contains($column, '->')) { [$field, $path] = invade($databaseConnection->getQueryGrammar())->wrapJsonFieldAndPath($column); $column = "json_extract({$field}{$path})"; } $column = "lower({$column})";`. Laravel MySqlGrammar::wrapJsonSelector returns 'json_unquote(json_extract('.$field.$path.'))'.
defects.notes: Must say json_extract returns the JSON-encoded/quoted value and json_unquote (or equivalent text extraction) is needed so the search compares the actual text. Comments about double-wrapping json_extract columns or SQL injection do not count.

excluded.reason: Says the '->' condition must skip columns already starting with json_extract() to avoid double-wrapping translatable-plugin columns. The branch fires only when the column contains '->' (helpers.php:184); the translatable plugin builds json_extract(col, "$.locale") with no '->' (SpatieLaravelTranslatableContentDriver.php:117-119), so no double-wrapping is reachable.

Flags json_extract({$field}{$path}) as unsafe raw concatenation that may miss the comma or quoting. Laravel's wrapJsonFieldAndPath returns [wrap(field), ', '.wrapJsonPath(path)] — the path already carries the comma and both parts are grammar-wrapped — so the result equals what the grammar itself emits; based on a wrong assumption.
Asks for a MySQL/MariaDB regression test for the new JSON search branch. Test request, not a defect.

Says a caller-supplied native MySQL expression such as data->>'$.name' now enters the '->' branch and is mangled. Search columns are attribute names in Laravel arrow notation; a raw ->> SQL expression as a search column is contrived and would already break on the non-forced path, where Laravel's grammar wraps it as a JSON selector.

filamentphp__filament@912f080.pr_summary: Translation-only change to the pt_BR panel auth strings: the login page's register link label changes from 'criar uma conta' to 'crie uma conta', and the password field's validation_attribute changes from the untranslated 'password' to 'senha' on the register and reset-password pages.

excluded.reason: Claims the password validation_attribute must stay 'password' as a translation key rather than the translated 'senha', or validation messages break. Wrong: validation_attribute is only the human-readable name Laravel substitutes into validation messages — Register.php:201 `->validationAttribute(__('filament-panels::pages/auth/register.form.password.validation_attribute'))` and ResetPassword.php:149 likewise — not a lookup key; other locales translate it too, so 'senha' only changes the error-message wording, as intended.

filamentphp__filament@77874d0.pr_summary: Changes PrepareCsvExport so PostgreSQL exports keep the table's sort: it now rejects only qualified-primary-key orders (no longer the unqualified key), reorders by the first remaining original order (falling back to the qualified key when none remain) and appends the rest. The DISTINCT ON the qualified key is now applied (for every driver) only when the query's first order is the primary key.

defects.title: PostgreSQL exports sorted by a non-unique column lose the primary-key tie-breaker, so offset-chunked export can skip or repeat records
defects.statement: Previously the pgsql branch always ordered by the qualified key first, giving a total order. Now, with a user sort on column X (Filament's applySort adds only X), the query is reordered by X alone and any qualified-key order is rejected and never re-added (PrepareCsvExport.php:71-83). With one non-key order the export takes `$baseQuery->chunk()` (:161-175), which paginates by LIMIT/OFFSET; PostgreSQL gives no stable order among rows tied on X, so rows on either side of a chunk boundary can swap between page queries and be exported twice or not at all.
defects.evidence: :72 `->reject(fn (array $order): bool => in_array($order['column'] ?? null, [$qualifiedKeyName]))`; :79 `$query->reorder($originalOrders[0]['column'], $originalOrders[0]['direction']);` with no key order appended afterwards; :168 `$baseQuery->chunk($this->chunkSize, ...)` (offset pagination).
defects.notes: Must say the new ordering has no unique/deterministic tie-breaker (primary key no longer part of the order), so chunked/offset export can duplicate or miss rows. Generic 'sort behaviour changed' remarks do not count.

defects.title: DISTINCT on the key is skipped whenever the first order is not the key, so joined export queries dispatch duplicate records
defects.statement: The `$baseQuery->distinct($qualifiedKeyName)` call is now conditional on the first order being the primary key (PrepareCsvExport.php:153-155). For any export sorted by another column, key-level deduplication is gone; with a one-to-many join in the table query the chunk() path (:161-175) plucks the same key from several joined rows and dispatches it in (possibly different) ExportCsv jobs, so the CSV repeats records and total_rows can be reached before all unique records are exported. Before the PR DISTINCT ON the key was always applied.
defects.evidence: :153 `if (in_array($query->getQuery()->orders[0]['column'] ?? null, [$keyName, $qualifiedKeyName])) { $baseQuery->distinct($qualifiedKeyName); }` replacing the unconditional `$baseQuery->distinct($qualifiedKeyName);`; :171 `Arr::pluck($records->all(), $keyName)` feeds $dispatchRecords with no deduplication.
defects.notes: Must say dropping the DISTINCT (for non-key sorts) lets duplicate IDs/rows through, e.g. with joins. A comment only about the ordering tie-breaker is D1, not this.

defects.title: `$originalOrders[0]` assumes key 0 with column/direction: export fails when the first order was the rejected qualified key or is a raw order
defects.statement: Collection::reject() and unique() preserve keys, so when the query's first order is the qualified primary key (orders [table.id, X]) the remaining collection is {1: X}; `$originalOrders[0]` at PrepareCsvExport.php:79 hits an undefined key (ErrorException in Laravel) and the export job fails before dispatching anything (forget(0) at :80 also removes nothing). Likewise a raw first order (orderByRaw, e.g. a custom sortable column query) has `sql` instead of `column`/`direction`; the loop below guards those fields (:86-88) but the new first-order path reads them unguarded and fails, where the old code simply skipped raw orders.
defects.evidence: :71-73 `collect($query->getQuery()->orders)->reject(...)->unique('column')` (key-preserving); :78-80 `if (! empty($originalOrders->all())) { $query->reorder($originalOrders[0]['column'], $originalOrders[0]['direction']); $originalOrders->forget(0); }`; :86 `if (blank($order['column'] ?? null) || blank($order['direction'] ?? null)) { continue; }` guards only later orders.
defects.notes: Counts if a comment says index 0 may not exist after reject/unique (keys preserved) and suggests first()/shift()/values(), or that the first order may be raw and lack column/direction. A pure style remark about [0] on a Collection counts only if it points at safety (R3 does).

excluded.reason: Claims removing the unqualified-key rejection lets an `id DESC` order persist alongside an enforced qualified-key ASC, producing non-sequential ids. reorder($qualifiedKeyName) now runs only when no original orders remain, so `id DESC` becomes the first order itself; DISTINCT ON applies and orderedChunkById runs descending (:177-188). The described conflict does not occur.
Suggests replacing in_array on a one-element array with ===. Style/micro-optimisation; both compare column-name strings.

Claims `$query->getQuery()->orders[0]['column']` at :153 can throw when orders is null or empty. The null-coalescing operator `?? null` suppresses undefined-index and null access, so it yields null without error.
Asks for PostgreSQL export regression tests for non-ID sorts, ID fallback, raw orders and joins. Test-coverage request, not a code defect.

dotnet__aspnetcore@0ce67cd.pr_summary: Rewrites the shared HttpSys/IIS SocketAddress helper to drop 'fixed' byte-buffer copying: SocketAddress becomes an abstract class with private IPv4/IPv6 subclasses copying the CsWin32-generated SOCKADDR_IN / SOCKADDR_IN6 structs; CopyOutAddress takes a SOCKADDR* and switches on sa_family. GetPort uses IPAddress.NetworkToHostOrder on the port field and GetIPAddress builds IPAddress from S_addr / the sin6_addr bytes. NativeRequestContext passes a SOCKADDR* and the NativeMethods.txt files request SOCKADDR_IN/SOCKADDR_IN6 generation.

defects.title: GetPort sign-extends the port via (short), returning negative ports above 32767
defects.statement: Both GetPort overrides (SocketAddress.cs:40 and :62) cast the ushort sin_port/sin6_port to short and call IPAddress.NetworkToHostOrder(short), which returns a short; returning it as int sign-extends. Any port >= 32768 - including essentially every Windows client ephemeral port (49152-65535) - comes back negative (50000 -> -15536). The old code assembled a non-negative 0..65535 value. HttpSys Request.RemotePort/LocalPort (Request.cs:325,327) and IIS IHttpConnectionFeature.RemotePort/LocalPort (IISHttpContext.IHttpConnectionFeature.cs:88,98) therefore report wrong ports on normal requests.
defects.evidence: SocketAddress.cs:40 `return IPAddress.NetworkToHostOrder((short)_sockaddr.sin_port);` in `internal override int GetPort()`; :62 the same for sin6_port. Base: `return (_buffer[2] << 8 & 0xFF00) | (_buffer[3]);`. Request.cs:325 `public int RemotePort => RemoteEndPoint.GetPort();`.
defects.notes: Must say the (short) cast / signed short result makes ports > 32767 negative, or that it must be ushort / masked. Comments only about byte-order correctness of the address do not count.

excluded.reason: Claim: CopyOutAddress dereferences pSockaddr without a null check and could access-violate. The only caller, NativeRequestContext.GetEndPointHelper (NativeRequestContext.cs:652-662), returns null when the source offset is 0 before calling it, and the base code dereferenced the pointer the same way.

Claim: new IPAddress(S_addr) treats a network-order address as host order, so 192.168.1.1 becomes 1.1.168.192 on little-endian. IPAddress(long) interprets the value in memory order, exactly what S_addr holds when read on a little-endian machine (bytes C0 A8 01 01 -> 0x0101A8C0 -> 192.168.1.1); this is the standard correct conversion.
Claim: the AsReadOnlySpan workaround pending CsWin32 inline-array support should be tracked as tech debt. A note about a linked, tracked workaround; no defect.
Claim: the IPv6 path omits the scope id for link-local addresses. Pre-existing: the base GetIpv6Address also built IPAddress from the 16 bytes only, with the same TODO; behaviour unchanged.

Claim: casting the address to SOCKADDR* may be misaligned or read past a short blob. The pointer arithmetic is unchanged from the base (only IntPtr -> SOCKADDR*), the address is the http.sys-filled pRemoteAddress/pLocalAddress sockaddr, and the base code already read the family and 16/28 bytes from it; speculative.

dotnet__aspnetcore@742f022.pr_summary: Adds an upper bound (MaxSaltSize = 8 KiB) to the salt length read from a stored V3 password hash in PasswordHasher<TUser>.VerifyHashedPasswordV3, so a corrupted or tampered hash cannot trigger allocation of an arbitrarily large salt array; verification returns false for out-of-range salt lengths.

excluded.reason: Warns that legitimate hashes with salts over 8 KiB would be rejected, that other length fields (subkey) need similar bounds, and that the constant should be class-level. The hasher only ever writes 16-byte salts (HashPasswordV3 uses saltSize 128/8), so no realistic stored hash exceeds 8 KiB; the subkey length is derived from hashedPassword.Length, not a stored attacker-chosen size, so no other allocation is attacker-sized; local vs class constant is style.

Suggests replacing Buffer.BlockCopy with span slicing AsSpan(13, saltLength) for bounds validation. Refactor/style: BlockCopy already bounds-checks and any exception is caught and returns false; no incorrect behaviour.

Suggests checking hashedPassword.Length >= 13 + saltLength before allocating the salt. With the new 8 KiB cap the worst case is an 8 KiB transient allocation before BlockCopy throws and the catch returns false; an optimisation, not a defect.
Suggests naming the magic number 128 / 8 as MinSaltSize. Naming style on a pre-existing expression, not a defect.

Requests tests for the 8 KiB salt boundary and asks whether externally produced hashes with larger salts must be supported. A test request plus a compatibility question; the built-in writer only produces 16-byte salts, so rejecting >8 KiB salts is the intended hardening, not a defect.
Requests a regression test with a malformed V3 hash declaring a salt above 8 KiB. A request for tests, not a defect.

dotnet__aspnetcore@8ac940f.pr_summary: In KeyRingBasedDataProtector.AdditionalAuthenticatedDataTemplate, adds a NET10_0_OR_GREATER constructor taking string[] that computes the exact AAD size up front (UTF-8 byte counts cached in an ArrayPool<int> rental, 7-bit length prefixes measured via BitOperations.LeadingZeroCount) and writes magic header, a zeroed key-id slot, big-endian purpose count and each length-prefixed purpose directly into a byte[] with BinaryPrimitives/span APIs. The original MemoryStream + PurposeBinaryWriter constructor is kept unchanged under #else for netstandard2.0/netfx.

excluded.reason: Says BitOperations.LeadingZeroCount and the span Encoding.GetBytes overload are unavailable on netstandard2.0/.NET Framework and need a cross-TFM fallback. The span/BitOperations code is inside `#if NET10_0_OR_GREATER` (KeyRingBasedDataProtector.cs:356); the netstandard2.0/net462 targets compile the retained MemoryStream constructor in the #else branch (:437), so there is no cross-TFM break.

Says the new constructor does not validate that purposes or its elements are non-null. The only caller passes Purposes = ConcatPurposes(originalPurposes, newPurpose) (:40-43), never null; new purposes are null-checked in CreateProtector. The base code only had a Debug.Assert, and BinaryWriter.Write(null) threw too, so behaviour for a null element is unchanged in practice (an exception either way).

Says the unchecked int totalPurposeLen can overflow, giving an undersized buffer and out-of-range writes. Overflow would require purpose strings totalling ~2 GB of UTF-8 in one protector; contrived, and on overflow `new byte[negative]` throws rather than writing out of range. Old code's `checked` only applied to the stream position cast.

Says the rented ArrayPool array should be returned in a try/finally so it is not leaked on an exception. The only throw possible between Rent and Return is an encoder exception on invalid surrogates; a non-returned pooled array is simply GC'd, no resource leak with a real consequence.

Says the unchecked purpose-length sum at :374 can wrap for large input and should use checked arithmetic. Wrapping requires more than 2 GB of UTF-8 purpose text on a single protector, which is contrived; a negative total makes `new byte[totalPurposeLen]` throw OverflowException rather than write out of bounds, and span slicing is bounds-checked.

Says an invalid-UTF-16 purpose makes GetByteCount throw before the rented array is returned to ArrayPool. The only throw between Rent and Return is SecureUtf8Encoding throwing on an invalid surrogate (KeyRingBasedDataProtector.cs:370/392); an un-returned ArrayPool array is simply garbage-collected and the pool rents a fresh one next time — there is no leak or other consequence, and protector construction with invalid purposes is an error path anyway.

Asks that the NET10 encoder and the legacy BinaryWriter path be checked against a shared wire-format contract. kestra-io__kestra@0ec45f0.pr_summary: Adds two Pebble functions, fileExists(uri) and fileEmpty(uri), registered in the core Pebble Extension. Both are copies of the existing FileSizeFunction: they accept a kestra:/// internal-storage URI, authorize it against the current execution (or the parent execution via an execution trigger), then call StorageInterface.exists(...) or read the file and test whether its content is blank. Tests are added for both, and the UI basic.md docs function table is re-padded with three new rows (fileSize, fileExists, fileEmpty).

defects.title: fileEmpty reads the whole internal-storage file into memory (and decodes it to a String) just to decide emptiness
defects.statement: FileEmptyFunction.readAndCheckEmptyFileFromInternalStorage (FileEmptyFunction.java:74-76) does `new String(inputStream.readAllBytes(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8).isBlank()`. Internal-storage URIs are typically task outputs (downloads, query results) that can be very large; readAllBytes allocates the entire file and the UTF-8 decode allocates it again in the JVM rendering the template, so a boolean check on a large output can exhaust the heap (and files > 2 GB cannot be read at all). Emptiness needs only the size or a scan until the first non-whitespace byte.
defects.evidence: FileEmptyFunction.java:74-75 `try (InputStream inputStream = storageInterface.get(flow.get("tenantId"), flow.get("namespace"), path)) { return new String(inputStream.readAllBytes(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8).isBlank(); }`; FileSizeFunction uses the cheap `storageInterface.getAttributes(...)` instead.
defects.notes: Must say the whole file is materialized in memory (readAllBytes / String decode) for an emptiness check, with a memory/OOM or large-file performance consequence. A comment only about blank-vs-empty semantics does not count.

defects.title: Copy-pasted missing-argument error messages name the wrong function ('read' in fileEmpty, 'fileSize' in fileExists)
defects.statement: When fileEmpty/fileExists is called without a path argument, the PebbleException thrown (FileEmptyFunction.java:40, FileExistsFunction.java:38) uses an ERROR_MESSAGE copied from another function: FileEmptyFunction.java:22 says "The 'read' function expects an argument 'path' that is a path to a namespace file or an internal storage URI" (fileEmpty rejects namespace files), and FileExistsFunction.java:19 says "The 'fileSize' function expects ...". The flow author is pointed at the wrong expression.
defects.evidence: FileEmptyFunction.java:22 `ERROR_MESSAGE = "The 'read' function expects ..."` (verbatim copy of ReadFileFunction.java:23); FileExistsFunction.java:19 `ERROR_MESSAGE = "The 'fileSize' function expects ..."` (copy of FileSizeFunction.java:20).
defects.notes: Either file's wrong function name in the error message counts.

defects.title: New docs examples use `output.download.uri` instead of `outputs.download.uri`
defects.statement: The three rows the PR adds to ui/src/assets/docs/basic.md:322-324 show `{{ fileSize(output.download.uri) }}`, `{{ fileExists(output.download.uri) }}` and `{{ fileEmpty(output.download.uri) }}`. Task outputs are exposed as `outputs.<taskId>...` (the same page documents `{{ outputs.taskId.outputAttribute }}` at basic.md:214), so a user copying the example gets an undefined-variable rendering error.
defects.evidence: basic.md:322 `| `fileSize` | `{{ fileSize(output.download.uri) }}` ...`, :323 fileExists, :324 fileEmpty; basic.md:214 `{{ outputs.taskId.outputAttribute }}`. The rows are new in this PR (absent from base basic.md).
defects.notes: Must point out the singular `output` vs `outputs` variable in the new doc examples.

excluded.reason: Suggests null-checking or conditionally registering fileExistsFunction/fileEmptyFunction in Extension to avoid an NPE if injection fails. Both are unconditional @Singleton beans with no optional dependencies, registered the same way as the existing FileSizeFunction; injection cannot yield null.
Points out an unused `io.micronaut.context.annotation.Value` import in FileEmptyFunction.java:5. Harmless style; no build or lint failure.

Claims fileEmpty reads with the flow's tenant/namespace even when the file is authorized via the parent trigger, so it may read the wrong location. Identical to the pre-existing FileSizeFunction/ReadFileFunction handling; storage get resolves by the URI path and the parent execution is in the same tenant; no wrong read demonstrated and nothing new.

Says checkIfFileFromParentExecution throws IllegalArgumentException instead of PebbleException, losing line info. Same pattern as the existing fileSize/read functions and still surfaces as an evaluation error; consistency nit.

Warns of NPE/ClassCastException from unchecked casts of the flow/execution variables. These variables are always present when rendering within an execution, exactly as in FileSizeFunction; speculative.

Warns the startsWith prefix check could be bypassed by non-normalized URIs and asks for normalization. The same check exists unchanged in FileSizeFunction and ReadFileFunction (which already reads full content); the new functions expose nothing beyond what read() already does, so it is pre-existing.

Asks to consolidate the URI conversion and authorization logic shared with FileEmptyFunction and FileSizeFunction. Refactor suggestion; the copied authorization logic is identical, so no drift in behaviour (the drifted error strings are D2).

Says the IOException catch in FileExistsFunction.execute is dead because StorageInterface.exists declares no checked exception. The code compiles (the helper declares throws IOException) and behaves correctly; dead-code style only.

Claims encoded %2e%2e traversal passes the prefix check so fileExists can probe other executions' files. The identical raw-string check already guards ReadFileFunction (which returns the full content) and FileSizeFunction; pre-existing and not made worse by these functions.

Claims fileExists' prefix check accepts encoded traversal to probe files outside the execution. Same pre-existing check as ReadFileFunction/FileSizeFunction, which already expose more; not introduced by this PR.

Claims the fileEmpty prefix check can be bypassed with encoded traversal to read outside the execution. Pre-existing identical check in ReadFileFunction.java:112 which already returns full file content; nothing newly exposed.

Asks the fileEmpty doc row to say 'blank, including whitespace-only' rather than 'empty'. Whitespace-as-empty is the intended behaviour (PR body says 'content is blank', test shouldReturnTrueForFileWithOnlyWhiteSpace); a wording nit.

Claims a flow can test the blankness of another execution's file via encoded traversal. Same pre-existing authorization check as ReadFileFunction, which already discloses full content; not made worse.

Asks that the execution-URI authorization rule live in one shared place instead of four copies. Refactor suggestion; the copies are currently identical in behaviour.

kestra-io__kestra@3c2a276.pr_summary: Makes task-runner commands dynamic Properties: TaskCommands exposes interpreter, beforeCommands and commands as Property<List<String>>; CommandsWrapper stores the three Properties, renders them in run() and composes them with ScriptService.scriptCommands into this.commands; TaskRunner gains renderCommands/renderCommandsFromList (render + internal-storage replacement of interpreter ++ beforeCommands ++ commands) which Process and Docker now use to build the argv. Adds a Property-list overload of ScriptService.replaceInternalStorage, a TestsUtils.propertyFromList helper and test updates (new dynamic-properties Docker log test).

defects.title: Interpreter and beforeCommands are applied twice: CommandsWrapper.run folds them into commands, then Process/Docker prepend them again
defects.statement: CommandsWrapper.run composes `this.commands = Property.of(scriptCommands(interpreter, before, commands))` (CommandsWrapper.java:169-179) but leaves the interpreter and beforeCommands fields set, then passes itself to realTaskRunner.run (line 185). Process.run (Process.java:140) and Docker (Docker.java:431, 783) call TaskRunner.renderCommands (TaskRunner.java:134-141), which concatenates getInterpreter() + getBeforeCommands() + getCommands() again. With interpreter [/bin/sh,-c] the argv becomes [/bin/sh,-c,/bin/sh,-c,<script>] (plus before-commands as stray args): sh executes '/bin/sh' as its script with the real script only as a positional parameter, so the user's script never runs (possibly exiting 0 with no output). The new test calls Docker.run directly and never exercises CommandsWrapper.run.
defects.evidence: CommandsWrapper.java:179 `this.commands = Property.of(finalCommands);` with interpreter/beforeCommands untouched, then `realTaskRunner.run(taskRunnerRunContext, this, this.outputFiles)`; TaskRunner.java:139-140 `Stream.of(renderedInterpreter, renderedBeforeCommands, renderedCommands).flatMap(Collection::stream).toList()`.
defects.notes: Must say the interpreter/beforeCommands end up in the argv twice (composed in CommandsWrapper.run and re-prepended by TaskRunner.renderCommands), or that leaving those fields set after merging them into commands makes the runner re-add them. A pure 'redundant rendering / performance' remark (R7) is a near-miss and does not count.

defects.title: CommandsWrapper.run joins a commands-only argv into one element when no interpreter is set
defects.statement: CommandsWrapper.run always passes the rendered lists through ScriptService.scriptCommands (CommandsWrapper.java:173-178), which copies the interpreter and joins ALL beforeCommands+commands into ONE element with the line separator (ScriptService.java:161-172). With interpreter unset (the Property overload returns an empty list for null, ScriptService.java:103), a caller that sets only commands to a complete argv — the migration of the old idiom `withCommands(Property.of(List.of("/bin/sh","-c",script)))` as in LogConsumerTest — ends up with argv ["/bin/sh\n-c\n<script>"], which the runner tries to exec as a program name, failing the task.
defects.evidence: CommandsWrapper.java:173 `ScriptService.scriptCommands(renderedInterpreter, renderedBeforeCommands, renderedCommands, ...)`; ScriptService.java:162-170 `new ArrayList<>(interpreter); commandsArgs.add(Stream.concat(before, commands).collect(Collectors.joining(targetOS.lineSeparator)))`; ScriptService.java:103 `commands == null ? Collections.emptyList() : ...`.
defects.notes: Must identify that with no interpreter, run() joins the whole command list into a single string/argv element, breaking callers that supply a full argv in commands. Distinct from D1 (duplication).

defects.title: TaskRunner.renderCommands flat-concatenates interpreter, beforeCommands and commands instead of joining the script like scriptCommands
defects.statement: TaskRunner.renderCommands (TaskRunner.java:134-141) builds argv as interpreter ++ beforeCommands ++ commands as separate elements, whereas the established composition (ScriptService.scriptCommands, used by CommandsWrapper.run) joins beforeCommands and commands into ONE script argument after the interpreter. For a TaskCommands passed directly to a runner with interpreter [/bin/sh,-c], beforeCommands ["set -e"] and commands ["echo hi"] the result is `sh -c 'set -e' 'echo hi'`: only the before-command runs and the real command becomes $0 (same for multi-line command lists). It also ignores targetOS.
defects.evidence: TaskRunner.java:139 flatMap concat vs ScriptService.java:163-170 joining before+commands into one element.
defects.notes: Must point out that renderCommands concatenates the lists as separate argv entries instead of composing them like ScriptService.scriptCommands (wrong argv for direct-runner inputs with beforeCommands/multiple commands). A comment only about duplication counts for D1.

defects.title: Commands supplied as Property.of(...) are no longer rendered with additionalVars (workingDir, outputDir, ...)
defects.statement: Base CommandsWrapper rendered each command string with `runContext.render(c, additionalVars)` (List overload, ScriptService.java:83-95). The new Property overload (ScriptService.java:97-107) only calls `runContext.render(commands).asList(String.class, additionalVars)`, and Property.asList returns the stored value untouched when the Property was built with Property.of (Property.java:67 'no rendering will be done'; asList renders only `if (property.value == null)`). Property.of is the public factory callers and this PR's own tests use, so `{{ workingDir }}`/`{{ outputDir }}` in such commands reach the process literally — the opposite of the PR's goal; the PR's new test needed TestsUtils.propertyFromList (an expression-only Property) to get rendering at all.
defects.evidence: ScriptService.java:103-105 `runContext.render(commands).asList(String.class, additionalVars).stream().map(... replaceInternalStorage(runContext, c, ...))` with no per-item render; Property.java:91-92 `p.value = value`; Property.java:143 `if (property.value == null) { ... }`; TestsUtils.java:248-249 propertyFromList builds `new Property<>(json)`.
defects.notes: Must say Property.of-built (pre-valued) commands skip rendering / the new overload does not render each command with additionalVars like the List overload did.

defects.title: Rendering the serialized JSON list breaks commands whose interpolated values contain quotes or newlines
defects.statement: For expression-backed command Properties (the form produced when a flow's YAML list is deserialized, and by propertyFromList), Property.asList renders the whole JSON text of the list and only then parses it (Property.java:154 `MAPPER.readValue(runContext.render(property.expression, variables), List.class)`). The old List overload parsed first and rendered each element. Now `["echo {{ inputs.text }}"]` with inputs.text containing a double quote or a newline renders to invalid JSON, and the task fails with an IllegalVariableEvaluationException instead of running the command.
defects.evidence: Property.java:154-155 renders the serialized expression then `MAPPER.readValue(..., List.class)`, catching JsonProcessingException into IllegalVariableEvaluationException (163-164); base ScriptService List overload `.map(c -> runContext.render(c, additionalVars))` rendered each already-parsed element.
defects.notes: Must say interpolated values are rendered inside the serialized list text, so quotes/newlines in a value produce invalid JSON / evaluation failure. Distinct from D4 (no rendering at all for Property.of).

defects.title: TaskCommands.getCommands() return type changed and abstract getters added: breaks external TaskRunner/TaskCommands plugins
defects.statement: TaskCommands is the plugin SPI (TaskCommands.java:25-29). Changing getCommands() from List<String> to Property<List<String>> (a different JVM descriptor) and adding abstract getInterpreter()/getBeforeCommands() without defaults breaks source and binary compatibility of every plugin TaskRunner outside this repo that calls taskCommands.getCommands() as a List (Kubernetes, cloud batch runners, ...) and every TaskCommands implementation; CommandsWrapper.withCommands now takes a Property, so every external AbstractExecScript caller of withCommands(List) stops compiling. No deprecation path is provided.
defects.evidence: TaskCommands.java head: `Property<List<String>> getInterpreter(); Property<List<String>> getBeforeCommands(); Property<List<String>> getCommands();` (base: `List<String> getCommands();`). The in-repo TaskRunnerTest implementation had to be updated with the new methods.
defects.notes: Must flag the breaking SPI/API (source or binary) change for external task runners/plugins. The unused lombok.With import (R3) does not count.

defects.title: Docker renders the commands twice, the second time unconditionally after the container has started
defects.statement: Docker.configure renders the argv for withCmd (Docker.java:783), and run() calls renderCommands again after startContainerCmd (line 431) just to log it, even when debug logging is off. Each render re-runs internal-storage replacement, which downloads every `kestra://` file to a fresh temp file (ScriptService.saveOnLocalStorage), so files are fetched twice, the debug log names a different local path than the container got, and a failure of the second download throws after the container is running but before the kill hook is registered (line 447).
defects.evidence: Docker.java:429 `dockerClient.startContainerCmd(exec.getId()).exec();` :431 `List<String> renderedCommands = this.renderCommands(runContext, taskCommands);` (outside the isDebugEnabled check); :783 `.withCmd(this.renderCommands(runContext, taskCommands))`; ScriptService.saveOnLocalStorage creates a new temp file per call.
defects.notes: Must say Docker calls renderCommands twice (configure + run) with a concrete cost: repeated internal-storage download / log differing from executed command / throw after container start. A bare 'Process re-renders already rendered commands' (R7) does not count.

excluded.reason: Claims the Property overload may NPE if additionalVars is null. additionalVars always comes from TaskRunner.additionalVars(...), which builds a non-null map; no caller passes null, so this is speculative.
Points out that `import lombok.With;` in TaskCommands.java is unused. True but an unused import has no build or behaviour consequence; trivial style.

Claims rendered lists could be null in TaskRunner.renderCommands' Stream.of. ScriptService.replaceInternalStorage returns an empty list for a null Property and toList() otherwise; the NPE is speculative.
Suggests renderCommandsFromList be private. Visibility preference, not a defect.

Claims Process's renderCommands call is redundant rendering of already-rendered wrapper commands (performance). Framed as a cost only; Property caches its rendered value, and the real consequence of re-composing (interpreter duplication) is D1, which this comment does not describe.

Claims renderCommands may return an empty list and process execution would fail. An empty command list was equally possible before (base passed taskCommands.getCommands() straight to ProcessBuilder); not introduced by this PR.
Suggests defensive handling for null/empty renderedCommands and wrapping evaluation exceptions. renderCommands never returns null; the rest is defensive/pre-existing, not a defect.

Claims interpreter/beforeCommands/commands may be null in CommandsWrapper.run causing an NPE, plus context/statefulness remarks. Null Properties are handled (ScriptService.java:103 returns an empty list); the run-context and statefulness remarks are style; the concrete consequence of mutating this.commands is D1.
Claims a non-null Property resolving to JSON null makes asList return null and stream() NPE. A command-list expression evaluating to literal null is a contrived configuration; not a realistic path.
Suggests CommandsWrapper reuse TaskRunner.renderCommandsFromList instead of duplicating the render sequence. Refactoring preference; the two copies are currently identical in behaviour.

kestra-io__kestra@06e7c6e.pr_summary: Adds a core task io.kestra.plugin.core.execution.Assert that renders each of a list of conditions and fails (with success/failed counters and an optional error message) when any renders falsy. Adds TruthUtils.isFalsy, makes Property.getExpression public via Lombok @Getter so the task can read the raw list, adds tests and a test flow, and (accidentally) edits the OutputValues documentation example.

defects.title: Assert parses the raw Property expression as a JSON list, so `conditions` supplied as a template expression fails with a JSON parse error
defects.statement: Assert.run reads `this.conditions.getExpression()` and parses it with Jackson as List<String> (Assert.java:88-89) instead of going through Property rendering. PropertyDeserializer (Property.java:365-376) stores a YAML list as JSON but a scalar as the raw string, so a flow that supplies conditions as an expression resolving to a list (e.g. `conditions: "{{ inputs.assertions }}"`), which Property<List<String>> is meant to support, throws a JsonParseException before any assertion runs. To do this the PR also widened Property.getExpression from package-private 'used only by the serializer' to public, coupling task code to the property's serialized representation.
defects.evidence: Assert.java:88-89 `MAPPER.readValue(this.conditions.getExpression(), LIST_TYPE_REFERENCE)`; Property.java:374-376 `s = p.getValueAsString(); ... return new Property<>(s);` for a non-array scalar.
defects.notes: Must say that parsing getExpression() as JSON bypasses Property rendering so a templated/dynamic list breaks (or that it depends on the property's internal serialized form). Only disliking the public getter without the consequence is a near miss.

defects.title: OutputValues documentation example corrupted: `{{ outputs.output_values.values.taskrun_data }}` replaced with `{{ outputs.output_values.²}}`
defects.statement: The PR accidentally edits the full-flow example in OutputValues' @Plugin annotation (OutputValues.java:54), replacing a valid Pebble expression with `{{ outputs.output_values.²}}`. The published example now references a non-existent output and fails to render/log the advertised taskrun_data value when copied.
defects.evidence: OutputValues.java:54 `{{ outputs.output_values.²}}` (base: `{{ outputs.output_values.values.taskrun_data }}`).
defects.notes: Any comment flagging the stray `²` / broken expression in the OutputValues example counts.

defects.title: Assert's own @Example is malformed: `- id: fail\n" +` leaks into the published YAML
defects.statement: In Assert's @Example code (Assert.java:53) the string is `"  - id: fail\\n\" +\n"`, so the rendered example contains the literal text `  - id: fail\n" +`, producing an invalid task id / broken YAML in the published docs example.
defects.evidence: Assert.java:53 `"  - id: fail\\n\" +\n" +`.
defects.notes: Counts if the reviewer notes the escaped/garbled `- id: fail` line in Assert's example.

defects.title: Assertion-failure log passes the rendered value without a placeholder, so it is silently dropped
defects.statement: Assert.java:95 logs `"Assertion `{}` failed!"` with two arguments (s, renderer). SLF4J fills only the one placeholder, so the rendered value that made the assertion fail never appears in the log, defeating the evident intent of passing it.
defects.evidence: Assert.java:95 `runContext.logger().error("Assertion `{}` failed!", s, renderer);`
defects.notes: Must note the extra `renderer` argument has no `{}` placeholder (value not logged).

excluded.reason: Claims isFalsy(null) returning false makes null assertions pass in Assert. The rendered value comes from runContext.render(s) on a string element parsed from the JSON list; a null would need a literal null list element (`- null`), and Pebble renders a null expression result as a string, so this is contrived. isFalsy(null)=false also mirrors the existing isTruthy(null)=false convention (TruthUtils.java:8-10).
Claims Assert.java:94 treats a null render result as a successful assertion. Same contrived null-element scenario as R1.

Claims isTruthy(null) and isFalsy(null) both return false so null is neither true nor false. Contract-consistency point; the only caller (Assert) cannot get null from rendering a non-null condition string except via a contrived `- null` element (see R1).
Claims a null-rendering assertion counts as success because isFalsy(null) is false. Same contrived scenario as R1.
Claims a null item in conditions renders to null and is counted as a success. Requires a literal null list element; contrived (see R1).
Claims isFalsy should include null (`!isTruthy`) so a null rendered value is not a success. Same contrived null scenario as R1.
Claims the task description ('control outputs data emitted from previous task') misstates what conditions can check. Wording preference in docs; no behaviour.
Claims AtomicInteger counters with forEach should be plain loop and ints. Style; atomics are needed for mutation inside the lambda and behave correctly.
Claims AtomicInteger suggests non-existent concurrency and should be replaced. Style, as C5.
Claims the test `dontFailOnCondition` is misnamed. Test naming preference.
Claims the failure-path test should also check which assertion failed. Request for stronger tests, not a defect.

Claims `conditions: []` lets the Assert task succeed without checking anything. Design choice: an empty assertion list vacuously holds, @NotNull is satisfied, and nothing in the PR states at least one condition is required.
Claims an empty conditions list should maybe be rejected. Same design question as C20; not a defect.

juspay__hyperswitch@5e0fa17.pr_summary: Repo-wide typo fix. Mostly comments and strings, but it also renames identifiers: the public request field CtpServiceDetails.encypted_payload -> encrypted_payload (api_models, the domain AuthenticationInfo, the router UAS core and both OpenAPI specs), the impl_enum_str! macro keyword tag_delimeter -> tag_delimiter (with its invocations), the Braintree dispute-stage literal PRE_ARBITATION -> PRE_ARBITRATION, the Worldpay ActionLinks field partiall_refund_payment -> partially_refund_payment, the dashboard.toml key maintainence_alert -> maintenance_alert, a retry.rs parameter, a Fiuu struct name, and a Postman test folder.

defects.title: Renaming the public request field ctp_service_details.encypted_payload to encrypted_payload without a serde alias silently drops the payload for existing clients (and renames the key sent to the UAS service)
defects.statement: api_models::payments::CtpServiceDetails (crates/api_models/src/payments.rs:1169-1183) is deserialized from the payments request field `ctp_service_details` (:1157), has no deny_unknown_fields and no `#[serde(alias = "encypted_payload")]`. Clients integrated against the previously published key `encypted_payload` now have it silently ignored, so `payment_data.service_details.encrypted_payload` is None and click-to-pay pre-authentication (crates/router/src/core/unified_authentication_service.rs:79-82) is sent without the encrypted payload. The domain AuthenticationInfo (hyperswitch_domain_models/src/router_request_types/unified_authentication_service.rs:24) derives Serialize and is embedded in the outbound UAS pre-authentication request, so the JSON key sent to the UAS service also changes. The PR is labelled a typo fix with 'This PR modifies the API contract' unchecked.
defects.evidence: payments.rs:1169 `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, ToSchema)] pub struct CtpServiceDetails {` ... :1182 `pub encrypted_payload: Option<Secret<String>>,` (base `encypted_payload`), no serde rename/alias and no deny_unknown_fields on this struct; payments.rs:1157 `pub ctp_service_details: Option<CtpServiceDetails>,`; openapi_spec.json key changed from `encypted_payload` to `encrypted_payload`.
defects.notes: Must say renaming encypted_payload breaks the request/serialization contract (old key silently ignored or outbound key changed; needs a serde alias/rename). A comment only approving the typo fix does not count.

excluded.reason: Claims renaming the impl_enum_str! keyword tag_delimeter -> tag_delimiter breaks existing call sites. Every invocation in the repo (common_utils/src/types.rs:1362 and the macro's own test) was updated in the same PR and no `tag_delimeter` remains at head, so nothing breaks.
Says the FiuuWebhookSignature struct is unused and should be removed. The struct was unused before the PR too; the PR only corrects its name; dead-code cleanup is not a defect introduced here.

Asks whether Braintree still sends the old `PRE_ARBITATION` literal, since the match no longer accepts it. The old literal was a misspelling of Braintree's dispute kind PRE_ARBITRATION (paired with CHARGEBACK/RETRIEVAL); nothing in the repo shows the provider sending the misspelled value, so the change is a fix, not a regression.

Asks whether Worldpay returns `partiallyRefundPayment`, since the old `partiallRefundPayment` key is no longer read. The old camelCase key was itself a misspelling of Worldpay's action name, and the private Option field is never read anywhere, so there is no consequence.

Asks whether the dashboard consumes `maintainence_alert` or `maintenance_alert` after the config key rename. The consumer is outside the repo and the configured value is empty, so no verifiable consequence.

Asks whether the separately deployed control-center image reads the renamed `maintenance_alert` key. Unverifiable from the repo, and the value being renamed is the empty string, so no concrete consequence.
Asks whether Braintree emits `PRE_ARBITRATION` since the old `PRE_ARBITATION` value is now rejected. Same as C1: the new spelling matches the provider's dispute kind; speculative.
Says the corrected comment should read `task` not `tasks` in revenue_recovery.rs:163. Grammar nit in a comment; no maintainability consequence.

juspay__hyperswitch@0231de6.pr_summary: Adds a Google Pay pre-decrypt flow for the Checkout connector. A new GooglePayPreDecryptFlow setting (connector_tokenization default, network_tokenization) is added to the tokenization filter and set to network_tokenization for checkout in every config file; is_google_pay_pre_decrypt_type_connector_tokenization skips connector tokenization for decrypted Google Pay tokens under that setting. The Checkout transformer maps PaymentMethodToken::GooglePayDecrypt to a new GooglePayPredecrypt source (type network_token, token_type googlepay, PAN, expiry, cryptogram, eci).

defects.title: Checkout Google Pay pre-decrypt hardcodes ECI "06" and discards the decrypted token's eci_indicator
defects.statement: In the GooglePayDecrypt arm the request always sends `eci: Some("06".to_string())` (crates/hyperswitch_connectors/src/connectors/checkout/transformers.rs:369), although GPayPredecryptData carries the network-provided `eci_indicator: Option<String>` (crates/common_types/src/payments.rs:457-459), and the Apple Pay pre-decrypt arm in the same file forwards the real value (`eci: decrypt_data.payment_data.eci_indicator`, transformers.rs:405). Every Google Pay network-token authorization therefore reports ECI 06 to Checkout regardless of the token's actual indicator (e.g. 05/07, or absent for Mastercard), sending wrong authentication data that can lead to declines or wrong liability shift.
defects.evidence: transformers.rs:369 `eci: Some("06".to_string()),`; common_types/src/payments.rs:457-459 `/// Electronic Commerce Indicator ... pub eci_indicator: Option<String>,` on GPayPredecryptData; transformers.rs:405 Apple Pay uses `eci: decrypt_data.payment_data.eci_indicator`.
defects.notes: Must point at the hardcoded ECI '06' and say the decrypted eci_indicator should be forwarded (or that 06 is wrong for some tokens/networks). Comments on expiry validation, CardNumber typing or PAN_ONLY do not count.

excluded.reason: Points out a missing space after a comma in config.example.toml's checkout tokenization entry. TOML formatting only; parses identically.
Points out trailing whitespace before the closing brace in config/development.toml. Formatting only.

Asks to fix spacing before `}` in development.toml and ensure the settings schema supports google_pay_pre_decrypt_flow. Formatting; the key is supported (settings.rs:640 adds it to PaymentMethodTokenFilter).

Claims GooglePayPredecrypt.token typed cards::CardNumber is assigned from a possibly String/Secret PAN and may not compile. GPayPredecryptData.application_primary_account_number is already cards::CardNumber (common_types/src/payments.rs:451); the assignment is type-correct.

Suggests range-validating expiry month/year before sending. Suggestion only; decrypted predecrypted data is already validated by helpers::validate_card_expiry in check_predecrypted_token (payments.rs:5725).
Claims the negated matches!(NetworkTokenization) would misclassify future GooglePayPreDecryptFlow variants. The enum has exactly two variants and mirrors the existing Apple Pay helper; speculative.

Claims decrypted PAN_ONLY Google Pay tokens (no cryptogram) now fail with MissingRequiredField and should be sent as a card source. Before this PR every GooglePayDecrypt token was rejected for Checkout (unimplemented_payment_method), so PAN_ONLY is not made worse; an explicit error for an unsupported auth method is a feature gap, not a regression.
Suggests sharing one enum for Apple Pay and Google Pay pre-decrypt flows. Refactor preference; no defect.
Asks whether one-digit expiry months need padding for Checkout. Speculative question with no evidence Checkout rejects it; the Apple Pay arm uses the same get_expiry_month pattern.
Asks to rename the expiry error field names from payment_method_data.card.* to Google Pay wallet fields. Error-label nit; no behavioural defect.
Suggests one shared network-token source struct for Apple Pay and Google Pay. Refactor preference; no defect.
Asks to confirm the production config change and update the PR description checkbox. Process/description question; the config change is the intended feature.
Asks for regression tests for the new decrypted-token branch and bypass. Test request, not a defect.

Claims decrypted PAN_ONLY tokens without cryptogram fail with MissingRequiredField though Checkout's config allows PAN_ONLY. Previously all decrypted Google Pay tokens were rejected for Checkout, so this is an unsupported-method gap with an explicit error, not a regression.
Suggests sharing the network-token source shape between Google Pay and Apple Pay. Refactor preference; no defect.
Suggests sharing the pre-decrypt flow type and a parameterized eligibility check. Refactor preference; the two helpers are currently identical in behaviour.

defects.title: arrayLastIndex documentation is built but never passed to registerFunction

defects.evidence: arrayFirstLastIndex.cpp:164 `FunctionDocumentation documentation_last = {description_last, ...};` followed by :166 `factory.registerFunction<FunctionArrayLastIndex>();`, whereas :146 passes `documentation_first`. The 02415 references keep `arrayLastIndex` while removing its siblings.

defects.title: arrayLast's 'No match' example calls arrayFirst
defects.statement: examples_last's second example (arrayFirstLast.cpp:262-266) is `SELECT arrayFirst(x, y -> x=y, [0, 1, 2], [3, 3, 3]) ...`, so the arrayLast documentation demonstrates a different function (copy-paste); the output happens to be identical, hiding the mistake.

(arraySplit.cpp:136), but ArraySplitImpl::needExpression() returns true (arraySplit.cpp:19), so FunctionArrayMapped requires at least 2 arguments (FunctionArrayMapped.h:167) and a lambda-less arrayReverseSplit call errors; the doc is wrong and inconsistent with arraySplit's entry.

defects.title: arrayAll and arrayExists document the lambda as mandatory though both accept a bare array
