ClickHouse__ClickHouse@40a4654.pr_summary: Fixes S3Queue/AzureQueue retries after a failed insert. ObjectStorageQueueSource tracks each started file with a state (Processing/ErrorOnRead/Cancelled/Processed), throws QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED instead of inserting a half-read file on cancel/drop, turns read errors into ErrorOnRead + early end of the chunk stream, and commit() decides per state: setProcessed, setFailed without charging a retry (insert failure; now releases keeper processing nodes via a new generic resetProcessing()), or setFailed charging a retry (read error). The check request before removing processing_node_id_path is dropped from the Ordered and Unordered setProcessed transactions, the Unordered resetProcessingImpl is removed, setProcessing treats a Failed file with zero retries as processable, and Ordered setProcessingImpl reads processed+failed nodes with a MULTI_READ. The integration test test_exception_during_insert is rewritten.

defects.title: Read error after rows were already emitted no longer aborts the insert: the partial rows are committed and the file is retried, duplicating data
defects.statement: Before the PR, a pull() failure on a file that had already produced rows (processed_rows > 0) re-threw, failing the insert pipeline so none of the file's rows were committed. Now the catch at ObjectStorageQueueSource.cpp:599-609 always marks the file ErrorOnRead and returns an empty chunk, which ends the stream normally. The chunks of that file returned by earlier generate() calls (:584-596) have already gone down the pipeline; the insert completes and the caller runs commit(true) (StorageObjectStorageQueue.cpp:581, or generate() :463-465), where the ErrorOnRead branch (:690-694) calls setFailed(..., reduce_retry_count=true), leaving the file retriable. On retry the whole file is read again, so the rows inserted before the error are inserted a second time (duplicate data in the destination/MVs).
defects.evidence: head Source.cpp:604-608 `processed_files.back().state = FileState::ErrorOnRead; ... /// Stop processing and commit what is already processed. return {};` with no processed_rows check; the removed base code was `if (file_status->processed_rows == 0) { ... return {}; } throw;`. :463-465 `if (!chunk && commit_once_processed) commit(true);`; StorageObjectStorageQueue.cpp:581 `source->commit(/* success */true);` after the pipeline finishes; commit :690-694 `case FileState::ErrorOnRead: file_metadata->setFailed(exception_during_read, /* reduce_retry_count */true);` (retriable when retries remain).
defects.notes: Must say that a read error after some chunks of the file were already emitted now ends the insert successfully (instead of throwing), so the partial rows are committed while the file is marked failed/retriable, leading to duplicate rows on retry. Comments only about the lost in-pass returnForRetry re-queue (zero-row case) do not count.

defects.title: Keeper response indices not shifted after dropping the check request: session-expiry case throws LOGICAL_ERROR and failures are attributed to the wrong request
defects.statement: The PR removes makeCheckRequest(processing_node_id_path, version) that used to sit before the two removals, but keeps the old index maps. In the new resetProcessing (ObjectStorageQueueIFileMetadata.cpp:279-331) the multi is [0]=remove processing_id node (versioned), [1]=remove ephemeral processing node, yet index 1 is treated as the 'remove processing id path' failure (unexpected_error -> LOGICAL_ERROR) and index 2 (nonexistent) as the benign ephemeral-node case. In Unordered setProcessedImpl (ObjectStorageQueueUnorderedFileMetadata.cpp:123-199) the multi is [0]=remove id, [1]=remove ephemeral, [2]=create /processed but request_index still maps REMOVE_PROCESSING_ID_PATH=1, REMOVE_PROCESSING_PATH=2, SET_PROCESSED_PATH=3. Keeper reports ZOK for ops before the failing one, so when the keeper session expired (the ephemeral node is gone — the case the code's own comment calls normal) the multi fails at index 1 and both functions throw LOGICAL_ERROR 'Failed to remove processing id path' instead of logging: this aborts debug/sanitizer builds and in release escapes commit() (resetProcessing is reached from setFailed(reduce_retry_count=false) on every insert failure), leaving the rest of the batch uncommitted. In Unordered, a ZNODEEXISTS on creating /processed (index 2) is now reported as the benign 'Failed to remove processing path' warning and setProcessed returns normally (file locally Processed without a persisted marker) instead of the intended LOGICAL_ERROR. Ordered setProcessedImpl (OrderedFileMetadata.cpp:439-492) keeps the same 4-slot enum over what is now a 3-request multi ([0]=processed, [1]=remove id, [2]=remove ephemeral), so a missing ephemeral node at index 2 now also hits the LOGICAL_ERROR branch.
defects.evidence: IFileMetadata.cpp:279-285 `check_processing_id_path_idx = 0; remove_processing_id_path_idx = 1; remove_processing_path_idx = 2;` with only two requests pushed (remove id, remove processing_node_path); :311-316 index-1 failure -> `unexpected_error = true; failure_reason = "Failed to remove processing id path"` -> :330-331 `throw Exception(ErrorCodes::LOGICAL_ERROR, ...)`. Unordered .cpp:125-133 two removes then `request_index[CHECK_PROCESSING_ID_PATH] = 0; [REMOVE_PROCESSING_ID_PATH] = 1; [REMOVE_PROCESSING_PATH] = 2; [SET_PROCESSED_PATH] = 3;` then the create at :140-142. Diff removes `requests.push_back(zkutil::makeCheckRequest(processing_node_id_path, processing_id_version.value()));` from Unordered setProcessedImpl and Ordered setProcessedRequests (:431-435). Ordered enum :442-448 unchanged. processing_node_path is Ephemeral (Ordered .cpp:312).
defects.notes: Must identify that the response-index constants/map were not updated after removing the check request (in resetProcessing, Unordered setProcessedImpl, or Ordered setProcessedImpl tied to this change), so a failure is attributed to the wrong request (ephemeral-node miss -> LOGICAL_ERROR, /processed-exists misreported) or an index past the responses is used. The claimed out-of-bounds read is essentially unreachable (an earlier branch always matches first), so comments whose only stated consequence is OOB still count for spotting the misalignment. A comment only about Ordered's pre-existing layout (processed request first, named CHECK) without tying it to the removed check is a near-miss. R2 (the else-branch unreachable chassert) does not count.

defects.title: Insert-failure path wipes the attempt's processed rows and timestamps before the queue log entry is written
defects.statement: setFailed(reduce_retry_count=false) now calls resetProcessing() (IFileMetadata.cpp:386-389), whose SCOPE_EXIT runs FileStatus::reset() (:267-269, reset at :66-73 sets processed_rows=0, processing_start_time/end_time={}, retries=0). commit() then calls appendLogElement (Source.cpp:697-700), which reads rows_processed, processing_start_time and processing_end_time from that status. So every system.s3queue_log/azure_queue_log entry for a file whose insert failed reports 0 rows and no start time, whereas before the PR (setFailed only called onFailed) the attempt's statistics were logged.
defects.evidence: IFileMetadata.cpp:267 `SCOPE_EXIT({ file_status->reset(); });`; FileStatus::reset `processing_start_time = {}; processing_end_time = {}; processed_rows = 0; retries = 0;`; :388 `resetProcessing();` then :391 `file_status->onFailed(exception_message);` (sets only end time); Source.cpp appendLogElement `.rows_processed = file_status_.processed_rows, ... .processing_start_time = file_status_.processing_start_time`.
defects.notes: Must say the reset of FileStatus during the insert-failure path loses processed rows / processing times before appendLogElement records the failure. Comments about resetting local status on keeper-cleanup exceptions (C9/C25) are a different claim.

defects.title: New comment says Cancelled files 'will not be set as Failed', but commit() sets them Failed
defects.statement: generateImpl marks the half-read file FileState::Cancelled with the comment 'Mark file as Cancelled, such files will not be set as Failed' (ObjectStorageQueueSource.cpp:489-490 and :513-514), but commit() handles Cancelled by falling through to Processing and calling setFailed(exception_message, false) (:677-688), which increments ObjectStorageQueueFailedFiles, sets the local status Failed and logs processed=false. The comment misdescribes the implemented behaviour (what is avoided is charging a retry).
defects.evidence: :489 `/// Mark file as Cancelled, such files will not be set as Failed.`; :677-687 `case FileState::Cancelled: [[fallthrough]]; case FileState::Processing: { ... file_metadata->setFailed(exception_message, /* reduce_retry_count */false);`; IFileMetadata.cpp:364 `ProfileEvents::increment(ProfileEvents::ObjectStorageQueueFailedFiles);`, :391 `file_status->onFailed(exception_message);`.
defects.notes: Must point out the contradiction between the Cancelled comment and commit() calling setFailed for Cancelled files. C3 (Cancelled is redundant because commit treats it like Processing) is a simplification suggestion and does not say the comment is wrong; R9 does not count.

defects.title: Refactor leftovers: orphaned setProcessedImpl(bool) declaration and a now-unfed returnForRetry/objects_to_retry queue
defects.statement: The PR deletes the definition and only caller of ObjectStorageQueueUnorderedFileMetadata::setProcessedImpl(bool remove_processing_nodes_only) but leaves its declaration in ObjectStorageQueueUnorderedFileMetadata.h:31, advertising a reset path that no longer exists. It also removes the only call to FileIterator::returnForRetry (the read-error catch in generateImpl), leaving returnForRetry, objects_to_retry and their branches in nextImpl/isFinished (ObjectStorageQueueSource.cpp:69-72, 95-105, 159-174) as dead code that suggests failed reads are re-queued in-pass.
defects.evidence: Unordered .h:31 `void setProcessedImpl(bool remove_processing_nodes_only);` with no definition after the diff; `git grep returnForRetry` at head finds only the declaration (Source.h:60) and definition (Source.cpp:159) — no caller.
defects.notes: Either leftover counts: the orphaned bool overload declaration, or the unused returnForRetry/objects_to_retry machinery. Comments arguing the in-pass retry should be restored (C24/C34) are a behaviour claim, not this.

excluded.reason: Claims the LOG_TEST reloads file_status->state instead of using the loaded `state`, a redundant atomic op. Trivial cost inside a test-level log on a non-processable branch (IFileMetadata.cpp:233-234); not a defect.

Claims the multi error handling lacks a case for an overall failure with all ops ZOK, hitting the unreachable chassert. If every op returned ZOK the multi code is ZOK and the function returned earlier (:290-291); the real problem at this site is the index misalignment (D2), which R2 does not name.
Suggests replacing the MULTI_READ code with tryGet on a vector of paths for clarity. Refactoring preference; the MULTI_READ code (OrderedFileMetadata.cpp:250-285) is functionally correct.
Asks for a nullptr check after dynamic_cast of responses[0] to GetResponse. When a get op in a multi read returns ZOK its response is a GetResponse; the null case is unreachable.

Claims chassert(processed_rows > 0) on cancellation can fail if cancel happens before any rows are read. A file is Processing at the loop top only after a previous iteration's pull returned a chunk (reader creation and pull happen in the same iteration, :544-596); only a zero-row chunk could violate it, which is contrived, and the assert is debug-only.

Suggests chassert(!processed_files.empty()) before processed_files.back() in the reader branch. The reader is created only together with processed_files.emplace_back (:544-567); defensive-style request, not a defect.
Suggests catching specific exception types instead of catch(...). Style; recording the message and stopping is the established pattern.
Says the log format 'insert {}succeeded' reads awkwardly. It renders 'insert succeeded' / "insert hasn't succeeded" correctly; cosmetic.

Claims files in Processing state should not reach commit and cancelled files need a distinct error message. Processing/Cancelled files legitimately reach commit(false) when the pipeline fails mid-file; commit(true) guards with LOGICAL_ERROR; message wording is cosmetic.

Questions whether Processing files on a failed insert should reduce the retry count. Not charging a retry for insert failures is the purpose of the fix (PR title); read errors still reduce retries (:690-694). Speculative.

Claims that without MULTI_READ a previously failed file with no processed watermark is not classified as failed. The claim transaction always starts with addCheckNotExistsRequest(failed_node_path) (OrderedFileMetadata.cpp:309-310) and returns {false, Failed} when it fails (:350-351), so the file is still classified Failed.
Suggests removing the Cancelled state because commit() treats it like Processing. Simplification preference; it does not identify a misbehaviour (the misleading comment is D4).

Claims generate_random_files materialises 11M unused rows per call, risking multi-GB memory/OOM in CI. Test-harness resource speculation; the list is local to generate() and freed per call, and nothing in the code shows the CI worker's limit is exceeded.
Claims the integration worker can OOM because generate_random_files retains eleven million unused rows per call. Same speculative test-resource concern as C4; not a verifiable defect of the PR.
Suggests sharing the duplicated cancellation/table-drop unfinished-file handling. Duplication/style preference; both copies are consistent.
Claims ~20 s is too short for ingesting each 11M-row batch, so the test may be flaky on slow CI. Timing speculation not verifiable from the code.

Claims SCOPE_EXIT resets local status even if keeper cleanup throws, letting the file be claimed locally while keeper markers still exist. Local claiming still goes through setProcessingImpl's keeper transaction, which fails while the processing node exists; the throwing cases are LOGICAL_ERROR paths (the D2 misclassification). No concrete wrong outcome.

Claims a successful reset leaves processing_id_version set so the destructor may remove another processor's ephemeral claim. On the commit path setFailed resets processing_id/version right after resetProcessing (:393-394); the iterator's direct resetProcessing call (Source.cpp:149) behaved the same before the PR (the old Unordered resetProcessingImpl also left the version set). Pre-existing, not introduced here.

Claims the processed_rows > 0 chassert on cancellation fires if cancel happens right after createReader before any pull. Reader creation and the first pull happen in the same loop iteration with no cancellation check in between; only a zero-row chunk could reach it (contrived; debug-only assert). Same as R5.
Asks to rename reduce_retry_count because false now resets processing. Naming preference.

Claims an existing processed node with empty data leaves processed_node unset so the claim transaction checks not-exists and retries forever. No code in this repo creates the Ordered processed node with empty data (setProcessedRequests always writes node_metadata.toString(); getMetadataPaths for Ordered does not include 'processed'), so the scenario is not reachable from the code shown.

Claims processing_id_version stays set after a successful reset, so the destructor marks the file Failed after reset(). On the commit path setFailed clears the version right after resetProcessing; the iterator path (Source.cpp:149) had the same behaviour before the PR with the old Unordered resetProcessingImpl. Pre-existing.

Claims read failures are no longer returned to the current iterator, so the retry waits for the next listing. The file stays retriable in keeper and is picked up on the next poll; a latency change consistent with the PR's commit-per-state design, not a correctness defect.

Claims a keeper error from resetProcessing escapes before onFailed records the insertion error. Only reached on the LOGICAL_ERROR paths (whose trigger is D2) or keeper connection exceptions; the status is reset to None as designed. Not an independent defect.
Claims an empty-data processed node is ignored, looping the claim forever. Same unreachable scenario as C21.
Claims an existing max-processed node with empty data causes an endless claim loop. Same unreachable scenario as C21.
Asks to rename `success` to `insert_succeeded` in the commit() header comment (Source.h:146). Cosmetic; the comment's meaning is still accurate.
Claims zero-row read failures are no longer requeued via returnForRetry, deferring retry to a future polling cycle. Same as C24: retry still happens; latency only.

Claims the rewritten test times out because with merges stopped and parts_to_throw_insert=3 the first batches cannot insert. Speculative about MergeTree part counts under the test's settings; not verifiable by reading and the test is designed to hit Too many parts on the third batch.

ClickHouse__ClickHouse@36ea28a.pr_summary: A compile-time refactor. The Identifier constructors and the Identifier/IdentifierView popFirst/popLast bodies move out of src/Analyzer/Identifier.h into a new src/Analyzer/Identifier.cpp, so the header no longer pulls in boost split/join. Most asserts become chassert. Several headers (IQueryTreeNode.h, QueryNode.h, UnionNode.h, ColumnTransformers.h) stop including Identifier.h, and the files that used it transitively (FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp, SetsSerialization.cpp, StorageKafkaUtils.cpp, PostgreSQLReplicationHandler.cpp) now include what they need directly.

excluded.reason: Claim: The initializer list for `Identifier::Identifier` is excessively long on a single line. Split it across multiple lines to improve readability and maintainability. -- Rejected: Line-length/formatting preference only.

Claim: The Identifier constructor for full name strings fails to initialize the `parts` member variable, leaving it default-constructed as an empty vector despite the comment stating it should split the full name by '.' separators. This will cause incorrect behavior when parts are accessed. -- Rejected: Wrong: the constructor body fills `parts` with `boost::split(parts, full_name, [](char c) { return c == '.'; });` (Identifier.cpp:22-25, and the same at 28-31). This is the original header logic, moved verbatim.

Claim: Consider simplifying this section using standard library facilities such as assigning subranges directly instead of manually constructing result vector. E.g.: parts.assign(parts.begin() + parts_to_remove_size, parts.end()); followed by updating full_name accordingly. -- Rejected: Style suggestion on code moved verbatim from the header; behaviour is correct.

Claim: The `IdentifierView::popLast` method incorrectly uses `assert` instead of `chassert`, contradicting the stated replacement rationale.   -- Rejected: IdentifierView::popLast (Identifier.cpp:77) keeping plain `assert` while its siblings use chassert is a cosmetic inconsistency. Before the PR all four used assert, so no check was lost, and it compiles because <cassert> arrives through the boost includes. Moving the bodies back into the header would undo the point of the PR.

Claim: switching three pop guards from assert to chassert changes sanitizer-build (NDEBUG) behaviour so invalid removals now abort. Rejected: chassert only makes an existing precondition check stricter in more build types; a violated precondition would otherwise corrupt the string (resize underflow), so firing the check is not a regression, and asking for a PR-description note is not a code defect.

Claim: IdentifierView::popLast still uses assert while the other three moved pop methods use chassert, so it alone skips the check in sanitizer NDEBUG builds. Rejected: before the PR all four used plain assert (base Identifier.h:137,162,302,320), so no check is lost; the inconsistency is cosmetic (same as R4).
Claim: IdentifierView::popLast keeps assert while siblings moved to chassert; asks whether intentional. Rejected: same as C2 -- cosmetic inconsistency, no weakening versus the pre-PR code.

ClickHouse__ClickHouse@3143520.pr_summary: Adds a jemalloc arena whose extent-alloc hook madvise()s new extents MADV_DONTDUMP (JemallocNodumpAllocatorImpl), an STL allocator over it with a NoDumpString alias, and an AWS SDK MemorySystemInterface (AwsNodumpMemoryManager) that ClientFactory installs via aws_options.memoryManagementOptions before Aws::InitAPI. Encrypted-disk and named-collection encryption keys and the FileEncryption APIs (Encryptor, fingerprints, encrypted read/write buffers) switch from String to NoDumpString, and configure_config.cmake sets USE_AWS_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT when the aws_s3 or google_cloud_cpp targets exist. Unit tests for both allocators are added.

defects.title: USE_AWS_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT is set in the wrong CMake scope, too late, so the AWS nodump memory manager is never used
defects.statement: The AWS SDK only routes allocations through SDKOptions.memoryManagementOptions.memoryManager when the SDK itself is compiled with USE_AWS_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT, which is generated into aws/core/SDKConfig.h. contrib/aws-cmake/CMakeLists.txt:121-123 declares `OPTION(USE_AWS_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT ... OFF)` and immediately configure_file()s SDKConfig.h. The PR's `set(USE_AWS_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT 1)` lives in src/configure_config.cmake:87/91, included from src/CMakeLists.txt:21 — a different directory scope, processed after `add_subdirectory (contrib ...)` (CMakeLists.txt:482 vs 578) — and the variable is not consumed by src/Common/config.h.in. So the SDK is built with memory management OFF, InitAPI ignores the AwsNodumpMemoryManager installed at src/IO/S3/Client.cpp:990-993, and the advertised exclusion of S3 credentials/SDK data from core dumps does not happen.
defects.evidence: src/configure_config.cmake:87 `set(USE_AWS_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT 1)`; contrib/aws-cmake/CMakeLists.txt:121 `OPTION(USE_AWS_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT "Aws memory management" OFF)` then :122 `configure_file("${AWS_SDK_CORE_DIR}/include/aws/core/SDKConfig.h.in" ...)`; CMakeLists.txt:482 `add_subdirectory (contrib EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)` precedes :578 `add_subdirectory (src)`; `git grep USE_AWS_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT` finds only these three lines.
defects.notes: A comment must say the flag set in configure_config.cmake does not reach the AWS SDK's build/SDKConfig.h (scope or ordering), so the memory manager passed to InitAPI has no effect. Saying only that the google_cloud_cpp branch should not set it (R13) does not count.

defects.title: Short keys (16-byte AES-128, the default) live in NoDumpString's inline SSO buffer, never in the nodump arena
defects.statement: NoDumpString is std::basic_string with a custom allocator (src/Common/JemallocNodumpSTLAllocator.h:86-91). libc++'s small-string optimisation stores up to 22 chars inside the string object without calling the allocator, so 16-byte AES-128 keys (AES_128_CTR is DEFAULT_ENCRYPTION_ALGORITHM, src/Disks/DiskEncrypted.cpp:30) are kept inline in DiskEncryptedSettings::current_key / all_keys map nodes (src/Disks/DiskEncryptedTransaction.h:22-25), Encryptor::key (src/IO/FileEncryptionCommon.h:98) and the named-collection key — all objects in ordinary, dumpable memory. Only keys longer than the SSO capacity (AES-192/256) are actually protected, so the default configuration still dumps its keys.
defects.evidence: JemallocNodumpSTLAllocator.h:87-91 `using NoDumpString = std::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, NoDumpCharAllocator>;`; DiskEncryptedTransaction.h:25 `std::unordered_map<UInt128, NoDumpString> all_keys;` (default node allocator); DiskEncrypted.cpp:30 `DEFAULT_ENCRYPTION_ALGORITHM = Algorithm::AES_128_CTR`; FileEncryptionCommon.h:24 `AES_128_CTR, /// Size of key is 16 bytes.`
defects.notes: Must identify small-string optimisation keeping short keys inside the string object (outside the allocator), so they remain dumpable. Complaints only about temporary std::string copies from config do not count.

defects.title: madvise failure message reports errnoToString(-1) instead of errno
defects.statement: In JemallocNodumpAllocatorImpl::alloc (src/Common/JemallocNodumpAllocatorImpl.cpp:36-44) madvise returns -1 on failure and sets errno, but the code passes the return value to errnoToString, so the exception text reads 'Unknown error -1' instead of the real reason in both the MADV_DONTDUMP and MADV_NOCORE branches (unlike mallctl, which does return the error code).
defects.evidence: JemallocNodumpAllocatorImpl.cpp:36-38 `if (auto ret = madvise(result, size, MADV_DONTDUMP)) { throw std::runtime_error(Poco::format("Failed to run madvise: %s", errnoToString(ret))); }`; base/base/errnoToString.h `std::string errnoToString(int the_errno = errno);`
defects.notes: Must say the madvise return value (-1) rather than errno is passed to errnoToString. Comments about the throw itself crossing jemalloc's callback belong in the excluded group.

excluded.reason: Claims AwsNodumpMemoryManager should catch exceptions from JemallocNodumpAllocatorImpl (init or madvise failure) and return nullptr. Arena setup throws only at singleton construction, and madvise(MADV_DONTDUMP) on a freshly mapped anonymous extent does not fail on supported kernels; mallocx returns NULL rather than throwing. Not a reachable crash (and the AWS manager is not even active, see D1).

Claims a failing madvise in the extent hook throws through jemalloc's C callback and can terminate the server. madvise(MADV_DONTDUMP/NOCORE) on an extent just returned by the default mmap-based hook does not fail in practice, so the throw path is effectively unreachable; robustness hardening, not a defect.
Same claim as C5: throwing from the jemalloc extent hook crosses C frames on madvise failure. The failure is not reachable on freshly mapped anonymous extents; not a defect.
Asks to document why AwsNodumpMemoryManager's Begin()/End() are no-ops. Empty hooks are the normal MemorySystemInterface implementation; documentation request.
Suggests moving the JemallocNodumpAllocatorImpl.h include from the header to the .cpp. Include-placement style.
Says Poco/Format.h is unused in JemallocNodumpSTLAllocator.h. Unused include; style.

Claims the STL allocator lacks rebind/propagate_on_container_*/max_size and may be rejected by some libraries. std::allocator_traits supplies all these defaults for a minimal C++11 allocator; it is used only with std::basic_string under libc++ and the tests exercise it.

Claims allocate() ignores alignof(T) and could misalign over-aligned types. The allocator is only instantiated for char (NoDumpCharAllocator) and jemalloc's size-class alignment covers any non-over-aligned type; hypothetical.
Asks the allocator to forward alignof(T) for over-aligned element types. Same as R6: only used with char; hypothetical.
Claims containers of over-aligned types (alignas(64)) could be misaligned because allocate() omits alignof(T). Same as R6; no such instantiation exists.

Claims toNoDumpString taking std::string by value copies sensitive data into dumpable heap memory. Callers pass config.getString() rvalues (moved, no extra copy), and the plaintext key already lives permanently in the Poco configuration in ordinary memory, so this adds no exposure; hardening suggestion.

Claims toNoDumpString does not erase the ordinary std::string source, so config-derived keys stay in dumpable memory. The same key text is held for the whole process lifetime by the Poco configuration in ordinary heap, which the PR never claimed to protect; the transient copy adds no new exposure. Not a defect of this change.

Claims callers like toNoDumpString(config.getString(key_path)) leave key copies in dumpable memory and the source should be wiped. As for C2, the configuration itself retains the plaintext; the temporary adds nothing.

Claims config.getString() creates an ordinary string holding the key at DiskEncrypted.cpp:60/68/125/131. The configuration object already holds that plaintext in ordinary memory for the process lifetime; not a new exposure introduced by the PR.
Claims the temporary getString result is not erased and can appear in a core dump. Same as C19: the source config remains dumpable anyway; hardening suggestion.
Claims toNoDumpString leaves the original config key in dumpable memory at DiskEncrypted.cpp:60,68,125,131. Same as C19; not a defect of the change.

Claims boost::algorithm::unhex(key_hex) creates a dumpable temporary copy of the decoded named-collection key. The hex form (equivalent information) is already held in the configuration in ordinary memory; the transient adds no new exposure.
Claims the named-collection constructor decodes the key through a plain std::string temporary that is not cleared. Same as R8: key_hex is retained in the configuration anyway.
Claims key_hex and the decoded intermediate for named collections remain on dumpable pages. Same as R8/C17; not a new exposure.

Claims S3 credentials passed to ClientFactory::create as ordinary Strings stay dumpable even with the SDK manager. ClickHouse-side credential strings come from configuration/settings that are in ordinary memory regardless; the PR only claims SDK-internal allocations, so this is a scope remark, not a defect of the change (the real problem, D1, is that the SDK manager is inactive).
Says templating unhexKey is unnecessary since it is only used with NoDumpString. Style preference; behaviour identical.

Generic request to double-check findKeyByFingerprint and logging paths for implicit String copies of keys. Names no concrete leak; findKeyByFingerprint returns NoDumpString and callers keep NoDumpString.
Suggests const unsigned char* and key.data() instead of reinterpret_cast<uint8_t*>(key.c_str()) for OpenSSL. Style on effectively unchanged code; the cast is valid and the storage contiguous.
Claims USE_AWS_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT should not be set for the Google Cloud target. Setting it in that branch is harmless in itself; the comment does not say the setting is ineffective (D1).

Claims `key = boost::algorithm::unhex(key_hex)` fails to compile because std::string cannot be assigned to a basic_string with a different allocator. basic_string has a templated operator= from any type convertible to basic_string_view<char, char_traits<char>>, which std::string is, so this compiles (the PR builds and its tests run).

Asks what happens on platforms with neither MADV_DONTDUMP nor MADV_NOCORE, where the hook is a no-op. Linux has MADV_DONTDUMP and FreeBSD MADV_NOCORE; other jemalloc-enabled targets are not relevant here. Platform hypothetical.
Same claim as C3: if no advisory constant exists the allocator silently provides dumpable memory. Not reachable on supported jemalloc platforms.
Asks builds without jemalloc to make the lack of dump exclusion explicit since NoDumpString becomes a plain allocator. Deliberate documented fallback in the header; design suggestion.
Claims NoDumpString silently uses the normal allocator when USE_JEMALLOC is off. Intentional fallback visible in the alias; production builds use jemalloc. Design preference, not a defect.

Asks whether recycled/retained extents can bypass the no-dump marking since only the alloc hook advises. The arena's extents all originate from its own alloc hook and the MADV_DONTDUMP VMA flag persists across purge/reuse; speculative, no concrete path shown.
Asks the tests to verify the no-dump property rather than just allocation. Test-coverage request.

ClickHouse__ClickHouse@f9987c8.pr_summary: Enables the binary-search path over the primary-key index (KeyCondition::matchesExactContinuousRange) for conditions whose key column is wrapped in a monotonic function chain, as long as every function in the chain (and every set-index mapping's function chain) reports is_always_monotonic over the full range; previously any monotonic chain disabled the fast path. It also lets ALWAYS_TRUE RPN elements pass through the continuity check. Adds a stateless test checking that Enum/Enum-cast and 'AND 1 = 1' conditions use binary search while toDayOfMonth(ts) still uses generic exclusion search.

defects.title: Non-strict (non-injective) monotonic chains are still classified as POINT constraints, so multi-column keys are wrongly treated as one continuous range (wrong exact ranges / count())
defects.statement: The new pre-pass (KeyCondition.cpp:2903-2939) admits any chain whose functions are is_always_monotonic, but ignores is_strict. The constraint classifier below (2956-2971) still marks a column POINT when the RPN element's range is a single value (element.range.left == element.range.right) or a one-element set — but with a monotonic chain that value lives in the FUNCTION's result space; for a non-injective function such as toDate/toStartOfHour/toStartOfInterval/Float conversion (all report is_always_monotonic without is_strict) the preimage on the key column is a RANGE of keys. With ORDER BY (ts, b) and WHERE toDate(ts) = D AND b = 5, both columns are marked POINT, the continuity check passes, and MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor takes the binary-search branch. That branch only tests the first and last marks for can_be_false and then asserts (chassert) and records the whole middle as an exact range (MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor.cpp ~1545-1557), although middle marks contain rows with b != 5. exact_ranges feed the trivial-count optimisation in optimizeUseAggregateProjection.cpp:576-595 (exact_count += rows in exact ranges), so SELECT count() ... WHERE toDate(ts)=D AND b=5 over-counts in release builds and trips the chassert in debug builds; without exact ranges it at least reads a wider mark range than the exclusion search would. Before the PR any chain returned false, so this is newly exposed.
defects.evidence: KeyCondition.cpp:2917 `if (!monotonicity.is_always_monotonic) return false;` (no is_strict check); 2964-2966 `if (element.range.left == element.range.right) column_constraints[element.key_column] = Constraint::POINT;` (range is post-chain). IFunctionDateOrDateTime.h:90 and toStartOfInterval.cpp:50 return {.is_monotonic = true, .is_always_monotonic = true} with is_strict=false; FunctionsConversion.h:3405 same for any Float conversion. MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor.cpp binary-search branch: trims only first/last mark then `chassert(check_in_range(result_exact_range, ...) == BoolMask(true, false)); exact_ranges->emplace_back(...)`. optimizeUseAggregateProjection.cpp:595 `exact_count += ...getRowsCountInRange(exact_ranges[i])`.
defects.notes: Must say that a non-strict / non-injective always-monotonic function turns an equality into a key RANGE, so treating it as POINT (or not requiring is_strict) breaks the continuity assumption for later key columns (wrong/too-wide ranges, wrong exact count, or assertion). A comment merely saying 'Field{} as range is odd' or 'check monotonicity direction' does not count.

defects.title: New test uses the non-existent time zone 'Asia/shanghai' (wrong case), so the second query block fails and the test output mismatches its reference
defects.statement: tests/queries/0_stateless/03518_key_condition_binary_search.sh:25 declares `DateTime64(3, 'Asia/shanghai')`. ClickHouse resolves time-zone names by exact, case-sensitive match against the embedded tzdata list (contrib/cctz-cmake/CMakeLists.txt:66 generates `if (std::string_view("<TZ>") == name) ...`), falling back to cctz's filesystem loader, which on a case-sensitive Linux filesystem finds no `Asia/shanghai` file; DateLUTImpl then throws BAD_ARGUMENTS 'Cannot load time zone Asia/shanghai' (src/Common/DateLUTImpl.cpp:76-77). The multi-query block aborts at CREATE TABLE, the grep -c for 'generic exclusion search' prints 0 instead of the reference's 1 (03518_key_condition_binary_search.reference:2), so the new stateless test fails in CI.
defects.evidence: sh:25 `timestamp DateTime64(3, 'Asia/shanghai')`; every other test/source spelling is 'Asia/Shanghai' (src/Client/ClientBaseHelpers.cpp:47, src/Functions/dateTimeToSnowflakeID.cpp:142); no lowercase region/city tz name appears anywhere else in tests/queries (git grep -E "'(europe|asia|america)/[a-z]" finds none); getTimeZone lookup is exact string equality (contrib/cctz-cmake/CMakeLists.txt:66); DateLUTImpl.cpp:76 `if (!cctz::load_time_zone(time_zone, &cctz_time_zone)) throw ... "Cannot load time zone {}"`.
defects.notes: Must say the time-zone name casing is wrong ('Asia/Shanghai') and the test will error/fail. Severity kept at medium because it only breaks the new test, not the product; it would likely pass on a case-insensitive macOS filesystem via the fallback loader.

excluded.reason: Suggests skipping non-relevant RPN element types early in the new monotonic-chain loop. Micro-optimisation/readability. For elements with no chain, the check `!elem.monotonic_functions_chain.empty() && ...` short-circuits with no function call (KeyCondition.cpp:2926); RPN is tiny. No defect.

Claims the two full passes over rpn and possible copies of getIndexesMapping are a performance concern. Performance speculation: the RPN is a handful of elements per query and this runs once per part; two linear passes have no measurable cost. getIndexesMapping is iterated by const reference. Not a defect.

Claims the `set_index->size() != 1` restriction is unexplained and should be documented or relaxed. The size()==1 restriction is the pre-existing rule of the second loop (KeyCondition.cpp:2956, `element.set_index->size() == 1` → POINT; any other set falls through to `return false`); a multi-element set is not a single continuous range, so the restriction is correct. Documentation request only.
Notes the new shell test lacks a trailing newline. Missing trailing newline in a shell script is formatting only; bash runs it fine.

Asks the test to assert the fallback query's returned rows, not just the generic-search log line. This is a request for stronger test coverage/assertions, not a defect in the change; the test's actual breakage (the time-zone name) is D2.

Claims the test pipeline discards results and stderr so failing SQL can go unnoticed; asks for pipefail and separate result assertions. This is a request for stronger test coverage/assertions, not a defect in the change; the test's actual breakage (the time-zone name) is D2.

Claims the new pre-pass duplicates the singleton-set eligibility decision of the classification loop and should be merged into one traversal. The two checks agree (both require FUNCTION_IN_SET with size()==1); a refactoring preference with no drift or behavioural consequence.

Claims the test inserts one row (one mark) so the binary-search loops never execute; asks for multi-mark data. This is a request for stronger test coverage/assertions, not a defect in the change; the test's actual breakage (the time-zone name) is D2.

Asks for a positive test of an always-monotonic wrapped key selecting binary search. This is a request for stronger test coverage/assertions, not a defect in the change; the test's actual breakage (the time-zone name) is D2.

Claims the new check passes the constant's type (types.front()) instead of the key argument type for LEFT_CONST wrappers into getMonotonicityForRange. The wrapper's getMonotonicityForRange forwards to the function, and the functions reachable here with a left constant (binary arithmetic plus/minus/divide/intDiv) ignore the type argument entirely (FunctionBinaryArithmetic.h:2841 `getMonotonicityForRange(const IDataType &, ...)`); no concrete misclassification is shown.

Asks the test to assert binary search per SELECT instead of one aggregated count. This is a request for stronger test coverage/assertions, not a defect in the change; the test's actual breakage (the time-zone name) is D2.

Claims boundary-search bugs go undetected because the table has one mark and only logs are counted. This is a request for stronger test coverage/assertions, not a defect in the change; the test's actual breakage (the time-zone name) is D2.

Claims the new check bypasses isFunctionReallyMonotonic's guard against toDateTime(Date) with overflow behaviour Ignore. That guard is applied when the chain is built (KeyCondition.cpp:1657 `if (!isFunctionReallyMonotonic(*func, *key_column_type)) return false;`), so such a function never enters monotonic_functions_chain; the claim is wrong.

Claims LEFT_CONST wrappers make types.front() the constant's type, misclassifying chains as always monotonic. Same as C6: the reachable left-constant functions ignore the type argument, so no concrete misclassification follows.

Asks both test pipelines to preserve the client exit status so SQL errors are not masked by grep -c. This is a request for stronger test coverage/assertions, not a defect in the change; the test's actual breakage (the time-zone name) is D2.

ClickHouse__ClickHouse@79224f2.pr_summary: Replaces a chassert in ObjectStorageQueueIFileMetadata::prepareSetProcessingRequests with graceful handling: it now try-locks the shared per-file processing_lock and returns std::nullopt when the lock is held or the local state is non-processable (possible when several S3/Azure Queue tables on one server share a keeper path). FileIterator::next (ObjectStorageQueueSource.cpp) nulls out rejected objects, skips them after the Keeper multi, and compacts new_batch; the integration test raises the number of tables sharing a path from 3 to 10.

defects.title: new_batch is compacted but file_metadatas is not, so surviving objects are paired with the wrong file metadata
defects.statement: When prepareSetProcessingRequests returns nullopt for some entry, ObjectStorageQueueSource.cpp:240-252 rebuilds new_batch without the null entries, but file_metadatas (filled per original index at :196) keeps its original size and order and is not cleared on the ZOK path. next() then returns `object_infos[index]` with `file_metadatas[index]` (:268-270). After the first skipped file, every later object is paired with another file's metadata: debug/sanitizer builds hit the chassert `Mismatch {} vs {}` (:272-275) — the very kind of assert the PR set out to fix — and release builds process file A while committing/failing/resetting file B's Keeper state (B may be owned by another table, A's processing node is left dangling), leading to lost or duplicated files. This is exactly the multi-table-same-path scenario the PR's test (10 tables) exercises.
defects.evidence: :196 `file_metadatas[i] = metadata->getFileMetadata(...)`; :208 `new_batch[i] = nullptr;`; :240-251 only new_batch is compacted (`new_batch_copy[i++] = std::move(object); ... new_batch = std::move(new_batch_copy);`); file_metadatas is cleared only in the tryMulti failure branch (:237); :268-270 `std::make_pair(object_infos[index], file_metadatas.empty() ? nullptr : file_metadatas[index])`.
defects.notes: Must say file_metadatas is not filtered/compacted alongside new_batch (index misalignment between objects and metadata / path-mismatch assert). Comments about resize()+assign efficiency do not count.

excluded.reason: Claims the unique_lock in prepareSetProcessingRequests is released before the caller executes the Keeper requests, creating a race. The in-process processing_lock is only a local optimisation (trySetProcessing calls it that); correctness comes from the atomic Keeper multi, which fails if another processor already created the processing node, and the failure branch falls back to per-file processing. No correctness race is introduced.

Suggests rewording the try_lock log message ('on this server' twice) and checking callers treat nullopt as a benign skip. Log wording nit; the only caller handles nullopt by skipping a file another table is already processing, as intended.

Claims the second 'being processed by another table' log in the non-processable-state branch is a copy-paste error. LOG_TEST-level wording with no behavioural effect; since filterProcessableFiles already dropped Keeper-processed/failed files, a local Processing/Processed state there does typically come from another table sharing the file_status on this server.
Suggests reserve()+push_back instead of resize()+indexed assignment when compacting new_batch. Micro-style preference with negligible cost.
Asks to remove or reword the second 'another table' log in the non-processable-state branch. Same as R3: LOG_TEST wording only, no behavioural consequence.
Asks to keep the competing-table log only in the failed-lock branch because Processed/Failed files also emit it. Same as R3/C1: test-level log wording.
Asks the 'Successfully set N files as processing' log to use num_successful_objects instead of new_batch.size(). Log-count accuracy nit at LOG_TEST level; no behavioural effect.
Same as C2: the success log overstates the count by including rejected entries. Log wording nit.
Asks for a deterministic test of a rejected-then-accepted batch. Test-coverage request, not a code defect (the underlying bug is D1).

Claims an all-rejected batch submits an empty Keeper transaction whose error branch assumes a failed index. ZooKeeper::multiImpl returns ZOK immediately for empty requests (ZooKeeper.cpp:753-754), the success loop skips null entries and the compacted empty batch makes the while loop fetch the next batch; no failure.
Suggests sharing the processability predicate between trySetProcessing and prepareSetProcessingRequests. Refactoring suggestion; the two copies are currently identical, so no drift exists.

Claims releasing the mutex before tryMulti lets another table append a competing create request so one multi fails and blocks the rest of its batch. The Keeper multi is atomic and its failure branch clears file_metadatas and falls back to per-file trySetProcessing; this is a pre-existing optimistic design with a correct fallback, not a correctness defect of this PR.

ClickHouse__ClickHouse@f9d51fa.pr_summary: Adds two CurrentMetrics, ReadonlyDisks and BrokenDisks, updated at the end of DiskLocalCheckThread::run() by the delta between the disk's readonly/broken flags sampled before and after the check. Logs the check period when the check thread starts, gives DiskLocal a per-disk logger name `DiskLocal(<name>)`, and drops the now-redundant disk name from the check thread's messages (its logger is already `DiskLocalCheckThread(<name>)`).

defects.title: ReadonlyDisks is delta-only and misses the readonly state set at startup: it undercounts and goes negative on recovery
defects.statement: The gauges are maintained purely as deltas inside DiskLocalCheckThread::run() (DiskLocalCheckThread.cpp:50-51 sample, 83-84 add), but `readonly` is also set outside the thread: IDisk::startup runs checkAccess() before startupImpl (IDisk.cpp:205-218) and DiskLocal::checkAccessImpl sets `readonly = true` when the root is not writable (DiskLocal.cpp:664, 671) without touching the metric; the checker is still started afterwards (DiskLocal.cpp:763-764). The first run() samples readonly=true and, if the disk is still readonly, adds 0, so a disk readonly from startup is never counted; when it later becomes writable run() sets readonly=false and adds -1, so ReadonlyDisks goes negative. The counter is never initialised from the disk's state when the checker starts.
defects.evidence: DiskLocalCheckThread.cpp:83 `CurrentMetrics::add(CurrentMetrics::ReadonlyDisks, diskStatusChange(readonly, disk->isReadOnly()));` with `bool readonly = disk->isReadOnly();` sampled at run() start; DiskLocal.cpp:664 `readonly = true; return;` in checkAccessImpl (no metric update); IDisk.cpp:216-218 `checkAccess(); } startupImpl(context);`; DiskLocal.cpp:763 `if (disk_checker && disk_checker_can_check_read) disk_checker->startup();`; DiskLocalCheckThread.cpp:59 `disk->readonly = false;` when can_write.
defects.notes: Counts if a comment says the metrics only record transitions inside run() and so miss the initial/startup readonly state (checkAccessImpl), leading to an undercount or a negative ReadonlyDisks after recovery. Comments about SYSTEM RESTART DISK or disk removal leaving stale contributions do not count (SYSTEM RESTART DISK throws NOT_IMPLEMENTED and disks cannot be removed at runtime). Comments about exceptions from canRead/canWrite do not count (they are noexcept).

excluded.reason: Claims the startup log's `check_period_ms * 1e6` double conversion is error-prone and may lose precision. formatReadableTime takes nanoseconds as double; the conversion is correct and precision is irrelevant for a log line. Style.

Claims the startup and recovery log messages omit the disk name, so entries cannot be correlated with disks. The check thread's logger is named `DiskLocalCheckThread(<disk name>)` (DiskLocalCheckThread.cpp:25), so every message carries the disk name.
Asks for const on the by-value bool parameters of diskStatusChange. Style; no effect.
Asks to make diskStatusChange static/anonymous-namespace to avoid ODR issues. No other definition exists and missing-prototypes is not enabled; style.
Claims the 'Disk is readonly' log should include the disk name. The logger name already includes it (DiskLocalCheckThread.cpp:25).
Claims removing the disk name from log messages hurts debuggability with multiple disks. The logger name `DiskLocalCheckThread(<name>)` already includes it.

Claims metrics can become stale if run() returns early or canRead/canWrite throw, and that mixing isReadOnly()/fields may mismatch. canRead()/canWrite() are noexcept, the need_stop return changes no state, and isReadOnly/isBroken are plain reads of the same fields; no inconsistency arises.

Claims a removed disk's checker leaves its contribution in the gauges because shutdown() does not subtract it. Disks cannot be removed at runtime (DiskSelector.cpp:148 defers removal to server restart), so the scenario is unreachable.

Claims shutdown/restart of a disk (startupImpl resetting broken) leaves BrokenDisks stale. SYSTEM RESTART DISK throws NOT_IMPLEMENTED (InterpreterSystemQuery.cpp:1383-1386) and disks are not removed at runtime, so startupImpl never re-runs on a live disk; unreachable.
Asks that the two-argument DiskLocal constructor also use a disk-named logger. Pre-existing constructor, unchanged by the PR; logging consistency preference.

ClickHouse__ClickHouse@3eee886.pr_summary: Replaces the ad-hoc attachToGroupIfDetached/detachFromGroupIfNotDetached + setThreadName pattern in ~25 thread-pool task lambdas with a reworked noexcept RAII ThreadGroupSwitcher(thread_group, thread_name, allow_existing_group) that no-ops for a null or identical group, raises LOGICAL_ERROR (caught and logged; abort in debug) when attaching over a different group unless allow_existing_group, restores the previous group, and checks nesting in its destructor. Adds a debug-build check in ThreadPool::worker that a job leaves ThreadStatus/ThreadGroup unchanged, LOGICAL_ERROR checks in ProfileEvents::getProfileEvents, a static_assert forbidding ThreadPoolCallbackRunnerLocal on GlobalThreadPool, gives the polygon dictionary a local ThreadPool with three new CurrentMetrics, and stops Aggregator from running the attach/detach wrapper for inline converter/merge calls.

defects.title: Thread names are no longer set for pool tasks that run without a thread group (or in the same group)
defects.statement: Every converted site previously called setThreadName(...) unconditionally (e.g. threadPoolCallbackRunnerUnsafe, ThreadPoolCallbackRunnerLocal, PipelineExecutor 'QueryPipelineEx', UniqExactSet, DWARFDecoder, PrettyWriter, SystemReplicas, pushing/completed pipeline executors). The new ThreadGroupSwitcher constructor returns before naming when thread_group is null (ThreadStatusExt.cpp:177-178) or equals the current group (:184-189); setThreadName is reached only on the attach path (:202-203). The pool worker resets the name to the default 'ThreadPool' before every job, so tasks scheduled from a group-less context (background/startup work through the callback runners, pipelines or formats run outside a query) now run under the generic/stale pool name, degrading system.stack_trace, logs, profilers and the OpenTelemetry span name derived from getThreadName() (ThreadPool.cpp:803-814).
defects.evidence: ThreadStatusExt.cpp:177 `if (!thread_group) return;` and :184-189 same-group early return precede :202-203 `if (thread_name[0] != '\0') setThreadName(thread_name);`. The diff removes unconditional `setThreadName(thread_name.data());` (runner, old line 154), `setThreadName(my_thread_name.data());` (old 190), `setThreadName("QueryPipelineEx");`, `setThreadName("UniqExaConvert")`, `setThreadName("DWARFDecoder")`, `setThreadName("SystemReplicas")`, etc. ThreadPool.cpp:807 uses getThreadName() for the span operation name unless it is DEFAULT_THREAD_NAME.
defects.notes: Counts if the comment says the requested thread name is not applied when the group is null (or equal to the current group), i.e. naming became conditional on attaching, at the switcher or at any converted call site. Comments that only ask for a name instead of "" at Aggregator/DistributedSink/merge-task sites do not count: those sites never set a name before.

excluded.reason: Asks for consistent 'thread pool' wording in the new PolygonDictionary metric descriptions. Style; 'threadpool' matches adjacent entries.
Asks to const-qualify initial_thread/initial_thread_group in ThreadPool.cpp. Style.

Claims the new debug check throwing in the worker can std::terminate and that shared_ptr comparison can false-positive. The throw is inside the worker's try block (ThreadPool.cpp:766-829) and is recorded as the job's exception; comparing ThreadGroupPtr compares the managed object identity, which is what is intended.
Claims null pointers / master_thread_id access in the debug-check message may crash. Both pointers are guarded by ternaries (ThreadPool.cpp:799) before dereferencing.
Claims thread_name could be nullptr and the 15-byte limit is unenforced. Every caller passes a literal or c_str(); no reachable null; the length note documents setThreadName's own limit.
Says noexcept on the destructor is redundant. Style.
Claims the GlobalThreadPool static_assert can be bypassed via cv/ref-qualified types. No caller does so; hypothetical.
Claims a dangling c_str() if ThreadGroupSwitcher stores the name pointer. It does not store it (used only inside the constructor) and the std::string outlives the switcher.
Claims 'ParallelCompres' is a typo. Thread names are capped at 15 bytes and this is the pre-existing name.

Claims the noexcept constructor swallowing a failed attach silently runs compression outside the group, unlike the old deterministic attach. Failures are LOGICAL_ERROR invariant violations (abort in debug) or setpriority errors that would already fail the query's main-thread attach; not a reachable regression.
Asks for a meaningful thread name instead of "" for the Aggregator converter. That task never set a name before; style.
Asks for a meaningful thread name instead of "" for Aggregator merge_bucket. Never set a name before; style.
Points out inconsistent capitalisation of 'CurrentThread' vs 'Current thread' in error messages. Style.
Claims thread_name[0] is UB if nullptr is passed. No caller passes nullptr; hypothetical.
Claims catching all exceptions in the switcher constructor hides failures. Deliberate, documented design; the only throws are LOGICAL_ERRORs that abort in debug builds.
Suggests a name instead of "" for DistributedSink onFinish and questions allow_existing_group=false. The lambda never set a name before, and it runs as a fresh pool job where false is correct.
Asks to document the "" and allow_existing_group arguments. Documentation request.
Asks for a descriptive name instead of "" in ReplicatedMergeMutateTaskBase. Background executor thread keeps its own name, and the switcher never named it before; style.

Claims a pool callback still runs after the switcher's group switch failed (conflicting group or attach failure), under the wrong or no group. The old attachToGroupIfDetached pattern also ran the task under the existing group; the conflict is now a LOGICAL_ERROR that aborts in debug/CI builds, and attach failures (setpriority) would already fail the query's own attach first. Not a regression.

Claims a rejected group switch still runs the callback charged to an unrelated query. Same as C1: behaviour matches the old attachToGroupIfDetached (task ran under the existing group) and the new LOGICAL_ERROR aborts in debug builds; no regression.

Claims the header's promise that the switcher 'asserts' is wrong because the conflict is caught and logged. In ClickHouse a LOGICAL_ERROR exception aborts in debug/sanitizer builds, which is the assertion meant; the doc is accurate.

Claims that if restoring the previous group throws, the destructor only logs and leaves the thread without its group or partially attached. The base destructor restored the group the same way (and would throw from a destructor); attach failure is not a realistic path here. Not introduced by this PR.

Claims with allow_existing_group=true a failed attach after detaching the previous group loses the caller's group permanently (merge/mutation tasks). The base switcher also detached before attaching and lost the group on a throwing attach; the only throwing path (setpriority for os_thread_priority) would fail the owning query first. Pre-existing and contrived.
Claims the allow_existing_group path can leave the previous group unrestored and the thread partially attached if attachToGroup throws. Same as C13: pre-existing ordering, contrived failure path.
Asks that a failed construction restore the original group after detaching it. Same as C13: pre-existing and contrived.

Claims a throwing attachToGroup (setpriority failure) leaves the worker partially attached and loses the original group because the catch disables cleanup. setpriority failure requires os_thread_priority without CAP_SYS_NICE, which already fails the query's main-thread attach before pool tasks are scheduled; contrived.

Claims makeCell's recursion creates an independent 128-thread pool per cell, multiplying concurrency. Parallel scheduling only happens for depth <= kMultiProcessingDepth (2) with 4 rows per cell, so at most ~17 pools with 4 jobs each, the same parallelism the global-pool runner had; the 128 is a cap, not threads spawned.

Claims every deep cell constructs and destroys a pool it never uses. ThreadPoolImpl's constructor allocates no threads or queue storage (ThreadPool.cpp:164-182) and finalize on an empty pool joins nothing; the overhead is negligible, no concrete consequence.
Claims creating/destroying a pool per recursively divided cell costs repeated setup/teardown. Same as C6: the empty pool is a few atomics and a mutex; no measurable regression grounded in the code.

Claims the new debug check in ThreadPool::worker only runs when the job returns normally. It is a debug-only diagnostic added by this PR; missing the exception path is a limitation of new instrumentation, not a regression or bug.
Asks to include the requested group's master_thread_id in the conflict error. Diagnostic nicety; style.
Asks for a group-only overload so merge tasks need not pass "". API style preference.

ClickHouse__ClickHouse@d67628c.pr_summary: Changes PipelineExecutor to start with use_threads = 1 instead of the granted CPU-slot count and to throttle thread spawning: ExecutorTasks tracks an atomic idle_threads counter and spawnThreads stops acquiring slots once more than 4 threads are idle, guarded by a try-lock so only one thread spawns at a time. Several stateless and integration tests asserting thread counts are relaxed (mostly to >= 1).

defects.title: Initial tasks and all initial async tasks are assigned to thread 0, serializing async (remote) sources on one thread
defects.statement: initializeExecution now calls tasks.init(num_threads, 1, ...) (src/Processors/Executors/PipelineExecutor.cpp:372), so ExecutorTasks::fill (src/Processors/Executors/ExecutorTasks.cpp:176-208) wraps next_thread to 0 after every element: every initial async task goes into thread 0's async queue and every initial task into queue 0. Async tasks are thread-affine: processAsyncTasks pushes a ready async task into executor_contexts[task.thread_num] (src/Processors/Executors/ExecutorTasks.cpp:228) and only that thread's tryPopAsyncTask (src/Processors/Executors/ExecutorTasks.cpp:69) takes it; rescheduling via pushTasks keeps the executing thread's number (src/Processors/Executors/ExecutorTasks.cpp:143). So all async sources that start the pipeline (remote/distributed reads) are processed by thread 0 for the whole query even after more threads start — a parallelism regression for distributed queries, which is why 02845's peak-thread thresholds had to be dropped from 77/95 to 1.
defects.evidence: src/Processors/Executors/PipelineExecutor.cpp:372 `tasks.init(num_threads, 1, profile_processors, …)` (base: `size_t use_threads = cpu_slots->grantedCount();`). src/Processors/Executors/ExecutorTasks.cpp:185-193 `async_task_queue.addTask(next_thread, …); ++next_thread; if (next_thread >= use_threads) next_thread = 0;`; src/Processors/Executors/ExecutorTasks.cpp:228 `executor_contexts[task.thread_num]->pushAsyncTask(node);`.
defects.notes: Must identify that passing use_threads=1 to init/fill concentrates the initial async tasks on thread 0 (thread-affine), losing parallelism. A generic 'may reduce parallelism' without the init/fill mechanism is a near-miss; C16 (scan overhead stealing ordinary tasks from queue 0) does not count.

defects.title: Thread-count regression tests weakened to vacuous `>= 1` checks
defects.statement: tests/queries/0_stateless/01415_overlimiting_threads_for_repica_bug.sql:11, tests/queries/0_stateless/02015_global_in_threads.sh:11 and tests/queries/0_stateless/02845_threads_count_in_distributed_queries.sql.j2:105,219 now assert `length(thread_ids) >= 1` / `peak_threads >= 1`, which any executed query satisfies (the 02845 comment still says 'we have 95 parts'). These tests were written to catch under- or over-parallelisation regressions and can no longer fail, so D1 and future regressions pass CI silently.
defects.evidence: tests/queries/0_stateless/02845_threads_count_in_distributed_queries.sql.j2:105 `if(peak_threads >= 1, 'ok', …)` (was >= 77); :219 (was >= 95); tests/queries/0_stateless/02015_global_in_threads.sh:11 `length(thread_ids) >= 1` (was >= 32); tests/queries/0_stateless/01415_overlimiting_threads_for_repica_bug.sql:11 `>= 1` (was >= 16).
defects.notes: Must say the thresholds were relaxed to trivially-true values so the tests no longer detect loss of parallelism (or excessive spawning).

defects.title: Throttled spawning leaves granted CPU slots unacquired but still counted by ConcurrencyControl
defects.statement: ConcurrencyControl::allocate counts every granted slot in cur_concurrency immediately; granted slots return only when an acquired slot is destroyed or the allocation is freed. Before, spawnThreads acquired every granted slot; now it stops once tasks.shouldSpawn() is false (src/Processors/Executors/PipelineExecutor.cpp:389, src/Processors/Executors/ExecutorTasks.h:75: more than 4 idle threads), so the remaining granted slots sit unused yet counted against concurrent_threads_soft_limit until the query ends, delaying/under-granting other queries.
defects.evidence: src/Processors/Executors/PipelineExecutor.cpp:389 `while (tasks.shouldSpawn() && (slot = cpu_slots->tryAcquire()))`; src/Common/ConcurrencyControl.cpp allocate: `cur_concurrency += granted;`. The PR relaxes test_concurrent_threads_soft_limit (`ConcurrencyControlSlotsAcquired == 100` -> `1..100`), consistent with slots granted but not acquired.
defects.notes: Must say that not acquiring granted slots keeps them reserved in ConcurrencyControl so other queries lose concurrency. Comments only about this query using fewer threads are D1, not this.

defects.title: Comment on upscale still says use_threads never drops below the initially granted count
defects.statement: src/Processors/Executors/PipelineExecutor.cpp:393-395 keeps `NOTE: this will not decrease use_threads below initially granted count`, but use_threads is now initialised to 1 (src/Processors/Executors/PipelineExecutor.cpp:372) regardless of the grant and grows one spawned thread at a time; the note describes the removed behaviour and misleads readers reasoning about the finish condition (src/Processors/Executors/ExecutorTasks.cpp:88).
defects.evidence: src/Processors/Executors/PipelineExecutor.cpp:394 `/// NOTE: this will not decrease \`use_threads\` below initially granted count`; :372 `tasks.init(num_threads, 1, …)`.
defects.notes: Must point at the stale 'initially granted count' comment.

excluded.reason: Asks for a comment explaining TOO_MANY_IDLE_THRESHOLD = 4. Documentation request, not a defect.
Says TOO_MANY_IDLE_THRESHOLD is misnamed as a minimum. Naming preference; 'stop spawning when idle exceeds this' matches shouldSpawn (ExecutorTasks.h:75).
Asks to document why tasks.init gets 1. Documentation request; does not describe D1's consequence.

Says try_to_lock can miss spawns and leave the executor under-spawned. Every executing thread calls spawnThreads() after each processed task (PipelineExecutor.cpp:325), so a skipped attempt is retried; if no task runs there is nothing for new threads to do.
Asks for TSA annotations on spawn_lock. The mutex guards no data (it serializes the spawn loop); convention only.

Says the spawn loop can acquire all slots before any worker registers as idle, defeating the idle cap. Not a regression (base spawned all granted threads anyway); it is a limit on the effectiveness of a timing heuristic, with no concrete wrong behaviour.

Says scheduled-but-not-yet-idle workers bypass the idle cap so short queries can still launch every worker. Same as base behaviour at worst; a heuristic-effectiveness remark, not a defect introduced by the PR.
Says the idle threshold ignores scheduled workers so the loop can queue the entire allocation. At worst equals the pre-PR behaviour; optimisation-quality remark, not a regression.
Says shouldSpawn only counts threads already idle so every granted slot can still spawn immediately. At worst equals the pre-PR behaviour; not a defect introduced by the PR.
Asks to describe idle_threads as a waiting-thread count. The header comment ('changed with threads_queue.size()') is accurate; wording preference.

Asks whether stealing initial runnable tasks from queue 0 causes scan overhead. Speculative performance question; those tasks remain stealable and no concrete cost is shown (the async-affinity consequence is D1).

elastic__elasticsearch@5e318eb.pr_summary: Replaces the static TestEntitlementBootstrap with TestEntitlementsRule, a JUnit @ClassRule on ESTestCase (TEST_ENTITLEMENTS) that sets TestPolicyManager's active / trivially-allowing / entitled-packages state per suite and resets it (plus node base-dir paths) afterwards. Node path grants become Closeable NodeGrants created via TEST_ENTITLEMENTS.newNodeGrant, threaded through a NodeGrantProvider parameter on InternalTestCluster and a Closeable parameter on MockNode (the 2-arg MockNode ctor and IndicesServiceCloseTests pass a no-op); ESIntegTestCase calls revokeNodeGrants when replacing a TEST-scoped cluster. TestPolicyManager.resetAfterTest is removed and setEntitledTestPackages now always starts from the framework defaults.

defects.title: revokeNodeGrants() dereferences POLICY_MANAGER without the null guard newNodeGrant has
defects.statement: POLICY_MANAGER is null unless es.entitlement.enableForTests is true (TestEntitlementsRule.java:77-82). newNodeGrant guards on that (:148-150) but the public revokeNodeGrants (:164-167) unconditionally calls POLICY_MANAGER.clearModuleEntitlementsCache(). Its one caller, ESIntegTestCase.buildAndPutCluster (:550-552), invokes it whenever a TEST-scoped cluster is still in the `clusters` map when the next cluster is built. In the normal flow afterInternal's finally (:613-614) calls clearClusters() after every TEST-scoped test so that branch is not reached, but whenever it is (e.g. clearClusters threw while closing before clusters.clear() ran, or any future caller) and entitlements are disabled, the result is a NullPointerException in test setup instead of a no-op.
defects.evidence: TestEntitlementsRule.java:80-81 `} else { POLICY_MANAGER = null; }`; :148 `if (POLICY_MANAGER == null) { return () -> {}; }` but :165-166 `BASE_DIR_PATHS.keySet().retainAll(List.of(TEMP)); POLICY_MANAGER.clearModuleEntitlementsCache();` unguarded; ESIntegTestCase.java:550-552 `if (testCluster != null) { IOUtils.closeWhileHandlingException(testCluster::close); TEST_ENTITLEMENTS.revokeNodeGrants(); }`; isEnabledForTest defaults to "false" (:253). Reachability limited: afterInternal :613-614 `if (currentClusterScope == Scope.TEST) { clearClusters(); }` empties the map after each test.
defects.notes: A comment must identify the missing POLICY_MANAGER null check in revokeNodeGrants / NPE when entitlements are disabled. Graded low because the normal TEST-scope path clears the cluster map first (hunt graded it high on the assumption every second test reaches it). Thread-safety, typo or naming remarks do not count.

defects.title: The new revokeNodeGrants() call on TEST-scoped cluster replacement is effectively never reached, so per-test grants are not revoked
defects.statement: The PR adds TEST_ENTITLEMENTS.revokeNodeGrants() inside `if (testCluster != null)` in buildAndPutCluster (ESIntegTestCase.java:550-553) as the 'where feasible' revocation between TEST-scoped clusters. But afterInternal (:608-615) closes the cluster and calls clearClusters() after every TEST-scoped test, emptying `clusters`, so clusters.remove(clazz) at :540 returns null and the revocation is skipped. Because NodeGrant.close() is a no-op (TestEntitlementsRule.java:199-205), grants for every previous test's node directories stay active until the suite ends, so the intended per-test isolation is not delivered and the added line is dead in the normal path.
defects.evidence: ESIntegTestCase.java:540 `TestCluster testCluster = clusters.remove(clazz);`, :550-552 revoke only `if (testCluster != null)`; :613-614 `if (currentClusterScope == Scope.TEST) { clearClusters(); }`; clearClusters :562-565 `clusters.clear()`; TestEntitlementsRule.java:204 `// onClose.accept(this);` (close does nothing).
defects.notes: Must say the revocation in buildAndPutCluster is not reached for normal TEST scope because clusters were already cleared after the previous test, so grants accumulate across tests. Low because the PR body accepts grants living until suite end.

excluded.reason: Claims the finally block's active.set(false) should be compareAndSet(true,false) to avoid a race. Only the thread that won compareAndSet(false,true) at TestEntitlementsRule.java:108 enters that finally, so set(false) at :128 is exactly the matching release; there is no race.
Suggests encapsulating the finally-block reset (:123-127) in a PolicyManager reset method. Refactoring preference; the reset is correct.
Points out the typo 'suits' in the assertion message at :131. Cosmetic typo, no functional effect.
Asks for clearer documentation of newNodeGrant. Documentation request, not a defect.
Suggests renaming NodeGrant to EntitledNodePaths. Naming preference.
Describes that the path collections deliberately copy and loop per path to handle duplicates. It describes the intended design (:237-249), which the code implements; no problem.
Suggests renaming sharedDataDir() to sharedDataDirs(). Naming preference.
Points out a 'productions' typo in a comment. Cosmetic typo carried over from the deleted class.

Claims removing resetAfterTest duplicates/scatters the reset logic for isActive/isTriviallyAllowingTestCode. The field initialisers (TestPolicyManager isActive=false, isTriviallyAllowingTestCode=true) and the rule's single finally block (:123-127) now own the reset; nothing is duplicated or lost.

Claims IndicesServiceCloseTests should pass a real node grant instead of `() -> {}` or the node may hit denied filesystem access. Its node paths come from createTempDir(), which lies under the TEMP base dir that initialize() registers for the whole run (TestEntitlementsRule.java:88-92), so no concrete denial is shown; speculative.

Claims the 2-arg MockNode constructor (MockNode.java:245) now supplies no grant so NodeTests/MockNode direct callers will hit entitlement denials. Those callers build settings on createTempDir() homes covered by the globally registered TEMP dir; no reachable denial is demonstrated, and the no-op is a deliberate choice of the PR.

Suggests IndicesServiceCloseTests use newNodeGrant so access does not depend on the global temp allowance. The candidate itself concedes the current paths are covered; hypothetical future-proofing, not a defect.

Asks how direct nodes such as ExternalTestCluster's client obtain config/data grants when path.home is outside the temp tree. Speculative: no caller shown to use a non-temp home with entitlements active.
Asks for a focused test of the rule's grant lifecycle. Test request, not a defect.

Claims removing the WithEntitlementsOnTestCode import leaves {@link WithEntitlementsOnTestCode} in EntitlementMetaTests Javadoc unresolved. EntitlementMetaTests extends ESTestCase, whose nested annotation WithEntitlementsOnTestCode is an inherited member type and resolves by simple name in the class Javadoc, so the link still resolves.

elastic__elasticsearch@bef908c.pr_summary: Renames the feature-flagged `multi_dense_vector` field mapper to `rank_vectors`: MultiDenseVectorFieldMapper/MultiVectorIndexFieldData/MultiVectorDVLeafFieldData become RankVectorsFieldMapper/RankVectorsIndexFieldData/RankVectorsDVLeafFieldData, the mapping CONTENT_TYPE, FeatureFlag name and three search capabilities are renamed, registrations/YAML tests/unit tests updated, and several error messages drop the 'multi' wording. Script-side MultiDenseVector* classes keep their names.

defects.title: Changed error messages in MultiDenseVectorScriptDocValues break existing unit-test assertions
defects.statement: The PR rewrites MISSING_VECTOR_FIELD_MESSAGE (MultiDenseVectorScriptDocValues.java:20, now "A document doesn't have a value for a vector field!") and the get() UnsupportedOperationException text (MultiDenseVectorScriptDocValues.java:60, now "accessing a vector field's value ..."), but MultiDenseVectorScriptDocValuesTests still asserts the old 'multi-vector field' wording at lines 179, 182, 203, 206 (assertEquals on the missing-value message) and 229, 255 (containsString on the get() message). The tests only skip when the feature flag is off, and FeatureFlag is always enabled in snapshot builds (FeatureFlag.java:72-73), so testFloatMissingValues, testByteMissingValues, testFloatGetFunctionIsNotAccessible and testByteGetFunctionIsNotAccessible fail in CI.
defects.evidence: MultiDenseVectorScriptDocValues.java:20 `MISSING_VECTOR_FIELD_MESSAGE = "A document doesn't have a value for a vector field!"`; :60 `"accessing a vector field's value through 'get' or 'value' is not supported, ..."`. MultiDenseVectorScriptDocValuesTests.java:179 `assertEquals("A document doesn't have a value for a multi-vector field!", e.getMessage());` (also 182, 203, 206) and :229/:255 `containsString("accessing a multi-vector field's value through 'get' or 'value' is not supported,"`. The test class's @BeforeClass only assumeTrue(FEATURE_FLAG.isEnabled()), and FeatureFlag.java:72-73 forces enabled on snapshot builds. The PR's diff to this test file only updates lines 34, 118, 145.
defects.notes: A comment counts if it says the renamed error text in MultiDenseVectorScriptDocValues no longer matches assertions in MultiDenseVectorScriptDocValuesTests (either the missing-value message or the get()/value message), so those tests will fail. Comments merely preferring different wording of the messages (without noting the test mismatch) do not count.

excluded.reason: Claims MultiDenseVectorScriptDocValues should be renamed to include 'Rank' to avoid confusion. Naming preference: the PR deliberately limits the rename to the mapper/field-data layer; the script-side classes are consistently named and referenced, nothing breaks.
Claims the Javadoc 'rank-vectors's' possessive is ungrammatical. Comment grammar only, no behavioural or maintainability consequence.
Claims RankVectorsDVLeafFieldData.java:48 error message still says 'multi-vector field' and should say rank vectors. The message remains accurate and nothing matches on it; wording preference.

Claims MultiDenseVector.java's EMPTY message should keep 'Multi Dense' for clarity. Wording preference; the message still explains the missing value and how to check it, and MultiDenseVectorTests was updated accordingly.

Claims the iterator() message in MultiDenseVectorDocValuesField now says rank_vectors while the class is still MultiDenseVector*, which is confusing. The message names the user-facing field type users actually map, and the tests (MultiDenseVectorScriptDocValuesTests.java:118,145) were updated to match; not a defect.

Claims existing indices with `multi_dense_vector` mappings will fail to open after upgrade and older nodes cannot parse `rank_vectors` during rolling upgrades.
