Asks to rename MultiDenseVectorFieldTypeTests to RankVectorsFieldTypeTests. Test class naming preference, no defect.

elastic__elasticsearch@e355340.pr_summary: Makes snapshot finalization run on the SNAPSHOT thread pool from the start: SnapshotsService.finalizeSnapshotEntry now submits a SnapshotFinalization AbstractRunnable to the SNAPSHOT executor (with a shutdown-aware onRejection), and the clone-metadata computation runs inline instead of forking again. BlobStoreRepository.finalizeSnapshot asserts it is on SNAPSHOT, fetches RepositoryData with the SNAPSHOT executor instead of DIRECT, and writes the SnapshotInfo blob inline rather than forking it.

excluded.reason: Claim: Threading assumption tightened with asserts. `finalizeSnapshot(...)` now asserts SNAPSHOT thread at entry and before root blob update. Please confirm all call paths into `finalizeSnapshot` are executed on `ThreadPool.Names.SNAPSHOT`, and that the `SubscribableListener` chain never invokes these stag -- Rejected: All production calls into finalizeSnapshot go through SnapshotFinalization.doRun on the SNAPSHOT pool (SnapshotsService.java:1402-1403, 1540); the wrappers (S3Repository:394, SourceOnlySnapshotRepository:99, FilterRepository:80) call through synchronously. The direct test callers (BlobStoreRepositoryRestoreTests:175, AbstractSnapshotIntegTestCase:546) run on TEST- threads, which ThreadPool.assertCurrentThreadPool explicitly permits (ThreadPool.java:1051-1053). In the chain, getRepositoryData(executor, …) completes inline on the SNAPSHOT caller or via ThreadedActionListener(executor) (BlobStoreRepository.java:2257, 2273), and every metadata write completes on SNAPSHOT, so the root-blob assert holds.

Claim: The comment inaccurately implies network usage; update it to specify writing "to the repository" since operations may be local (e.g., `FsRepository`). -- Rejected: Comment wording nit; the head comment (BlobStoreRepository.java:1838) says nothing about the network and is accurate.

Claim: Potential performance regression: `SNAPSHOT_FORMAT.write(...)` is now executed inline (no `executor.execute(...)`). If this write performs blocking IO to the blob store, it will directly occupy a SNAPSHOT thread and may reduce throughput / increase tail latency. Previously it was still scheduled on  -- Rejected: The write already ran on the same SNAPSHOT pool before (it was forked to `executor`); running it inline on a SNAPSHOT thread that is already there saves one fork and uses no extra threads. No throughput regression.

Claim: The SnapshotFinalization class comment lacks specificity regarding preparatory steps, the purpose of FinalizeSnapshotContext, and concrete examples of subsequent activities (e.g., snapshot completion or delete operations), reducing code clarity and developer understanding. -- Rejected: Javadoc wording preference, not a defect.

Claim: The TODO comment incorrectly prescribes moving logic to `BlobStoreRepository#finalizeSnapshot` as a solution, but this approach may be unworkable due to implementation constraints.   -- Rejected: TODO comment wording preference; the TODO says only 'consolidate', no behaviour is affected.

Claim: Potential NPE: `SnapshotsInProgress.get(clusterService.state()).snapshot(snapshot)` may return `null` if the snapshot entry is removed/changed between queuing `SnapshotFinalization` and execution (bigger window now that execution is async). `entry.failure()` and later uses would then NPE. Suggest gu -- Rejected: The finalizing snapshot is held under currentlyFinalizing/endingSnapshots, and only its own finalization removes the entry on this master. The entry could only disappear if this node lost mastership and the new master finished finalizing before the queued task ran; that is contrived. The same window already existed before via the async getRepositoryData callback (SnapshotsService.java:1346-1356) and runNextQueuedOperation.

Claim: You assert SNAPSHOT thread inside the `metadataListener` callback, but `ListenableFuture` does not inherently guarantee listener execution thread unless documented/controlled. Today it works because `metadataListener` is completed on SNAPSHOT thread in both branches, but if future changes complete i -- Rejected: Speculative. metadataListener completes synchronously inside doRun on the SNAPSHOT thread in both branches (completeWith / onResponse), so the listener added afterwards runs inline on SNAPSHOT. The assertion documents exactly that invariant.

Claim: `onRejection` treats only `EsRejectedExecutionException` with `isExecutorShutdown()` as a normal shutdown case. Other rejections (e.g., queue full) are routed to `onFailure()` which logs ERROR and asserts false, potentially turning transient load into 'unexpected failure'. Consider handling non-shut -- Rejected: SNAPSHOT is a SCALING executor (ThreadPool.java:160). Scaling executors reject only on shutdown, so the non-shutdown branch is unreachable.

Claim: the metadataListener future is now completed synchronously and should be replaced by passing the metadata directly. Rejected: simplification suggestion the PR itself flags with a TODO (SnapshotsService.java:1458-1459); behaviour is correct.

Claim: BlobStoreRepositoryRestoreTests.testSnapshotWithConflictingName calls finalizeSnapshot from the test thread, so the new SNAPSHOT-thread assertion fails. Rejected: ThreadPool.assertCurrentThreadPool explicitly accepts threads whose name starts with 'TEST-' or 'LuceneTestCase' (ThreadPool.java:1051-1053), which is exactly the test runner thread, so the assertion passes.

Claim: while the finalization waits on the SNAPSHOT queue, FailPendingRepoTasksTask can remove the entry so snapshot(snapshot) returns null and NPEs. Rejected: finalizeSnapshotEntry is only called while this finalization owns the repository loop (currentlyFinalizing, SnapshotsService.java:1344-1369), and FailPendingRepoTasksTask for the repo is only submitted from the loop owner's own getRepositoryData/delete failure paths; the entry can only vanish on a master failover, which is contrived and already possible before via the async getRepositoryData callback (same as R6).

Claim: after the root blob update the continuation (cleanupOldMetadata) runs on the cluster-state thread, contradicting 'stay on SNAPSHOT'. Rejected: a question about code the PR did not change -- the writeIndexGen completion and cleanupOldMetadata threading are identical before and after, and no new assertion covers that stage, so nothing regresses.

elastic__elasticsearch@5e604e4.pr_summary: Adds a bulk fast path for reading sparse TSDB (ES819) numeric doc values as doubles when the ES|QL planner knows nulls were filtered (nullsFiltered): BaseSparseNumericValues now implements a new OptionalSingletonDoubles.tryReadDoubles, which positions a second 'jump' IndexedDISI on the last doc, and if the number of value indices between first and last doc equals the doc count, decodes whole blocks and converts them in bulk. BlockDocValuesReader.ToDouble becomes a sealed interface with bulk convert/readThenConvert and concrete implementations (half-float, float, double, scaled-float), SingletonDoubles.read tries the fast path first, BlockFactory gains doubles(double[], int), and an assertion is added to SingletonLongs for nullsFiltered.

defects.title: Fast path ignores `offset`: compares the value count from docs[offset..] with the full docs.count() and builds a block of docs.count() positions, so partial-page reads (offset>0) can return wrong values / a wrongly sized block
defects.statement: tryReadDoubles starts at firstDoc = docs.get(offset) (ES819TSDBDocValuesProducer.java:1507) but checks `valueCount == docs.count()` (1534) and returns `factory.doubles(values, docs.count())` (1554). The documents to load are docs[offset..count), i.e. count-offset of them. With offset>0 (ValuesFromSingleReader.load re-reads the remainder of a single-segment non-decreasing page after a jumbo split by row-stride readers; ValuesFromSingleReader.java:57-58,115) the correct condition is valueCount == docs.count()-offset. As written: normally the check just fails and the optimisation is silently lost; but when the range [docs[offset], docs[count-1]] happens to contain exactly `offset` extra valued docs not in the page (common in TSDB where a filter leaves gaps between tsids), the check passes and the method returns docs.count() values that include values of docs not in the page, with docs.count() positions instead of count-offset. sanityCheckBlock (ValuesSourceReaderOperator.java:306-315) then throws IllegalStateException, failing the query (and without that check the values would be misaligned).
defects.evidence: ES819TSDBDocValuesProducer.java:1507 `final int firstDoc = docs.get(offset);`, 1532 `final int valueCount = lastIndex - firstIndex + 1;`, 1534 `if (valueCount == docs.count()) {`, 1554 `return factory.doubles(values, docs.count());`. Contrast readThenConvert (BlockDocValuesReader.java) which sizes by `docs.count() - offset` and loops `for (int i = offset; ...)`. ValuesFromSingleReader.java:115-116 `r.reader.read(loaderBlockFactory, docs, offset, ...)` then `operator.sanityCheckBlock(r.reader, docs.count() - offset, target[r.idx], r.idx)`.
defects.notes: Must say the fast path mishandles a non-zero offset (count/size compared or built against docs.count() instead of docs.count()-offset). Comments only about docs being unsorted/duplicated (R5) or empty docs (R3) do not count.

excluded.reason: Claims LongToScaledFloat's `v / scalingFactor` can yield Inf/NaN if scalingFactor is 0 or non-finite. Division by scalingFactor is unchanged from the base lambda `l -> l / scalingFactor`; scaling_factor validity is enforced at mapping parse time, so this is pre-existing and not introduced here.
Suggests `!nullsFiltered` instead of `nullsFiltered == false`. `== false` is the Elasticsearch codebase convention (enforced by its checkstyle); pure style.

Claims docs.count() could be 0 so docs.get(offset)/docs.get(count-1) would throw. read() is never called with empty docs: ValuesFromSingleReader.loadFromSingleLeaf already calls docs.get(offset) before any reader, and pages have at least one position; unreachable.

Claims lazy initialisation of jumpDISI is not thread-safe. Doc-values iterators and their ColumnAtATimeReader are single-threaded per driver (like the existing currentBlockIndex/currentBlock mutable state); no concurrent access exists.

Claims the first/last-rank arithmetic gives wrong results if docs are unsorted or contain duplicates. nullsFiltered is true only for the main source path (EsPhysicalOperationProviders.java:349; the lookup path passes false at AbstractLookupService.java:435), where docs within a segment are unique and non-decreasing, so the first/last arithmetic is sound for sorted unique docs. (The real problem in this arithmetic is the offset, D1, which R5 does not mention.)
Points out the truncated comment `// bulk convert from the`. Truncated comment `// bulk convert from the` (line 1549) is a cosmetic nit with no behavioural or misleading effect.
Points out the assertion message typo 'nullFiltered'. Typo in an assertion message (BlockDocValuesReader.java:149); trivial.

Claims `assert nullsFiltered == false` in SingletonLongs is inverted. Wrong: the assertion sits in the branch where the doc has NO value, so `assert nullsFiltered == false` fires exactly when nulls were supposed to be filtered but a doc lacks a value — the intended check.
Says SortableShortToHalfFloat's array convert duplicates the scalar conversion. Duplicated one-line conversion inside SortableShortToHalfFloat is a style/refactoring preference with no drift.

Says the fallback readThenConvert does not assert nullsFiltered like the direct path. The fallback readThenConvert appending nulls is the pre-existing behaviour of SingletonDoubles.read; not asserting nullsFiltered there is a consistency preference, not a defect.

Claims `new double[valueCount]` is allocated before circuit-breaker accounting in factory.doubles. valueCount is bounded by the page's doc count (the same size the builder path allocates), so this is a negligible, bounded allocation with no concrete heap-exhaustion path.

Claims the bulk path always uses decoder.decode while longValue uses decodeOrdinals when bitsPerOrd != -1, corrupting ordinal-encoded values. Unreachable: tryReadDoubles is only reached through SingletonDoubles over numeric doc values of double/float/half_float/scaled_float fields, which are opened with maxOrd = -1 (getNumeric(FieldInfo) -> getNumeric(entry, -1), ES819TSDBDocValuesProducer.java:185), so bitsPerOrd is always -1 here.
Asks to share the advanceExact/null/build traversal across the four readThenConvert implementations. Refactoring preference; no drift exists.
Asks to document that the returned block covers docs[offset..count). Documentation request (the underlying offset bug is D1).

Claims repeated doc IDs let the rank-span check pass while emitting values of unrequested docs. nullsFiltered is only true on the main source path where docs within a segment are unique (the lookup/enrich path passes false), and the codec comment (isDense) documents the same assumption; not reachable.
Asks for a test of the sparse double fast path. Test request.
Asks readThenConvert to call convert(long) instead of restating the conversion. Refactoring preference; no drift.
Asks the four converters to share the traversal loop. Refactoring preference (same as C3).
Asks to name/document BlockFactory.doubles' count as an exact position count. Naming/documentation preference.
Asks to rename `expectedCount` to `positionCount`. Naming preference (same as C12).
Claims docs like [1,1,3] make the bulk path return values for [1,2,3]. Duplicate doc IDs do not reach this path (same as C5): nullsFiltered is only set on the main source path with unique docs.

elastic__elasticsearch@a3bac5f.pr_summary: Adds upgrade-compatibility tests for archive indices and searchable snapshots created in ES 5 and 6 with a custom analyzer using the deprecated 'standard' token filter: two new snapshot zips, four new *CustomAnalyzerIT classes, and a TestSnapshotCases constants class now used by the existing Restore/MountFromVersion5/6IT. recover() gains a warnings consumer; restore/mount requests use WarningsHandler.PERMISSIVE and hand the response warnings to per-test assertions (a no-op consumer for the basic cases). README documents how the snapshots were created.

defects.title: ES_VERSION_6 constants point at the v5 snapshots, so every 'version 6' test actually restores/mounts a v5 snapshot
defects.statement: TestSnapshotCases defines ES_VERSION_6 = "5" (TestSnapshotCases.java:21) and ES_VERSION_6_STANDARD_TOKEN_FILTER = "5_custom_analyzer" (:24), a copy-paste of the v5 constants. copySnapshotFromResources loads "snapshot_v" + version + ".zip", so RestoreFromVersion6IT and MountFromVersion6IT (which previously passed "6") now load snapshot_v5.zip and the new RestoreFromVersion6CustomAnalyzerIT / MountFromVersion6CustomAnalyzerIT load snapshot_v5_custom_analyzer.zip; the added snapshot_v6_custom_analyzer.zip is never used. Existing ES6 archive/searchable-snapshot coverage is silently lost and the new v6 custom-analyzer case never tests a v6 index, while all tests stay green.
defects.evidence: TestSnapshotCases.java:21 `public static final String ES_VERSION_6 = "5";` and :24 `public static final String ES_VERSION_6_STANDARD_TOKEN_FILTER = "5_custom_analyzer";`; the diff changes `super(version, "6")` to `super(version, TestSnapshotCases.ES_VERSION_6)` in RestoreFromVersion6IT/MountFromVersion6IT; AbstractUpgradeCompatibilityTestCase copySnapshotFromResources resolves "snapshot_v" + version + ".zip".
defects.notes: Must say ES_VERSION_6 and/or ES_VERSION_6_STANDARD_TOKEN_FILTER hold v5 values so v6 tests load v5 fixtures. Pointing at either constant or at any of the four v6 test constructors with that reason counts.

defects.title: README labels the new version-6 custom-analyzer recipes as 'Version 5'
defects.statement: README.md adds two v6 custom-analyzer recipes but titles them '### Create Index Version 5 - Custom-Analyzer' (README.md:127, which uses the v6 'doc' type) and '### Add documents Version 5 - Custom-Analyzer' (README.md:186, POSTing via the v6 API), duplicating the v5 headers at :70 and :168. Anyone regenerating snapshot_v6_custom_analyzer.zip cannot tell which recipe is for v6.
defects.evidence: README.md:70 and :127 both read '### Create Index Version 5 - Custom-Analyzer'; :168 and :186 both read '### Add documents Version 5 - Custom-Analyzer'; the second of each is the v6 recipe.
defects.notes: Either mislabelled header counts. A comment only about 'doc' vs '_doc' mapping-type naming without the Version 5/6 mislabel is a near-miss.

defects.title: PERMISSIVE warnings handler with a no-op consumer drops strict warning checks for the basic restore/mount tests
defects.statement: recover() in ArchiveIndexTestCase (:61) and SearchableSnapshotTestCase (:56) now sets RequestOptions with WarningsHandler.PERMISSIVE for every test, and the basic-case constructors pass a no-op consumer (`o -> {}`). ESRestTestCase builds its client with setStrictDeprecationMode(true), so before this PR any unexpected deprecation warning on a basic v5/v6 restore or mount failed the test; now such warnings are silently accepted, weakening the existing basic compatibility tests.
defects.evidence: Diff: `request.setOptions(RequestOptions.DEFAULT.toBuilder().setWarningsHandler(WarningsHandler.PERMISSIVE));` in both recover() implementations; basic constructors `this(version, indexCreatedVersion, o -> {});`; ESRestTestCase.java:1551 `builder.setStrictDeprecationMode(true);`.
defects.notes: Must say the basic (non-custom-analyzer) cases lose strict/unexpected-warning detection because of PERMISSIVE plus the no-op consumer. A generic request for more assertions does not count.

excluded.reason: Suggests merging the two adjacent string literals "The [standard] token filter is " + "deprecated ..." into one. Pure style; the concatenation is behaviourally identical.

Claims the new custom-analyzer tests could pass with a broken analyzer after upgrade because the upgraded-cluster check only counts documents. A request for stronger test assertions; the PR introduces no bug, and adding analyzer-exercising checks is a test-coverage wish.
Suggests removing the redundant warningsConsumer parameters from verifyCompatibility/recover since the field is already stored. API simplification preference; behaviour is correct.

elastic__elasticsearch@902352a.pr_summary: Makes `content` optional on messages of the unified chat-completion inference API: UnifiedCompletionRequest.Message's parser declares `content` with optionalConstructorArg, OpenAiUnifiedChatCompletionRequestEntity gains a `case null` branch that omits the content field, and two unit tests that expected null content to fail serialization are deleted.

defects.title: Message wire serialization still treats content as required, so a content-less message NPEs if the request is serialized over transport
defects.statement: The parser now accepts a Message with content == null (UnifiedCompletionRequest.java:125-130), but Message.writeTo still calls out.writeNamedWriteable(content) (line 161) and Message(StreamInput) calls in.readNamedWriteable(Content.class) (line 151). UnifiedCompletionAction.Request.writeTo serializes the whole UnifiedCompletionRequest, so writing a request holding a content-less message throws a NullPointerException. Optional content stops at the REST parser and the OpenAI entity. At head the action executes on the coordinating node and nothing forwards it between nodes, so this is latent rather than a failure on today's path; the wire format needs writeOptionalNamedWriteable/readOptionalNamedWriteable (with a TransportVersion gate).
defects.evidence: UnifiedCompletionRequest.java:126 `optionalConstructorArg(),` for ParseField("content"); :151 `in.readNamedWriteable(Content.class),`; :161 `out.writeNamedWriteable(content);`. No sendRequest/reroute in x-pack/plugin/inference/.../action at head, so the path is currently not exercised.
defects.notes: Must say Message.writeTo / the StreamInput constructor still require content and will NPE / need optional named writeables now that content can be null. Comments only about OpenAI JSON omitting `content` (R1, C3) or about the QA mock service calling content().toString() do not count.

excluded.reason: Asks to confirm that omitting `content` matches OpenAI's schema and to validate that null content only occurs with tool_calls. Omitting content is the PR's intended behaviour (assistant messages with tool_calls have no content); for other roles the upstream API rejects with its own 400, which ES surfaces. A request for validation/tests, not a bug.

Says a `{"role":"user"}` message without content now parses and is sent to OpenAI, and asks for role-specific enforcement. Same as R1: upstream validates and returns an error; the PR deliberately relaxes the ES-side check.

Says the QA TestStreamingCompletionServiceExtension (line 177) calls message.content().toString() and would throw for a content-less message. Test-only mock plugin; no test sends a content-less message, so nothing breaks.
Asks for a test asserting a content-less message serializes without a `content` field, replacing the deleted tests. Request for tests.
Asks for a positive test of the new `case null` serialization. Request for tests.

elastic__elasticsearch@761281a.pr_summary: Tightens entitlement resolution so that only classes in the system class loader's unnamed module receive the agent entitlements (CreateClassLoaderEntitlement); previously any unnamed module from any class loader (e.g. script class loaders) fell into the agent branch. PolicyManager gains an agentsModule constructor parameter compared by identity, EntitlementInitialization passes ClassLoader.getSystemClassLoader().getUnnamedModule(), tests are updated for the new constructor, and a changelog entry is added.

excluded.reason: Claims AGENTS_MODULE (the system class loader's unnamed module) may not be the agent's real module if the agent is loaded by another or the bootstrap loader, causing identity mismatches. The APM agent is attached with -javaagent, whose JAR is loaded by the system class loader into exactly that unnamed module; nothing in the repository shows agent code calling entitlement-checked methods from another loader, so no concrete mismatch is demonstrable.

Suggests requireNonNull(agentsModule) because a null would silently disable the agent branch. The only production caller passes a non-null static (EntitlementInitialization.java:61/120) and the sibling entitlementsModule/pluginResolver are not null-checked either; defensive-style suggestion, no reachable failure.

Warns that only the exact agentsModule instance now receives agent entitlements, so other unnamed modules fall through to NONE, and asks to justify identity comparison. That is precisely the intended fix (stop granting agent entitlements to script/other unnamed modules), and ClassLoader.getUnnamedModule() returns a stable instance, so == is correct.

Asks for tests asserting the system loader's unnamed module gets CreateClassLoaderEntitlement and an independently loaded unnamed module does not. Test-coverage request; the production logic is correct.
Asks for a regression test with non-empty agent entitlements covering both sides of the agent-module identity check. Test-coverage request, not a defect.

elastic__elasticsearch@2adcb2d.pr_summary: Adds a ProjectsDelta record (added/removed ProjectId sets) to ClusterChangedEvent, computed once in the constructor from the previous and current Metadata project maps via Sets.difference (which returns fresh HashSets, wrapped unmodifiable), exposed via projectDelta(). A fast path returns a shared empty delta when both states hold only the default project. A new test covers no change, adding, adding+removing and removing all non-default projects.

excluded.reason: Claims the accessor projectDelta() should be named projectsDelta() to match the field and the nodesDelta pattern. Naming preference; the method works and the new API is used consistently.

Claims the fast path's size()/hasProject() checks are redundant and should cache the maps and use containsKey. Micro-optimisation: hasProject is a containsKey on the same map and projects() returns the field; no measurable effect.
Claims calculateProjectDelta needs defensive null checks on the metadata. Unreachable: the constructor requireNonNull's both states and ClusterState.metadata() is never null.
Claims a shortcut for identical metadata objects is missing. Optional optimisation; identical metadata yields empty differences and the common single-default-project case already short-circuits.
Claims EMPTY_PROJECT_DELTA should live inside the ProjectsDelta record. Code-organisation preference with no behavioural effect.
Claims EMPTY_PROJECT_DELTA is declared after the method using it. Declaration-order style; static fields are initialised before any instance is constructed, so behaviour is correct.
Says the test comment 'Remove all projects' is inaccurate because the default project is retained. Wording nit in a test comment; the test logic and assertions are correct.
Says 'Remove all projects' suggests an empty-project state though the default project remains. Same test-comment wording nit as C1.

Suggests TimestampFieldMapperService.applyClusterState should consume the new projectDelta().removed() instead of computing removals itself. Follow-up adoption suggestion (the PR only introduces the API); the existing consumer is unchanged and correct.

elastic__elasticsearch@a9973f6.pr_summary: Changes the entitlement checker-method naming convention so every check method names the target class: instance methods check$pkg_Class$method (receiver as second argument), static methods check$pkg_Class$$method, constructors check$pkg_Class$. parseCheckerMethodSignature derives static-ness from '$$', MethodKey gains a hasReceiver component that InstrumenterImpl sets from the visited method's access flags, and tests are updated.

defects.title: Production checker check$java_lang_System$exit was not migrated to the new '$$' static spelling, so entitlement initialization throws (System.exit never instrumented)
defects.statement: With the new parser a name without '$$' is an instance check (InstrumentationServiceImpl.java:73-78) that must take (Class<?>, <object receiver>, ...) (119-133). The PR leaves the real bridge interface untouched: EntitlementChecker.java:16 still declares `check$java_lang_System$exit(Class<?> callerClass, int status)` (implemented in ElasticsearchEntitlementChecker.java:31 and the Java23 variant). EntitlementInitialization.initialize calls lookupMethodsToInstrument on that interface, the second argument is the primitive int, so parseCheckerMethodSignature throws IllegalArgumentException and entitlement bootstrap fails; even if it parsed, hasReceiver=true would never match the static System.exit key built by InstrumenterImpl (hasReceiver=false).
defects.evidence: InstrumentationServiceImpl.java:73 `int classNameEndIndex = checkerMethodName.lastIndexOf("$$");` :75-76 `if (classNameEndIndex == -1) { targetMethodIsStatic = false;`; :119-121 `checkerMethodArgumentTypes.length < 2 || ... || checkerMethodArgumentTypes[1].getSort() != Type.OBJECT` -> throw. Head EntitlementChecker.java:16 `void check$java_lang_System$exit(Class<?> callerClass, int status);` (file not in files.txt).
defects.notes: Must say the existing production check method(s) (System.exit) still use the old single-'$' static spelling and are now parsed as instance methods, failing initialization or never matching. Parser edge-case comments (no '$', empty method name) do not count.

defects.title: Invalid-name error message still documents the old (now reversed) convention
defects.statement: The IllegalArgumentException text (InstrumentationServiceImpl.java:86-93) still says `check$$methodName (instance)` and `check$package_ClassName$methodName (static)`, which the new parser respectively rejects (missing class) and treats as an instance method - steering checker authors into the D1 mistake.
defects.evidence: InstrumentationServiceImpl.java:90 `"It should be either check$$methodName (instance), check$package_ClassName$methodName (static) or "` vs :73-82 ('$$' => static) and :101-103 (blank class rejected).
defects.notes: Count a comment that the error message / format description is outdated or contradicts the new naming rules (including the nit inside C6).

defects.title: testParseCheckerMethodSignatureStaticMethodIncorrectArgumentCount no longer exercises the static branch

defects.evidence: Tests.java:236 `assertParseCheckerMethodSignatureThrows("It must have a first argument of Class<?> type", "check$ClassName$staticMethod");`; InstrumentationServiceImpl.java:123-126 instance message `"It must have a first argument of Class<?> type, and a second argument ..."`.
defects.notes: Counts: the static-arg-count test still uses a single-'$' name so it goes through the instance branch. C8 names the same cause but wrongly claims the test fails (it passes via the shared substring).

excluded.reason: Suggests using lastIndexOf('$') plus a preceding-character check instead of lastIndexOf("$$") to find the class boundary. lastIndexOf("$$") is the intended static separator and no concrete mis-parsed input is named.

Claims a name with no '$' skips the format exception and crashes in substring(0,-1). Wrong: InstrumentationServiceImpl.java:85 checks `classNameStartIndex == -1 || ...` and throws first (covered by testParseCheckerMethodSignatureOneDollarSign-style cases).

Claims a checker named check$Class$$ yields an empty method name without validation. Contrived first-party typo in the checker interface; the resulting key simply never matches, no reachable production consequence.
Claims Type::getInternalName throws on primitive argument types in InstrumenterImpl. Wrong and pre-existing: that mapping predates the PR and the existing System.exit(int) key relied on it.
Points out a missing 'is' in the MethodKey javadoc. Grammar nit.

Claims hasReceiver is unused dead code and should be renamed isInstance. Wrong: it is a record component used in equals/hashCode for the checkMethods lookup (InstrumenterImpl.java:171-178); naming preference.
Asks to remove the unreachable '<init>' comparison in TestMethodUtils.methodKeyForTarget. Redundant but harmless test-helper code; style.
Asks to remove the '<init>' check in TestMethodUtils since reflect.Method cannot be a constructor. Redundant but harmless test-helper code; style.

elastic__elasticsearch@4d9b96f.pr_summary: Makes PolicyManager.checkFileRead/checkFileWrite(Path) return early (allow) when the path belongs to a FileSystem whose class differs from the default filesystem's class (captured once in DEFAULT_FILESYSTEM_CLASS), logging the skip at debug, so e.g. ZipPaths are no longer checked against host-path grants. Also adds debug logging to FileAccessTree.checkPath and isParent.

defects.title: Skipping checks for non-default filesystems lets a component read/modify protected host files through a zip filesystem
defects.statement: checkFileRead/checkFileWrite now return immediately for any Path whose FileSystem class is not the default one (PolicyManager.java:311-325, 328-330, 357-359). A zip/jar FileSystem is backed by a host file, and opening it is not entitlement-checked on that archive: only the default provider's newFileSystem is instrumented (EntitlementInitialization.java:307-327, and it checks JVM-global-state, not file read), and the zipfs provider's own access to the archive comes from the jdk.zipfs system module, which isTriviallyAllowed (PolicyManager.java:610-621). Before this PR, operations on the resulting ZipPaths were checked (and denied) against the component's grants. Now a plugin without file entitlements can read, and write entries into, any zip/jar on disk (e.g. another plugin's jar) via FileSystems.newFileSystem(protectedArchive).
defects.evidence: PolicyManager.java:313 if (path.getFileSystem().getClass() != DEFAULT_FILESYSTEM_CLASS) { ... return false; } and checkFileRead: if (isPathOnDefaultFilesystem(path) == false) { return; }; EntitlementInitialization.fileSystemProviderChecks instruments only FileSystems.getDefault().provider().getClass(); ElasticsearchEntitlementChecker.checkNewFileSystem(..., Path path, ...) only calls checkChangeJVMGlobalState; isTriviallyAllowed: if (systemModules.contains(requestingClass.getModule())) return true.
defects.notes: Must say that non-default filesystems such as zipfs can be backed by protected host files, so exempting them lets a component reach (read/write) protected data. A comment only asking whether class vs instance comparison is intended (C4/C7), or claiming a plugin-defined delegating filesystem bypasses checks (C3, blocked by default-provider instrumentation), does not count.

excluded.reason: Claims the new checkPath debug log is too verbose for production and should be trace. It uses the Supplier overload, so nothing is formatted unless debug is enabled for this logger; log-level preference.
Claims the new isParent debug log may cause excessive log volume. Lazy supplier, no cost unless debug is enabled; preference.
Asks to stop logging the full grant list on every path check. Only evaluated when debug logging is enabled for this class; logging preference.
Asks to remove the per-check debug statements that join the whole granted-path list. Lazy suppliers cost nothing unless debug is enabled; logging preference.

Claims String.join(",", paths) in the debug log would NPE if paths were null. paths is an internal array built in the FileAccessTree constructor and never null, and the existing code already dereferences paths.length.
Claims getFileSystem().getClass() is computed twice instead of using the local variable. Trivial redundancy with identical results; style.

Claims a delegating wrapper filesystem lets a caller reach forbidden host files because its class differs from the default. The wrapper's provider must still call the default provider, whose methods are instrumented with the wrapper (plugin) class as caller, so the host-path check still runs; the real exposure is through system-module-backed filesystems like zipfs (D1).

Asks whether distinct instances of the same filesystem class should also be exempt, since the check compares classes. Design clarification; there is one default filesystem instance and no concrete wrong outcome is shown.

Asks whether filesystem identity rather than implementation class should be compared, and notes PathUtils may swap the default filesystem in tests. Design clarification / test-only speculation without a concrete failure.
Asks for tests covering both sides of the new filesystem guard. Test request.

elastic__elasticsearch@a6a4623.pr_summary: Lets the highlight option max_analyzed_offset be -1, meaning 'use the index setting index.highlight.max_analyzed_offset'. A new QueryMaxAnalyzedOffset value class resolves a negative query value to the index limit, and DefaultHighlighter, PlainHighlighter, CustomUnifiedHighlighter, CustomFieldHighlighter and AnnotatedTextHighlighter take that type instead of Integer. AbstractHighlighterBuilder validation is relaxed from '> 0' to '>= -1' with a new error message; unit, YAML REST and integration tests are updated and new tests cover -1.

defects.title: testInvalidMaxAnalyzedOffset still draws from [-100, 0], which now includes the valid -1 and 0: random test failures
defects.statement: Validation now rejects only values < -1 (AbstractHighlighterBuilder.java:568), but HighlightBuilderTests.testInvalidMaxAnalyzedOffset (HighlightBuilderTests.java:578-584) still builds its 'invalid' input from randomIntBetween(-100, 0). When -1 or 0 is drawn (2 in 101 runs) parsing succeeds, expectParseThrows fails and the suite goes red. The PR only updated the expected message.
defects.evidence: HighlightBuilderTests.java:580 "{ \"max_analyzed_offset\" : " + randomIntBetween(-100, 0) + "}"; AbstractHighlighterBuilder.java:568 if (maxAnalyzedOffset != null && maxAnalyzedOffset < -1) {
defects.notes: Must say the random range in testInvalidMaxAnalyzedOffset now includes valid values (-1 and/or 0) so the test fails intermittently. A comment only about the message text does not count.

defects.title: No transport-version gate for the new -1 value: older nodes in a mixed cluster reject it when deserializing
defects.statement: maxAnalyzedOffset is still serialized as a plain optional int (AbstractHighlighterBuilder.java:212 writeOptionalInt) with no TransportVersion check, and readFrom runs it through the setter (line 168 maxAnalyzedOffset(in.readOptionalInt())). During a rolling upgrade, a -1 accepted by an upgraded coordinating node is sent to older data nodes whose setter still throws 'must be a positive integer', so shard requests fail instead of using the index limit. Nothing rejects or translates -1 for older nodes.
defects.evidence: AbstractHighlighterBuilder.java:212 out.writeOptionalInt(maxAnalyzedOffset); :168 maxAnalyzedOffset(in.readOptionalInt()); base setter: if (maxAnalyzedOffset != null && maxAnalyzedOffset <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("... must be a positive integer").
defects.notes: Must identify the rolling-upgrade / mixed-cluster serialization problem with sending -1 to nodes that do not understand it. Generic 'add BWC tests' does not count.

defects.title: YAML REST test asserts the new error message but is gated only on 7.12.0, failing in mixed-version runs
defects.statement: 30_max_analyzed_offset.yml:118-133 now expects `[max_analyzed_offset] must be an integer >= -1`, but its requires block is still cluster_features gte_v7.12.0. When the YAML suite runs against a mixed or older cluster, a node without this change answers `must be a positive integer` and the match fails; a new cluster feature/version requirement is needed.
defects.evidence: yml: requires: cluster_features: ["gte_v7.12.0"] ... - match: { error.caused_by.reason: "[max_analyzed_offset] must be an integer >= -1" }
defects.notes: Must say the changed error-message assertion needs a new version/feature gate (or tolerate the old message) for mixed-version/BWC test runs.

defects.title: Relaxed validation newly accepts 0, and the javadoc/docs contradict the -1-only rule
defects.statement: Before, max_analyzed_offset <= 0 was rejected; the new check (AbstractHighlighterBuilder.java:568) also accepts 0, which QueryMaxAnalyzedOffset.create keeps as 0, giving LimitTokenOffsetAnalyzer(..., 0): silently no highlights where a 400 was returned before. The new javadoc (line 564) says 'a negative int' means use the index default although only -1 is accepted, and the highlighting reference still describes only non-negative values.
defects.evidence: AbstractHighlighterBuilder.java:564 "maxAnalyzedOffset" might be non-negative int, null (unknown), or a negative int (defaulting to index analyzed offset).; :568 maxAnalyzedOffset < -1.
defects.notes: Must note that 0 is now accepted, or that the javadoc says any negative value while only -1 is valid. One facet suffices. A pure request to document -1 in the reference docs, with no contradiction named, is not enough.

excluded.reason: Claims getNotNull() is a confusing name since it returns a primitive. Naming preference; the method behaves correctly.
Claims getNotNull() is misleading and callers could NPE on a null wrapper. Naming preference; every call site null-checks the wrapper first.
Suggests keeping an Integer variable and renaming the wrapper in PlainHighlighter for clarity. The reviewer itself says the logic is equivalent; readability suggestion.
Claims the constructor comment says negative values are resolved while the constructor just assigns. The resolution happens in create(), which does exactly that; a misplaced comment, trivial.
Asks to move the negative-resolution comment from the constructor to create(). Trivial comment placement.
Suggests resolving the sentinel at the entry points and keeping Integer downstream instead of a wrapper class. Design preference; behaviour is correct.

elastic__elasticsearch@10d682d.pr_summary: Adds a critical X.509 keyUsage extension to certificates generated by elasticsearch-certutil and security auto-configuration: self-signed CAs default to keyCertSign,cRLSign, HTTP certificates/CSRs to digitalSignature,keyEncipherment. CertGenUtils gains KEY_USAGE_MAPPINGS/KEY_USAGE_BITS, buildKeyUsage/isValidKeyUsage and keyUsage parameters; certutil ca/cert get --ca-keyusage; the interactive certutil http wizard can prompt for CA and certificate key usages. Tests and docs updated.

defects.title: HttpCertificateCommandTests is flaky: an empty random CA key-usage subset makes the wizard use the default while the test expects no bits
defects.statement: In the 'change CA defaults' branch the test sets caKeyUsage = randomSubsetOf(KEY_USAGE_MAPPINGS.keySet()) (HttpCertificateCommandTests.java:383); randomSubsetOf picks a size in [0, 9], so the subset is empty ~1 in 10 times and the test types an empty line. HttpCertificateCommand.tryReadInput (HttpCertificateCommand.java:1178) returns the default [keyCertSign, cRLSign] on empty input, so the CA carries bits 5 and 6, and assertExpectedKeyUsage(caCertKey.v1(), caKeyUsage) (line 474) — which asserts every non-expected bit is false — fails. The test fails on roughly 5% of seeds.
defects.evidence: HttpCertificateCommandTests.java:383 `caKeyUsage = randomSubsetOf(CertGenUtils.KEY_USAGE_MAPPINGS.keySet());` then `terminal.addTextInput(Strings.collectionToCommaDelimitedString(caKeyUsage));` (empty string for an empty subset). HttpCertificateCommand.java:1178 `if (Strings.isEmpty(input)) { return defaultValue; }` with default DEFAULT_CA_KEY_USAGE. CertGenUtilsTests.java:268-273 asserts bits not in the expected set are false. Contrast CertGenUtilsTests.java:211 which uses randomNonEmptySubsetOf.
defects.notes: Must say the random subset can be empty and empty input yields the default key usage, so the assertion fails (flaky test). Suggesting randomNonEmptySubsetOf is the fix. Comments only about duplicates, trailing commas or separator-only input in readKeyUsage do not count.

excluded.reason: Suggests Map.ofEntries() instead of Map.of() for KEY_USAGE_MAPPINGS. Style preference.

Says the key usage mapping constants are test-only and belong in a test utility. KEY_USAGE_MAPPINGS is used in production (buildKeyUsage, HttpCertificateCommand prompts at lines 765/948/1055); only KEY_USAGE_BITS is test-only, a placement nit.

Says the public KEY_USAGE_BITS is unused and a second source of truth. It is used by CertGenUtilsTests.assertExpectedKeyUsage and testBuildKeyUsage checks its keys against KEY_USAGE_MAPPINGS; the values are fixed by X.509 and have not drifted. API-surface nit.
Suggests buildKeyUsage's exception list the allowed values. Error-message improvement; the interactive path lists them and the names are the RFC 5280 names.
Suggests renaming --ca-keyusage to --keyusage. Naming preference; consistent with --ca-dn and also accepted by `cert`.

Says a comma-only --ca-keyusage value (e.g. ',,,') yields an empty list and so no keyUsage extension. Contrived input: only a value made entirely of commas does this (splitStringByCommaToArray drops empties); any real token is validated and unknown ones throw.
Says getCaKeyUsage should use values() to allow repeated --ca-keyusage flags. The option is documented as one comma-separated list; value() is intended.
Says readKeyUsage accepts duplicate usages and should dedupe/require non-empty. Duplicates are harmless (bits OR-ed in buildKeyUsage); empty tokens between values are rejected.

Says entering ',' at the interactive key-usage prompt yields a certificate without the keyUsage extension because String.split drops trailing empties. True mechanically (',' .split(',') is empty and buildKeyUsage returns null) but contrived input: a user deliberately typing only separators; not a normal path.

Says split(',') lets ',' and a trailing comma through, silently omitting the extension. Same contrived separator-only input as C3; a trailing comma after a valid usage yields exactly the usages typed.
Says 'digitalSignature,' bypasses the empty-entry check and creates a certificate with only digitalSignature. That is exactly what the user listed; harmless leniency, not a defect.
Says `--ca-keyusage ,` produces a CA without the keyUsage extension. Same contrived separator-only input as R6.

Says a CA can be generated with a keyUsage lacking keyCertSign. Only when the user explicitly overrides the usages to exclude it; the PR deliberately lets the user choose, and the default includes keyCertSign. Validation suggestion, not a defect.
Says --ca-keyusage digitalSignature yields a CA unable to sign certificates. Explicit user override, same as C4; not a defect of the default path.
Says the interactive CA prompt accepts usages without keyCertSign. Explicit user choice, same as C4.
Says an interactive CA override can drop keyCertSign. Same user-override validation suggestion as C4.
Says the HTTP certificate prompt allows TLS-incompatible usages like cRLSign alone. Explicit user override; the defaults are correct; validation suggestion.

Says DEFAULT_CA_KEY_USAGE is duplicated in HttpCertificateCommand and CertificateTool. The copies agree (both List.of("keyCertSign", "cRLSign")); a duplication that has not drifted is a refactor suggestion.
Says CertificateTool.java:114 re-declares the CA usage default. Same non-drifted duplication as C5.

Says the legacy elasticsearch-certgen (CertificateGenerateTool.java:406) still generates CAs without keyUsage by passing null. Pre-existing behaviour of the deprecated tool, unchanged by this PR, which scopes the fix to certutil and auto-configuration.
Says CertificateGenerateTool CAs still lack key usage. Same pre-existing, out-of-scope legacy path as C16.

Says the test-only KEY_USAGE_BITS duplicates the names and could drift from KEY_USAGE_MAPPINGS. The bit indices are fixed by X.509 and currently correct; a speculative drift/placement nit (same as R3).
Asks to derive the test bit indexes from KEY_USAGE_MAPPINGS. Same non-drifted duplication nit as R3/C17.

Says the test comment 'We register 1 extension with the subject alternative names and extended key usage' (HttpCertificateCommandTests.java:~702) omits key usage. A test comment already miscounted before the PR; trivial.
Says the certutil.md --ca-keyusage entry should list the exact accepted names. Request for more documentation; the accepted names are the RFC 5280 names the doc cites.
Asks for a @param keyUsage Javadoc entry on generateCSR. Request for documentation.
Says the CA and certificate key-usage prompt texts are duplicated and should share a helper. Refactor/style suggestion.

elastic__elasticsearch@e38d20c.pr_summary: When error_trace is false, SearchService.maybeWrapListenerForStackTrace now logs the shard failure at DEBUG, prefixed [nodeId][index][shard], before stripping stack traces for transport to the coordinating node. The helper now takes the ShardSearchRequest (for its channel version and shard id) and ClusterService instead of a TransportVersion; the version parameter is dropped from the scroll and QuerySearchRequest executeQueryPhase overloads and their transport handlers, and in the rank-feature, query-by-id and scroll paths the wrap moves after findReaderContext so the stored shard request is used. Adds search and async-search integration tests of the logging, a MockLog pattern-plus-exception expectation, ErrorTraceHelper utilities and a changelog.

defects.title: Async-search logging tests assert the logs immediately after a 0ms-timeout submit, so they race the shard execution (flaky seen tests, vacuous unseen test)
defects.statement: In the three new AsyncSearchErrorTraceIT logging tests, the polling loop waits for the FIRST submission to finish before MockLog capture starts; inside the capture a SECOND submission is sent with wait_for_completion_timeout=0ms (AsyncSearchErrorTraceIT.java:180, 214, 248) and mockLog.assertAllExpectationsMatched() runs right after (181, 215, 249). The 0ms submit can return before the shard query phases have failed and logged, and assertAllExpectationsMatched() does not wait (MockLog.SeenEventExpectation.assertMatched checks seenLatch.getCount()==0 without awaiting). The seen-log tests are therefore timing-dependent/flaky, and the error_trace=true unseen test can pass before any shard has run.
defects.evidence: AsyncSearchErrorTraceIT.java:160-181: first submit with `wait_for_completion_timeout=0ms`, loop `while (responseEntity.get("is_running") ... isRunning)` polls it; then `try (var mockLog = MockLog.capture(SearchService.class)) { ErrorTraceHelper.addSeenLoggingExpectations(...); getRestClient().performRequest(searchRequest); mockLog.assertAllExpectationsMatched(); }` re-sends the same 0ms searchRequest. MockLog.java:113-115 assertAllExpectationsMatched calls assertMatched (no await); awaitAllExpectationsMatched exists (119-131) but is not used.
defects.notes: Must say the captured (second) async submit uses wait_for_completion_timeout=0ms / is not waited on before asserting the logs, making the logging assertions racy/flaky or vacuous. Comments only about the polling loop being unbounded do not count.

defects.title: Scroll (and legacy-context query-by-id) phases now decide stack-trace clearing from the stored original request's channel version, not the current channel
defects.statement: Previously the scroll and QuerySearchRequest handlers passed channel.getVersion() of the channel carrying THIS request. Now executeQueryPhase(InternalScrollSearchRequest) uses readerContext.getShardSearchRequest(null) (SearchService.java:865-866), which for LegacyReaderContext returns the ShardSearchRequest stored when the scroll was created; maybeWrapListenerForStackTrace reads its getChannelVersion() (SearchService.java:552). The same applies at line 909-910 for a legacy reader context. In a mixed-version (rolling upgrade) cluster a scroll created via a new coordinator (or locally, channelVersion=current) and continued via a coordinator older than ERROR_TRACE_IN_TRANSPORT_HEADER will have its stack traces stripped even though that coordinator never sends the error_trace header and expects traces; the reverse case keeps traces that should be cleared.
defects.evidence: LegacyReaderContext.java:74-76 `getShardSearchRequest(ShardSearchRequest other) { return shardSearchRequest; }`. SearchService.java:865-866 `final ShardSearchRequest shardSearchRequest = readerContext.getShardSearchRequest(null); listener = maybeWrapListenerForStackTrace(listener, shardSearchRequest, ...)`. SearchService.java:552 `if (request.getChannelVersion().onOrAfter(ERROR_TRACE_IN_TRANSPORT_HEADER) ...)`. Removed from SearchTransportService scroll handler: `channel.getVersion()`. ShardSearchRequest.java:248 local construction sets `channelVersion = TransportVersion.current()`.
defects.notes: Must say the scroll path now uses the version of the stored/original shard request (from LegacyReaderContext) instead of the current channel's version, affecting the error_trace compatibility decision in mixed-version clusters. Only matters in rolling upgrades and only affects diagnostics, hence low.

defects.title: Tests set the SearchService logger to DEBUG globally and never restore it
defects.statement: SearchErrorTraceIT.java:47-50 and AsyncSearchErrorTraceIT.java:48-51 call Configurator.setLevel("org.elasticsearch.search.SearchService", Level.DEBUG) in @BeforeClass, and SearchServiceTests.java:186 does so inside a test, with no teardown. MockLog.close() only removes its appender and ESTestCase.restoreLoggingLevel only restores the ROOT level, so every later test class in the same JVM runs with SearchService at DEBUG (extra shard-failure logging with full stack traces), making results depend on execution order.
defects.evidence: SearchErrorTraceIT.java:47-50 `@BeforeClass public static void setDebugLogLevel() { Configurator.setLevel("org.elasticsearch.search.SearchService", Level.DEBUG); }` (no @AfterClass). ESTestCase.java:587-594 restoreLoggingLevel restores only `LoggerFactory.provider().setRootLevel(capturedLogLevel)`. The idiomatic @TestLogging mechanism (LoggingListener) restores per-logger levels.
defects.notes: Must say the SearchService log level change is not restored/leaks to later tests. Low: consequence is extra logging and order-dependence, not a failure.

excluded.reason: Claims maybeWrapListenerForStackTrace takes needlessly heavy ClusterService and ShardSearchRequest parameters. Design preference: the package-private helper needs the request for getChannelVersion() anyway and clusterService is a SearchService field; nothing is broken.
Wants 5xx shard failures logged at WARN instead of DEBUG. DEBUG is a deliberate, justified choice (PR body on log volume) and failures are still surfaced on the coordinator; opinion, not a defect.

Claims clusterService.localNode() and request.shardId() are evaluated even when DEBUG is off. Wrong: both are evaluated inside the Supplier lambda passed to logger.debug at SearchService.java:557-560, only when DEBUG is enabled.

Claims the debug log can NPE if localNode() or request is null while handling a failure. These listeners run only while a started node serves shard requests (local node set), only when DEBUG is enabled, and request is dereferenced for getChannelVersion() earlier; contrived.
Claims the "[%s]%s" format misplaces a bracket. Self-refuting: ShardId.toString() is "[index][shard]", giving [nodeId][index][shard] exactly as described and as the tests' regex expects.

Says the error_trace=true unseen-log test in SearchErrorTraceIT passes even with no shard failure and should assert the response's failed shards. Test-strength request; the same query is proven to fail shards by the sibling seen-log tests, and the synchronous _search returns only after all shards respond.
Says the multi-search unseen-log test only checks absence of logs and should assert subresponse shard failures. Test-strength request, not a defect of the change.

Says the async polling loops have no deadline and could spin forever if a search stays running. Same pattern as the pre-existing tests in the class, the searches fail fast, and the test framework's suite timeout bounds it; nicety.

Says PatternAndExceptionSeenEventExpectation does not verify the stack trace was non-empty at log time, so logging after clearing would still pass. Request for a stronger test assertion; the production code logs before clearing (SearchService.java:557-565).

Says the log prefix omits the remote-cluster alias so CCS shard failures cannot be matched to the coordinator's identifier. Enhancement request; the node id + index + shard still identify the failing shard and the PR does not promise CCS alias correlation.

ollama__ollama@af112d6.pr_summary: Adds path validation to model creation: CreateHandler rejects any r.Files key failing a new validRelative() check (empty, leading '/', leading './' or '../', '.', '..', or embedded '/./' '/../' segments) and re-keys the map by filepath.Clean. convertFromSafetensors additionally opens every destination through an os.Root on its temp dir (OpenFile with O_CREATE) to enforce containment, wrapping failures in the new errFilePath, and now closes the converted bin file. Adds unit tests for both.

defects.title: Handler validates before cleaning, so './model.safetensors' and 'nested/../model.safetensors' get HTTP 400 despite the PR's stated contract and its own converter tests
defects.statement: CreateHandler runs validRelative on the raw key before cleaning it (server/create.go:50-57), and validRelative rejects any path starting with './' and any '/../' segment (create.go:161-188). The PR body promises to 'properly handle relative paths (like ./model.safetensors)', and TestConvertFromSafetensors (create_test.go:84-93) treats './model.safetensors' and 'nested/../model.safetensors' as valid, but through the API those keys now get 400 'file path must be relative'; filepath.Clean is applied only after validation so it can never rescue them. TestValidRelative (create_test.go:~141) locks in the rejection, and the converter tests bypass the handler so the inconsistency is not caught. API clients that previously sent './x.safetensors' now fail.
defects.evidence: create.go:51-56 `for k, v := range r.Files { if err := validRelative(k); err != nil { c.AbortWithStatusJSON(http.StatusBadRequest, ...); return }; files[filepath.Clean(k)] = v }`; create.go:172 `if strings.HasPrefix(path, "./") || strings.HasPrefix(path, "../")`; create_test.go `name: "ValidRelativeWithDot", filePath: "./model.safetensors", wantErr: nil`.
defects.notes: Must say validation precedes cleaning / validRelative rejects contained dot-paths like './model.safetensors' that the PR says (and converter tests expect) are valid. The CLI sends base names, so only API callers are affected.

defects.title: Nested file keys pass validRelative but fail the O_CREATE containment probe because parent directories do not exist yet
defects.statement: validRelative accepts nested keys such as 'dir/file.txt', but convertFromSafetensors now calls root.OpenFile(fp, O_CREATE|O_WRONLY) (create.go:277) before createLink, and OpenFile does not create intermediate directories; for 'weights/model.safetensors' it fails with ENOENT and is reported as errFilePath 'file path must be relative: invalid path ...'. Previously createLink's MkdirAll (create.go:~723) handled nested keys. For the base-model Files branch errFilePath is not in the bad-request list (create.go:100), so it surfaces as a generic server error with a misleading message.
defects.evidence: create.go:277 `f, err := root.OpenFile(fp, os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)` then `return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid path %s: %v", errFilePath, fp, err)`; createLink performs `os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o755)` only afterwards.
defects.notes: Must identify that the O_CREATE probe fails for keys in subdirectories (missing parent). A comment only saying O_CREATE has a file-creation side effect (R5) without the nested-path failure does not count.

defects.title: Unconditional map allocation turns an omitted 'files' into an empty map, making errNeitherFromOrFiles unreachable
defects.statement: CreateHandler now always does `files := make(map[string]string, len(r.Files)); ...; r.Files = files` (create.go:50-58), so a request with neither 'from' nor 'files' has a non-nil empty r.Files. The later `else if r.Files != nil` branch (create.go:98) is then taken, detectModelTypeFromFiles returns "" for the empty map and convertModelFromFiles returns errUnknownType, so the client gets 'unknown type' instead of the intended "neither 'from' or 'files' was specified" (create.go:110), which is now dead code.
defects.evidence: create.go:50 `files := make(map[string]string, len(r.Files))`, :58 `r.Files = files`; :98 `} else if r.Files != nil {`; :110 `ch <- gin.H{"error": errNeitherFromOrFiles.Error(), ...}`; convertModelFromFiles default case `return nil, errUnknownType`.
defects.notes: Must say r.Files becomes non-nil when omitted so the neither-from-nor-files error is replaced by 'unknown type'. Status stays 400; only the message/branch changes.

excluded.reason: Suggests replacing validRelative with io/fs.ValidPath. Refactoring preference; no concrete behavioural defect is claimed.

Claims validRelative only checks '/' so Windows backslash paths like '..\..\windows' bypass it. Containment is enforced by os.Root in convertFromSafetensors (create.go:267-281), which rejects backslash traversal and absolute paths on Windows, and GGUF keys are never used as filesystem paths; no escape is reachable.
Asks to confirm the Go toolchain supports os.OpenRoot/Root.OpenFile. go.mod declares `go 1.24`, which provides these APIs; no build break.

Claims the O_CREATE containment check needlessly creates files and should use Stat. The empty file is created in a throwaway temp dir and immediately replaced by createLink; the side effect itself is harmless (the real consequence, failing nested paths, is D2, which R5 does not mention).
Says adding errFilePath to the adapter error-classification loop is ineffective because both branches return 400. True but a redundancy/style point with no behavioural consequence.

Claims the valid-path TestConvertFromSafetensors cases cannot pass because the '{}' safetensors fixture has no tensors. Not demonstrated from the code: the fixture flows into convert.ConvertModel with a minimal config/tokenizer and the PR's CI ran these tests; speculation about test fixture adequacy, not a verified defect.

Claims keys like 'a//b.gguf' and 'a/b.gguf' collide after filepath.Clean and one digest is silently dropped. Contrived: a client must send two keys naming the same file; before the PR they already resolved to the same destination path for safetensors.
Claims 'a//b' and 'a/b' normalize to the same key so one digest is dropped nondeterministically. Same contrived duplicate-key scenario as C10.

Claims 'a//model.safetensors' and 'a/model.safetensors' clean to the same key and one silently wins. Same contrived duplicate-key scenario as C10; they already mapped to the same destination file before the PR.

ollama__ollama@498792c.pr_summary: Adds integration tests: api_test.go (generate/chat streaming and non-streaming field checks, ps, list, show, embeddings) and model_arch_test.go (build tag `models`: generate across ~23 chat model architectures and compare embeddings with hard-coded expected vectors, with soft/hard timeouts and OLLAMA_MAX_VRAM skips). Switches the default integration model from orca-mini to llama3.2:1b across existing tests.

defects.title: Soft-timeout skip compares time since package init against a per-test remaining-time budget, so later model-arch subtests (the embed suite) skip early
defects.statement: getTimeouts (integration/model_arch_test.go:49-57) returns softTimeout as the time remaining from the moment the test calls it until deadline-2m. Each subtest then skips when `time.Now().Sub(started) > softTimeout` (lines 82, 135), where `started` is a package-level var set at package load (line 20). Elapsed-since-package-start is compared against remaining-time-from-test-start, so all time spent by earlier tests (the other integration tests, and TestModelsGenerate before TestModelsEmbed) is double counted: once TestModelsEmbed starts after a long generate run, elapsed can already exceed its softTimeout and every embedding subtest is skipped silently.
defects.evidence: model_arch_test.go:20 `started    = time.Now()`; :57 `return -time.Since(deadline.Add(-2 * time.Minute)), ...` (= deadline-2m-now, a remaining duration computed when each Test* starts); :82/:135 `if time.Now().Sub(started) > softTimeout { t.Skip("skipping remaining tests to avoid excessive runtime") }`.
defects.notes: Must say the skip uses the package-global `started` (package age / time used by earlier tests) against a softTimeout that is already a per-test remaining budget, so subtests (especially embed ones) skip too early. A comment only about getTimeouts readability or named returns (R1) does not count.

defects.title: New TestAPIEmbeddings still uses orca-mini despite the PR's switch to llama3.2:1b
defects.statement: The PR switches the integration suite from orca-mini to llama3.2:1b and rewrites every other default-model occurrence, but the newly added TestAPIEmbeddings (integration/api_test.go:408) hard-codes `Model: "orca-mini"` and pulls it (line 416), so a clean run still downloads the old, larger model just for this test.
defects.evidence: api_test.go:408 `Model:  "orca-mini",`; :416 `PullIfMissing(ctx, client, req.Model)`; all other default-model uses (basic_test, llm_test, max_queue_test, concurrency_test, utils_test, api_test generate/chat/list) now say "llama3.2:1b".
defects.notes: Must point at the leftover orca-mini in the new embeddings test. orca-mini:latest in the chatModels arch list is intentional and does not count.

defects.title: TestAPIChat reports a missing created_at as 'missing total_duration'
defects.statement: In TestAPIChat the final-response check `if response.CreatedAt == nilTime` (integration/api_test.go:224) emits `final response missing total_duration`, the message of the real TotalDuration check at line 230-231, so a created_at regression is misreported as a total_duration failure.
defects.evidence: api_test.go:224-225 `if response.CreatedAt == nilTime { t.Errorf("final response missing total_duration: %#v", response)`; :230-231 `if response.Metrics.TotalDuration == 0 { t.Errorf("final response missing total_duration: ...`.
defects.notes: Must name the wrong diagnostic on the CreatedAt check.

defects.title: TestAPIListModels runs PullIfMissing under a 10-second context, so it fails on a cold runner
defects.statement: TestAPIListModels creates a 10s context (integration/api_test.go:297) and passes it to PullIfMissing(ctx, client, "llama3.2:1b") (line 303), which streams a registry pull under that ctx. When the model is not already present (the test run alone, e.g. `-run TestAPIListModels`, on a fresh install) a ~1.3GB download cannot finish in 10s, the pull is cancelled and the test fails with `pull failed` before List is exercised. It only passes when an earlier test already pulled the model.
defects.evidence: api_test.go:297 `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)`; :303 `if err := PullIfMissing(ctx, client, "llama3.2:1b"); err != nil { t.Fatalf("pull failed %s", err)`; utils_test.go:178 `pullError = client.Pull(ctx, pullReq, fn)` uses the caller's ctx. Other tests give pulls 1-15 minutes.
defects.notes: Must say the 10s context also bounds the model pull in the list-models test so a cold pull fails. Line numbers in reviews may be off (C4 cites 275/281).

excluded.reason: Suggests named return values for getTimeouts to clarify soft vs hard timeout. Style preference; the comment above the function already says 'Soft timeout, hard timeout' and the values are correct in themselves (the real bug is how the soft value is compared, D1).

Asks for clarification of the developer comment 'Cut-and-paste the following into the table above' (model_arch_test.go:172). Documentation preference; the comment accurately describes the printed expected vector that follows.
Suggests extracting the hard-coded "llama3.2:1b" into a constant. Style/maintainability preference; every usage is consistent and no behaviour is affected.

Claims that on a stall timeout the generate/chat goroutine leaks on the unbuffered done channel and races the next subtest via the shared req. Only reachable after the subtest has already failed on a timeout, and the same goroutine/unbuffered-done pattern is the pre-existing one in DoGenerate (utils_test.go:254-268); it makes a failing test fail noisier, not a defect worth recording.

Claims the arch loops pull each model before checking its size against OLLAMA_MAX_VRAM, wasting downloads on small-VRAM runners. Design choice: the size is read from the local List, which requires the model to be present; the VRAM skip exists to avoid inference OOM/timeouts, not downloads, and nothing breaks.

Claims small-VRAM runners spend budget downloading models they will skip because PullIfMissing precedes the VRAM check. Same as C1: a deliberate ordering (the size comes from the local model list), an efficiency preference, not a defect.

Claims fixed expected embedding vectors are compared against mutable :latest tags and may fail when a tag is retargeted. Speculative future drift of external registry tags, not a defect in this code; the vectors are intentionally regenerated via the printed output.
Asks that the done_reason assertion also cover non-streaming generation. Deliberate exclusion with a TODO at api_test.go:63-64 explaining it; a coverage request, not a defect.
Asks to remove commented-out assertions in api_test.go. Style/cleanup preference; the commented code carries explanatory notes and does not affect behaviour.

Claims an all-zero embedding makes cosineSimilarity NaN so `sim < 0.99` passes. cosineSimilarity is pre-existing (embed_test.go:30) and an all-zero, correct-length embedding from a model is a contrived failure mode; a test-hardening suggestion, not a defect introduced here.

ollama__ollama@0b52f18.pr_summary: `ollama create` uploads model files and adapters to the server in parallel (errgroup capped at GOMAXPROCS-1, a mutex guarding the rebuilt Files/Adapters maps) instead of sequentially; the CLI sets req.Model instead of the deprecated req.Name; progress rendering now caps the number of rendered state lines at terminal height - 1, with default 80x24 constants when the terminal size is unknown.

defects.title: Progress truncation renders the OLDEST states, hiding active and final status lines once there are more states than terminal rows
defects.statement: progress.go:118 renders `for i := range min(len(p.states), termHeight-1)`, i.e. the first termHeight-1 states. States are append-only (Add, progress.go:86-91) and chronological: 'gathering model components', one 'copying file' spinner per blob (now all added at once by the parallel uploads), then the server-side status spinners and 'pulling' bars from client.Create (cmd.go:161-178). Once a create has more than ~22 states, the newest lines — in-flight uploads, the server's conversion/'writing manifest' status and the final 'success' — are never drawn; the user watches finished spinners until exit. When stderr is not a terminal, GetSize fails and output is capped at 23 lines regardless. The PR description itself says it shows 'the last lines that fit'; the code does the opposite. The cap applies to every command using progress.
defects.evidence: progress.go:118 `for i := range min(len(p.states), termHeight-1) { fmt.Fprint(p.w, p.states[i].String(), "\033[K")` iterates from index 0; Add: `p.states = append(p.states, state)`. cmd.go adds createBlob spinners (createBlob: `p.Add(status, spinner)`) before client.Create's fn adds bars/spinners.
defects.notes: Must say the truncation hides progress lines: either that it keeps the first/oldest rather than the latest/active states, or that states beyond the terminal height are no longer shown (R3 framing counts). Comments only about p.pos/cursor movement exceeding the rendered rows (C1/C3/C6) or the trailing newline (C7) do not count.

excluded.reason: Suggests replacing the mutex-protected map with a pre-allocated slice to avoid locking overhead. Style/micro-optimisation; the locked map is correct and lock cost is negligible next to multi-GB uploads.

Claims the goroutine closures capture the loop variables f and digest, so all goroutines see the last iteration's values. Wrong: go.mod declares `go 1.24.0`, and since Go 1.22 range variables are per-iteration.

Says that with more states than rows, p.pos = len(states) makes the next render move the cursor up past the drawn rows and overwrite/clear earlier terminal output. The pos mismatch is real but harmless: once capped, the block (termHeight-1 lines plus the trailing-newline row) fills the whole screen, and CUU (\033[A) clamps at the top row, which is exactly the block's first line; nothing outside the block is visible to overwrite, and StopAndClear likewise clears only the screen the block occupies.

Says p.pos tracking the total count moves the cursor above the rendered block and overwrites unrelated output, plus an extra newline. Same clamped, harmless mismatch as C1; the extra newline is cosmetic (C7).

Says p.pos = len(p.states) at line 125 makes redraws rewind beyond the displayed area and overwrite earlier output. Same as C1: cursor-up clamps at the top row, which is the block start when the block fills the screen.
Says the newline condition uses the full state count so the last visible line emits a newline leaving a blank row. Cosmetic one-blank-row effect; no functional consequence.
Asks the test error message at cmd_test.go:693 to print req.Model instead of req.Name. Trivial test-message nit.
Asks for a test exercising the parallel multi-blob upload path. Request for tests.
Asks to wrap upload errors with the source path. Error-message improvement; os.Open/EvalSymlinks errors already include the path.
Asks each worker to include its source path in createBlob errors. Same error-message suggestion as C5.
Says the Files and Adapters upload loops duplicate logic and should share an implementation. Refactor suggestion; the two copies are identical, no drift.

ollama__ollama@2ed14f2.pr_summary: Reworks the experimental client2 registry Pull to fetch per-chunk digests from a new /chunksums endpoint and download chunks concurrently, verifying each chunk and writing it directly into the final blob file through a new DiskCache.Chunked/Chunker API (removing the relay-reader pipeline and the whole-blob verification of copyNamedFile). The new registry server's /api/pull coalesces progress into one per-model update on a ticker and supports stream:false. The CLI pull bar label/initial value is adjusted and chunks.Parse becomes generic.

defects.title: Chunksums fetch/parse errors and Chunked open errors are swallowed: Pull succeeds and links a manifest with a missing or incomplete layer
defects.statement: In Registry.Pull, an error from c.Chunked (server/internal/client/ollama/registry.go:477-481) is handled with `t.update(l, 0, err); continue`, and an error yielded by r.chunksums (non-200 status, request error, scanner error, bad digest/range; registry.go:485-489) with `t.update(l, progress.Load(), err); break`. Neither error is returned nor fed into the errgroup, so g.Wait() (542) returns nil, the manifest blob is stored and c.Link (553) commits the model; Pull returns nil. The new server's trace Update (server/internal/registry/server.go:283-289) ignores err, so the client sees success. A registry that 404s/5xxs chunksums for a large layer, or a connection drop mid-chunksums body, yields a 'successful' pull whose model references an absent or partial blob.
defects.evidence: registry.go:486-489 `if err != nil { t.update(l, progress.Load(), err); break }`; 478-481 `if err != nil { t.update(l, 0, err); continue }`; afterwards `if err := g.Wait(); err != nil { return err }` then `blob.PutBytes(c, md, m.Data)` and `return c.Link(m.Name, md)`. chunksums (740-810) yields errors for non-200, send errors, s.Err(), invalid digest/range. server.go Update only stores `progress[l] = n`.
defects.notes: Must say that a chunksums (or Chunked/open) error does not fail Pull — break/continue without returning the error — so the model is committed/reported successful with a missing layer. Comments only about error message wording (R15) or Content-Location validation (R14) do not count.

defects.title: Chunks are written in place at the final blob path; an interrupted pull leaves a full-size file with holes that later pulls accept as cached by size alone
defects.statement: DiskCache.Chunked (server/internal/cache/blob/chunked.go:26-36) opens the final content-addressed path c.GetFile(d) and Put writes each chunk concurrently at its offset (io.NewOffsetWriter, line 53); a failed chunk leaves its partial bytes (no truncate, unlike copyNamedFile). Because chunks finish out of order, a completed chunk near the end extends the file to its full size while earlier ranges are zero holes. If the pull is interrupted (ctrl-C, a chunk error cancelling the errgroup, crash), the next Pull's size-only `exists` check (registry.go:448-451) and Chunked's own `info.Size() == size` pre-check (chunked.go:29-31, returning a no-op Chunker) both accept the corrupt file, skip every chunk hash check and link the manifest over a corrupt blob. The in-progress file is also visible under its final digest name to concurrent readers.
defects.evidence: chunked.go:27-32 `name := c.GetFile(d); info, err := os.Stat(name); if err == nil && info.Size() == size { return &Chunker{}, nil }; f, err := os.OpenFile(name, os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY, 0o666)`; Put 44-46 `if c.f == nil { return nil }`; cache.go Get returns Size from os.Stat; registry.go:449-450 `info, err := c.Get(l.Digest); return err == nil && info.Size == l.Size`. copyNamedFile (cache.go:498-501) truncates on error; Chunker never does.
defects.notes: Must identify that partially downloaded data lives at the final blob path and a size-only check (exists or Chunked pre-validation) will then treat an incomplete/interrupted blob as complete. The oversized-existing-file / missing O_TRUNC claim (R3, C17, C28) is a different, contrived scenario and does not count.

defects.title: Blob GETs no longer carry the registry auth token/User-Agent: authenticated pulls of small layers from the registry fail
defects.statement: The chunk download in Pull builds its request with plain http.NewRequestWithContext (registry.go:499) instead of r.newRequest, which the base used for every blob request and which sets the `Authorization: Bearer <signed token>` and User-Agent headers (registry.go:824-839). For layers below the chunking threshold, cs.URL is the registry's own /v2/<ns>/<model>/blobs/<digest> endpoint (registry.go:717-727), so the request is now unauthenticated: pulling a private model (or from any registry that requires the key) gets 401/403 for those blobs and the pull fails, where it previously worked.
defects.evidence: head registry.go:499 `req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "GET", cs.URL, nil)` then `sendRequest(r.client(), req)`; base Pull: `req, err := r.newRequest(ctx, "GET", blobURL, nil)`; newRequest: `if r.Key != nil { token, err := makeAuthToken(r.Key) ... req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token) }`. chunksums still uses r.newRequest (756), so only the blob GETs lost auth.
defects.notes: Must say blob/chunk requests bypass newRequest and so lose the Authorization (key-signed) header, breaking authenticated/private pulls. Severity medium because the path is behind the client2 experiment.

defects.title: Whole-layer digest and chunk coverage are never verified: a chunksums list with gaps/out-of-range chunks commits a blob that does not match its digest
defects.statement: The old path wrote each blob through copyNamedFile/checkWriter, which hashed the whole layer against l.Digest. Now each Chunker.Put verifies only the chunk hash supplied by the chunksums response (chunked.go:48-56), and nothing checks that the yielded ranges cover [0, l.Size) exactly, are within bounds, or that the assembled file hashes to l.Digest (registry.go:485-540, 797-808: chunks.Parse checks only start<=end). A chunksums body that ends early at a token boundary, omits ranges, or lists ranges past l.Size makes Pull link a blob stored under a digest it does not match (holes, or a file extended past the layer size).
defects.evidence: chunked.go Put: `cw := &checkWriter{d: d, size: chunk.Size(), ... w: io.NewOffsetWriter(c.f, chunk.Start)}` with d the per-chunk digest; no Close/commit step verifies l.Digest (Close is just `c.f.Close()`); chunksums loop yields every parsed (digest, range) with URL blobURL and no bounds/coverage bookkeeping; Pull links after g.Wait.
defects.notes: Must say that per-chunk verification does not establish the layer digest / complete coverage (gaps, truncation, out-of-range chunks) and that Pull commits without a final whole-blob or coverage check. Swallowed chunksums errors are D1; interrupted-pull size-only cache hits are D2.

defects.title: Streaming /api/pull (client2) never sends a terminal "success" status and emits empty-status progress lines
